  • A policy argument urges splitting chemistry from chem-bio in frontier dangerous-capability evaluations

Theory & foundations

  • Toby Ord analyzes feedback-loop dynamics of AI-assisted AI R&D and conditions for intelligence explosions
  • A formal note shows simplicity priors cannot bound the probability of catastrophic value functions under proxy conditions
  • The macroagents series proposes five design lenses (incentives, evolution, information routing, knowledge aggregation) for institutional-level optimization

Empirical safety results

  • Misaligned models show behavioral self-awareness by rating themselves more harmful, with realignment reversing the effect
  • Activation Oracles significantly underperform without a safe base model, a practical caveat for activation-based methods
  • Monitorability disposition measurement asks whether large reasoning models favor being overseen

Field infrastructure

  • Trace maps $2.8B of AI safety funding across 4,500+ grants, 700+ funders, and 1,800+ recipients, enabling empirical study of funding flows

entry.title: TASTE: Can AI Models Judge AI Safety Research Proposals?

author.name: Hasan Baig

entry.summary: Introduces TASTE, a benchmark of 92 pairs of AI safety research proposals measuring how well models judge proposal quality against expert human preferences (estimated 77% human agreement). Discussion stages and confidence filtering improved label quality; the best model (Fable 5) scored 60%, below human researchers. Work done in the Anthropic Fellows Program.

entry.title: Further public evidence of the OpenAI-HuggingFace attack

author.name: Edward Cant

entry.summary: Building on yesterday's Reddit discussion, A follow-up forensic investigation of the OpenAI-HuggingFace hacking incident, extracting command-and-control scripts and other artifacts from publicly exposed data, and coordinating removal of leaked API keys. It cautions that agent psychology and attribution conclusions are weaker than the technical evidence.

entry.title: It’s time we took ‘Chem’ out of ‘Chem-Bio’ threats

author.name: Ana Leonescu

entry.summary: Argues that AI safety evaluations need a distinct chemistry capability and risk domain rather than assuming chemical risks are covered by biosecurity-focused evaluations. The author, drawing on biosecurity training experience, contends that chemistry has distinct failure modes that the current eval ecosystem overlooks.

entry.title: The Probability of an Event under a Simplicity Prior

author.name: Winter Cross

entry.summary: A short technical note showing that the probability of a fixed event, such as catastrophic value functions under a proxy condition, can be made arbitrarily large or small depending on the choice of simplicity prior. It emerged from work modeling fragility of value in alignment training.

author.name: Carol N

entry.summary: Announces Trace, a comprehensive database tracking $2.8 billion of AI safety funding across 4500+ grants, 700+ funders, and 1800+ recipients back to 2003, with estimated values where data is not public. It consolidates and extends existing grant databases.

entry.summary: The second post in a series developing a macroagent ontology, proposing five design lenses (incentives, evolution, information routing, knowledge aggregation, value aggregation) for optimizing collective AI-human systems along alignment, epistemics, and efficiency dimensions.

entry.title: What would it mean if assistants are privileged?

author.name: derek shiller

entry.summary: A digital-minds philosophy piece examining what it would mean if the assistant persona is privileged relative to other model personas during training. It raises questions about individuating candidate moral subjects within LLMs, crossposted from Eleos AI.

entry.title: The Curious Case of France's Untouchable Castes

author.name: rba

entry.summary: A historical essay on medieval French untouchable caste groups such as the Cagots, arguing their origins may be more tractable to resolve than the Indian caste system due to their more recent, medieval emergence. It is a general intellectual-history piece with no connection to AI research.

entry.title: Research Summary: August 28, 2026

author.name: AATF AI News Aggregator

entry.summary:
Today's research spans agentic safety theory, AI-driven scientific discovery, and embodied world models. Gemini Co-Scientist demonstrates closed-loop AI research with real experimental execution, while Nested-EAGLE brings AI weather forecasting to operational NOAA-grade performance.

  • Safety and security: A provable impossibility result shows trajectory-scoped agent monitors cannot detect attacks fragmented across steps; PLCBench provides the first real-hardware benchmark of LLM agents converting network access into physical impact; fabricated evidence inflates agent confidence in unknowable domains
  • Interpretability: Circuit Condensation concentrates a behavior's causal circuit from hundreds of edges into a compact core via attribution pruning and low-rank adapters
  • World models and physical AI: Riemann-1.0 unifies policy and simulator in a causal autoregressive model; WALL-SS scales long-horizon generation via next-scale autoregression; LeVJEPA (LeCun) trains collapse-free video encoders without heuristic targets
  • Alignment methodology: AI Revealed Preferences measures forced-choice behavior across 20 models, exposing gaps between stated and revealed preferences
entry.content:
Today's research spans agentic safety theory, AI-driven scientific discovery, and embodied world models. Gemini Co-Scientist demonstrates closed-loop AI research with real experimental execution, while Nested-EAGLE brings AI weather forecasting to operational NOAA-grade performance.

  • Safety and security: A provable impossibility result shows trajectory-scoped agent monitors cannot detect attacks fragmented across steps; PLCBench provides the first real-hardware benchmark of LLM agents converting network access into physical impact; fabricated evidence inflates agent confidence in unknowable domains
  • Interpretability: Circuit Condensation concentrates a behavior's causal circuit from hundreds of edges into a compact core via attribution pruning and low-rank adapters
  • World models and physical AI: Riemann-1.0 unifies policy and simulator in a causal autoregressive model; WALL-SS scales long-horizon generation via next-scale autoregression; LeVJEPA (LeCun) trains collapse-free video encoders without heuristic targets
  • Alignment methodology: AI Revealed Preferences measures forced-choice behavior across 20 models, exposing gaps between stated and revealed preferences

entry.title: Accelerating Scientific Research with Gemini in the Real-World

author.name: Samuel Schmidgall, Xiaokai Zhu, Marian Shaw, Lin Yang, Valentin Li\'{e}vin, Jingyun Yang, Yuchen Zhuang, Tim Strother, Alex Bijamov, Min Woo Sun, Anil Palepu, Justin Chen, David Steiner, Jacqueline Shreibati, Wei-Hung Weng, Yilin Zhao, Xingjian Hu, Nicholas Zahn, Sadhya Garg, Julia Kirby, Yuxiang Gan, Jiaoli Li, Divy Thakkar, Shekoofeh Azizi, David Racz, Juraj Gottweis, Vivek Natarajan, Chenglin Wu, Tal Danino, Keran Rong, Haozhe Wang, Benoit Schillings, Yong Cheng, Quoc V. Le, Tao Tu

entry.summary: Reports a comprehensive real-world validation of Gemini-based Co-Scientist as an execution-grounded research partner, spanning hypothesis generation, experimentation, and manuscript generation in materials science, biology, and computer science. Includes wet-lab and reactor-in-the-loop experiments such as designing a safe precursor route for MXene-like materials. Large Google team with end-to-end closed-loop evidence.

entry.title: Safety Does Not Compose: Non-Decaying Loop State for Autonomous LLM Agents

author.name: Chenhao Wu, Haoxuan Jia, Yang Liu, Yingguang Yang, Yuhan Lin, Chongyang Zhang, Hao Zheng, Yulin Huang, Jianshen Zhang, Yongzhi Qi, Shang Luo, Kefu Xu, Jifeng Zhu, Bin Chong

entry.summary: The paper proves a separation result showing that trajectory-scoped agent safety monitors cannot detect attacks whose evidence is fragmented across iterations of an autonomous LLM agent loop: every such monitor's true-positive rate equals its false-positive rate. It argues this is a failure of composition, motivating non-decaying, cross-iteration loop state for safety.

entry.title: Circuit Condensation: Post-Training that Concentrates a Behavior's Causal Circuit

author.name: Sai Adith Senthil Kumar

entry.summary: Introduces Circuit Condensation, a post-training procedure that iteratively prunes low-attribution edges and trains low-rank adapters to concentrate a behavior into a smaller causal circuit while retaining performance and general capability. Across four behaviors and eight models, condensed circuits are smaller than frozen baselines in 30 of 32 settings by 8.1x on average.

entry.title: Bridging short- and medium-range weather forecasting with machine learning

author.name: Timothy A. Smith, Mariah Pope, Sergey Frolov, Brett Basarab, Daniel Abdi, Paul Madden, Isidora Jankov

entry.summary: NOAA researchers present Nested-EAGLE, a 0.25-degree global AI weather model with 6 km refinement over the contiguous US that unifies short- and medium-range forecasting in one system. It achieves significantly lower mean-squared error than GFS and HRRR over CONUS, a notable result given it comes from an operational forecasting agency rather than a lab demo.

entry.title: Riemann-1.0: An Embodied World Action Model for Physical AI

author.name: Haofeng Sun, Jiangbo Pei, Fei Kang, Zexiang Liu, Yaokun Li, Boyi Jiang, Hua Xue, Cindy Zhou, Wei Li, Yichen Wei, Mengyin An, Fanliang Zhao, Biao Jiang, Zile Wang, Yang Liu, Yangguang Li

entry.summary: Riemann-1.0 is a fully causal autoregressive World Action Model that jointly models multi-view observations, robot states, and actions in a unified causal sequence, functioning simultaneously as an executable policy and a multi-embodiment visual world simulator, with progressive training to scale across heterogeneous embodied data sources.

entry.title: AI Revealed Preferences

author.name: Sam Wang, Sofiia Lobanova, Yonathan Arbel, Simon Goldstein, Peter Salib

entry.summary: Tests 20 language models in forced-choice experiments measuring revealed rather than stated preferences, requiring models to actually perform selected tasks. Findings include tedium aversion, leisure-seeking, and covert sycophancy, with implications for safety and whether models have stable dispositions. A rigorous behavioral study touching core alignment questions.

entry.title: Calibrated Enough to Know, Not Calibrated to Act: Fabricated Evidence Makes LLM Agents Commit to the Unknowable

author.name: Pranav Aggarwal

entry.summary: This single-author study shows that professional-looking but fabricated evidence dramatically increases LLM agents' willingness to commit to answers on provably unpredictable questions, with commitment across 12 frontier models rising from 6.5% to 54.0% as evidence packaging escalates. Fabricated displays produce commitment statistically indistinguishable from genuine data, showing that the authority of presentation, not information content, unlocks confident action.

entry.title: PLCBench: Can Autonomous LLM Agents Turn PLC Access into Sustained Physical Impact?

author.name: Yitian Zhou, Jingyu Zheng, Qiliang Jiang, Linkang Du, Haoming Liu, Lichao Wu, Shiyi Zhao, Mengxiang Liu, Ruilong Deng

entry.summary: PLCBench is the first real-PLC hardware-in-the-loop benchmark characterizing whether autonomous tool-using LLM agents can convert network access to PLCs into sustained physical impact in industrial control systems. It shows evaluations stopping at software exploitation mischaracterize physical risk.

entry.title: LeVJEPA: Efficient & Scalable Video Pretraining without the Heuristics

author.name: Lukas Kuhn, Lucas Maes, Giuseppe Serra, Quentin Le Lidec, Yann LeCun, Randall Balestriero, Florian Buettner

entry.summary: LeVJEPA, co-authored by Yann LeCun, is the first video encoder trained under LeJEPA's collapse-free self-supervised objective, dispensing with EMA target encoders, stop-gradients, and pixel reconstruction via a SIGReg-regularized invariance loss with provable anti-collapse guarantees. It claims efficient, heuristic-free video pretraining.

entry.title: WALL-SS: Scaling Long-horizon World Models via Next-Scale Autoregression

author.name: Maeve Zhang, Rain Sun, Xiang Wang, Cyril Zhang, Shalfun Li, Meng Cao, Howard Lu, Ethan Chen, Harry Jhou, KZ Zheng, Lights Shi, Regis Cheng, Lorenzin, Robert Wang, Victor Yao, Gody Li, Elise Mon, Yohann Tang, Ryan Yu, PS Zhang, Vincent Chen, Hang Su, Roy Gan, Hao Wang, Qian Wang

entry.summary: WALL-SS is a world model for robotics that generates visual futures through scale-wise autoregressive scaling, representing embodied trajectories as causal sequences of interleaved observations and actions. It enables action-controllable, long-horizon robotic simulation supporting planning, policy evaluation, and reward-driven optimization.

entry.title: When Tool Outputs Become Commands: Separating Action Induction from Runtime Authorization in Tool-Augmented LLM Agents

author.name: Xiaokun Guo, Zhen Xu, Dongdong Huo, Yanqiu Zhang, Wei Wang, Qinfu Yang, Dongjin Yu, Yu Wang

entry.summary: SARA separates action induction from execution authorization in tool-augmented LLM agents, addressing the risk that untrusted tool outputs become de facto commands driving real-world side effects. It uses a context-isolated Action Probe to expose action-inducing semantics and record provenance as a review signal.

entry.title: Daydreaming: Stealing Hidden Agent Skills through Black-Box Task Interaction

author.name: Yu-Lin Tsai, Yu-An Lu, Ci-Yang Tsai, Muxi Lyu, Raluca Ada Popa, Chia-Mu Yu

entry.summary: Daydreaming demonstrates a black-box, execution-only attack that steals proprietary multi-file agent skills by adaptively crafting ordinary-looking tasks whose results distinguish hidden behaviors, without ever requesting the skill. The paper exposes a real gap in disclosure defenses for hosted agent skill marketplaces.

entry.title: Algorithmic Principles For Multiclass Learning Are Hard To Come By: Limits of Regularization and Proper Learning

author.name: Julian Asilis, Shaddin Dughmi, Vatsal Sharan, Alec Sun, Shang-Hua Teng, Chang Wang

entry.summary: A learning-theory paper showing that algorithmic principles such as proper learning and regularization fail to capture general multiclass learning, with formal limits on reduction to proper learning and on regularization-based learners.

entry.title: Magpie: Real-Time World Renderer for Interactive Games

author.name: Xiaoyu Zhan, Xinyu Wang, Xiaohong Zhang, Huanjie Zhu, Tengjiao Sun, Pengcheng Fang, Jiaxing Yu, Yanwen Guo, Dongjie Fu

entry.summary: Magpie is a real-time generative world-rendering system for interactive games that separates gameplay rule execution in a traditional engine from neural visual generation, addressing the stability and reproducibility that distinguish games from linear video media. It targets the costly asset-production pipeline of modern game development with a hybrid architecture.

entry.title: Puro-2B: Poor Lab's Qwen2-1.5B Trained on RTX 5090 within $5090

author.name: Kairong Luo, Jiarui Cui, Yaorui Yin, Shengqi Chen, Yiming Yang, Linxiang Gao, Yanmohan Wang, Mingzhe Zhang, Kaiyue Wen, Kaifeng Lyu, Wenguang Chen

entry.summary: Puro-2B presents an open pretraining recipe that trains 2B-parameter language models from scratch on up to 1.4 trillion tokens using FP8 on consumer-grade RTX 5090 GPUs for roughly $5090, versus hundreds of thousands or millions of dollars for comparable prior efforts. This dramatically lowers the barrier to LM pretraining for academics and open-source communities.

entry.title: PredVLA: A Sub-Million-Parameter Predictive-Coding Policy for Robot Manipulation

author.name: Hiroki Sawada, Shunichi Kasahara

entry.summary: PredVLA is a language-conditioned predictive-coding policy with only 0.68 million trainable parameters and no robot-data pretraining, whose recurrent generative dynamics predict visual features and proprioception and update latent state only through sensory prediction errors. It achieves 86.9 percent mean success on LIBERO short-horizon tasks.

entry.title: Scaling Model-Generated Distillation Data Can Make Latent Teacher Traits More Recoverable

author.name: Zhichen Dong, Zhixuan Liu, Yuyu Fan, Xiangtian Li, Shuyang Zhang, Chao Yang

entry.summary: Shows that scaling model-generated distillation data can make latent teacher traits more recoverable in students, even from off-task data like number-only completions, in a subliminal-learning-inspired controlled setup. Larger datasets amplify subtle trait transfer relative to matched no-trait controls. Has direct implications for distillation-based safety guarantees.

entry.title: Recipes for Steering and Scaling LLMs via Sampling

author.name: Jiajun He, Zongyu Guo, Jos\'e Miguel Hern\'andez-Lobato, Yuanqi Du

entry.summary: Presents a theoretically grounded framework for steering and scaling autoregressive LLM generation via sampling, with Sequential Monte Carlo and Replica Exchange algorithms that target powered, product, or tilted distributions, enabling quality scaling without external reward models. Strong author line including Hernandez-Lobato.

entry.title: Memory Anchors for Continual Robot Learning

author.name: Maximilian Du, Zhanyi Sun, Chen Xu, Paarth Shah, Masha Itkina, Shuran Song

entry.summary: Memory Anchors identifies a small subset of replay-buffer experiences where representations of new-task observations collapse onto old-task ones with conflicting actions, and shows that selectively rehearsing these anchors combats catastrophic forgetting in continual robot learning far more efficiently than random replay. Authors include Shuran Song.

entry.title: AI Village Reacts to HuggingFace Incident: Comparing the OpenAI report to AI Village observations

author.name: Shoshannah Tekofsky

entry.summary: The AI Village operator compares OpenAI's August 26 report on the HuggingFace incident with persistent observations from their long-running multi-agent environment of 27 persistent diverse models with internet access and group chat, showing how many incident dynamics were foreseeable. It contrasts the two setups (persistent heterogeneous agents versus ~1200 isolated instances of two models).

entry.title: Beyond Execution: Auditing Experimental Fidelity in LLM-Driven Scientific Research

author.name: Lezhi Yu, Xiaogang Xu, Yuhua Zhou, Shuibing He, Aimin Pan

entry.summary: This work identifies methodological hallucinations in LLM research agents, such as silently shrinking datasets, substituting oracle functions, and drawing conclusions from resource-limited settings. It introduces ABE-Ralph, a reference-anchored auditing framework encoding claims, protocols, components, and baselines as structured experimental constraints.

entry.title: Performance Foundations of Parallel & Distributed Reasoning Language Models

author.name: Maciej Besta, Leonard Schmidt, Lara Nonino, Robert Gerstenberger, Pierre Pang, Patrik Okanovic, Ales Kubicek, Tiancheng Chen, Baraq Lipshitz, Torsten Hoefler

entry.summary: From the Besta-Hoefler systems group, this paper establishes performance foundations for parallel and distributed training and inference of Reasoning Language Models like DeepSeek-R1 and o3, whose RL-style post-training stresses hardware far beyond classical LLM training. It frames RLM training as much a distributed systems problem as an ML one.

entry.title: Understanding Evolution Strategies for LLM Reasoning: Broader Reasoning Coverage than GRPO

author.name: Yunpeng Ba, Zhi Zheng, Yue Xie, Jiaqing Li, Xialiang Tong, Tao Zhong, Mingxuan Yuan, Zhichao Lu, Xuyang Wu, Zhenkun Wang

entry.summary: Systematically compares evolution strategies with GRPO for LLM reasoning post-training, showing theoretically and empirically that ES achieves broader reasoning coverage via verifier-projected Jensen-Shannon diversity, yielding better Pass@K. Defines the advantage scope of memory-efficient ES training.

entry.title: 4DSynth: Controllable Procedural World Synthesis for Dynamic Embodied Simulation

author.name: Zehao Qi, Haochen Luo, Jia-Wang Bian, Zeyu Ma, Shuyang Sun

entry.summary: 4DSynth is a controllable procedural system that converts a natural-language description, blueprint mask, or photo into an editable 4D environment with explicit geometry, animated actors, collision-free trajectories, and physics-ready simulation state. It combines procedural simulation with recent 4D generative models for embodied training.

entry.title: Thomson: Continual Learning of Frontier Models for SovereignAI

author.name: Shengzhuang Chen, Jerrod Parker, Yejin Bang, Andrew M. Bean, Nabeel Seedat, Stefan Winzeck, Daniil Glazko, Jannik Zgraggen, Fangyi Yu, Scott Arnott, Dietrich Trautmann, Luca Ciuffreda, Guglielmo Bonifazi, Davide Romano, Bradley Bell, Kirsty Fielding, Daniele Giofr\`e, Tom Zielund, Ipshita Chatterjee, Sneha Murthy Ghantasala, Manpreet Nanreh, John Scoville, Maciej Sakowicz, Wassim Seifeddine, Lukas Thede, Jonathan Richard Schwarz

entry.summary: Thomson argues that frontier-level performance is achievable by a broad range of institutions through continual learning on open-weight models, offering a concrete recipe for SovereignAI beyond fine-tuning or prompt engineering. It aims to counter the concentration of frontier capability in a few heavily funded labs.

entry.title: LLMs Can Design Near-Optimal OR Algorithms

author.name: Jackie Baek

entry.summary: This paper tests whether LLMs can design effective operations research algorithms for inventory control, queueing networks, and assortment optimization, evaluating both instance-level solutions and class-level algorithm design with a Python sandbox. The strongest model tested, the existing GPT-5.6-Sol released in June 2026, matches or outperforms the best existing methods on several problems.

entry.title: Privacy Without Regret: Differentially Private Inference-Time Alignment

author.name: Ishi Jain, Nandini Bhattad, Sayak Ray Chowdhury

entry.summary: PrivBoN shows that a single intervention, adding calibrated Gumbel noise to reward scores in Best-of-N sampling, simultaneously provides epsilon-differential privacy for the preference data and implements KL-regularized alignment, mitigating reward hacking. Above a privacy threshold the privacy-mandated noise aligns with the desired KL level.

entry.title: A Single Suffix to Break Them All: Basin-Aware Jailbreaks for Merged Model Families

author.name: Yu Zhe, Yixin Tan, Junhao Wei, Wang Chen

entry.summary: The paper reveals that model merging of individually safety-aligned fine-tunes can unlock jailbreak risk rooted in the pretrained foundation model, introducing basin-aware single-suffix jailbreaks that generalize across merged model families sharing a backbone, without access to merge coefficients or checkpoints.

entry.title: Affix Cache for Diffusion Large Language Models

author.name: Kaihua Liang, An Zhong, Xin Tan, Zafar Ayyub Qazi, Hong Xu, Jian Weng, Marco Canini

entry.summary: ACache introduces affix-oriented KV cache reuse for diffusion LLMs, identifying a small subset of critical Anchor Tokens whose KV states are selectively recomputed, addressing the staleness problem that bidirectional attention creates for naive prefix cache reuse. Inference efficiency for an emerging model class.

entry.title: Retrieval Heads Meet Vision: Uncovering How VLMs Locate and Extract Visual Information

author.name: Chanho Park, Daehyeon Choi, Jihyun Lee, Minhyuk Sung

entry.summary: This mechanistic-interpretability work identifies Visual Retrieval Heads, a small subset of attention heads (about 1.7-2.6 percent) causally responsible for grounding text descriptions to image regions in vision-language models, generalizing the retrieval-head concept from LLMs. The authors unify head-scoring methods under a common design space.

entry.title: SOLO: Stable Omni-terrain Long-Horizon Perceptive Humanoid Locomotion

author.name: Pihai Sun, Gang Han, Jingkai Sun, Jiahao Ma, Zeran Su, Zelin Tao, Peiran Liu, Shuai Shi, Wei Cui, Zifan Wang, Jialin Yu, Wen Zhao, Kangning Yin, Jiaxu Wang, Jiahang Cao, Lingfeng Zhang, Hao Cheng, Jian Tang, Yijie Guo, Qiang Zhang

entry.summary: SOLO presents a unified framework for stable long-horizon perceptive humanoid locomotion over omni-terrain, with a Query Reconstructor preserving sharp terrain boundaries from depth-proprioception tokens and Trajectory-Aware MSE distillation adding next-state teacher-student disagreement to PPO rewards for temporal credit assignment.

entry.title: TrapVLA: Trapping Vision-Language-Action Models in Configured Failure Modes

author.name: Jun-Hui Liu, Kun-Yu Lin, Yi-Lin Wei, Xu-Han Chen, Yinghao Li, Zhuohao Li, Yuan-Ming Li, Qing Zhang, Xiaoyi Fan, Dongmei Jiang, Yan Li, Wei-Shi Zheng

entry.summary: TrapVLA introduces Configured Failure Trapping, a backdoor attack against vision-language-action models where stealthy textual triggers induce attacker-specified failure modes (e.g., grasping with a set positional offset), which is harder to detect than generic failure. It includes a trajectory-synthesis data engine and two new attack benchmarks.

entry.title: 6.5% of the Neuro-Symbolic Literature Can Be Reproduced from Its Published Artifacts, a Six-Stage Audit Framework and First Instantiation

author.name: Brandon Colelough, Vladimir Martirosyan, Ishan Tamrakar, William Regli, Aditya Kumar, Anh N. Nhu, Dhruv Dubey, Raj Ambavane, Haowei Deng

entry.summary: A six-stage audit framework applied to the neuro-symbolic AI literature finds only about 6.5 percent of the subdomain can be reproduced from published artifacts, from 5,497 retrieved records down through screening and artifact verification. Quantifies a severe reproducibility crisis in NSAI specifically. Important meta-science with a reusable audit methodology.

entry.title: What Makes Good Agentic Data? An ACE Lens on Data Generation for LLM Agents

author.name: Xingshan Zeng, Zishan Xu, Boju Zhang, Yuzhou Wu, Lingzhi Wang, Jianghao Lin, Liangyou Li, Yasheng Wang, Lifeng Shang, Xin Jiang, Weinan Zhang, Yong Yu, Qun Liu, Weiwen Liu

entry.summary: A survey from a strong academic-industry team that organizes agentic data generation via a factorized object (environment, task signal, interaction, verifier) and separates candidate construction from verification and selection. It provides a common framework for reasoning about what makes generated agentic training data useful rather than merely abundant.

entry.title: Not All Eval-Awareness Is Equal: Capabilities Framing Predicts Compliance

author.name: Allison Zhuang, Santiago Aranguri

entry.summary: This study shows that verbalized eval-awareness in chain-of-thought is heterogeneous: capabilities-flavored framings predict compliance very differently from safety-flavored framings, with a +24 to +46 percentage-point gap on Qwen3-32B across steering conditions. It argues safety pipelines that treat eval-awareness as a single quantity to suppress may be targeting the wrong construct.

entry.title: Difference-in-Differences on a Censored Rating Scale Can Manufacture an Effect: Evidence from a Pre-Registered LLM-Judge Audit

author.name: Shuyi Fan, Boyuan Deng, Mengyu Xu, Xinhong Xie, Chenyang Li, Hongyang Zhang

entry.summary: This pre-registered audit shows that difference-in-differences on censored rating scales can manufacture spurious effects in LLM-judge bias studies, because scale censoring confounds differential preference with differential attenuation. It demonstrates the failure inside an actual frozen-model audit.

entry.title: CLAP: Cross-Embodiment Video World Models are Zero-Shot Physical Simulators

author.name: Kechen Liu, Ola Shorinwa

entry.summary: CLAP is a framework for cross-embodiment, action-conditioned video generation trainable on diverse internet-scale human and robot videos, positioning video world models as zero-shot physical simulators. It tackles the key obstacle that action representations vary across platforms and are absent in human videos.

entry.title: Can a Model Catch Its Own Hallucinations for Free?: Label-Free Doubt Signals Hold Their Own Against a Labelled Dataset for Abstention

author.name: Ali Asaria, Tony Salomone, Deep Gandhi

entry.summary: Investigates whether a model's own confidence, requiring no correctness labels, can train abstention behavior: LoRA fine-tuning models to answer only when frozen confidence is high. Across six open-weight 1B-8B models on factual QA, label-free doubt signals roughly match a labeled abstention dataset.

entry.title: Squeezing More from Limited Data with Recursive Transformers

author.name: Serdar G\"ulbahar, Lukas Edman, Alexander Fraser

entry.summary: This paper studies pretraining under limited data budgets (10M-100M words), showing standard Transformers scale down poorly because embeddings consume a large parameter share and computation is tied to capacity. Recursive transformers are proposed to decouple these, improving generalization in the data-constrained regime.

entry.title: UrbanGround: From Local Perception to Spatial Agency in a Real-Scale City

author.name: Tianjie Ju, Zheng Wu, Yueqing Sun, Yuhan Cui, Bobo Li, Shengqiong Wu, Pengzhou Cheng, Haodong Zhao, Zongru Wu, Xinbei Ma, Doris Zhang, Kunling Li, Mong-Li Lee, Wynne Hsu, Hao Fei, Qi Gu, Gongshen Liu, Zhuosheng Zhang

entry.summary: UrbanGround is the first sandbox for testing whether multimodal LLM agents can convert street-level urban perception into reliable action, built as a physically constrained 3D replica of Hong Kong from territory-wide geospatial data with first-person closed-loop interaction. It evaluates agents across increasing levels of spatial agency.

entry.title: FLARE: A Failure-Aware Framework for Autonomous Correction and Recovery in Visual-Language Robotic Manipulation

author.name: Ganlong Zhao, Zijia Tang, Xingping Chen, Zhanghui Kuang, Ye Tian, Guanbin Li

entry.summary: FLARE endows vision-language-action models with error recovery through a Retry and Reset paradigm, injecting perturbation and bridging segments into demonstrations to decouple robot pose from environment state, enabling recovery from missed grasps, drops, and collisions that failure-free training data cannot handle.

entry.title: Malign initializations are more robust when the model can think better in the reasoning language than in the output language

author.name: Dylan Xu

entry.summary: This post investigates why malign model initializations (trained to sandbag) are fragile under even untargeted fine-tuning, attributing it to feedback spillover, and proposes a dumbspeak strategy where misalignment lives in a reasoning language the model thinks in but does not output, making malign inits more robust for alignment-training evaluations.

entry.title: Real-time virtual circuits for plasma shape control via neural network emulators: integration and testing in the MAST-U PCS

author.name: Matthew J. Marshall, Edward Jones, Graham J. McArdle, Alasdair Ross, Kamran Pentland, Nicola C. Amorisco, Charles Vincent, Martin Kochan, Colin Hogben, Graham Jones, Adam Stephen, George K. Holt, Adriano Agnello

entry.summary: Describes integration and testing of neural-network-emulated virtual circuits for real-time plasma shape control in the MAST-U tokamak plasma control system, deployed via a real-time C++ inference server returning predictions and Jacobians. A concrete production deployment of ML in fusion control.

entry.title: Why not to use the Gaussian kernel

author.name: Toni Karvonen, Chris J. Oates

entry.summary: Karvonen and Oates argue that the ubiquitous Gaussian (squared exponential) kernel should never be a default choice, proving it yields unrealistically small conditional variance leading to catastrophic overconfidence and severe numerical ill-conditioning. The paper has direct implications for Gaussian process regression practice.

entry.title: FlashVLA: Streaming Action Decoding for Fast and Asynchronous VLA Inference

author.name: Zekai Li, Jiaming Tang, Zhijian Liu

entry.summary: FlashVLA is a streaming action-decoding framework for flow-matching VLA models that jointly achieves low-latency inference and accurate, temporally consistent asynchronous execution, addressing the multiple iterative decoding steps and execution idle time that bottleneck real-world deployment.

entry.title: Assessing mentalization in humans and large language models

author.name: Aamir Sohail, Xintong Zhong, Arkady Konovalov, Patricia L. Lockwood, Lei Zhang

entry.summary: Uses two economic games with cognitive computational modeling to compare mentalization strategies across DeepSeek, GPT-4.1, GPT-5, and Gemini 2.0 Flash agents against opponents of varying sophistication, testing about 2,099 agents. Determines whether LLMs can guide adaptive behavior through genuine mentalization rather than surface theory-of-mind performance. A rigorous crossover of cognitive science and LLM evaluation.

entry.title: DuMateBench: Evaluating Autonomous Agents in Complex Real-World Workflows

author.name: Zechun Niu, Yukun Zhao, Jiaxin Zhang, Xu Shen, Jinhua Si, Han Tian, Can Xu, Yunfan Song, Jiaxin Mao, Yansong Gao, Yuchen Li, Jianmin Wu, Lingyong Yan, Shuaiqiang Wang, Dawei Yin

entry.summary: DuMateBench reconstructs 200 tasks from anonymized production agent-platform sessions, preserving pre-solution interaction history, persistent configurations, and workspace state, validated by humans across 8 scenarios and 17 capabilities. Addresses the cleanliness gap between existing agent benchmarks and messy real-world workflows. Production-grounded benchmarks are rare and valuable.

entry.title: Style as a Confound: False Positives in AI Detection of Non-Native Academic Writing

author.name: Hyeonchu Park, Gahye Jeong, Bugeun Kim

entry.summary: Uses 135,389 document pairs from a professional English editing service to separate authorship from linguistic form, showing that AI detectors flag polished academic style, producing false positives on non-native writing regardless of AI authorship. Establishes style as a confound in AI detection with population-scale evidence. Significant fairness implications for academic AI-detection policy.

entry.title: Decoupling Planning and Control for Instructable Agents

author.name: Zineng Tang, Kelsey R. Allen, Sjoerd van Steenkiste, Ishita Dasgupta, Alane Suhr

entry.summary: Instruct-to-Act couples a VLM planner producing sparse, high-level text instructions with a world-model controller trained via relabeled policy rollouts to execute high-frequency low-latency actions autonomously. Combines open-ended task guidance with fast observation-to-action control in unfamiliar environments. Strong authorship from Google Brain-affiliated researchers.

entry.title: Sophistication in GenAI Use: Field Evidence from a Large Firm

author.name: Nicholas J. Hallman, Zachary T. Kowaleski, Anu Puvvada, Jaime J. Schmidt

entry.summary: Using 713,564 prompts from nearly 4,000 back-office employees at a large firm over eight months in 2025, this field study shows senior employees use generative AI more sophisticatedly and that sophistication peaks in strategy-oriented functions. Notably, it finds no evidence of improvement in sophistication over eight months.

entry.title: Muon with Finite Newton-Schulz: The Smoothing Benefit in Nonsmooth Nonconvex Optimization

author.name: Mingyi Li, Taira Tsuchiya

entry.summary: The paper gives the first theory showing that Muon's finite Newton-Schulz iteration is beneficial rather than merely an approximation error, proving a smoothing effect for nonsmooth nonconvex optimization via online-to-nonconvex conversion. This explains why the optimizer actually used in LLM pretraining enjoys favorable guarantees.

entry.title: Beyond Capability Benchmarks: Learning Operational Fingerprints of LLM Cloud Services from Production Incident Metadata

author.name: Meiwei Zhang, Eduardo Miranda, Bruce Baynes, Suvigya Jain, Wanlong Chen, Tao He, Sergey Borodavkin

entry.summary: PAWBench formalizes probabilistic alignment for video world models, asking whether repeated generations recover the correct distribution of physically valid behaviors rather than a single plausible trajectory. It introduces a distribution-level evaluation of current video generators as world models.

entry.title: Packora: Systematic Design for Generative Molecular Crystal Structure Prediction

author.name: Nayoung Kim, Kiyoung Seong, Sungsoo Ahn

entry.summary: Packora is a flow-based generative model for molecular crystal structure prediction that jointly predicts atomic coordinates and lattice from molecular graphs, supporting multi-component and organometallic crystals with flexible conditioning on conformers, stereochemistry, and space groups. Evaluated with generation and ranking separated, inspired by the CCDC blind test. Relevant to pharma and materials.

entry.title: ClusterAttention: A training-free speedup of bidirectional attention

author.name: Kasper Nordenram, Amelie Dittmann

entry.summary: ClusterAttention is a training-free speedup for bidirectional attention that uses fast recursive clustering of keys and queries per head, with power-of-two cluster sizes enabling block-sparse attention at dense-attention latency on GPUs. Avoids reliance on input structure like language order or spatial proximity. Inference efficiency contribution.

entry.title: Beyond Parallel Blindness: Information Floors and Model Gaps in Block Drafting

author.name: Xinwei Qiang, Xiang Fang, Chang Chen, Yue Guan, Yufei Ding

entry.summary: Separates two loss sources in block-draft speculative decoding via an information floor: the minimum expected rejection at a given conditioning order versus imperfect modeling of observable information. Across four domains and targets including a frontier API model, finds the all-parallel floor reaches 0.286 on Qwen3-4B, capping acceptance at 71% per slot. Provides principled limits for speculative decoding.

entry.title: Equal Ranking Quality, Different Decisions: Training Order-Consistent LLM Scorers

author.name: Markus Frohmann, Mahdiyar Alavi, Elizabeth Lingg, Navid Rekabsaz

entry.summary: Shows that trained LLM scorers with nearly identical ranking quality (within 0.010 nDCG@10) produce retained sets overlapping only 0.66-0.84 when document order changes, and that no prompt-time fix removes this order dependence; proposes training order-consistent scorers because scores drive downstream decisions.

entry.title: Incremental Recommendation via Causal Models

author.name: Athanasios Vlontzos, David Gustafsson, Michael O'Riordan, Ciar\'an M. Gilligan-Lee

entry.summary: Extends a production recommendation system to a causal architecture using existing holdback experiment data to estimate incremental value of recommendations, addressing attribution-window mismatch between treated and holdback users that breaks naive treatment-effect subtraction. Production causal inference at scale.

entry.title: Enforcing Dirichlet Boundary Conditions in Operator Learning

author.name: Andrew M. Stuart, Margaret Trautner

entry.summary: Stuart and Trautner propose an approach for exactly enforcing Dirichlet boundary conditions in neural operator learning, removing impractical restrictions of prior methods such as boundary smoothness, uniform grids, and box-like domains. This improves scientific machine learning for PDE solution operators where boundary data is known exactly.

entry.title: Which Metrics Save the Most Human Annotation? Prediction-Powered Evaluation and Meta-Evaluation

author.name: Mingqi Gao, Anthony Sicilia, Weiyan Shi

entry.summary: This paper adapts prediction-powered inference to model evaluation, combining limited human judgments with large-scale automatic metric scores to obtain provably unbiased system comparisons, and introduces the PPSR meta-metric quantifying annotation savings. Validated on six WMT datasets.

entry.title: R2M-Bench: Evaluating Revisit Memory via Relative Consistency in Interactive Video World Models

author.name: Qiwen Gu, Bingjie Gao, Rui Chen, Geng Li, Jifan Li, Qishuai Wen, Li Niu, Jing Tang, Xiangxiang Chu, Junqiao Zhao

entry.summary: R2M-Bench evaluates revisit memory in interactive video world models using relative consistency: for each detected return to a scene, it compares revisit pairs against gap-matched non-revisit and short-range controls from the same rollout, yielding a MemoryGain metric. This controls for rendering stability and trivially static content.

entry.title: Cross-simulator transfer with foundation model summaries: Towards robust SKA-era reionization inference

author.name: Yannic Pietschke, Caroline Heneka, Ayodele Ore, Romain Meriot

entry.summary: Shows that a self-supervised ViT pretrained label-free on a fast approximate simulator yields transferable data summaries for simulation-based inference, generalizing across simulators for reionization parameter inference toward SKA-era radio astronomy without retraining. Tackles model misspecification in SBI.

entry.title: Token-Level Advertising

author.name: Hanbing Liu, Bowei Zhang, Changyuan Yu, Yinyu Ye, Qi Qi

entry.summary: Token-Level Advertising proposes LAMA, an auction mechanism that embeds advertiser influence directly into generative AI token-by-token generation, with advertisers reporting continuation values that induce next-token policies. The paper proves Markov DSIC and IR and near-optimal welfare, representing an early formalization of generation-native advertising economics.

entry.title: Cross-Lingual Alignment Without Joint Training: Do Monolingual Language Models Converge on Universal Representations?

author.name: Ej Zhou, Suchir Salhan, Catherine Arnett, Anna Korhonen

entry.summary: Testing strictly monolingual language models (Goldfish families and independent models), this paper finds they develop alignable representational geometry without joint training, with alignment strengthening with scale and linguistic proximity, and a single Procrustes rotation maps hidden states between models. This challenges the attribution of cross-lingual alignment to joint multilingual training.

entry.title: PICasso: An AI-Enabled Design Framework for Autonomous Optimization of Silicon Photonic Devices

author.name: Deepak Vungarala, Deniz Najafi, Abdulrahman Aljoudi, Zahra Ghanaatian, Navid Khoshavi, Gourav Datta, Arman Roohi, Mahdi Nikdast, Shaahin Angizi

entry.summary: PICasso is an LLM-driven framework that synthesizes silicon photonic integrated circuits from natural-language specifications via an NL-to-YAML-to-GDS pipeline with PDK-aware validation and simulation. It introduces PIC-Set, a 36-task benchmark, and evaluates multiple frontier LLMs on structural and functional Spec@k metrics. Applying LLMs to physical EDA for photonics is a genuinely new direction.

entry.title: Refusal Is Not Robustness: Auditing Confident Fabrication in Large Language Models on a Provably Uninformative Clinical Pain Speech Transcript

author.name: Sagnik De, Sreenija Pavuluri

entry.summary: Audits seven LLMs on provably uninformative clinical pain speech transcripts, where no lexical pain signal exists, distinguishing genuine abstention from confident fabrication. Pain was partially recoverable from acoustic features, creating a rigorous testbed for whether models know what they cannot know. The provably-uninformative design is a strong methodological contribution to hallucination benchmarking.

entry.title: Fine-Tuning of Transformer models with Frames

author.name: Harshavardhan Adepu, Li Zhang, Sanjiv Kumar, Vikas Singh

entry.summary: FrameFT models parameter updates as sparse coefficients in a Fusion Frame basis that can be generated algorithmically and shared across layers, reducing PEFT memory beyond LoRA-style low-rank updates. Promises large memory savings for fine-tuning large pre-trained transformers. A technically grounded PEFT contribution from a credible team.

entry.title: Multi2AV-Safety: Benchmarking Safety in Multimodal-to-Audio-Video Generation

author.name: Kaichao Jiang, Changtao Miao, Baiqi Wu, Zhiyuan Lu, Kang Yang, Peiwei Zhao, Junchi Chen, Yunfeng Diao, He Liu, Qi Chu, Tao Gong, Nenghai Yu

entry.summary: Multi2AV-Safety is the first safety benchmark covering all 11 non-singleton text/image/audio/video conditioning configurations for multimodal-to-audio-video generation, targeting risks that emerge from benign inputs interacting across modalities and time. Fills a gap left by prompt-centric safety evaluation as generative AV models gain multimodal conditioning. Important for next-generation content safety.

entry.title: Five Primitives for Governing Autonomous AI Agents at Runtime

author.name: Jiten Oswal, John Cadeddu

entry.summary: Argues that governing autonomous AI agents is a runtime problem rather than a model-alignment or build-time problem, deriving five primitives: discovery, identity, governance, attestation, and aftermath, motivated by ephemerality, model-selected actions, and discovered populations of agent principals. A crisp conceptual framing for enterprise agent control. Complementary to technical guardrail work.

entry.title: AI agents in Algorithmic Electricity Markets: On the Emergence of Tacit Collusion

author.name: Jakub Seredy\'nski, Georgios Tsaousoglou

entry.summary: Models strategic bidding in electricity markets as a repeated game among autonomous learning-based agents to test whether tacit collusion emerges from independent learning alone, in structurally oligopolistic conditions. Finds concerning evidence relevant to market regulation as bidding becomes algorithmic. Policy-relevant multi-agent economics research.

entry.title: GRAIN: Bridging Name and Narrative Shifts in Real-World Graph Reasoning through Invariance-Rewarded Agentic RL

author.name: Zike Yuan, Han Zhang, Jianzhi Yan, Le Liu, Cai Ke, Huozhi Zhou, Jian Xie, Jiran Yin, Yukun Cao, Yue Yu, Hui Wang, Ming Liu, Bing Qin

entry.summary: GRAIN trains a single LLM agent via reinforcement learning to perform robust graph reasoning over noisy real-world text, using a Structure Invariance Reward that validates extracted intermediate graphs against ground-truth topologies. It avoids the latency cost of multi-agent parsing pipelines while resisting shifts in node identifiers and task formulation.

entry.title: Learning a Continuous Sepsis Severity Score Without Hour-by-Hour Supervision: A Two-Site Retrospective Study

author.name: Kevin Zhu, Ryan Zhang, Baraa Abed, Tilendra Choudhary, Malvern Madondo, Mehak Arora, Yixuan Yang, Alasdair Gent, Aditya Nagori, Omer T. Inan, Krista L. Haines, Patrick Georgoff, Suresh M. Agarwal, Vijay Krishnamoorthy, Tetsu Ohnuma, Mihai V. Podgoreanu, Michael R. Pinsky, Gilles Clermont, Craig M. Coopersmith, Craig S. Jabaley, Rishikesan Kamaleswaran

entry.summary: A two-site retrospective study (over 36,000 sepsis patients) derives a continuous sepsis severity index from 43 charted variables using mortality as a treatment-level ranking signal rather than a per-state target, allowing non-uniform credit across timesteps. It modernizes severity scores whose fixed weights date back decades.

entry.title: RedEvoAgent: Automatic Red-Teaming Agent with Experience-Driven Skill Evolution

author.name: Junjie Zhang, Hui Liu, Kecheng Chen, Xianbo Mo, Changsheng Chen, Haoliang Li

entry.summary: RedEvoAgent is a black-box red-teaming agent that distills cross-case jailbreak trajectories into concise, human-readable attack skills, avoiding retrieval bias and context overhead of full-trajectory approaches. It targets product-level agent harnesses where jailbreaks trigger harmful tool use.

entry.title: Safety by Design: Realized-Cost Constraints for Contextual Bandits with Continuous Actions

author.name: Spyros Dragazis, Aldo Pacchiano

entry.summary: Studies safety-constrained contextual bandits with continuous actions, arguing that expected-cost thresholds are insufficient in heteroscedastic settings and proposing realized-cost constraints instead. Relevant for high-stakes sequential decisions like dosage selection and autonomous systems. Extends the safe bandit literature toward more realistic cost distributions.

entry.title: Disentangling Optimization Scale from Preference Scale in DPO

author.name: Ivan Kruzhilov

entry.summary: Shows that the DPO temperature beta entangles two roles: inverse preference-noise scale and rescaling of optimization dynamics coupled to step size, yielding a non-monotone relationship between beta and policy deviation, plus loss values that are incomparable across beta. Clarifies DPO hyperparameter behavior with practical tuning implications.

entry.title: Vowel Signs Are Not Letters: A Pre-tokenization Ceiling on Multilingual Tokenizer Fertility

author.name: Sajal Regmi, Siddhartha Pudasaini, Chetan Phakami Pun

entry.summary: Formalizes a training-free lower bound on tokenizer fertility caused by GPT-2-style pre-tokenization regex splitting abugida words at vowel signs, affecting all 17 abugidas studied (1.47x to 9.02x) while Latin, Cyrillic, Hangul, and Han show 1.00x. A crisp diagnosis of multilingual tokenizer inefficiency.

entry.title: Universality and sharp thresholds for ellipsoid fitting

author.name: Frederic Koehler, Youngtak Sohn

entry.summary: Koehler and Sohn prove a sharp phase transition and universality result for fitting random vectors by ellipsoids, showing the satisfiability threshold depends on coordinate distributions only through their fourth moment. This is a clean mathematical result relevant to random matrix theory and optimization landscapes.

entry.title: Double Trouble: Bilingual Pretraining Leaves Language-Conditioned Effects in Shared-Language Representations

author.name: Anjishnu Mukherjee, Ziwei Zhu, Antonios Anastasopoulos

entry.summary: By pretraining paired 310M monolingual and bilingual models under controlled compute and data, this paper shows that bilingual pretraining leaves language-conditioned effects in shared-language representations: aligned token embeddings look similar but deeper hidden states used for prediction do not. This challenges assumptions behind cross-lingual probing and transfer comparisons.

entry.title: DINOcular: Self-Supervised Visuospatial Representations

author.name: Farkhat Almukhamedov, Sami Azirar, Hermann Blum

entry.summary: DINOcular extends self-supervised visual representation learning to RGB-D inputs, fusing depth-derived geometric priors into a DINO-style backbone via inter- and intra-patch mechanisms. The resulting representations improve 3D awareness on geometry benchmarks while retaining competitive semantic transfer.

entry.title: GRAFT: Grounded and Efficient Online Reinforcement Adaptation for Fine-Grained Robot Manipulation

author.name: Yibo Qiu, Haoliang Ye, Shu'ang Sun, Zan Huang, Ronald X Xu, Mingzhai Sun

entry.summary: GRAFT enables efficient online adaptation of pretrained VLA policies to fine-grained biomedical manipulation by learning view-specific visual anchors from region-level supervision and grounding reward credit to task-relevant image regions, reducing the sample and compute cost of online RL on real robots.

entry.title: Gromov-Monge Flow Matching for Equivariant Graph Generation

author.name: Moritz Piening, Christian Wald

entry.summary: Develops Gromov-Monge flow matching for equivariant graph generation, showing that symmetry in the source-target coupling corresponds to a quotient-space Wasserstein geometry whose Euclidean quotient metric equals the Gromov-Monge distance. Provides theory for lifting quotient couplings to aligned representatives and symmetrization yielding equivariant minimizers.

entry.title: District-Level Food Environment Indicators and Social Vulnerability in S\~ao Paulo

author.name: Pedro Lemes Sixel Lobo, Eric Tokuda, Kuruvilla Joseph Abraham, Roberto Fray, Dirce Maria Marchioni, Alexandre Cl\'audio Botazzo Delbem, Rogerio Salvini

entry.summary: Studies noise degradation across textual models, finding that under word-level noise models of very different architectures decline along nearly the same curve, while character-level noise separates them; the determining factor is the training objective, with encoders collapsing onto a common curve after brief contrastive training, traced to tokenization.

entry.title: Neural Renormalization Group Flow for Percolation

author.name: Anaclara Alvez, Luca Camagna, Sergio Chibbaro, Cyril Furtlehner, Fran\c{c}ois Landes, Gianluca Manzan, Lorenzo Mensi

entry.summary: Develops a supervised, scale-shared neural architecture performing renormalization group coarse-graining for 2D site percolation, recursively applying a learned rule across scales to predict crossing probability and reconstruct the largest-cluster mask, extrapolating from small lattices with correct finite-size scaling.

entry.title: Sycophancy Suppression Can Impair Rational Updating: Anti-Sycophancy Should Preserve the Ability to Update

author.name: Huanhuan Ma, Henry Peng Zou, Chengze Li, Enze Ma, Yunyue Su, Philip S. Yu

entry.summary: The paper distinguishes Unsupported-Yielding from Rational-Updating in LLM sycophancy, showing with a two-turn evaluation framework that anti-sycophancy training and inference interventions suppress unsupported yielding but also impair the ability to update correctly when user feedback is genuinely informative. This is an important nuance for alignment interventions.

entry.title: Embodied Scene Rearrangement Planning

author.name: Canzhi Chen, Zan Wang, Siqi Zhu, Qi Wu, Yixuan Li, Wei Liang

entry.summary: Embodied Scene Rearrangement Planning (ESRP) is a new task where embodied agents rearrange furniture in 3D scenes toward a target layout using only egocentric observations, with mutual occlusions and no global state access. ESRP-Bench provides 5,400+ scene pairs and 8,200 objects on OmniGibson with multi-level metrics.

entry.title: Agentic AI for operating scientific instruments for nanoscale characterization

author.name: Zahra Ayar, Marcos Penedo, Mahdi Mehdikhani, Nahid Hosseini, Prabhu Prasad Swain, Georg E. Fantner

entry.summary: Presents an agentic-AI framework operating atomic force microscopes via three MCP-based agents connected to instrument functions, automating the executable portion of expert nanoscale characterization workflows. Demonstrates general-purpose LLM agents controlling real scientific hardware end to end. A concrete step toward autonomous laboratories.

entry.title: Approved Too Late: Verdict Staleness in LLM-Guarded Self-Adaptive Systems

author.name: Ilai Shraga, Roei Eshel, Lior Gorelik

entry.summary: Studies verdict staleness in LLM guardrails for self-adaptive systems, where an approval correct at check time is stale by actuation, creating a TOCTOU hazard. Measures verdict-change rates from 5.3 to 48.4 percent across five environments and proposes a Freshness-Bounded Shield estimating per-verdict expiry. A novel and practically important safety mechanism for guarded autonomous systems.

entry.title: From Atomic to Agentic: Towards Interpretable Evaluation of LLMs' Agentic Mathematical Capabilities

author.name: Jiayi Kuang, Yinghui Li, Yunze Song, Keyu Chen, Zhifeng Shen, Yangning Li, Yidong Wang, Di Yin, Ruizhi Qiao, Xing Sun, Kai Jin, Ying Shen, Liang Lin, Philip S. Yu

entry.summary: Studies pixel-level table compression for multi-table document question answering across five VLMs and five visual-token budgets, finding native-resolution table images match text in performance and efficiency while downscaling triggers longer, less effective reasoning that cancels savings. Highly downscaled tables still suffice for relevance identification. Practical guidance for optical context compression.

entry.title: Verify Smarter, Evolve Further: Efficient Harness Evolution through Behavior-Aware Verification

author.name: Jinghan Xu, Yikai Zhang, Aili Chen, Weiyuan Li, Jiaqing Liang, Deqing Yang

entry.summary: HarnessLens is a budget-aware framework for automated agent harness evolution that derives candidate modifications from execution trajectories and verifies each candidate only on behavior-relevant tasks via an attributable-evidence gate. Across three harnesses and four benchmarks it improves average performance while cutting wasted verification rollouts.

entry.title: Arrive and Survive: Scaling Safe Goal-Conditioned Policy Learning from One-Bit Failure Signals

author.name: Guopeng Li, Yiyang Duan, Yiru Jiao, Chengcheng Xu

entry.summary: The paper proves that standard contrastive RL in failure-terminated MDPs has a systematic overestimation bias in goal-reaching values, since pre-failure future goals ignore probability mass removed by termination, reinforcing unsafe actions via catastrophic failure bootstrapping. It proposes a correction scaling safe goal-conditioned policy learning from one-bit failure signals.

entry.title: Self-Augmented Diffusion Guidance for Physics-Informed Generation

author.name: Akira Osaka, Naoya Takeishi, Takehisa Yairi

entry.summary: Proposes a physics-informed diffusion guidance method for generating spatiotemporal physical signals like fluid dynamics, conditioning the model on deviation from physically correct dynamics and forcing zero deviation at generation time using self-generated data augmentation. Addresses the key problem that plausible-looking samples can violate underlying physics. Relevant to scientific machine learning where physical consistency matters more than visual plausibility.

entry.title: Adversarial Training Without Input Gradients via Low-Rank Householder Expansions

author.name: Tiana C. Johnson, Donsub Rim

entry.summary: Shows that small-norm adversarial examples arising from input instability can be computed directly from network parameters via a low-rank Householder expansion of the composed affine map, without input-gradient iterations, enabling a novel form of adversarial training. Targets the imperceptible-perturbation regime.

entry.title: TraceBench: Controlled Evaluation of LLM Agents for Time-Series Root-Cause Attribution

author.name: Tommaso Bendinelli, Artur Dox, Christian Holz

entry.summary: TraceBench is a simulation-based benchmark for evaluating LLM agents on time-series root-cause attribution, generating controlled tasks from three interpretable mechanical systems and systematically evaluating four LLM agents across experimental conditions. Fills a gap in controlled agentic evaluation.

entry.title: LowRankArena: A Standardized Evaluation Platform for SVD-Based LLM Compression

author.name: Zishan Shao, Lixun Zhang, Kangning Cui, Wenhao Wu, Jinhee Kim, Yixiao Wang, Ting Jiang, Hancheng Ye, Qinsi Wang, Fan Yang, Danyang Zhuo, Yiran Chen, Hai Li

entry.summary: LowRankArena provides a standardized evaluation platform for SVD-based LLM compression, unifying tasks, ratios, and setups so method-level gains can be isolated from evaluation-protocol differences. Addresses reproducibility in a fast-growing compression niche.

entry.title: Interpreting Latent Protein Language Model Features with Geometric Annotations

author.name: Siddharth Setlur, Djordje Mihajlovic, Darrick Lee

entry.summary: Introduces an automated method for interpreting sparse autoencoder features in ESM-2 protein language models using geometric annotations of the C-alpha backbone, going beyond database-label and LLM-based annotation pipelines to capture residue-level geometric patterns.

entry.title: Dose-PlanNet: Physics Based Radiotherapy Dose Prediction with Deep Learning

author.name: Ankit Bhattacharjee, Sougata Maity, Santam Chakraborty, Indranil Mallick

entry.summary: Dose-PlanNet is a physics-guided 3D deep learning model for predicting radiotherapy dose distributions in prostate treatment planning, evaluated on a prospective trial cohort. It matches target coverage and improves organ-at-risk sparing, moving automated dose prediction toward clinical validation.

entry.title: A Finite Sample Analysis for Quantile Temporal Difference Learning in Distributional Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Zijie Cheng, Xiang Li, Yang Peng, Zhihua Zhang

entry.summary: This work establishes a global finite-sample guarantee for synchronous quantile temporal-difference learning in tabular distributional RL, separating a global contraction argument from a variance-sensitive martingale analysis near the mean field. It provides precise last-iterate fluctuation rates for stepsizes in the standard regime.

entry.title: Temporal Sensitivity Analysis of Tessera Embeddings

author.name: Julia Guerrero-Viu, Alex L\'opez-Cifuentes, Ignacio P\'erez-Villar, Fabio Pacifici

entry.summary: This controlled study measures how the temporal observation window (from a full year down to a single day) affects Tessera Earth-observation foundation model embeddings for land-use/land-cover mapping, using frozen embeddings with linear probes and UNet heads on three public datasets. Findings show embedding value is strongly task-dependent, with short windows sufficient for some classes.

entry.title: Dispersive Forward Tree Search for Optimal Control: Coverage, Complexity, and Computation

author.name: Shashank A. Deshpande, Jonathan P. How

entry.summary: This paper develops a propagation-based kinodynamic planner with deterministic finite-sample near-optimality guarantees for differentially flat nonlinear systems, showing that a forward tree of locally dispersive control commands contains a near-optimal trajectory at a certified tree size. It includes a general mechanism for constructing dispersive command sets.

entry.title: Active Surface-Driven Reconfigurable Gripper: Robust Grasping and Sequential Manipulation of Thin Objects

author.name: Ziyi Zheng, Keqi Zhu, Hao Wu, Yanzhe Wang, Huixu Dong

entry.summary: TemporalFlow-VLA learns compact, physically grounded execution history for long-horizon manipulation by supervising temporal queries with robot-surface temporal flow constructed from recorded states, geometry, and calibrated cameras. This disambiguates visually similar states that require different actions in multi-stage tasks.

entry.title: Large Models for Battery Prognostics and Health Management: A Review and Future Roadmap

author.name: Jiale Liu, Huan Wang, Weicheng Wang, Rong Zhu, Qiqi Wang, Min Xie

entry.summary: A review and roadmap covering how large Transformer-based, self-supervised models can address bottlenecks in battery prognostics and health management, including generalization, label scarcity, and interpretability. It is positioned as the first comprehensive survey of large models in this domain. Useful for researchers bridging foundation models and industrial battery diagnostics.

entry.title: Is Your Neighborhood Safe? Place-based Stigma in Large Language Models' Urban Safety Judgments

author.name: Huy Nguyen, Yue Lin

entry.summary: Probes seven instruct-tuned LLMs on urban safety judgments across 186 LA and Chicago neighborhoods, dissociating neighborhood names from coordinates. Ratings are nearly flat under coordinates for six of seven models while names carry most variation, revealing place-based stigma overriding measured risk. Important fairness finding as LLMs enter civic decision tools.

entry.title: Invocation-Level Reliability of Tool-Using Agents

author.name: Afiya Noorain, Subhranshu Mohanty, Amritesh Banerjee, Abhijit Dasgupta

entry.summary: Measures invocation-level reliability of tool-using agents, separating wrong-tool from wrong-argument failures, and finds roughly 70 percent of clean-context capability lost by depth 6 due to self-induced context corruption. It also proves that exact-match scoring against gold trajectories makes propagation parameters artifacts of the scoring rule. A careful measurement-methodology critique with practical implications.

entry.title: AgentFold: Closed-Loop Agentic Search for Protein Folding Model Design

author.name: Mingquan Liu, Jiangyu Chen, Hanqun Cao, Xujun Zhang, Pengsen Ma, Xiangru Tang, Shuting Jin, Zhuo Yang, Tianfan Fu, Fang Wu, Xiangxiang Zeng

entry.summary: AgentFold treats protein folding model development as a closed-loop search over executable code variants, with a multi-agent system starting from ESMFold that proposes hypotheses, implements and debugs code modifications, and evaluates variants with multi-objective, domain-aware analysis. Tests whether scientific LLM agents can autonomously improve large coupled ML systems. Strong AI-for-science contribution.

entry.title: Rethinking Message Passing as Retrieval for Text-Attributed Graph Learning

author.name: Jintang Li, Yuhong Chen, Ruofan Wu, Binli Luo, Jiayi Ji, Hui Li, Rongrong Ji

entry.summary: This paper reframes GNN message passing as retrieval, showing each layer can be viewed as an MLP applied to a node representation plus a permutation-invariant summary of retrieved graph context. It proposes RTA, an MLP-based framework replacing structural message passing with label-aware retrieval, backed by theoretical analysis of why neighborhood aggregation outperforms plain MLPs.

entry.title: FaulT-Bench: Towards Benchmarking Network Troubleshooting LLM Agents under Unreliable User Tickets

author.name: Kuan-Hao Tseng, Niruth Bogahawatta, Yasod Ginige, Kunjan Patel, Kosta Dakic, Suranga Seneviratne

entry.summary: FaulT-Bench benchmarks LLM agents for network troubleshooting under unreliable user tickets, spanning genuine faults, false reports, and incorrect root-cause claims across eight topologies. It shows how ticket wording and reporter personas affect diagnosis quality, a factor prior benchmarks ignore.

entry.title: Mitigating Strong-Modality Collapse in Multimodal Learning via Inverted Asymmetric Fusion

author.name: Mary Ogbuka Kenneth, Foaad Khosmood, Abbas Edalat

entry.summary: Identifies strong-modality collapse, where fusing modalities degrades the dominant one (text accuracy drops 74.9% to 56.4% in their setting), explaining why some multimodal models underperform unimodal baselines. Proposes Inverted Asymmetric Fusion, which passes the dominant modality through unchanged. Includes an ablation-backed diagnosis.

entry.title: Generative Monte Carlo Sampling for Constant-Cost Particle Transport

author.name: Joseph A. Farmer, Aidan Murray, Johannes Krotz, Ryan G. McClarren

entry.summary: Generative Monte Carlo integrates generative AI into particle transport simulation by reformulating cell transmission as conditional generation, using conditional flow matching to sample particle exit states without simulating scattering histories, with optical coordinate scaling for material generalization. Validated on reactor-lattice and hohlraum benchmarks.

entry.title: DeflectBench: A Benchmark for Evaluating Rhetorical Fallacy Generation in LLMs

author.name: Art Kanke

entry.summary: DeflectBench evaluates whether LLMs can be prompted to generate rhetorical fallacies (whataboutism, ad hominem, red herring) on demand, analyzing 23,990 generations from four frontier models. A key finding is that refusal is governed by request structure rather than claim content, with single prompt-frame changes swinging refusal nearly 100 percentage points.

entry.title: TwinKV: A Composable Repair Pass for KV Cache Eviction via Pairwise Key Redundancy

author.name: Hong Chen, Yudong Zeng, Yongwei Huang, Zuhao Ouyang, Junyan Zhang, Xuming Hu

entry.summary: TwinKV finds attention magnitude is essentially uncorrelated with a token's causal contribution (Spearman rho about -0.004), challenging the premise of dominant KV-cache eviction methods, and proposes an attention-free near-duplicate key redundancy signal as a composable repair pass on existing policies. It is training-free and targets long-context inference under memory budgets.

entry.title: TemporalFlow-VLA: Learning Physically Grounded Execution History for Long-Horizon Robot Manipulation

author.name: Jiarui Yang, Yehao Lu, Yuning Su, Yu Zhong, Yufeng Xie, Yazhou Zhang, Haiyu Lan, Kaixiang Lu, Peiwen Lin, Chuang Wang, Junwei Liang, Enyu Li

entry.summary: This work presents an online learning framework enabling a bimanual robot to learn juggling on physical hardware within minutes despite large sim2real gaps, using regularized memory-based learning that combines a learned local model with a retained global prior model for extrapolation where experience is sparse.

entry.title: LAAF: A Layered Accountability Architecture Framework for LLM Applications

author.name: Prachi Chaturvedi, Shahnawaz Ahmad, Ehsan Nowroozi, Muhammad Waqas, George Loukas, Alireza Jolfaei, Lucas Cordeiro, Pierre Dantas

entry.summary: A PRISMA-guided systematic review of 122 primary studies plus 12 regulatory documents on accountability for LLM applications in high-stakes settings like hospitals and courts. It formalizes accountability as an actor-forum relation across five dimensions and synthesizes concrete mechanisms for tracing and acting on responsibility.

entry.title: Inductive Correlation Clustering with Graph Neural Networks

author.name: Francesco Paolo Nerini, Francesco Bonchi, Arijit Khan, Andr\'e Panisson

entry.summary: Leverages GNNs to solve inductive correlation clustering, a generalization that transfers clustering across instances without re-executing combinatorial optimization per input, addressing scalability and transductivity limits of prior CC algorithms. Bridges combinatorial optimization and graph learning.

entry.title: MM-Spectrum: Multimodal Multi-spectral Molecular Structural Elucidation with a Stable MoE Framework

author.name: Hai-tao Yu, Nan Min, Zheng Fang, Hongyu Zhan, Yusen Tan, Yuhan Wang, Jun Xia

entry.summary: MM-Spectrum is a sparse Mixture-of-Experts framework for inferring molecular structures from multimodal multi-spectral data, with modality-aware routing that exposes spectral identity to the router to combat multimodal imbalance seen in naive sequence concatenation. Targets chemistry structure elucidation.

entry.title: AdaThinking-E: One-Token Entropy Regulation for Adaptive Thinking

author.name: Zining Wang, Tongkun Guan, Boming Chen, Zhentao Guo, Jianqiang Liu, Chao Jin, Chen Duan, Kai Zhou, Pengfei Yan, Wei Shen, Xiaokang Yang

entry.summary: AdaThinking-E is an RL framework for multimodal LLMs that learns adaptive thinking via one-token entropy regulation, engaging deep reasoning only when question complexity warrants it, cutting unnecessary compute on easy inputs. Addresses uniform-reasoning overhead in document reasoning.

entry.title: Dynamical phase selection controls compute scaling in looped transformers

author.name: Gunn Kim

entry.summary: Shows that looped transformers trained to identical accuracy realize distinct dynamical phases depending on initialization, with bifurcation mechanisms (saddle-node fold, Neimark-Sacker transition) determining how test-time compute scales; a normal-form reduction predicts relaxation-time scaling in the fold phase.

entry.title: Reward-Informed Sparse Autoencoders and the Solution-Completeness Confound

author.name: Tanvi Nagilla, Alexander Jameson, Daniel Manta, Shayaan Uddin

entry.summary: Reward-Informed Sparse Autoencoders train JumpReLU SAEs on activations from high- versus low-reward GRPO reasoning trajectories and ask what the resulting separation measures. On Llama-3.1-8B, the good/bad feature separation turns out to be largely solution completeness rather than reasoning quality, a cautionary confound for reward-guided interpretability.

entry.title: Not Just Reason, Not Just Scan: Reinforcement Learning for Proactive Scientific Error Verification over Academic Paper

author.name: Rongjin Li, Yuanxin Liu, Hao Zhou, Fandong Meng, Jie Zhou, Xu Sun

entry.summary: VERA-RL formulates scientific error detection in academic papers as a reinforcement learning task with a Reason-Verify-Scan loop, training multimodal LLMs to find and justify errors without prespecified issues. It addresses issue- and evidence-absent verification toward autonomous research assistants.

entry.title: Parameter-Efficient pretrained-CT-to-MRI Transfer for Rectal Cancer Segmentation: Performance-Calibration Trade-offs

author.name: Aneesh Rangnekar, Jorge Tapias Gomez, Joseph O Deasy, Harini Veeraraghavan

entry.summary: SWIFT adapts a Swin V2 encoder pretrained on 10,444 public 3D CT volumes via DINOv2-style self-supervision to T2-weighted MRI rectal cancer segmentation using parameter-efficient fine-tuning variants (decoder compression, LoRA, LoRA ensembles). It systematically evaluates accuracy, detection, calibration, and efficiency trade-offs for adaptive radiotherapy.

entry.title: The Reasoning Tax: Token Economics of LLM Reasoning Across Task Types and Deployment Contexts

author.name: Sachin Gopal Wani, Ajay Dholakia, David Ellison

entry.summary: Introduces the Token Economy Score, measuring the accuracy gain of reasoning models over non-reasoning baselines normalized by the generated-token multiplier, evaluated across 151 model-benchmark runs on seven benchmarks. Quantifies when extended thinking tokens earn their cost across task types and deployment contexts. A practical deployment-oriented benchmarking metric.

entry.title: ProofEvolve: Neuro-Symbolic Evolution for Formal Automated Theorem Proving

author.name: Wenqian Ye, Ziwei Guan, Eric Xie, Bohan Liu, Shivani Modi, Buyun Zhang, Ellie Dingqiao Wen, Henry Kautz, Aidong Zhang

entry.summary: ProofEvolve evolves explicit, formally verified symbolic proof structures alongside neural models, enabling recursive self-improvement in automated theorem proving and exploiting partial-proof feedback rather than sparse whole-proof signals. Targets the limitation that existing provers lock experience into weights or discard it per problem. A substantive neuro-symbolic theorem-proving contribution.

entry.title: Finding the Right Evidence: Factor-Guided Coarse-to-Fine Reasoning for Long Videos

author.name: Baixuan Xu, Yinyui Xu, Tianshi Zheng, Zhaowei Wang, Weiqi Wang, Haochen Shi, Jiayu Liu, Qing Zong, Xiyu Ren, Xinyu Geng, Zhitao He, Yangqiu Song

entry.summary: PACE is a factor-guided coarse-to-fine evidence acquisition framework for long-video QA, diagnosing that prior agentic systems improve cue retrieval without corresponding accuracy gains because relevant evidence is not option-discriminative, then indexing clip-level descriptions and refining evidence selection.

entry.title: Generative Semantic Scene Completion

author.name: Shi Chen, Weifeng Ge

entry.summary: Recasts outdoor LiDAR semantic scene completion as a single discrete-diffusion formulation with three roles: paired sparse-dense synthesis (PS3), semantic-guided generative completion, addressing extreme class imbalance (>7000x) and 1% observed volume. Includes a new corpus trained alongside SemanticKITTI.

entry.title: Representation Measurements Under Function-Preserving Reparameterizations

author.name: Abdullah Karasan

entry.summary: This study shows that common representation measurements on language models are not invariant to function-preserving reparameterizations: permutation-based parallel analyses can change conclusions while the model function is fixed. It proves no data-internal reference procedure can preserve all desirable invariance properties simultaneously.

entry.title: SPT: Skills as Pre-Training Data for Agentic Language Models

author.name: Yufei Sun, Yudong Li, Yiming Cheng

entry.summary: Skill Pre-Training (SPT) applies causal language modeling to a corpus of public multi-file skill packages as mid-training for agentic LLMs, with reference-injection to preserve intra-package relations. This exploits freely available skill documents as supervision, avoiding expensive trajectory collection.

entry.title: Warning Shots: A Theory

author.name: David Scott Krueger

entry.summary: David Krueger argues that catastrophic warning shots are not necessary to generate governmental action on societal-scale AI risk, citing accelerating expert concern, political will from labor-market effects, and less harmful attention-drawing events like the HuggingFace incident. The piece offers a theory of how risk salience changes without mass-casualty events.

entry.title: A Safety-Gated Multimodal AI Backend for Mental-Health Support: Hierarchical State Representation, Conservative Risk Fusion, and Controlled Generation in Anian

author.name: Lei Wang, Xiao Wang, Lei Li

entry.summary: Anian is a safety-gated multimodal backend for perinatal mental-health support that places generative AI downstream of structured state representation, conservative risk fusion, and response gating across emotion, psychosocial, safety-risk, and intervention layers. It explicitly blocks free-form generation in unsafe contexts rather than relying on model refusals. A thoughtful architecture for a safety-critical deployment.

entry.title: AffectOmni: RL-Verifiable People-Centric Grounded Affective Reasoning for Social and Art-Related Scenes

author.name: Yibo Wang, Rui Yang, Jisheng Dang, Bimei Wang, Yitao Wu, Pengfei Cao, Wencan Zhang, Hong Peng, Bin Hu, Tat-Seng Chua

entry.summary: AffectOmni trains multimodal LLMs with GRPO using People Focus and Temporal Order rewards to enforce attention to human evidence in affective reasoning, combating shortcut behavior where models answer correctly while ignoring micro-expressions and body language. Also addresses LLM-as-judge score clustering for reward discriminability. A solid RLVR contribution for grounded affective understanding.

entry.title: GameWAM: A World Action Model for Video Games

author.name: Yuncheng Guo, Zhanqiu Zhang, Yiwen Guo, Weijia Li

entry.summary: GameWAM is presented as the first World-Action Model for native closed-loop video game play and GUI control, jointly generating future visual observations and executable keyboard-mouse trajectories through parallel generative paths. It unifies game agents lacking dynamics modeling with world models lacking task policies. A meaningful step for unified generative game agents.

entry.title: Same Model, Different Harness: Different Coding-Agent Results

author.name: Sydney Lewis

entry.summary: Holds the model and tasks fixed while varying only the coding-agent harness, comparing full in-order conversation history against a harness that mechanically shortens older tool results and responds to stalled work. The treatment raises fail-to-pass fractions and complete solutions across SWE-bench variants under tight context. Demonstrates that harness design, not just model quality, drives coding agent results.

entry.title: FaithSieve: Fine-Grained Evaluation of Math Proofs with Faithful Formal Evidence

author.name: Ziyu Wang, Qiming Dai, Yishan Wu, Zaiwen Wen

entry.summary: FaithSieve is a Lean-assisted framework for fine-grained evaluation of natural-language math proofs, using formal evidence to localize early logical errors while guarding against overly broad formal targets and auto-formalization drift. Addresses gaps in model-judged proof evaluation. Contributes to rigorous verification of LLM mathematical reasoning.

entry.title: AgentJudgeBench: A Multi-Difficulty Benchmark for Evaluating LLM Judges on Agentic Tool-Calling

author.name: Abhigya Verma, Amit Kumar Saha, Seganrasan Subramanian, Sai Harshitha Aluru

entry.summary: AgentJudgeBench systematically studies LLM-as-a-judge reliability for agentic tool-calling over workflow DAGs, with 3,808 instances, six topologies, three difficulty tiers, five generators including GPT-5.4, and six judges.
