entry.summary: Introduces ICON decomposition, which quantifies how much variance each concept explains in a network layer after accounting for all other concepts and the outcome, fixing the confounding problem of per-concept screening in shortcut detection. Validated on synthetic data with known ground truth and on skin-lesion and brain-imaging models. Strong author group including established interpretability researchers.

entry.title: Unsupervised Post-Training of Foundation Models: A Survey

author.name: Yijie Xu, Qianyi Cai, Huizai Yao, Yili Wang, Tianfu Wang, Cehao Yang, Xingbo Yao, Zhiyu Guo, Aiwei Liu, Xuming Hu, Weiyu Guo, Hui Xiong

entry.summary: A survey of Unsupervised Post-Training: cataloging 80 strict UPT methods that derive learning signals from same-lineage model artifacts rather than external oracles, organized by signal source, with analysis of when post-training improves the model versus recursively amplifies error. Also maps deployment constraints via an Input Visibility by Update Persistence view. A substantial synthesis of an emerging paradigm.

entry.title: Training Alignment Auditors via Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Paul Rosu, Rowan Wang

entry.summary: Trains LLM alignment auditors with reinforcement learning, with the policy investigating target models that may have hidden behaviors planted via system prompts and an informed LLM judge comparing investigations to references for reward. Finds pairwise rewards more robust than pointwise and that clean targets (no planted behaviors) matter. Directly advances scalable oversight tooling for frontier models.

entry.title: Retrieve, Match, Escalate: Accurate and Scalable Product Linking with VLM-Distilled Cross-Encoders and Agentic VLMs

author.name: Jian Wang, Steven Xu, Sanjyot Thete, Maryam Barouti, Tom Tang, Elaine Wu, Charu Sareen, Kyle MacDonald

entry.summary: Presents a production retrieve-then-match cascade for marketplace-scale product linking: retrieval surfaces candidates, a lightweight VLM-distilled text cross-encoder auto-resolves the high-confidence majority, and an agentic multimodal VLM handles hard cases. Computation is spent in proportion to difficulty across billions of records.

entry.title: Conditional Total Correlation and the Serial Depth of Adaptive Parallel Sampling

author.name: Chuling Wen, Weijie Liang, Jian Lu

entry.summary: Studies adaptive parallel sampling of discrete vectors motivated by masked diffusion models, proving an exact identity: every policy's KL divergence equals the expected conditional total correlation accumulated over its reveal rounds, making conditional total correlation the exact information cost of within-round parallelism. Yields lower bounds on serial depth.

entry.title: A Self-Evolving Multi-Agent Framework Defense against LLM Jailbreak Attacks

author.name: Tongyan Hu, Bryan Hooi

entry.summary: Proposes a self-evolving multi-agent test-time defense against LLM jailbreaks built on persistent cross-interaction rule memory: when an attack succeeds, the framework abstracts the failure into a method-level rule capturing the structural attack wrapper rather than the harmful topic, and reuses it against future inputs. Enables defenses to accumulate experience rather than remain static after deployment.

entry.title: SwarmWorld: Stigmergic technological evolution in societies of language-model agents

author.name: Subhadeep Pal, Fiona Y. Wang, Markus J. Buehler

entry.summary: Presents SwarmWorld, where initially homogeneous LLM agents self-organize without assigned roles into evolving technological societies, exploring a spatial environment, processing resources, constructing persistent artifacts, and writing executable controllers evaluated deterministically. Demonstrates stigmergic coordination through a shared environment outperforming independent search.

entry.title: OpenCVL: An Open, Diverse, and Large-Scale Dataset for Fine-Grained Cross-View Localization

author.name: Zimin Xia, Mubariz Zaffar, Junsheng Fu, Alexandre Alahi, Julian F. P. Kooij

entry.summary: Introduces OpenCVL, a large-scale open dataset of 617,388 ground-aerial image pairs across 41 European cities for fine-grained cross-view localization, sourced from permissive platforms for long-term availability. Addresses the diversity and scalability limits of high-end sensor-collected benchmarks as a GNSS alternative.

entry.title: Capacity Overflow: A Blind Spot for Backdoor Attacks in Vision MoE

author.name: Xiaocheng Zou, Tiancheng Zheng, Xiaolin Xu, Ruyi Ding

entry.summary: Identifies batch-dependent capacity-bounded token dispatch in vision Mixture-of-Experts as an overlooked attack surface and proposes a stealthy three-phase supply-chain backdoor: inject a backdoor in an early MoE layer, neutralize it under normal capacity in a deeper layer, and use a batch-adaptive capacity factor to reactivate it at high load.

entry.title: Belief Cascades Drive Persuasion in LLM Agent Networks

author.name: Haoyi Qiu, Genglin Liu, Pranav Narayanan Venkit, Kung-Hsiang Huang, Saadia Gabriel, Chien-Sheng Wu, Nanyun Peng

entry.summary: Introduces a controlled testbed for agent-to-agent persuasion in LLM networks grounded in real-world ego-network topologies, showing across four backbones, five graphs, and 55 statements that persuasion dynamics depend on topology, competition, topic, and model prior. Direct exposure predicts stance change, and peer relays carry measurable influence.

entry.title: Serving Masked Diffusion LLMs: Characterization and Design Principles from Real Hardware

author.name: Farhana Amin, Sabiha Afroz, Mona Moghadampanah, Dimitrios S. Nikolopoulos

entry.summary: This systems paper characterizes masked diffusion LLM serving under real concurrent load using LLaDA-8B-Instruct with a D2F adapter on a single H200, finding that request difficulty is discrete rather than continuous. It derives design principles for dLLM serving stacks, warning against importing autoregressive serving assumptions.

entry.title: Granite.Trust Policy Tools: Shareable, Actionable Policies for Generative AI Applications

author.name: Nathalie Baracaldo, Nicolas Mello, Kush R. Varshney, Heiko Ludwig, Kate Soule, David Cox

entry.summary: IBM researchers present Granite.Trust Policy Tools: a YAML-based Actionable Policy schema for specifying what generative AI responses can and cannot contain, with exception-based governance, plus a synthetic data generation pipeline. The tools aim to make per-organization safety policies shareable and enforceable.

entry.title: Recursive Agentic Reasoning

author.name: Shengxin Zhang, Xiaomin Wu, Xiyang Wu, Jing Xie

entry.summary: This work unifies test-time reasoning methods as recursion operators over an agent reasoning trace: GROW for deepening, PRUNE for decomposition, and BRANCH for sampling and selection, evaluated under a shared harness with identical prompts, token budgets, and grading across five benchmarks and three frontier models. It enables apples-to-apples comparison of iterative refinement, decomposition, and repeated sampling.

entry.title: TRACE: An Evidence-Grounded Benchmark for Safety Evaluation of Large Reasoning Models

author.name: Zhenyu Wu, Siyuan Chen, Changchun Yang, Jiaqi Dong, Min Zhou, Ali Almadan, Talal Hammad, Faisal Wahbo, Aminullah Tora, Mona Alshahrani, Xin Gao

entry.summary: TRACE is an evidence-grounded safety benchmark covering the entire large reasoning model inference pipeline: prompts, intermediate reasoning traces, and final responses, spanning nine risk categories in two languages with evidence annotations rather than binary labels. It targets the unexamined gap of unsafe content inside reasoning traces.

entry.title: From State to Action: OODA-Tool for Reliable Multi-Turn Tool Use

author.name: Rongfeng Guo, Yinxuan Huang, Yusen Wu, Maoqing Zhong, Yunlu Chen, Meng Tang, Teng Long, Vincent Tao Hu

entry.summary: OODA-Tool is a typed closed-loop policy for multi-turn tool use, inspired by Boyd's Observe-Orient-Decide-Act cycle, that separates state preservation from action realization to mitigate state-action competition in autoregressive policies. Instead of generating actions directly from interaction history, decisions route through an explicit state-maintenance step. This targets a known failure mode where pressure to emit the next call overwrites accumulated context.

entry.title: PeakBench: Benchmarking Resource-Aware Tool Invocation in LLM Agents

author.name: Zhi-Kai Chen, Xu-Xiang Zhong, Song-Yan Li, De-Chuan Zhan, Han-Jia Ye

entry.summary: PeakBench is a benchmark of executable multi-tool LLM agent workflows with execution-grounded dependency annotations and measured resource profiles, targeting the neglected dimension of resource-aware parallel tool invocation. It exposes a practical failure mode: serial execution is safe but slow, while resource-agnostic parallelism risks avoidable overflows. This fills a real gap in agent benchmarking.

entry.title: Recursive Experiential-Working Memory Evolution for Long-Horizon Agent Harnesses

author.name: Zhaochen Yu, Yingcheng Wu, Zhenfei Yin, Kaiyuan Chen, Zhe Zhao, Mengdi Wang, Shuicheng Yan, Ling Yang

entry.summary: Recuris is a recursive experiential-working memory architecture for long-horizon agent harnesses: working memory tracks task progress and guides skill selection from experiential memory, and execution becomes structured evidence that localizes failures to specific memory components. A fixed Meta-Agent converts that evidence into localized, validation-gated skill-memory updates. It forms a bounded recursive memory-evolution loop for long-horizon self-improvement.

entry.title: 'Ghaib in Translation' aka Unseen Harm: Measuring Cross-Script Safety Inconsistency with 'Missed-in-Urdu' Scores in LLM Hate Speech Detection

author.name: Fawzia Zehra (Fuzzy), Kara-Isitt, Sonal Khosla, Stephen Swift

entry.summary: Tests five major LLMs on hate speech detection across Nastaliq Urdu, Roman Urdu, English, and code-switched data, finding 16 to 32 percent label instability between original-script and translated classification and high Missed-in-Urdu rates. It quantifies the cost of Urdu near-absence from safety evaluation.

entry.title: Groundhog Bit-Flip Attack: Seeding Infinite Generation Loops in Mixture-of-Experts LLMs through Bit Flips

author.name: Huakang Lin, Tiancheng Zheng, Mingxuan Sun, Tianhong Xu, Fan Zhang, Yunsi Fei, Ruyi Ding

entry.summary: Presents GBFA, the first bit-flip Denial-of-Wallet attack against MoE LLMs: flipping routing-layer bits tied to expert activations associated with end-of-sequence tokens extends token generation substantially, inflating serving cost. Exploits the new attack surface created by adaptive expert routing.

entry.title: Beam Search, Self-Consistency, and the Limits of Inference-Time Scaling for Grammar-Constrained Text-to-SQL in Small Language Models

author.name: Ty Chermsirivatana, John MacCormick

entry.summary: Studies the model-size versus inference-compute trade-off under grammar-constrained text-to-SQL with 0.5B to 7B quantized Qwen2.5-Instruct models on Spider. Finds the constrained regime behaves differently from unconstrained settings, delimiting when beam search and self-consistency help small models.

entry.title: One Form to Transfer Them All: Pretraining Multilingual Language Models Beyond Native Orthography

author.name: Muge Zhang, Aaron Jencks, Krishna Badikela, Yulia Tsvetkov, Sachin Kumar

entry.summary: Systematically compares orthographic text, romanization, and IPA input representations for autoregressive multilingual pretraining across three model scales and eight languages in four typologically related pairs. Finds romanization generally works best for cross-script knowledge transfer, with implications for low-resource languages using different scripts.

entry.title: MolEmb: Multimodal Large Language Models Can Be Strong Molecular Embedding Models

author.name: Xinjian Zhao, Xiangru Jian, Yaoyao Xu, Xiaozhuang Song, Wei Pang, Lei Bai, Tianshu Yu

entry.summary: MolEmb adapts multimodal LLMs to serve as general molecular embedding models that condition embeddings on both a molecular profile and natural-language semantic context, rather than producing unconditional vectors from single-view specialist encoders. It targets reusable representations for property prediction, virtual screening, and retrieval in computational chemistry.

entry.title: RePolicy: Reinforcement Learning for Safety-Policy Invocation in Agent Safeguards

author.name: Houcheng Jiang, Boxuan Zhang, Qiyong Zhong, Junfeng Fang, Xiang Wang, Xiangnan He

entry.summary: RePolicy learns safety-policy invocation for agent safeguards through reinforcement learning: given an agent trajectory and a dynamic policy library, it invokes the applicable policy and produces a policy-grounded rationale and judgment, trained via supervised initialization on PolicyTraj-20K followed by GRPO with verifiable rewards. It outperforms prompting and SFT baselines across six agent settings.

entry.title: Benchmarking LLM Judges for Voice-Agent Evaluation: Reliability, Calibration, and Human Oversight

author.name: Anupam Purwar, Shashank Singh, Kritika Srivastava

entry.summary: This paper benchmarks LLM-as-a-Judge evaluation of conversational voice agents, comparing human judgments against GPT-4.1 and GPT-5 on telecom and retail voice-agent conversations across quality and safety dimensions. It tests sensitivity to three evaluation configurations, examining metric-level correlations, evaluator consistency, and systematic biases. It matters because voice-agent deployment is scaling faster than reliable automated evaluation methods.

entry.title: EviDx: Evidence-Aware Active Diagnosis with Scaffolded LLM Agents

author.name: Lihang Zeng, Shaoting Zhang, Xiaofan Zhang

entry.summary: EviDx is an evidence-aware active diagnosis framework that treats clinical diagnosis as an active evidence-seeking process, pairing patient-specific diagnostic environments with a clinical diagnostic scaffold for LLM agents. It specifies how patient evidence should be exposed, scaffolded, and controlled at runtime, moving beyond static case-to-answer prediction. This addresses a core gap in medical agentic systems.

entry.title: Meta$^n$: Recursive Self-Improvement through Emergent Depth

author.name: Zae Myung Kim, Young-Jun Lee, Seungyeon Jwa, Dongyeop Kang

entry.summary: Meta^n is a recursive self-improvement scheme that keeps the meta-operation fixed and recurses on its input: the fixed operation reads traces of the solver stack below plus the code producing them, then writes the next layer as a strategic pre-process and callable helper library. Because the operation never changes and its input strictly grows, the system avoids the instability that caps prior self-editing systems at roughly two meta-levels. It is a careful design for emergent meta-depth.

entry.title: Fidelity Preference, Not Demographic Preference: A Pixel-Level Attribute-Sensitivity Audit of Image Aesthetic/Preference Scorers

author.name: Mingyang Xu

entry.summary: This pixel-level audit of four widely used aesthetic/preference scorers (LAION-Aesthetics, PickScore, ImageReward, HPSv2) finds that along skin-lightness the dominant effect is fidelity preference: unaltered images score highest with an inverted-U penalty for perturbations in either direction, and placebo arms show the penalty is operator-dependent rather than purely demographic. It disentangles fidelity from demographic bias in data-filtering scorers.

entry.title: When May an Agent Stop? Evidence-Carrying Termination for Tool-Using LLMs

author.name: Jason Liu

entry.summary: Evidence-Carrying Termination (ECT) lets a tool-using agent return COMPLETE only when a typed certificate binds every required answer claim to valid, in-scope trace evidence, with deterministic replay reconstructing the claimed value. In a locked static study across 48 synthetic tasks with eight fault types, ECT produced 0/288 unsafe completions versus 252/288 for an inspected termination-critic baseline. It offers a strong, verifiable answer to when agents may stop.

entry.title: Luce: Relightable Gaussians for 3D Asset Generation

author.name: Mayank Singh, Michele Stoppa, Alvise Memo, Rui Yu, Harsha Kalli, Srimanth Gunturi, Muhammad Ahmed Riaz, Behrooz Shahsavari, Waleed Abdulla, David E. Jacobs

entry.summary: Luce unifies geometry and physically based rendering materials in a voxelized multimodal Gaussian cloud with modality-specific primitives, compressed by a VAE into a material-aware latent space. A rectified-flow transformer generates relightable 3D assets from a single image compatible with standard rendering pipelines.

entry.title: RAGSentinel: Certifiable Geometric Consensus for Robust Retrieval-Augmented Generation

author.name: Yueyang Quan, Anjun Gao, Yufei Xia, Minghong Fang, Zhuqing Liu

entry.summary: RAGSentinel is a training-free, label-free defense against knowledge-base poisoning in black-box RAG, using a surrogate encoder to measure query-conditioned hidden-state shifts and removing shared topic directions. It moves beyond instruction-following and text-consistency defenses that adaptive attackers can imitate.

entry.title: Mechanistic Circuit Identification for Controllable Data Generation

author.name: Nakyung Lee, Sangwoo Hong, Jungwoo Lee

entry.summary: Connects training-dynamics-based data valuation with mechanistic interpretability, identifying model-internal circuits that causally govern learnability, challenge, and alignment utility signals. It then uses these circuits for mechanistic control of synthetic data generation beyond heuristic prompting.

entry.title: Multi-Modal Anomaly Detection: A Survey

author.name: Xudong Mou, Zexin Wu, Chuan Luo, Shiru Chen, Xudong Liu, Chunming Hu, Renyu Yang

entry.summary: A survey of multi-modal anomaly detection organized by assumptions about how abnormality is defined rather than by architecture. Formalizes the problem, identifies five intrinsic characteristics, and organizes methods into normality-assumption and complementary paradigms for safety-critical applications.

entry.title: MacroAgent: Regularity-Aware Macro Legalization with LLM-Agent-Designed Contour Algorithms

author.name: Jiaxi Jiang, Xufeng Yao, Yuxuan Zhao, Yuntao Lu, Peiyu Liao, Zuodong Zhang, Yibo Lin, Bei Yu

entry.summary: MacroAgent uses LLM agents to discover regularity-aware contour algorithms for VLSI macro legalization within a four-stage clustering, contour generation, template matching, and refinement pipeline. Targets robustness, cost, and regularity issues in existing legalization approaches.

entry.title: Rollout-Decoded Reconstruction for Long-Horizon Prediction in Latent World Models

author.name: Rishi Shah, Rishav Shrestha

entry.summary: Proposes Rollout-Decoded Reconstruction, a single loss term that free-runs latent world models during training exactly as in evaluation and penalizes decoded rollout reconstruction. Substantially extends valid prediction time on the chaotic Kuramoto-Sivashinsky equation with a one-flag A/B design.

entry.title: Transforms for LLM Quantization: The Great Inversion and Format Co-Design

author.name: Ehsan Jokar

entry.summary: A survey formalizing the transform stage of 4-bit LLM quantization pipelines (rotations, scalings, permutations) around the Great Inversion principle: allocation-flexible coding rewards energy concentration while grouped shared-scale quantization rewards within-group flattening, connecting to classical transform coding theory.

entry.title: Output Dilution: Redundant but Fragile Representations in MoE Models

author.name: Orion Reblitz-Richardson

entry.summary: Shows in OLMoE-1B-7B that moral content is linearly decodable from nearly every expert-layer combination yet far more fragile than in matched dense models (4.2x robustness gap), traced to output dilution: expert averaging shrinks feedforward signal reaching the residual stream.

entry.title: Mitigating LLM sycophancy with RL-based fine-tuning: Bayesian Truth Serum approach

author.name: Serhii Mytsyk, Yiming Zhang, Vikram Krishnamurthy

entry.summary: Mitigates LLM sycophancy by using the Bayesian Truth Serum peer-prediction mechanism as reward in Group Relative Policy Optimization, treating a group of the model's own responses as respondents so no external ground truth is needed for fine-tuning.

entry.title: Prefix-Denoising Consistency: Test-Time Verification for Diffusion Language Models

author.name: Yuki Ichihara, Naoto Iwase, Mohammad Atif Quamar, Junpei Komiyama

entry.summary: Introduces Prefix-Denoising Consistency, a test-time self-verification method for diffusion language models exploiting that correct trajectories are more stable under prefix-conditioned regeneration than incorrect ones.

entry.title: A Storage-Retrieval Gap in Parametric Knowledge Graph Memory

author.name: Martino M. L. Pulici, Cuong Xuan Chu, Evgeny Kharlamov, Volker Tresp

entry.summary: Studies compiling knowledge graphs offline into per-entity LoRA adapters serving as a parametric knowledge layer injected as weights rather than context text, finding on MetaQA that correct adapters recover generalizable factual knowledge with zero query-time context cost.

entry.title: When Pruning Meets Interpretability: Preserving Sparse Autoencoder Robustness in LLMs

author.name: Suchit Gupte, Xueru Zhang, Mohammad Mahdi Khalili

entry.summary: Systematically studies how LLM pruning affects sparse autoencoder interpretability tools, proving that SAE degradation under a fixed SAE is governed by a covariance-weighted perturbation energy, which magnitude pruning ignores while activation-aware methods like Wanda and SparseGPT implicitly control. Provides theory linking compression to interpretability reliability. Practically important as labs compress and probe models simultaneously.

entry.title: Retrieved But Not Reliable: A Survey on Attacks, and Defenses in Retrieval-Augmented Generation

author.name: Minh Tran, Cuong Dang, Tuc Nguyen, Khanh-Tung Tran, Minh Huynh Nguyen, Trinh Chau, Kien Le, Do Xuan Long, Jiahao Zhang, Hoang D. Nguyen, Thanh Le, Suhang Wang

entry.summary: A survey formalizing threat models over the corpus, retriever, and generator in RAG pipelines, organizing attacks by objective (accuracy, privacy, fairness) and cataloging stage-specific defenses. Addresses the fragmented treatment of RAG robustness in prior surveys. Timely given widespread RAG deployment and documented poisoning and leakage risks.

entry.title: Minimax Alternating Regret for the Experts Problem and Online Convex Optimization

author.name: Mengxiao Zhang

entry.summary: Resolves the open minimax alternating regret problem for the experts problem and online convex optimization, proving matching bounds including the surprising result that minimax alternating regret for the d-expert problem is Theta(log d), independent of horizon T, greatly improving the best-known O(T^(1/3) log^(2/3) d) estimate. Significant theoretical result motivated by game-playing dynamics. Clean, complete contribution.

entry.title: Learning New Facts with QLoRA: An Acquisition-Retention Frontier

author.name: Estelle Zheng, S\'ebastien Warichet, Emmanuel Helbert, Christophe Cerisara

entry.summary: Studies factual acquisition in Qwen3-4B fine-tuned on an OpenStreetMap-derived benchmark, showing QLoRA induces a rank-dependent acquisition-retention frontier: low ranks preserve out-of-domain capability but learn fewer facts, while higher ranks improve paraphrase generalization at increasing cost to unrelated capabilities. Challenges the assumption that PEFT inherently preserves pretrained skills.

entry.title: Lost but not erased: Finding traces of a forgotten language in neural speech models

author.name: Peter Plantinga, Charlotte Moore, Peter W. Donhauser, Krista Byers-Heinlein, Denise Klein

entry.summary: Uses ASR models trained on one language then switched to another to simulate international adoptees, finding birth-language traces persist in low pre-phonemic layers and are functional: early-exposed models re-learn the lost language 14% faster. Suggests adoptee language traces reflect ordinary learning dynamics rather than a biological critical period.

entry.title: Overview of SHROOM-Visions 2026: A Shared Task on Hallucination Detection in Large Vision-Language Models

author.name: Ra\'ul V\'azquez, Aman Sinha, Chuyuan Li, Claudio Savelli, Eduardo Cal\`o, Emilio Raimond, Stella Frank, Hengyu Luo, Flavio Giobergia, Vincent Segonne, Lorenzo Vaiani, J\"org Tiedemann, Timothee Mickus

entry.summary: Overview of the SHROOM-Visions 2026 shared task at EMNLP, extending hallucination detection to large vision-language models with fine-grained span-level detection over image-conditioned generation. Built on the SHEEP dataset designed for longitudinal evaluation across model generations.

entry.title: Targeting the Attention Heads Behind Object Hallucination in LLaVA

author.name: Armaan Sandhu, Abhilasha Senapati, Hima Kammachi

entry.summary: Uses interpretability-guided diagnosis of object hallucination in LLaVA-1.5-7B: ranking attention heads by image-attention drops around hallucinated words and ablating candidates yields a 32-head set. Restricted head-sliced LoRA and inference-time grounding controller interventions lower CHAIRs from 0.370 to 0.230 on held-out COCO images.

entry.title: SHIFT-LLM: Distribution Shift Correction in Depth-Pruned LLMs

author.name: Ali Bahri, Hang Li, Hongliang Li, Zhitang Chen

entry.summary: Introduces SHIFT-LLM, a training-free post-pruning correction for depth-pruned LLMs: a Linear Residual Adapter at each pruning site preserves the identity pathway and adds a lightweight affine residual calibrated via closed-form least-squares regression, approximating the missing residual update without gradient computation.

entry.title: Bootstrapping a 4D LiDAR Annotation Tool from Video Foundation Models

author.name: Jihun Kim, Hyun-Kurl Jang, Hyemin Yang, Jinnyeong Yang, Hyeokjun Kweon, Kuk-Jin Yoon

entry.summary: Introduces LiDAR-SAM2, which bootstraps 4D LiDAR segmentation supervision automatically from a 2D video foundation model (SAM2) via multi-view projection and spatio-temporal aggregation, with a tailored modality interface. Aims to produce temporally coherent LiDAR labels without any human annotation.

entry.title: Minima-KV: Retention-Preserving KV Cache Compression with Mixed-Format Paged Attention

author.name: Sergii Kozyrev (Minima AI, Inc), Davyd Maiboroda (Minima AI, Inc)

entry.summary: Minima-KV is a retention-preserving KV cache compression hierarchy that keeps recent and protected anchor pages in FP8 while moving older pages to packed 3-bit quantization, with heterogeneous-format decode via globally normalized online-softmax merging. On Qwen3.6-27B profiles it reports 3.5x compression at 18.3 KiB of attention KV per live token on a single 96-GB Blackwell GPU.

entry.title: Function-Level Execution Feedback for Code Preference Optimization

author.name: Idris Nechnech, Sehwan Kim, Jimin Seo, Yeongoon Kim, Minhae Oh, Sangwoo Hong, Jungwoo Lee

entry.summary: STEP-KTODER defines process supervision steps for code generation as module-level functions in decomposed multi-function programs, labeled by automatically generated unit tests, and combines function-level process supervision with whole-program outcome feedback via a code-specific stepwise KTO. It fills a gap where code lacks the natural chain-of-thought step structure of math reasoning.

entry.title: Data Mixing as Mixture Experiment: Response Surface Methodology and Optimal Design for Large Language Model Pretraining

author.name: Yicheng Mao, Hongru Du

entry.summary: This paper recasts LLM pretraining data mixing as a classical mixture experiment, using sparse second-order Scheffe response surfaces and optimal design over domain token shares to select mixtures from proxy-model runs. It brings formal experimental-design machinery to a problem currently handled with heuristic proxy methods.

entry.title: Discovering Adaptive Transmission Programs for Collective Innovation

author.name: C\'edric Colas, J\'er\'emy Perez, Eleni Nisioti, Akhilesh Mocherla, Pierre-Yves Oudeyer, Cl\'ement Moulin-Frier, Maxime Derex

entry.summary: This work formalizes collective transmission protocols as state-aware programs that route information and resources based on agent and collective states, going beyond static network-structure analyses. It uses LLM-guided evolutionary search to discover effective protocols in a collective discovery task. The work connects AI methods to the science of human collective intelligence and cultural transmission.

entry.title: PonderPounce: A Pretrained MLLM as an Episode Context Engine for Robot Control

author.name: Suhwan Choi, Jaeyoon Jung, Sungkyung Kim, Yunsung Lee, Youngjae Yu

entry.summary: PonderPounce reuses a pretrained multimodal LLM native causal context as robot episode memory: a System2 MLLM accumulates observations and demonstration reasoning to produce subgoals, while a System1 VLA executes from current observations and proprioception. It avoids purpose-built history mechanisms.

entry.title: On-policy Distillation with Verifiable Reward

author.name: Wenze Lin, Jiale Zhao, Xitai Jiang, Songde Rao, Yining Li, Shenzhi Wang, Bingxiang He, Gao Huang

entry.summary: OPDVR seamlessly combines on-policy distillation with verifiable rewards, letting dense token-level teacher guidance and sparse task-level correctness signals reinforce each other without the hyperparameter-heavy weighted mixing or heuristic switching of prior integrations.

entry.title: GGSS: Geodesic-Gated Spherical Steering for Inference-Time Debiasing of Generative Vision-Language Models

author.name: Yiqun Sun, Junyu Chen, Pengfei Wei, Lawrence B. Hsieh

entry.summary: Proposes GGSS, a norm-preserving inference-time debiasing method for generative vision-language models that discovers a counterfactual bias subspace on the unit hypersphere, steers visual tokens along geodesic arcs, and adaptively gates correction to tokens carrying demographic signal. Evaluated against ten adapted baselines across four generative VLMs.

entry.title: PointRL: Learning Point-Level Vision-Language Grounding from Verifiable Annotation Evidence

author.name: Jingyang Su, Pu Cao, Xiuze Jin, Longyue Zhang, Qing Song, Lu Yang

entry.summary: Proposes PointRL, a verifiable reinforcement learning framework for point-level visual grounding that converts bounding boxes, masks, and instance labels into pointing instructions with retained verifiability. Addresses the non-unique supervision space of pointing, including target coverage, count consistency, and duplicate suppression for multi-instance instructions.

entry.title: V-Link: Recovering Lost Visual Representations in Action DiT for Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Yehao Lu, Jiarui Yang, Yuning Su, Yufeng Xie, Yu Zhong, Yazhou Zhang, Haiyu Lan, Kaixiang Lu, Peiwen Lin, Chuang Wang, Zequn Qin, Enyu Li, Xi Li

entry.summary: Reveals an accessibility gap in vision-language-action models: the action expert has limited access to 3D geometric and 2D semantic information present in VLM features. Proposes V-Link, which learns complementary spatial and semantic query representations and injects them during VL-to-action feature transfer in action DiT architectures, improving fine-grained manipulation.

entry.title: Video-IFBench: Evaluating Instruction Following of Multimodal LLMs in Video Understanding Scenarios

author.name: Hongbo Liu, Peixian Chen, Sihan Liu, Peiyuan Zhang, Kai Zou, Dian Zheng, Xiaoxing Hu, Yuhao Dong, Mengdan Zhang, Yunhang Shen, Haoyu Cao, Wei Liu, Weibo Gu, Xing Sun, Shengjie Zhao

entry.summary: Video-IFBench evaluates whether multimodal LLMs actually follow diverse user-specified constraints in video understanding, rather than merely achieving task accuracy. It builds an instruction taxonomy spanning visually and audio-grounded constraints. This addresses a genuinely under-evaluated capability highly relevant to real-world deployment of video MLLMs.

entry.title: One Policy, Many Embodiments: Unified Camera-Centric Action Geometry Pre-training for Heterogeneous Embodied Manipulation

author.name: Xiaomi Embodied Intelligence Team, University of Macau, :, Shaoqing Xu, Fang Li, Guozhi Zhan, Zhixiang Duan, Yuhan Wang, Yuechen Luo, Shengyin Jiang, Hanbing Li, Zhiying Du, Longlong Wang, Longmei Jiang, Weixiang Liang, Ying Gong, Yong Pan, Ziping Zhao, Zhiyuan Chen, Yangwei You, Kun Ma, Qinyuan Liu, Hangjun Ye, Zhi-xin Yang

entry.summary: UCAG-P from Xiaomi and University of Macau introduces a camera-centric unified action formulation that aligns heterogeneous embodied datasets across robot morphologies and camera configurations into a shared geometric action space, enabling one VLA policy pre-trained across embodiments without action retargeting. Targets the data-heterogeneity bottleneck in scaling generalist manipulation policies.

entry.title: ESQ-Bench: A Multi-Tier Enterprise Oracle Benchmark for Evaluating NL2SQL Dialect Generalization and Silent Semantic Divergence

author.name: Sanjay Mishra, Divya Chukkapalli, Ganesh R. Naik

entry.summary: ESQ-Bench is an Oracle-first NL2SQL benchmark with three schema complexity tiers and a silent-divergence metric, released with six populated enterprise schemas on four SQL dialects and 550 gold-validated pairs. It addresses the gap between academic benchmarks like Spider and BIRD and realistic enterprise database environments.

entry.title: AgentRoom: Concurrent Multi-Agent Coding in a CRDT-Backed Shared Workspace

author.name: Seonglae Cho, Donghyun Lee

entry.summary: AgentRoom is a realtime collaborative editing protocol, backed by CRDTs, that lets multiple coding agents work concurrently in a shared workspace with file-level claims instead of sequential phase handoffs or uncoordinated sampling. It targets the serial bottleneck of current multi-agent coding systems and reduces task abandonment.

entry.title: More Rejective, Not More Discriminative: The Unit of Verification in Pre-Execution LLM Oversight

author.name: Yuchen Han, Cheng Yan, Wuyang Zhang

entry.summary: This paper introduces the twin-prefix framework to isolate how the unit of verification (how many actions one monitor call reviews) affects fallible LLM pre-execution oversight, showing that coarser review units make monitors more rejective without being more discriminative. It provides a controlled methodology for AI control protocol design.

entry.title: AHEAD: Adaptive Hindsight with Environment-Augmented Distillation for Agentic RL

author.name: Xiaolong Jin, Dingmin Wang, Vijay Lingam, Varun Kumar

entry.summary: AHEAD is a step-aware framework for multi-turn agentic RL that matches supervision sources to step types, applying teacher distillation with privileged environment information only at critical error steps while leaving routine steps to standard RL. It improves on uniform self-distillation that ignores the asymmetry between step types.

entry.title: Paritok-4B: Intent-Conditioned Context Compression for Coding Agents

author.name: Jiayu Shi, Luzhuo Chen

entry.summary: Paritok-4B is a 4B LoRA compressor for coding-agent trajectories that is extractive (96 percent of emitted identifiers, paths, and numbers appear verbatim in input) and intent-conditioned on the agent current task, reducing the token bill from re-sent file reads and tool outputs. It holds 96.2 percent extractiveness on held-out SWE-bench Lite output.

entry.title: VideoHarness-RSI: Recursive Harness Self-Improvement for Long-Video Understanding with Frozen Vision-Language Models

author.name: Guoyang Xu, Hao Chen

entry.summary: VideoHarness-RSI recursively searches executable context-construction programs around a frozen vision-language model for long-video understanding, with an outer-loop proposer iterating on prior programs and evaluation outcomes. It isolates how much gain comes from improving the context-construction program alone versus model changes.

entry.title: The Invisible Editorial Layer: Formalizing Undisclosed Inference-Time Steering, Probability Placement, and the Attribution Problem in Deployed Language Models

author.name: Augusto Camargo

entry.summary: This paper formalizes inference-time framing bias: systematic runtime steering of deployed model outputs toward institutional, ideological, or commercial frames without weight changes, and defines the Inference Attribution Problem of distinguishing foundation-model behavior from production-stack interventions. It argues evaluations conflate the model with the serving system. This raises important transparency and accountability questions for deployed LLMs.

entry.title: Evidence Blindness in Direct Corpus Interaction: Persistent Navigation with AtlasNav

author.name: Hongyu Guo, Zhiyu Zheng, Zhao Cao

entry.summary: This paper identifies Evidence Blindness in Direct Corpus Interaction: with a full corpus accessible, LLM agents progressively lose usable evidence as it fails to surface, remains unopened, or fails to expose decisive fragments under finite interaction budgets. It quantifies stage-wise evidence realization and shows dynamic-workspace methods substantially outperform raw interaction. The findings challenge assumptions that keeping the corpus in reach suffices.

entry.title: The Shadow Price of Intelligence: Quality Degradation in LLM Inference as a Supply Chain Problem

author.name: Elioth Sanabria

entry.summary: Models LLM inference degradation under compute congestion as a supply chain problem, showing that routing to smaller models or cutting reasoning hides costs in retries and churned lifetime value. Using newsvendor and retry-multiplier primitives, it argues the industry cost accounting for degraded service is systematically wrong.

entry.title: What Guides the Agent? Adjudicating Unauthorized Behavior via Localizing Behavior-Guiding Instructions

author.name: Yichao Gao, Yumo Zhang, Yunhao Yao, Haohua Du, Puhan Luo, Ruiqi Li, Zhiqiang Wang

entry.summary: Attnlocate is a runtime framework that localizes the context spans genuinely influencing tool-calling decisions in LLM agents, casting behavior-guiding instruction discovery as an object detection-like problem over attention. It targets dynamic injection during reasoning rather than static input filtering.

entry.title: Hierarchical Skill Retrieval for Data-Efficient Adaptation of Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Haoran Hao, Shahram Najam Syed, Jeff Schneider, Jeffrey Ichnowski

entry.summary: Hierarchical Skill Retrieval enables data-efficient adaptation of vision-language-action models by retrieving reusable sub-skills from prior demonstrations rather than requiring whole-task matches. It exploits the hierarchical structure of long-horizon manipulation where complete task matches are rare but skills abound.

entry.title: Not All Tokens Are Equal: Region-Aware Consistency Repair of Backdoors in MLLMs

author.name: Jiali Wei, Ming Fan, Mingkun Zhang, Haoyu Wang, Jun Sun, Guoheng Sun, Xiaoning Ren, Haijun Wang, Ting Liu

entry.summary: RACER is a model-level backdoor repair framework for multimodal LLMs based on the observation that backdoors induce layer-wise inconsistency in internal representations, enabling region-aware consistency repair that removes triggers embedded in images, text, or both rather than filtering inputs at inference.

entry.title: Simthesizer: An Agent-Driven Simulation Framework for LLM Serving Systems

author.name: Wonung Kim, Hyunmin Choi, Minsu Kim, Jaehong Cho, Yeongwook Kim, Jongse Park

entry.summary: Simthesizer enables agent-driven development of LLM serving simulators through composable abstractions, closing the gap between fast-evolving serving mechanisms like agentic workflows and disaggregated serving and the monolithic simulators that require invasive rewrites.

entry.title: Automatic Model Card Generation Using an LLM

author.name: Tajkia Rahman Toma, Balreet Grewal, Cor-Paul Bezemer

entry.summary: Introduces MCTidy and MCGenie, LLM-based tools that standardize existing Hugging Face model cards and generate new ones directly from repository data. Addresses the transparency gap caused by inconsistent or missing model documentation. Evaluated on 48 real model cards for retention, alignment, hallucination, and stability.

entry.title: The Frame Kernel Method for Multiscale Operator Learning

author.name: Branden Frieden, Ryan Whitehead, M. Keith Ballard, Robert M. Kirby, Varun Shankar

entry.summary: Introduces the Frame Kernel Method, a natively multiscale operator learning method that learns frame coefficients of output functions from frame coefficients of inputs, with interpolation proofs, error estimates, and convergence rates for PDE surrogate modeling.

entry.title: Understanding the Energy Scaling of Large Language Model Inference Across Context Lengths and Attention Architectures

author.name: Molka Chkir, Syed Muhammad Danish, Jos H\"oll, Arghavan Asad

entry.summary: Systematic empirical study of decode-phase LLM energy consumption across MHA, GQA, and GQA+SWA attention architectures, measuring GPU energy via hardware counters over varying context lengths, batch sizes, and workloads.

entry.title: Bayesian Flow Networks for Offline Trajectory Planning

author.name: Ludvig Killingberg, Helge Langseth

entry.summary: BFN-RL applies Bayesian Flow Networks to offline reinforcement learning, natively handling discrete and continuous trajectory spaces by evolving distribution parameters rather than noisy data, with a categorical planner and learned inverse model.

entry.title: Two Dimensions Govern Agnostic Multiclass Transductive Learning

author.name: Pahan Dewasurendra

entry.summary: Resolves an open question in learning theory: for agnostic multiclass transductive learning, the optimal excess error is governed by DS and Natarajan dimensions, holding for arbitrary label spaces up to logarithmic factors, with both terms shown necessary.

entry.title: A Token-Level Analysis of Sampled-Token Reverse-KL On-Policy Distillation

author.name: Bing Shao, Jiazheng Zhang, Long Ma, Yujiong Shen, Senjie Jin, Xin Guo, Yuming Yang, Mingxu Chai, Zhiheng Xi, Tao Gui, Qi Zhang, Xuanjing Huang

entry.summary: Analyzes per-token gradients of the sampled reverse-KL estimator in on-policy distillation, showing update mass concentrates on low-student-probability tokens with large teacher-student gaps, and derives a lightweight intervention based on this factorization.

entry.title: EXAONE Tabular 1.0 : Technical Report

author.name: Moonjung Eo, Min-Kook Suh, Hye-Seung Cho, Jiwon Kim, Seoyoon Kim, Sangjun Nam, Soonyoung Lee

entry.summary: Technical report for EXAONE Tabular, a compact tabular foundation model performing classification and regression via in-context learning without gradient updates, pretrained purely on a synthetic structural-causal-model prior. Its key contribution is an architecture redesign interleaving feature-axis attention with support-conditioned item-axis attention at every layer. Achieves strong performance across four public benchmarks.

entry.title: TraceML: An Empirical Analysis of Human-Agent Planning in Machine Learning Development

author.name: Jiarui Yan, Weiwei Sun, Sijie Li, Wenhan Li, Yiming Yang

entry.summary: Introduces TraceML, pairing 4,465 human Kaggle trajectories across 134 competitions with 430 paired human and 207 agent trajectories under a version-level schema to analyze why LLM agents underperform in autonomous ML development. Captures the development process rather than only final outcomes. Valuable resource for understanding and improving AI research agents.

entry.title: DataKernelBench: Can LLMs Optimize Database Queries on GPUs?

author.name: Gokul Karthik Kumar, Yotam Perlitz, Corey Lammie, Andrea Giovannini, Katja Hose

entry.summary: Introduces DataKernelBench, translating SQL into validated TorchPlan programs and evaluating LLMs writing CUDA or Triton kernels for database queries with execution-guided repair, finding the strongest full-query CUDA configuration achieves 2.11x speedup over torch.compile at full pass rate on TPC-H SF10 with an H100. Extends LLM kernel benchmarks beyond ML operators to irregular, data-movement-heavy workloads. Timely at the intersection of LLM agents and GPU systems.

entry.title: LM-X: Explainable Action Modeling with Progress, Event, and Uncertainty Prediction for Generalist Robot Manipulation

author.name: Jin Lou, Jingxuan Zhu, Andong Chen, Xupeng Wang, Yuan Xu, Yuexuan Li, Xingdong Zhu, Zhijie Zhu, Yingwei Ji, Wenpeng Nie, Jingyi Li, Liangliang Chen, Jinyan Liu, Zhiqi Song, Jidong Zhang, Hongming Li, Yuchen Zhu

entry.summary: LM-X adds three online supervised signals (return-to-go progress, event-to-go, uncertainty) to generalist VLA policies for robot manipulation, conditioning action generation explicitly and making control states visible during execution. Inspired by biological sensorimotor control principles.

entry.title: Unfolding Scientific Papers into Multi-Turn Generation Trajectories for Continued Pre-Training

author.name: Qiankai Xu, Qiguang Chen, Zixin Su, Wenhao Huang, Yue Gao, Jiaheng Liu, Ge Zhang

entry.summary: Presents a pipeline that unfolds scientific papers into multi-turn generation trajectories where a teacher model reconstructs the writing process: request, global plan, and pre-writing deliberation per section, with source text kept verbatim. Applied to continued pre-training, lifting synthetic thought-reconstruction to the document level.

entry.title: Controlling for Omitted Variable Bias in Deep Neural Networks

author.name: Manuel Pfeuffer, Roshan Prakash Rane, Kerstin Ritter, Sonja Greven

entry.summary: Shows that restricting correlations between confounders and predictions fails to correct omitted variable bias in deep networks, and proposes a control-variable approach based on generalized additive components to account for known confounders like demographics. Frames shortcut learning as an omitted variable bias problem.

entry.title: Finding and using interpretable latents in a neutrino foundation model with sparse autoencoders

author.name: Rapha\"el Bonnet-Guerrini, Johann Ioannou-Nikolaides, Inar Timiryasov, Vincenzo Piuri

entry.summary: First application of sparse-autoencoder-based mechanistic interpretability to particle physics, extracting a validated atlas of physical concepts from a neutrino foundation model trained on IceCube data. Causal interventions show the direction-reconstruction head underuses this information, motivating an uncertainty head that causally depends on the interpretable features.

entry.title: MathAdv: What Theorem Provers Know, Reason, Formalize, and Generalize

author.name: Jiaxin Yuan, Connor Martinez Lockhart, Xiaoyu Liu, Jiaqi Wang, Chenghao Deng, Xiayimei Han, Vlasios Mastrantonis, Dmitrii Gudin, Shaopeng Zhu, Abdirisak Abdullahi Mohamed, Bilal Hamdi Aytekin, Jiewen Lang, Zezheng Song, Furong Huang

entry.summary: MathAdv is a diagnostic theorem-proving benchmark spanning 13 domains of undergraduate and graduate mathematics, pairing Lean 4 proving with multiple-choice knowledge, fill-in-the-blank reasoning, and robustness-to-reformulation tasks. Reveals gaps between what provers know, reason, formalize, and generalize.

entry.title: When RAG Fails to Equalize: Geo-bias in Factual Question Answering over Public Companies

author.name: Abhinav Havaldar, Enrico Santus

entry.summary: Shows that RAG does not equalize factual QA accuracy across geographies: on a benchmark of about 2,000 public companies, no-context accuracy varies strongly by region, and perfect retrieval context improves but does not eliminate these gaps. Gains correlate with baseline accuracy, suggesting retrieval benefits already-knowledgeable regions.

entry.title: Unveiling Spectral Mechanisms in Training-Free LLM Text Detection

author.name: Haitong Luo, Xuying Meng, Weiyao Zhang, Wenji Zou, Shengfeng Lou, Xuefeng Jiang, Chungang Lin, Yujun Zhang

entry.summary: Provides theoretical and empirical analysis of training-free LLM text detection via spectral methods, connecting spectral energy to variance in proxy log-probability trajectories and explaining how broader human token choices create detectable fluctuations called generative vitality. Clarifies mechanisms and practical boundaries of the approach.

entry.title: Plans You Can Check: Verifier-Grounded Learning of an Open-Weight Planner for Executable Video-Editing

author.name: Haoyu Wang, Cheng Feng, Liuyang Bian, Ruiyang Huang, Lei Wei, Yafei Wen, Xiaoxin Chen, Xiaoying Tang

entry.summary: Introduces RefineCut, which trains a compact open-weight planner for executable video editing: the planner edits a typed timeline via structured patches checked by a deterministic verifier against a constraint ledger, learning from replayed multi-teacher trajectories rather than direct imitation. Targets the decision layer rather than pixel generation.

entry.title: A Statistical Audit of Physical AI Benchmark Redundancy

author.name: Zaruhi Navasardyan, Hrant Davtyan

entry.summary: A statistical audit constructing a 51-model by 12-benchmark matrix for physical AI, showing quantitative evidence that benchmark redundancy affects reported rankings — collapsing substitute benchmark pairs moves 22 of 51 models by three or more places. Proposes a principled benchmark selection method.

entry.title: MLLMCLIP: Feature-Level Distillation of MLLM for Robust Vision-Language Representations

author.name: Jongsuk Kim, Qiyu Wu, Zhuoyuan Mao, Hiromi Wakaki, Junmo Kim, Yuki Mitsufuji

entry.summary: MLLMCLIP distills multimodal knowledge from a generative MLLM teacher directly into a discriminative CLIP student via attention-based per-layer token selection, avoiding expensive synthetic hard-negative data pipelines. The goal is improving compositionality, especially attribute-object and relational reasoning, in vision-language representations. The heterogeneous distillation recipe is a clean alternative to cascade-based data augmentation.

entry.title: LLM Agents Perform Controlled Experiments Using Simulation Models

author.name: Yuchen Xia, Michael Weyrich, Nasser Jazdi, Johannes St\"umpfle, Johannes Sigel, Akshay Narla, Gavin K. Reynolds, Anna Jawor-Baczynska, Pol Llopart

entry.summary: This paper proposes a multi-agent framework enabling LLM agents to run controlled experiments with scientific simulation models for pharmaceutical process design, including task representation, experiment design, comparative simulation execution, and evidence-based recommendation synthesis. It moves agent evaluation beyond plausible text generation toward intervention-based reasoning about system behavior.

entry.title: BenchBench-Protocol: Evaluating Real-World Wet-Lab Protocol Reasoning and Modification

author.name: Aditya Sivakumar, Ashu Singhal, Nicholas Larus-Stone, Nithin Parsan

entry.summary: BenchBench-Protocol is a benchmark of 149 protocol-modification tasks reconstructed from real modifications scientists made to published wet-lab protocols, with weighted grading derived from actual diff-based changes. It evaluates whether LLMs can adapt experimental protocols accounting for prior choices and downstream steps.

entry.title: Are Android GUI Agents Robust Against Runtime Anomalies? AnTrap: Evaluating Agents in Dynamic Adversarial Environments

author.name: Guo Gan, Yilun Zhao, Cong Chen, Jinbiao Wei, Tingyu Song, Zheyuan Yang, Lin Fu, Hong Zhou

entry.summary: AnTrap injects dynamic runtime anomalies into Android GUI agent execution trajectories, organized into a four-layer taxonomy with ten subcategories, and evaluates 16 leading GUI models while preserving task solvability. It reveals universal vulnerability to dynamic anomalies even among the strongest models.

entry.title: Robust Code RL via Faulty-Code-Driven Test case Synthesis and Dense Reward Shaping

author.name: Yiwen Zhang, Xiaodong Yan, Zhenyu Huang, Deng Zhao, Liang Jiang, Qing Cui, Zujie Wen, Zhiqiang Zhang, Jun Zhou

entry.summary: RobustTests mitigates reward hacking in RLVR code training by synthesizing test cases from near-correct faulty code, guiding models to capture latent logical discrepancies, and applying dense reward shaping. It addresses false positives from insufficient test coverage that cause policy degradation.

entry.title: Preference Data Selection for Mitigating the Alignment Tax in Large Language Models

author.name: Minsu Kim, Jianxun Lian, Xing Xie, Steven Euijong Whang

entry.summary: BALIGN is a balanced preference-data selection strategy that mitigates the alignment tax (catastrophic forgetting of general capabilities) by identifying data-centric features from gradient analysis that dictate parameter drift, including the reference model log-probability. It frames alignment degradation as a data property rather than purely an optimization problem.

entry.title: MetaRAG: Belief-Action Aligned Policy Optimization for Agentic RAG

author.name: Qiuyi Qi, Tian Liang, Jiamu Wang, Jinjian Zhang, Wei Zhou, Pengcheng Zhu, Linjian Mo, Ming Kong, Jie Liu, Qiang Zhu

entry.summary: MetaRAG reformulates the search-versus-answer decision in agentic RAG as belief-action alignment, using verify-first action generation and internal belief probing to derive a consistency reward without external supervision. It trains agents to continue searching only when their own belief says evidence is insufficient.

entry.title: SA-Bench: Evaluating Semantic Alignment in LLM-Based Paper Reproduction

author.name: Xue Hu, Zewei Pan, Zeli Su, Zhou Liu, Wentao Zhang

entry.summary: SA-Bench defines semantic drift in LLM paper-reproduction code and provides a diagnostic benchmark with 1,491 Semantic Alignment Units across 30 ICLR, ICML, and NeurIPS 2025 papers, evaluating 12 generator configurations along numerical, methodological, protocol, and ordering drift dimensions. It measures scientific faithfulness beyond code execution success.

entry.title: ReproAgent: Contract-Guided Paper-to-Code Reproduction

author.name: Xue Hu, Zewei Pan, Zhongyuan Wang, Zhou Liu, Zeli Su, Wentao Zhang

entry.summary: ReproAgent is a four-stage Prepare-Plan-Generate-Repair pipeline for paper-to-code reproduction built around a persistent implementation contract with implementation-requirement and reference-evidence channels, addressing specification loss across long agent trajectories and implicit conventions absent from papers. It is a companion system to SA-Bench from the same group.

entry.title: Partial Identification under Causal Orders by Linear Programming

author.name: Eric Rossetto, Alessandro Antonucci

entry.summary: The authors show that any counterfactual query induces a partial topological ordering over relevant variables, enabling an explicit query parametrization that reduces partial identification of nested counterfactuals to a linear program, without requiring a fully specified causal graph. This generalizes the classical Tian-Pearl bounding framework. It is valuable for causal inference under incomplete domain knowledge.

entry.title: The Empire, Long Divided, Must Unite: Architectural Convergence in Three LLM Agent Harnesses

author.name: Dai Jiahong

entry.summary: A source-level case study of three deliberately opposed open coding-agent harnesses (LangChain deepagents, Earendil pi, DeepSeek dsh) finding architectural convergence: mature harnesses shed or modularize scaffolding while the harness layer, not the model, increasingly constrains agent behavior.

entry.title: WebMCP-Phalanx: Enforcing and Characterizing Trust Boundaries for Browser-Integrated LLM Agents

author.name: Lin-Fa Lee, YI-YU Chang, Kuo-Hui Yeh

entry.summary: WebMCP-Phalanx proposes a dual-layer runtime for the W3C WebMCP proposal, binding browser-exposed agent tools to principals via cryptographic capability credentials and provenance labels, plus a second layer against semantic prompt injection. It addresses subject-attribution spoofing and uncontrolled tool lifecycles.

entry.title: ChorusTIC: Training-Free Multivariate Time Series Classification via Chorus In-Context Learning

author.name: Juntao Fang, Shifeng Xie, Ruichu Cai, Shengji Zheng, Zijian Li, Keli Zhang, Lujia Pan, Themis Palpanas, Zhifeng Hao

entry.summary: ChorusTIC is a classification-native time series foundation model supporting training-free in-context classification across heterogeneous channel configurations, using random subchannel slot concatenation and a shared dual-axis encoder. It removes the need for task-specific classifier fitting on each dataset.

entry.title: Knowing When to Ask for Help: Bayesian Self-Escalation in Hierarchical LLM Agents

author.name: Nadeem Shaikh

entry.summary: Formulates intra-generation delegation as a Bayesian optimal-stopping problem where an agent recognizes during its own reasoning that it will likely fail and escalates to a stronger model. It derives the myopic escalation threshold in closed form and proves the optimal policy is time-varying.

entry.title: Contrastive Branch Policy Optimization

author.name: Ying Wang, Changlin Qiu, Bang Lin, Linbo Jin, Wen Jiang, Zhe Sun, Jingli Yang

entry.summary: CBPO disentangles rollout budget allocation from token-level credit assignment in branch-based RLVR, using generation entropy to screen branch positions and path- and node-level decay to distribute contrastive credit for multi-turn tool-using agents.

entry.title: FARCA: Fact-Aligned Reliability-Aware Credit Assignment for Reinforcement Learning with Factual Supervision

author.name: Qiming Xie, Wenjie Zheng, Xiangqing Shen, Rui Xia

entry.summary: FARCA tackles noisy factual credit assignment in RLVR with process-level factual supervision, decomposing it into credit localization and reliability ambiguity and transforming factual signals into localized, reliability-weighted policy updates to reduce hallucination from outcome-driven rewards.

entry.title: Beyond Static Interpretability: Anticipating Post-SFT Mechanisms from Pre-SFT Parameters for Better Tuning

author.name: Hang Chen, Jiaying Zhu, Wenya Wang

entry.summary: Proposes a forward-looking localization framework that estimates the post-SFT mechanistic state of a model from pre-SFT parameters and target data, avoiding the misleading retrospective neuron identification that disrupts locate-then-tune parameter-efficient fine-tuning.

entry.title: The RAT: A Unified Bayesian Model for RAG Evaluation

author.name: Pius von D\"{a}niken, Felix Matthias Saaro, Mark Cieliebak, Jan Deriu

entry.summary: The RAT is a unified Bayesian framework for RAG evaluation that jointly models retrieval success, abstention behavior, and answer correctness factorized along the pipeline information flow, separating user-facing task success from generator behavior given retrieval outcomes across 27 configurations.

entry.title: D$^3$-MOPD: Adaptive Dynamic Domain ScheDuling for Efficient Multi-Teacher Distillation

author.name: Zechen Sun, Zhiwei Zhang, Fei Zhao, Juntao Li, Mu Chuan, Huayu Deng, Guojian Zhan, Wenliang Chen, Yao Hu, Min Zhang

entry.summary: D3-MOPD dynamically schedules the domain mixture in multi-teacher on-policy distillation by repurposing per-domain reverse-KL signals already computed during training, avoiding wasted compute on fast-converging domains at zero overhead.

entry.title: On the Representational Geometry of Dynamic Programs

author.name: Richard F. M. Lim, Ruriko Yoshida

entry.summary: Shows that finite min-plus dynamic programs are shortest paths on DAGs, equivalently tropical polynomials, and proves graph, polynomial, and polyhedron descriptions form isomorphic semirings. Uses this geometry to give structural negative results on length generalization for DP targets.

entry.title: Learning Mixtures of Plackett-Luce Models for Multi-Objective Alignment

author.name: Dongyue Li, Ziniu Zhang, Lu Wang, Hongyang R. Zhang

entry.summary: Learns mixtures of Plackett-Luce models from multi-way rankings representing heterogeneous annotator preferences, addressing identifiability limits via ranking augmentation with base-LLM-generated responses and gradient-based estimation in embedding space. Relevant to multi-objective AI alignment.

entry.title: Neither Precision Nor Architecture Alone: Controlled Tests of Failure Remedies for Physics-Informed Neural Networks

author.name: Jinyuan Zhang, Peng He, He Hu, Yin Yuan, ShengShuo Jiao

entry.summary: A pre-registered 144-run controlled study testing whether FP64 precision or SSM backbones with sub-sequence alignment fix PINN failures on stiff PDEs, finding the remedies act on disjoint regime-and-seed slices and neither substitutes for the other.

entry.title: Escaping Low-Dimensional Overlap: Multi-Task Model Merging via High-Dimensional Sparse Disentanglement

author.name: Yihang Zhang, Shengke Sun, Junjie Wen, Feng Zeng

entry.summary: Proposes merging multi-task models via sparse autoencoders that project task vectors into a high-dimensional sparse feature space for feature-level disentanglement before fusion, targeting task interference from superposition.

entry.title: Reflection Steering: Disentangling Reflection from Reasoning in Activation Space for Token-Efficient Inference

author.name: Jiarui Hu, Zhiyuan Wen, Xiaoyun Liu, Jiaxing Shen, Yu Yang

entry.summary: Reflection Steering is a training-free activation-steering framework that disentangles reflection-related activations from general reasoning signals at each layer, controlling redundant verification in large reasoning models for token-efficient inference.

entry.title: Beyond Scaling: Self-Evolving LLM Agents for Hardware Kernel Optimization via an Experience-Driven Workflow and Experience Graph Memory

author.name: Siyuan Chen, Runlin Hou, Shenxiu Wu, Yansong Sun, Junming Cao, Yiyu Zhang, Shudi Shao, Junhao Qiu, Zhichao Lu, Qingfu Zhang

entry.summary: KOPE is an experience-driven framework for LLM-agent hardware kernel optimization that records optimization decisions with execution feedback in an experience graph memory, enabling agents to learn across runs rather than within a single task.

entry.title: Comparing Corrupted Constrained Learning Problems

author.name: Laura Iacovissi, Rabanus Derr, Robert C. Williamson

entry.summary: Presents a systematic privacy-attack evaluation of LLM-enhanced graph neural networks through a unified five-stage framework spanning dataset preparation, attack, risk assessment, and defense analysis across six real-world text-attributed graph datasets. It shows that the performance gains of enriching GNNs with LLM semantics come with underexplored privacy vulnerabilities. Important for anyone deploying GNN+LLM systems on sensitive graph data.

entry.title: How Edge of Stability Hinders SCAFFOLD in Federated Optimization

author.name: Anant Khandelwal, Michael Crawshaw, Mingrui Liu

entry.summary: Explains why the theoretically superior SCAFFOLD federated optimization algorithm often fails to beat simpler FedAvg in practice, attributing the gap to Edge of Stability and progressive sharpening dynamics. Empirically shows EoS-like behavior in both algorithms with sharpness equilibrium inversely related to step size. Nice example of deep learning dynamics informing federated learning.

entry.title: DualOPSD: Adaptive Privileged Teachers for On-Policy Self-Distillation

author.name: Yutong Chen, Guangfu Guo, Zhichao Xu, Kunpeng Liu

entry.summary: Proposes DualOPSD, an asymmetric alternating variant of on-policy self-distillation that adapts the privileged teacher toward the updated student distribution instead of keeping it fixed. On Qwen3-8B in non-thinking mode it improves avg@12 over OPSD by 23.61, 13.89, and 10.00 points on AIME 2024, AIME 2025, and HMMT 2025, with results at 1.7B scale as well. Notably, Qwen3-8B is an established 2025 model, so this is analysis of a post-training method on an existing model, not a new model release.

entry.title: The Dialect Tax: Dialectal Biases Persist throughout the Language Modeling Pipeline

author.name: Elle

entry.summary: Traces dialectal performance gaps (the dialect tax) through the full language modeling pipeline using parallel English dialect corpora that hold meaning fixed, finding that modern LMs encode dialectal texts unequally at tokenization, pre-training, post-training, and inference, while still recognizing semantic equivalence. Notably finds bypassing certain pipeline stages mitigates gaps. Important fairness diagnosis across model families and generations.

entry.title: Does Fine-Tuning Undo Activation Steering? Behavioural Recovery Without Weight-Edit Reversal

author.name: Philipp E. Glass, Allan Tucker, Yongmin Li, Alina Miron

entry.summary: Studies whether activation steering embedded into model weights survives subsequent fine-tuning, finding behavioral preservation tracks training-data agreement (refusal ablation losing 64 percent of its effect under SFT on average) while the weight edits persist mechanistically even as behavior recovers. Critical for steering-as-alignment-prior-to-release proposals. Suggests weight-level interventions are less durable than hoped.

entry.title: Distance Is Not Enough: Forget-Retain Alignment Gap Predicts LLM Relearning Robustness

author.name: Yi Chen, Hanna Hsieh, Shuhong Liu, Chuanbo Hua, Zihan Ma, Kun Wang, Joo-Young Kim

entry.summary: Introduces FRAG (Forget-Retain Alignment Gap), a training-free predictor of whether unlearned LLM knowledge will stay unlearned under relearning attacks, scoring whether an update affects forget-critical while sparing retain-critical weights, more reliably than global weight-distance metrics. Addresses the practical failure of unlearning being reversible by brief fine-tuning. Valuable for unlearning auditing.

entry.title: Narcissus: Program Synthesis Using Context-Aware LLM Approximations

author.name: Tilman Hinnerichs, Sebastijan Dumancic, Neil Yorke-Smith

entry.summary: Narcissus improves LLM-guided enumerative program synthesis for low-resource target languages by keeping LLM proposals as syntax trees and scoring each candidate expansion in context, rather than collapsing proposals to rule frequencies. This preserves structural information and avoids pruning valid rules when proposals err.

entry.title: Pointing the Way, Hiding the Destination: Practical Private Dense Retrieval at Scale

author.name: Peichun Hua, Danyang Chen, Junan Zhang, Haifeng Sun, Jingyu Wang, Diwen Xue, Mingyu Li, Yunming Xiao

entry.summary: Proposes a practical private dense retrieval scheme for hosted RAG where a learned deep-hash binary code acts as a privacy filter to shortlist candidates, with encrypted reranking and oblivious key transfer protecting the precise query and final selection. Avoids full-corpus cryptographic search without sacrificing retrieval quality.

entry.title: Why ML-based cough models do not generalize: a systematic cross-dataset evaluation for tuberculosis screening

author.name: Wensi Zhang, Tomas Teijeiro, J\'er\^ome Thevenot, David Atienza

entry.summary: Systematically evaluates cross-dataset generalization of ML and DL cough-based tuberculosis classifiers across three independent datasets, finding within-dataset ROC-AUC up to 0.755 but external performance frequently below 0.6. Shows representations organize by recording device and dataset rather than disease status, explaining the failure.

entry.title: Precipitation Downscaling Using Foundation Model-Conditioned Diffusion

author.name: Victor Nascimento Ribeiro, Jorge Guevara, Jorge Sebastian Moraga, Chris Lucas, Natalie Lord, Andrew Taylor, Edward Lockhart, Will Trojak, Johannes Schmude, Anne Jones

entry.summary: Investigates three conditioning strategies for diffusion-based precipitation downscaling: channel concatenation, cross-attention with a learned encoder, and cross-attention with the frozen Prithvi WxC weather foundation-model encoder. Addresses how large-scale atmospheric predictors should condition generation for hydrological impact modeling.

entry.title: How Robust Are Automated Fact-Checking Systems? A Cross-Benchmark Evaluation

author.name: Aida Usmanova, Zangir Iklassov, Markus Leippold, Ricardo Usbeck

entry.summary: Cross-benchmarks nine fact-checking systems, from sparse baselines to fine-tuned transformers, zero-shot LLMs, and top AVeriTeC 2025 entries, across four datasets spanning scientific, open-web, and climate domains. Finds systems fail to generalize across domains and simple baselines are often omitted in prior evaluations.

entry.title: HealthBench-Psych: A Mental Health Subset of OpenAI's HealthBench

author.name: Matthew Flathers, Phuong Anh Nguyen, Jill Noorily, Julian Herpertz, Meiting Chen, Jasreen Multani, Samuel Powell, Mason Granof, Mark Kalinch, John Torous

entry.summary: HealthBench-Psych is a mental-health subset of OpenAI's HealthBench, screened by an LLM rubric and validated via two rounds of blinded clinician review, yielding 610 conversations plus a hard variant. Addresses the need for specialty-resolved LLM health evaluation as millions turn to LLMs for psychological support.

entry.title: MTDiag: A Multi-Turn Diagnostic Dataset Towards Clinically Meaningful LLM Evaluation

author.name: Pia Chouayfati, Alexander M. Fichtl, Miriam Ansch\"utz, George Doumat, Georg Groh

entry.summary: MTDiag is a multi-turn diagnostic dialogue dataset built from DDXPlus, MIMIC-IV, and published case reports, normalized to a canonical schema and covering common ED presentations plus long-tail rare conditions. Motivated by evidence that LLMs degrade in multi-turn clinical settings versus static QA benchmarks.

entry.title: TOPAS: Workflow-Aware Prefix-State Scheduling for Multi-Agent LLM Serving

author.name: Hongqiu Ni, Han Tian, Chi Zhang, Guopeng Li, Haisheng Tan

entry.summary: TOPAS is a task-oriented prefix-aware scheduler for multi-agent LLM serving that jointly decides which agent KV prefixes to retain and which requests to schedule, balancing prefix locality against workflow progress under a shared cache budget. Reduces job completion time versus optimizing either objective alone.

entry.title: AWM: Answerable Working Memory for Long-Document VQA Agents

author.name: Dongzhuoran Zhou, Yuqicheng Zhu, Yule Liu, Zhen Yang, Rui Lu, Yuxiao Dong, Jie Tang, Evgeny Kharlamov

entry.summary: Introduces memory-only answerability, a diagnostic asking whether a long-document VQA agent's terminal working memory alone suffices to answer, exposing cases where agents reach the right page yet leave memory too generic to support grounded answering. Evaluates working-memory quality beyond final-answer correctness.

entry.title: From Passive Response to Proactive Correction: Enhancing LLM Robustness Against Input Fact Perturbations

author.name: Ping Wang, Xiangguo Sun, Bingbing Xu, Guocong Li, Xiaofeng Meng

entry.summary: Identifies that LLMs produce confident but wrong answers when user inputs contain misleading premises (fact perturbations), and proposes DEDUCE, a three-stage framework that detects errors via fact extraction and verification, devises corrections through multi-perspective deliberation, and delivers corrected answers rather than passively responding.

entry.title: Formal, Executable and Explainable Runtime Monitoring of Spoken Air Traffic Control Operational Procedures

author.name: Roberto Luvini, Giacomo Longo, Alessandro Armando, Enrico Russo

entry.summary: Presents a runtime verification framework for spoken air traffic control procedures, parsing radio communications into events linked to entities and checking controller-pilot exchanges, surveillance data, and onboard observations against formal procedural models. Aimed at aviation safety, where execution failures have caused fatal accidents.

entry.title: Can You Trust Frozen Hematology Foundation Models under Acquisition Shift?

author.name: Jai Kumar Sharma, Peeyush Tapadiya

entry.summary: Audits 15 frozen hematology and general vision foundation-model encoders across four acquisition domains, finding near-saturated in-domain accuracy but 34-72% cross-dataset macro-F1 drops and rank reordering, with the in-domain best encoder falling to 10th of 15 on the most-shifted target. Highlights reliability and calibration gaps under acquisition shift.

entry.title: See More, Detect Less? Taming Information Leakage in Multi-View Anomaly Detection

author.name: Shang-Fu Chen, Kuan-Chuan Peng, Jhih-Ciang Wu, Wen-Huang Cheng, Kai-Lung Hua

entry.summary: Identifies cross-view information leakage in multi-view anomaly detection: naively fused normal cues from intact views let decoders reconstruct anomalous regions, collapsing the reconstruction gap the detector relies on. Proposes GLAD, combining foundation-model features with global-local cross-view fusion that explicitly restricts decoder information.

entry.title: Not All Attention Heads Contribute to Critical Visual Token Selection: Head-Aware Pruning Matters More

author.name: Chaofang Ma, Lin Jiang, Carol Jingyi Li, Xingyu Liu, Zeyu Li, Jiang Xu, Wei Zhang

entry.summary: Shows that the ability to pinpoint critical visual tokens for pruning in VLMs is concentrated in a small fraction of attention heads, so aggregating attention across all heads in the pruning layer is suboptimal. Head-aware pruning selection improves inference efficiency while preserving quality.

entry.title: Where to Look Matters: On-Policy Self-Distillation for Long-Video Understanding

author.name: Kaishen Wang, Dongdi Zhao, Yijun Liang, Dingqiang Ye, Ruibo Chen, Heng Huang, Di Fu

entry.summary: Empirically shows that focusing VLM visual input on short question-relevant clue intervals beats full-video sampling across model scales with fewer frames, and introduces Clue-OPSD, a clue-privileged on-policy self-distillation framework for long-video understanding that teaches models where to look.

entry.title: Efficient Training with Foresight: Multi-Token Auxiliary Supervision for Autoregressive Image Generation

author.name: Guo Niu, Xiongfei Yao, Teng Wang, Nannan Zhu

entry.summary: Proposes MTAR, a unified training framework for autoregressive image generation introducing multi-token prediction to alleviate sparse, myopic next-token supervision, plus representation regularization and efficiency gains over dense full-sequence computation.

entry.title: PAGS: Autofocusing Photoacoustic Tomography via Speed-of-Sound-Adaptive Gaussian Splatting

author.name: Jiarui Ge, Jintao Ma, Bangxu Fan, Jinyan Zhang, Xiaokang Yang, Shuai Na, Xiaoyun Yuan

entry.summary: Proposes PAGS, a differentiable framework for blind autofocusing in photoacoustic computed tomography via speed-of-sound-adaptive Gaussian splatting, representing the pressure field with sparse Gaussian sources and a compact compensation field instead of dense medium recovery, addressing defocusing from SoS heterogeneity.

entry.title: AdaVDR: Adaptive Tool Use and Reflection for Video Deep Research

author.name: Xintong Zhang, Xiaomeng Fan, Shilin Yan, Ekko He, Zicheng Liu, Zijian Zou, Guannan Zhang, Yuwei Wu, Zhi Gao, Hongwei Xue

entry.summary: AdaVDR is an adaptive agent for video deep research that selects tools based on task requirements and backtracks only when intermediate results appear unreliable, reducing unnecessary costly interactions. It also introduces a data pipeline for training such agents. The work sits at the intersection of video understanding, agentic tool use, and retrieval-augmented reasoning.

entry.title: AI helps design new materials that work in the real world

author.name: Zach Winn | MIT News

entry.summary: MIT researchers developed CrysVCD, a framework published in Nature Computational Science that enforces valence and chemical-stability constraints before generative materials design, vastly improving the stability rate of AI-generated candidate materials versus post-hoc screening. Addresses the translation gap between generative materials proposals and industrially usable stable materials.

entry.title: Gated Activation Steering for Reducing Sycophancy & Hallucination in Medical Question Answering

author.name: Himanshu Tripathi, Subash Neupane, Shaswata Mitra, Sudip Mittal, Noorbakhsh Amiri Golilarz, Shahram Rahimi

entry.summary: This work proposes gated activation steering that selectively intervenes on LLM internal activations to reduce sycophancy and hallucination in medical question answering, avoiding the degradation caused by always-on steering or prompt-only safeguards. It addresses both failure modes in a single framework while preserving already-correct responses.

entry.title: SyPS: Measuring Sycophancy Prompt Sensitivity in Large Language Models

author.name: Lijia Huang, Yao Fu, Sihao Ren

entry.summary: SyPS measures sycophancy prompt sensitivity, testing whether sycophantic behavior is stable when the same situation is presented with varying user confidence, emotional framing, social consensus, or validation-seeking language. It extends fixed-prompt sycophancy evaluations with controlled counterfactual prompt variants.

entry.title: Quantifying System-Level Harms from AI Adoption in Complex Sociotechnical Systems

author.name: Paul Vautravers, Oliver Chalkley, Gabriel Downer, Kate S, Damian Ruck

entry.summary: This paper proposes a framework linking structured hazard analysis, component-level AI testing, and probabilistic system modeling to quantify how model-level failures translate into system-level harms in sociotechnical systems such as critical national infrastructure. It provides a traceable path from model behavior to systemic impact.

entry.title: OmniJudge or OmniBias? Diagnosing Multimodal Judges through Balanced, Decoupled Lenses

author.name: Guangzheng Hu, Ziyue Jiang, Weixu Qiao, Lixin Zhang, Jianye Kang, Yuru Wu, Rong Bao, Niantong Li, Wei Wang, Ziyi Cheng, Xinfa Zhu, HangRui Hu, Ting He, Bing Zhao, Lin Qu, Hu Wei, Jin Xu

entry.summary: D3-Omni is a balanced, decoupled benchmark diagnosing multimodal judges across text-to-image, text-to-video, and text-to-speech scoring, with 53 orthogonal binary dimensions and 10,671 samples designed to avoid positive-example bias and conflated failure modes. It reveals capability gaps in OmniJudge models that aggregate scores hide.

entry.title: OPDSearch+: On-Policy Distillation with RL Refinement for Search-Augmented Reasoning

author.name: Qinglin Ye, Zhiyuan Gu, Jingjie Xia, Yiheng Zhang, Kaiyan Zhao, Shunchao Zheng, Yuhang Mu, Wenchao Du, Yiming Wang

entry.summary: OPDSearch+ is the first on-policy distillation paradigm for search-augmented reasoning that requires no teacher fine-tuning, combining on-policy distillation with RL refinement to overcome data cost, teacher performance ceilings, and training instability. It targets making multi-turn search reasoning feasible for small language models.

entry.title: PhysMLLMs: Spatial Priors for Unified Referring Segmentation and Grounded Reasoning of Images and Videos

author.name: Siyao Yan, Bo Han, Jisheng Dang, Bimei Wang, Shude Wang, Hong Peng, Yulan Guo, Jianhuang Lai, Bin Hu, Tat-SengChua

entry.summary: PhysMLLMs injects physics-inspired spatial continuity priors into video MLLMs during training, aligning student global visual representations with a frozen teacher to stabilize object-centered representations over time. The goal is to reduce spatiotemporal inconsistencies such as jitter, drift, and identity switches in referring segmentation, especially under occlusion and similar distractors. It targets a documented weakness of current video MLLMs.

entry.title: RACE: Scalable Statistical Estimation of Functional Consistency in LLM Neurons
