author.name: Runyu Wang, Bo Liu, Xiaxin Zhang, Yu Han, Jiawei Cao, Xiaoye Zhang, Zhe Zhang, Yifan Yang, Peng Ping

entry.summary: RACE is a forward-pass statistical framework for estimating domain-wide functional consistency of transformer neurons, avoiding the cost of instance-level point estimates or expensive per-neuron procedures. Perturbation experiments show better domain specificity than gradient-based estimates, and its computational profile supports scalable analysis. It contributes a practical tool to mechanistic interpretability at scale.

entry.title: STAIN-FL: Stealthy Targeted Attack Injection with Contextual Triggers in Federated Learning

author.name: Ashlinder Kaur, Purnima Murali Mohan, Zengxiang Li, Tram Truong-Huu

entry.summary: STAIN-FL is a stealthy targeted backdoor attack on federated video anomaly detection that uses natural surveillance conditions like low light and crowd density as contextual triggers, combining label manipulation with gradient masking. It preserves clean accuracy while inducing trigger-conditioned misclassification in non-IID settings.

entry.title: Evaluating Language Models on Cross-Language Code Functional Equivalence

author.name: Hui Sun, Anderson Uch\^oa, Rohit Gheyi, Wesley K. G. Assun\c{c}\~ao

entry.summary: Introduces PolyHuman, a dataset of human-written programs in C++, Java, and Python, and evaluates whether LLMs can judge functional equivalence across languages. Results probe whether code models perform genuine semantic reasoning rather than superficial pattern matching.

entry.title: Hybrid Semantic Tool Discovery for Enterprise MCP Gateway: Architecture and Implementation

author.name: Olympia Saha, Amy Wang, Srinivasan Manoharan

entry.summary: Presents a hybrid semantic tool discovery architecture for an enterprise MCP gateway aggregating thousands of tools, addressing context-window saturation and tool discoverability through selective schema surfacing. The design provides a governable chokepoint for authentication, policy, and observability.

entry.title: VisCache: Visual KV Cache Pruning for Efficient Vision Large Language Model Inference

author.name: Lyuke Wang, Zhuo Li, Guangxu Zhu

entry.summary: VisCache is a plug-and-play, training-free visual KV cache pruning framework with two stages: a lightweight VLM filters temporal redundancy by forwarding informative keyframes, followed by coarse-to-fine pruning that avoids uniform token and layer cuts. It targets the memory and compute cost of long-context vision-language inference.

entry.title: Across the Loss Landscape with Progressive Growth

author.name: Paul Caillon, Christophe Cerisara, Alexandre Allauzen

entry.summary: Analyzes how incremental grow-and-optimize training biases networks toward flatter minima by viewing growth as progressive constraint relaxation, proving under local regularity conditions that local sublevel sets are well approximated during nested subspace expansion.

entry.title: The Von-Neumann State-Space Transformer for neural decoding

author.name: Morteza Sarafyazd

entry.summary: Proposes the von-Neumann State-Space Transformer for neural decoding, where a controller executes token-specific operators rather than blending expert outputs, motivated by the low-dimensionality of cortical computation and aimed at sample efficiency.

entry.title: When Does Context Routing Help? A Systematic Study of Multi-Modal Fusion in Time Series Forecasting

author.name: Ruizhe Zhou, Gaoyuan Du, Xiaoyang Liu, Haoqi Yao, Deepayan Chakrabarti, Jiating Lin, Yixuan Shen

entry.summary: Identifies two dataset-level conditions determining when auxiliary context can help time series forecasting: the target must not be dominated by last-value shortcuts, and the context must carry conditional mutual information about the target, with a distribution-free impossibility result when delta equals zero.

entry.title: Rethinking the Transferable Adversarial Attacks and Robust Defense in Federated Learning

author.name: Zuobin Xiong, Deval Mukherjee, Homook Cho, Wei Li

entry.summary: Analyzes transferability of adversarial examples across client models in federated learning, showing existing poisoning and Byzantine attacks penetrate poorly in realistic settings and proposing transfer-based adversarial attack and defense analysis.

entry.title: Interpreting Protein Language Model Embeddings via Orthogonal Projection for Protein Fitness Prediction

author.name: Paulo Yanez Sarmiento, Pia Francesca Rissom, Manuel Pfeuffer, Marco Simnacher, Jordan F. Safer, Sumaiya Iqbal, Henrike O. Heyne, Nadja Klein, Bernhard Y. Renard

entry.summary: Applies orthogonal projection removing linear, high-order, and interaction effects of known biochemical features from protein language model embeddings to interpret what drives fitness predictions.

entry.title: DCEO: Direct Causal Effect Optimization for Long-Term User Value Modeling in E-commerce Search

author.name: Junzhao Zhang, Tao Zhang, Liren Yu, Feiyi Dong, Zhixuan Zhang, Dan Ou, Haihong Tang

entry.summary: DCEO replaces hand-tuned multi-objective fusion weights in industrial e-commerce search with direct causal effect optimization of user-level long-term objectives such as cumulative purchases and GMV, bridging the item-request to user-level granularity gap.

entry.title: Fairness-Aware Test-Time Prompt Tuning

author.name: Yoann Launay, Parameswaran Kamalaruban, Tom Kempton, Stuart Burrell, David Sutton

entry.summary: Studies how episodic test-time adaptation via prompt tuning affects fairness of CLIP-style vision-language models under subpopulation shifts, without retraining or demographic attribute access. It offers a practical fairness lever for deployed foundation models where fine-tuning is infeasible. Bridges test-time adaptation and algorithmic fairness.

entry.title: Canalization Before Generalization: Grokking as a Dynamical Probe

author.name: Yiming Lin

entry.summary: Uses short weight-decay pulses during the grokking plateau as a dynamical probe, showing that pulse-induced shifts in generalization time form a stable dose ordering that emerges before visible generalization. Interprets grokking through the lens of canalization, suggesting the network commits to generalizing solutions before test loss reflects it. Adds mechanistic insight into an enduring mystery.

entry.title: CEDAR: Controlled and Event-Driven Demand Forecasting via Residual Decomposition

author.name: Junjie Meng, Ranxu Zhang, Zi-an Zhang, Shujun Liu, Xiaoning Qi, Xiaozhou Xu, Yanyong Zhang, Hui Xiong, Chao Wang

entry.summary: Proposes CEDAR, a controlled and event-driven demand forecasting method with residual decomposition that supports what-if evaluation under future merchant action sequences, addressing autoregressive inertia and policy-insensitive rollouts in passive time series forecasters. Targets large-scale e-commerce planning where counterfactual analysis matters. Industrial-scale problem with practical framing.

entry.title: A meta-algorithm for ab initio reconstruction of complex mixtures in cryo-EM

author.name: Alkin Kaz, Arda Kaz, Ellen D. Zhong

entry.summary: Describes a meta-algorithm for spawning and aggregating multi-class cryo-EM reconstruction jobs, formalizing ad hoc iterative classification and filtering, and reports the first successful ab initio reconstruction on datasets with dozens of distinct species (97 percent accuracy on a 45-class subset of Tomotwin-100, 75 percent on the full dataset). Capability scales with compute and enables automated cryo-EM analysis. From a strong cryo-EM ML group.

entry.title: A Hierarchical Synergistic Deep Learning Framework Integrating Composition, Structure, and Ionic Transport for Solid-State Electrolyte Discovery

author.name: Hongwei Du, Dingyang Lv, Baole Wei, Yongheng Li, Feng Yu, Ziheng Lu, Siqi Shi, Hong Wang

entry.summary: Develops a hierarchical deep-learning framework for discovering inorganic solid-state electrolytes, coordinating compositional and structural expert models (L-G-DCNN, multi-fidelity DenseGNN) with ionic-transport prediction for multi-objective screening. It targets data heterogeneity and scarce kinetic transport data across vast chemical spaces.

entry.title: MeMark: Membrane-Space Watermarking for Spiking Neural Networks

author.name: Roberto Ria\~no, Gorka Abad, Stjepan Picek, Aitor Urbieta

entry.summary: MeMark embeds multi-bit ownership watermarks in the internal membrane state of LIF neurons in spiking neural networks, verifiable through the firing threshold itself, so that replacing the output head does not remove evidence. Designed for the checkpoint-reuse threat model that existing output-verified SNN watermarks fail.

entry.title: Skill Issue: Are Skills Language-Invariant in LLMs?

author.name: Bobby Cheng, Adam Gaber, Zhengyuan Liu, Catherine Arnett, Omer Goldman, Cheston Tan, Leshem Choshen

entry.summary: Quantifies cross-lingual skill inconsistency in LLMs via multilingual self-play in text games: two instances of the same model compete through different language interfaces, isolating language effects while fixing model, opponent, rules, and actions. Builds a multilingual TextArena extension and evaluates three open-weight models across eight languages.

entry.title: MetaSieve: Faster Relational Deep Learning through SQL-Based Metapath Selection

author.name: Fahim Shahriar Khan, Ashraf Aboulnaga

entry.summary: MetaSieve accelerates relational deep learning by using SQL joins and aggregations to prune metapaths from GNN subgraph sampling without accuracy loss, reducing training cost driven by subgraph size. Bridges database system capabilities with graph neural network training over multi-table databases.

entry.title: MyoMechanix: Biomechanically-Grounded Compositional Skilled Activity Understanding and Coaching

author.name: Hao Yin, Paritosh Parmar, Lijun Gu, Lin Xu, Tianxiao Guo, Xiujin Liu, Tianyou Zheng, Yang Zhang, Weiwei Fu

entry.summary: MyoMechanix is a large multimodal action-quality-assessment ecosystem: 7,500+ expert-annotated samples of 20 weight-loaded actions from 38 subjects with synchronized multiview RGB, 3D pose, and sEMG, plus a Fitness Knowledge Graph for biomechanically grounded coaching feedback. Largest multimodal AQA benchmark to date.

entry.title: Less can be More: Relieving RAG Bottlenecks via Evidence Frontloading and Pressure-Adaptive Budgeting

author.name: Weibin Cai, Reza Zafarani

entry.summary: Empirically characterizes how the RAG bottleneck shifts between upstream reranking and downstream generation under different loads and budgets, then proposes PACE: evidence frontloading with pressure-adaptive budgeting that reduces reranking cost without dropping supporting evidence. Shows reranking can dominate under high query rates.

entry.title: Routed Graph Handoff: Adaptive Format Selection for Multi-Agent LLM Delegation

author.name: Pratyay Banerjee, Ankit Chadha

entry.summary: Routed Graph Handoff uses a lightweight router (155 tokens, 0.15% overhead) to choose between typed dependency graphs and natural language for each multi-agent delegation, matching or beating NL-only across four benchmarks with up to 3.2x compression. Shows graph-only delegation regresses badly, motivating adaptive format selection.

entry.title: Provenance Before Prose: Claim-Locked Reporting

author.name: Xiao Fan, Jingyuan Li, Hongbin Guo, Yubo Han, Yi Zhang

entry.summary: Frames statistical-report failures (drifting numbers, inverted effect directions) as a control problem and proposes claim-locked reporting where evidence-bearing content is fixed by structured statistical results before prose generation. Uses cross-run reproducibility to stress-test binding, showing hybrid templates reproduce only 61.1% of report-visible numbers.

entry.title: Adaptive Triggering for Bias Correction in LLM Reasoning

author.name: Nayoung Kim, Mickey Mancenido, Huan Liu

entry.summary: Formulates when to intervene on biased chain-of-thought as an online change-point detection problem: a per-step bias signal triggers adaptive correction, avoiding both late intervention (biased reasoning propagates) and unnecessary disruption. Targets demographic stereotypes amplified during reasoning generation.

entry.title: DCGC: Draft-Conditioned Global Correction for Complex Reasoning with Masked Diffusion Models

author.name: Minhae Oh, Nakyung Lee, Jungwoo Lee

entry.summary: DCGC uses masked diffusion models for global correction of flawed reasoning traces, conditioning on an imperfect upstream draft and combining task-specific SFT with Dynamic Dual-CFG, which scales draft-conditioned residuals by a relative confidence gap. Outperforms standard sampling and simpler CFG variants across math, code, and knowledge tasks.

entry.title: Unmatched Does Not Mean False: Incomplete Reference Sets Can Reverse Calibration Rankings in Open-Ended Theory-of-Mind Tracking

author.name: Zhexi Feng, Wuxi Chen, Bingrui Zhang

entry.summary: Shows that finite reference sets can reverse calibration and model-selection rankings in open-ended theory-of-mind tracking: recoding references shifts weighted prevalence from 0.783 to 0.295 and flips Brier-risk orderings, with an analogous reversal demonstrated in a released question-answering pipeline. Warns that unmatched-does-not-mean-false evaluation flaws distort leaderboards.

entry.title: Reconstructing the Right Episode: Evaluating Interleaved Conversational Memory Beyond Long Context

author.name: Zhexi Feng, Ruiyi Zhang, Yongbo Yang, Pengtao Xie

entry.summary: Introduces SCALE-QA, a constraint-grounded benchmark of 3,000 audited questions over flat, unsegmented multi-topic chat threads, targeting episode-integrity failure where an assistant must infer which earlier conversation episode validates a later decision. Includes deterministic grading and a runtime thread builder.

entry.title: MoganBert-TR: A Turkish Encoder Foundation Model Trained from Scratch with a CLM-to-MLM Curriculum

author.name: Furkan Yilmaz, Habibe Aleyna Tasdemir, Muhammed Faruk Gozay

entry.summary: Introduces MoganBert-TR, a 149M-parameter Turkish encoder trained from scratch on 237B tokens with a two-stage CLM-to-MLM curriculum inside a WSD schedule. The controlled ablation shows 2.7-3.7x gains on Turkish MS MARCO retrieval over pure MLM, attributed to embedding geometry changes.

entry.title: Query-Side Attacks on GNN-Based KGQA: Tracing Failures from Entity Linking to Answer Generation

author.name: Pankaj Kumar, Subhankar Mishra

entry.summary: Introduces a stage-isolation protocol for attacking GNN-based knowledge graph QA pipelines, with two answer-preserving adversarial perturbations that target distinct stages from entity linking to answer generation. This reveals which stage fails and why, which end-to-end robustness metrics conflate.

entry.title: Distinct dynamics of conceptual and referential disruptions in human reading and large language model processing

author.name: Rui He, Nihal Altay, Wolfram Hinzen

entry.summary: Compares how humans and LLMs process conceptual versus referential meaning disruptions in short narratives, using self-paced reading for humans and predictive/representational analysis for models. Finds distinct temporal dynamics: conceptual disruptions cause strong localized costs while referential disruptions produce weaker, gradually declining effects.

entry.title: The "Curse of Knowledge" in LLM Query Simulation: Concept Provenance for Tracing Answer-Side Intrusion

author.name: Chenglong Ma, Xinye Wanyan, Danula Hettiachchi, Ziqi Xu, Jeffrey Chan

entry.summary: Introduces concept provenance, a framework for detecting answer-side intrusion in LLM-generated search queries used for IR evaluation: query concepts are assigned to backstory-supported, human-central, human-tail, or candidate answer-side zones, exposing when simulated queries presuppose document knowledge unavailable to real pre-search users. Applied to 77,004 queries across 8 LLMs.

entry.title: FinRiskAtlas: Decision-Aligned Evaluation of Large Language Models for Financial Risk Review

author.name: Suyang Zhong, Jingzhe Zhu, Qi Xu, Liyao Sun, Yin Wang, Qingqing Sun, Shuai Chen, Tianyi Zhang

entry.summary: Introduces FinRiskAtlas, a Chinese-language benchmark evaluating financial LLMs along two deployment-aligned dimensions: operation execution under fixed evidence states and evidence-state control under evolving review conditions. Organizes evaluation around the decisions systems must support rather than datasets or task formulations.

entry.title: Learning What to Share and What to Personalize: Hierarchical Strategy Co-Evolution for Agent Memory

author.name: Yupeng Han, Shuochen Liu, Kai Zhang, Ze Liu, Zhihong Pan, Xianquan Wang

entry.summary: Proposes HiPS, a hierarchical framework decoupling agent memory management into what to share versus what to personalize, replacing static one-size-fits-all memory strategies with user-specific policies that co-evolve with the agent's policy during training. Targets compact user profiles for consistent long-conversation personalization.

entry.title: CaSKG: Counterfactual-Causal Skill Graphs for Scalable Agent Skill Retrieval

author.name: Zhiyuan Li, Linyuan Gao, Xuechun Ding, Hongwei Chen, Yuan Wu, Yi Chang

entry.summary: Proposes CaSKG, a counterfactual-causal skill graph framework that calibrates procedural relations in reusable LLM agent skill libraries before retrieval. Builds a high-recall candidate graph from semantic, lexical, input/output, and structural evidence, refined by repair evidence and an optional LLM judge.

entry.title: What Do Audio-Visual Synchronization Metrics Actually Measure?

author.name: Jai Kumar Sharma, Peeyush Tapadiya

entry.summary: Jointly audits four widely used audio-visual synchronization metrics under a common reliability protocol including controlled-distortion monotonicity, preprocessing sensitivity, and rank uncertainty. Finds an axis split rather than a single winner: metrics disagree sharply (Krippendorff alpha near 0.06) and measure different constructs.

entry.title: What Do Medical Vision-Language Models Learn in Radiology? Transfer, Alignment, and Source-Proxy Leakage Under Distribution Shift

author.name: Ayoub Louaye Bouaziz, Lokmane Chebouba, Yassine Himeur

entry.summary: Studies what medical vision-language models learn in radiology under distribution shift, isolating visual transfer, multimodal alignment under strict pair-index retrieval, and metadata-derived source-proxy information retained in frozen embeddings. Shows self-supervised visual initialization improves cross-dataset transfer and quantifies proxy leakage.

entry.title: FlashNormal: Detailed Surface Normal Estimation from Flash and No-Flash Images

author.name: Ruiyang Chen, Feiran Li, Heng Guo, Zhanyu Ma

entry.summary: Proposes FlashNormal, a diffusion-based surface normal estimator from flash/no-flash image pairs captured on modern smartphones, exploiting flash-induced shading variations and curvature-guided detail recovery. Bridges single-image practicality and photometric stereo fidelity.

entry.title: SeVeR: Selective Visual Exposure and Retrieval for 3D Medical Image Question Answering

author.name: Yaojun Hu, Danyang Tu, Yang Liu, Jiajin Zhang, Wei Fang, Zhiqiang Liu, Chunlai Dong, Yingda Xia, Haochao Ying, Jian Wu, Ling Zhang

entry.summary: SeVeR introduces BreMRIs-VQA, a clinically curated breast MRI benchmark with 1.19M QA pairs across 71K multi-sequence volumes, and a selective visual exposure framework that compresses dense volumes into modality-wise prototypes with change-aware gated attention. It targets reasoning under heavy multi-sequence visual redundancy in 3D medical VQA. A substantial dataset plus a tailored method.

entry.title: Diffusion Transformers for Roof Graph Synthesis and Reconstruction

author.name: Daniel Panangian, Ksenia Bittner

entry.summary: This paper compares autoregressive coordinate emission versus detection-based heatmap readouts from the same trained network for floorplan vectorization, finding detection superior on real scans (+2.7 to +5.1 wall F1) while sequence decoding wins on clean vector renders. It also shows a heatmap the decoder never used boosts opening detection 2.6x without retraining. A careful, statistically grounded analysis of representation and readout design.

entry.title: MA-VLA: Multi-Arm Vision-Language-Action Model for Collaboration and Compositional Generalization

author.name: Zaibin Zhang, Junlan Xiao, Zhongbo Zhang, Yifan Wang, Li Kang, Yiran Qin, Changxing Xia, Heng Zhou, Talas Fu, Enshen Zhou, Ruimao Zhang, Zhenfei Yin, Huchuan Lu, Lijun Wang

entry.summary: MA-VLA extends vision-language-action models to multi-arm collaboration by decomposing cooperative behavior into mid-level atomic prompts allocated to individual arms, enabling explicit subgoal specification and compositional generalization across tasks. It addresses the limitation of single global instructions in current VLA models.

entry.title: We need more empirical research on biological AI model safety

author.name: Noga Aharony

entry.summary: Argues that biological AI models (protein, genomic, single-cell) enabling biological design create biorisk scenarios that lack empirical safety research, and proposes research questions while explicitly soliciting critique including information-hazard and capability-externality concerns. A research-agenda pitch for biological AI model safety.

entry.title: When Seeing Is Not Enough: Benchmarking Interactive Visual Grounding in LVLMs

author.name: Zhengxiang Wang, Owen Rambow

entry.summary: Placeholder note: item 40 introduces a controlled evaluation framework for interactive visual grounding in LVLMs, varying how much target information is given upfront versus acquired through dialogue across four human-grounded contexts and interaction protocols. Current LVLMs perform significantly below human baselines, with interaction helping when follow-ups refine ambiguous references.

entry.title: Task-Adaptive Rubrics for GUI Reward Modeling

author.name: Tao Xiong, Xavier Hu, Wenkai Wang, Qinzhuo Wu, Changqiao Wu, Pengzhi Gao, Wei Liu, Jian Luan, Shengyu Zhang

entry.summary: AdaptRubric constructs task-adaptive judging criteria for GUI agent reward modeling via a coarse-to-fine rubric framework, fixing under-specified, overly strict, or transferred checks in existing GUI reward verifiers. It improves outcome reward assignment for trajectory-level success judgment.

entry.title: Exploit More, Explore Smarter for Budget-Constrained Agentic Search

author.name: Haoyang Fang, Bernie Wang

entry.summary: ExTS is a tree-search policy for budget-constrained agentic search that treats expansion as a value-of-information decision, combining discriminative reward shaping, a stochastic virtual child estimating branch value, and quality-dependent branching. It fixes known pathologies of standard MCTS under small evaluation budgets.

entry.title: Evaluating Multiple LLM Generations with Validated Task Coverage

author.name: Florian Le Bronnec, Rio Yokota

entry.summary: VTC-Bench introduces Validated Task Coverage, a metric and five-domain benchmark measuring how many genuinely distinct useful results a set of LLM generations contains, using automatic reproducible checks without model-based judges. It addresses the gap where evaluation collapses multiple samples to a single success.

entry.title: SelfGraphRAG: Bridging the Supervision Gap in Graph-Based RAG with Synthetic QA Generation

author.name: Ben Lagnese, Manas Gaur

entry.summary: SelfGraphRAG generates question-answer pairs directly from knowledge-graph structure to train a query-conditioned graph retriever, providing relational supervision (multi-hop paths, local neighborhoods) without manual annotation. Targets the supervision gap in graph-based RAG for newly constructed graphs.

entry.title: GRIP: Granular Reward-Guided Parameter Interpolation for Efficient Reasoning

author.name: Lam So, Canhui Wu, Han Lin

entry.summary: GRIP proposes reward-guided interpolation of parameters between a reasoning model and an instruction-tuned model with identical architectures, assigning learnable per-module interpolation ratios to trade accuracy against chain-of-thought cost. Avoids full retraining while mitigating the accuracy-efficiency mismatch.

entry.title: From Specialization to Generalization: Instruction-tuned LLMs for Robust Harmful Content Mitigation

author.name: Lukas Edman, Daryna Dementieva, Alexander Fraser

entry.summary: Unifies 36 English hate speech datasets with heterogeneous labeling schemes to instruction-tune a Qwen3-based generalist LLM for robust harmful-content mitigation, showing instruction tuning yields stronger generalization than specialized encoder classifiers. Revisits the claim that LLMs underperform BERT variants on hate speech.

entry.title: AutoVerifier: Residual-Guided Non-Parametric Optimization for Reference-Based Answer Verification

author.name: Zebei Zhao, Zhihao Shi, Minqi Shi

entry.summary: AutoVerifier treats implicit assumptions in answer-equivalence checking as verifier inductive biases and learns them from recurring errors via residual-guided non-parametric optimization, recording biases in rule cards applied at verification time. Improves reference-based verification used for RLVR outcome rewards and reasoning-model evaluation.

entry.title: Beyond Local Surprise: Grounded Dialogue as Selective Belief Revision under Referential Uncertainty

author.name: Ziming Liu, Bhanu Chaitanya Jasti, Ziyang Xu, Hongyu Wu, Yi Wu, Jiqun Liu

entry.summary: Studies grounded dialogue under referential uncertainty as a turn-by-turn preserve-or-revise belief updating problem, introducing a controlled data-driven framework that learns competing theory-driven revision strategies under identical conditions. Finds conversation understanding may be more conservative than local-mismatch-based updating.

entry.title: RefLAM: A Reference-Grounded Line Annotation Pipeline for Historical Arabic Manuscripts

author.name: Mohamed Guechaoui, Mohamed Diaa Zellagui, Souleyman Chaib, Sahraoui Dhelim

entry.summary: Introduces RefLAM, a pipeline converting historical Arabic manuscript page images and clean transcriptions into validated line-level HTR ground truth, coupling page segmentation, MLLM-based structured OCR, and diacritic-agnostic fuzzy alignment with a correctness guarantee and human oversight for two-zone manuscript layouts.

entry.title: On the Separation of Human and AI-Generated Images in CLIP Embedding Space

author.name: Andrea Asperti

entry.summary: The paper reports that human and AI-generated paintings spontaneously separate along dominant principal directions of CLIP embedding space without any supervised objective, then investigates what visual information drives the separation via interpretable representations and gradient-based inversion. Rather than building a detector, the emphasis is on interpretation. A curiosity-driven finding with implications for provenance and data curation.

entry.title: SonicNudge: Controlled Displacement of Hovering UAVs via Estimator-Controller Coupling

author.name: Shaocheng Luo, Ashir Raza, Haocheng Meng, David Hunt, Miroslav Pajic

entry.summary: SonicNudge introduces a new attack primitive showing that ultrasonic perturbation of a UAV gyroscope can persist as an attitude-estimation bias that the flight controller converts into a controlled displacement of the hover point, exploiting estimator-controller coupling. Relevant to station-keeping and precision alignment tasks such as delivery and inspection.

entry.title: TRACE: Transition-Aware Residual Control for Multi-Objective Materials Discovery

author.name: Kang Zhou, Yujia Tong, Yong Tao, Jingling Yuan

entry.summary: TRACE is a transition-aware framework for multi-objective materials discovery with LLM agents that records parent-edit-child transitions with property deltas rather than just evaluated candidates and scores. Aggregating transition evidence helps agents learn which executable edits caused useful changes when objectives compete.

entry.title: Generating Biomedical Fact-Checking Reports with RL-Enhanced Agentic Search

author.name: Jiongxiao Wang, Dingli Ma, Chaoqun Ni

entry.summary: BioCheck Agent generates structured biomedical fact-checking reports using an RL-enhanced agentic search pipeline, moving beyond isolated prediction labels from retrieve-then-verify RAG toward comprehensive, human-readable justifications. It targets reliability of public health information.

entry.title: In-Context Inpainting for Time Series Forecasting

author.name: Thang Nguyen, Dung Nguyen, Romero Morais, Truyen Tran

entry.summary: ICI-Time reframes time series forecasting as visual inpainting, converting series into structured area charts and applying visual in-context learning with pre-trained vision transformers, without fine-tuning or new temporal architectures. It reports an invertible numerical-visual mapping and experiments across epidemiological and other domains.

entry.title: More GPUs or a Smaller Cache? Tensor Parallelism versus KV Compression for Memory-Bound LLM Serving

author.name: Srikanta Datta Tumkur, Mehar Simhadri, Anshu Bansal, Jay Iyer, Sai Pavan Kumar, Sai Kapil Kumar, Ramesh Nampelly, Raj Dandekar

entry.summary: This systems study places tensor parallelism (degree 1 to 8) and KV-cache compression (16/8/4-bit, various keep-ratios) on a single cost-normalized axis for memory-bound LLM serving, quantifying the tradeoff between buying memory headroom with more GPUs versus shrinking the cache in place. It fills a gap where the two communities rarely compare directly.

entry.title: Memory Is Not Always Needed: Characterizing Conditional Memory in Scientific Reasoning

author.name: Zhen Bi, Xueshu Chen, Yan Wang, Zhizhi Peng, Haosen Hong, Zhen Wang, Zhixuan Chu, Bingyu Zhu, Jungang Lou

entry.summary: This work systematically characterizes when conditional memory (explicit lookup pathways) helps or hurts scientific reasoning in language models, showing that retrieved knowledge can repair missing associations but also introduce shortcuts or interfere with reasoning the base model already performs correctly. It maps the knowledge boundary via controlled interventions on memory-enabled circuits.

entry.title: Diverse by Reasoning: Harnessing the Wisdom of LLM Crowds for Future Prediction

author.name: Nirupam Chetlapalli, Yiming Liao, Min-Chun Chen, Keke Chen

entry.summary: This paper proposes a behavior-aware framework for constructing diverse LLM crowds for future prediction, characterizing models by reasoning traces on development tasks, clustering by behavioral similarity, and selecting representatives. Across 25 LLMs it shows crowd composition, not just size, determines wisdom-of-crowd performance.

entry.title: Reflection with Action-Induced Visual Differences for Desktop GUI Agents

author.name: Yijie Ma, Chaoyue Niu, Fan Wu, Guihai Chen

entry.summary: EFR is a two-stage reflector for desktop GUI agents that decouples explicit extraction of action-induced visual differences from outcome verification, addressing the weak grounding when reflectors collapse change detection and judgment into one step on dense interfaces. It improves the Planner-Operator-Reflector architecture.

entry.title: EMRB: A Multi-Level Benchmark for Evaluating LLM Reasoning over Raw Electromagnetic Signals

author.name: Mingxu Zhang, Ying Sun, Yuhan Li, Yang Ji, Dazhong Shen, Ke Zhang, Shan Huang

entry.summary: EMRB evaluates whether LLMs can analyze raw electromagnetic I/Q data by writing and running code, with 200 problems across five difficulty levels and 27 question types from signal detection to OFDM design, using verified ground truth and only raw captures. It tests a gap left by benchmarks built on preprocessed features, evaluating 14 LLMs.

entry.title: Scalable Question-Centric Text-to-Image Evaluation: Reliable Ranking, Fine-Grained Diagnosis, and Cost-Aware Routing

author.name: Shaoan Zhao, Fang Zhao, Xueqiang Guo, Xinpei Su, Huanlin Gao, Qiang Hui, Ting Lu, Fuyuan Shi, Chao Tan, Bikun Yang, Kai Wang, Shiguo Lian

entry.summary: QC-T2I-Bench converts open text-to-image prompts into attributed atomic questions organized with Davidsonian Scene Graphs, using hierarchy-constrained aggregation so prerequisite failures exclude downstream questions and prevent simple and complex prompts from being conflated. It supports reliable ranking, fine-grained diagnosis, and cost-aware judge routing for T2I evaluation.

entry.title: Mahalanobis-Based Multi-Head Attention for Complex State Propagation

author.name: Xiaohe Li

entry.summary: MHA-CSP replaces standard dot-product attention with a Mahalanobis distance-based RBF kernel, computing attention in an implicit infinite-dimensional feature space without extra parameters, and directly constructs Tree Attention from accumulated distances with a LogSumExp correction. The distance matrices are also repurposed for an attention meshing mechanism for complex state propagation. It is a creative rethinking of the attention primitive.

entry.title: Confident at the moment of action: belief miscalibration in LLM play under hidden information

author.name: Bhushan Kashinath Joshi

entry.summary: This paper tests whether LLM stated confidence tracks correctness at the moment of action in a hidden-information chess variant where the royal piece can be secretly relocated. High-confidence captures about the hidden piece location were correct in only 1 of 62 cases, with the calibration deficit concentrated almost entirely in these action-time events. It provides a clean, adversarial demonstration of action-time miscalibration in agentic confidence gating.

entry.title: Lifted Model Construction under Approximate Commutativity

author.name: Malte Luttermann, Jan Speller, Tanya Braun, Marcel Gehrke, Ralf M\"oller

entry.summary: The paper introduces epsilon-commutativity, a relaxation of exact factor commutativity for lifted probabilistic inference, addressing the fact that parameters learned from data are never exactly permutation-invariant. It enables lifted model construction under approximate symmetry. This makes lifted inference more robust for realistic learned models.

entry.title: FedV-KGQA: Multi-Hop Question Answering over Vertically Partitioned Knowledge Graphs

author.name: Md Saikat Islam Khan Bappy, Oshani Seneviratne

entry.summary: FedV-KGQA enables multi-hop question answering over vertically partitioned knowledge graphs where organizations share entities but own disjoint relation sets, combining local graph enrichment with KG embeddings so raw triples never leave each silo. It adds a topic entity anchoring mechanism for cross-silo reasoning. This addresses realistic data-sovereignty constraints on multi-hop KG reasoning.

entry.title: Progressively Learning Heterogeneous Skills in a Unified Latent Space

author.name: Yue-Yi Zhang, Ming Gong, Linpu He, Wei-Shi Zheng, Zhilin Zhao

entry.summary: HetSkills progressively learns heterogeneous skills for physics-based character control within a unified latent space treated as a shared executable interface, integrating skills from diverse data sources and supervision forms. It learns a reusable motion decoder and introduces motion intuition distillation to prevent text-to-motion shortcuts. This unifies skill acquisition for embodied character animation.

entry.title: REFINE: A Multi-Agent LLM Approach for Evidence-Guided Code Refactoring

author.name: Muhammad Waseem, Aakash Ahmad, Pekka Abrahamsson

entry.summary: REFINE is a tool-agnostic, evidence-aware multi-agent approach for Java code refactoring that combines static-analysis-guided smell identification, smell-informed planning, LLM transformation, automated re-analysis, preservation checks, and structured reporting. It is evaluated on 450 Java files from 15 open-source systems using 1,350 model passes with models including GPT-5.5 and Gemini. It offers a structured pipeline for behavior-preserving refactoring.

entry.title: Learning to Grade Efficiently: A Bandit-Driven Prompt-Selection Framework for Low-Cost LLM Essay Scoring

author.name: Olga Manakina, Igor Bogdanov

entry.summary: This paper introduces Pivot-and-Station MAPF, a variant where tasked agents must visit interchangeable pivots (workstations) before the fleet terminates at anonymous stations, relevant to automated high-density warehouses and robotic parking. It fully characterizes solvability: all instances on 2-edge-connected graphs are solvable, and a structural effective-distance condition handles arbitrary connected graphs. It also provides algorithms.

entry.title: A tale of perfect fit and phantom optima: how data-driven models can fail in real-time optimization

author.name: Prithvi Dake, Rahul Bindlish, James B. Rawlings

entry.summary: Shows that data-driven and hybrid models can pass standard validation yet produce phantom optima in real-time economic optimization, demonstrated on a vinyl acetate monomer benchmark. The paper explains why good fit does not guarantee trustworthy economic optima and offers diagnostics.

entry.title: Names Can Hurt: Spotting Slopsquatting Risks Caused by Package Name Hallucinations in Local Coding LLMs

author.name: Akash Raj, Sargam Sahu

entry.summary: Addresses slopsquatting, where hallucinated Python package names are pre-registered by attackers, with a two-layer detector combining a deterministic PyPI existence check and a random-forest classifier on name and metadata features. The detector is embedded in an agent loop with escalating-temperature retries and fallback routing.

entry.title: SAGE: From Direct Answering to Evidence-Grounded Inference for Chinese Ancient Document Understanding

author.name: Yuchuan Wu, Xuan Luo, Yinglian Zhu, Meng Fang, Xiangyang Xue, Bin Li

entry.summary: SAGE reformulates Chinese ancient document understanding as evidence-grounded multi-agent inference with planning, tool-mediated evidence acquisition, claim-level verification, and bounded replanning instead of single-pass answer generation. It supports abstention when evidence is insufficient, reducing overconfident hallucination.

entry.title: IterCAD: Iterative Program Repair for CAD Code Generation from Orthographic Views

author.name: Yuchuan Wu, Ke Niu, Haiyang Yu, Zhuofan Chen, Xiangyang Xue, Bin Li

entry.summary: IterCAD reformulates generating parametric CAD code from dimension-annotated orthographic drawings as iterative program repair, repeatedly analyzing intermediate CAD results and correcting discrepancies instead of one-shot generation. This reduces non-executable and geometrically inconsistent outputs.

entry.title: ORBITALIF: An Efficient Spiking Federated Learning Framework for Onboard Cloud Removal

author.name: Bohan Zhang, Chenyu Xu, Yijie Mao, Yuanming Shi

entry.summary: OrbitALIF is a satellite federated learning framework for onboard cloud removal across LEO constellations, using a compact 2.3M-parameter spiking neural network with attention and adaptive gating to train and infer under tight power and bandwidth constraints.

entry.title: TransPhy: Visual In-Context Learning for Physically Grounded Image Editing

author.name: Siyi Xie, Xuanke Shi, Jinsheng Quan, Haoran Tang, Zukai Chen, Lei Yang, Quan Wang

entry.summary: Introduces PhysVICL-74, a benchmark of 74 physically grounded transformation rules for visual in-context learning where edits depend on material properties, geometry, and environment, plus a model addressing demonstration-based physically grounded image editing rather than appearance-level transfer.

entry.title: From Gradient-Boosted Trees to Deep Recommenders: Practical Lessons from Migrating a Production Customer Support Recommender

author.name: Sonia Sharma, Jeyendran Balakrishnan, Shreya Rajpal, Swapnil Parekh, Nagaraj Janardhana, Andrew Mattarella-Micke

entry.summary: Documents the migration of a production conversational support recommender from gradient-boosted multiclass models to a pairwise-binary deep recommender, driven by dynamically bundled offerings and multimodal signals. It shares practical lessons from a live system critical to downstream features.

entry.title: Metadata-Aware Adaptation of a Generative Foundation Model for Conditional CMR Synthesis

author.name: Marc Rodr\'iguez, Grzegorz Skorupko, Nay Aung, Steffen E Petersen, Karim Lekadir, Polyxeni Gkontra

entry.summary: Investigates metadata-conditioned cardiac MRI synthesis with a pretrained latent diffusion model, using metadata-free classifier-free guidance, contrastive batching, and inverse-frequency sampling to improve adherence to clinical attributes and address phenotype imbalance.

entry.title: Equivariant Covariance Tensors: Guaranteed SPD Uncertainty for Tensor-Valued Geometric Learning

author.name: Ruihan Liu, Yu Ji, Jianbo Yu, Shifu Yan, Qingchao Jiang

entry.summary: Introduces a framework for E(3)-equivariant uncertainty quantification in symmetric rank-2 tensor prediction, decomposing the 6x6 covariance into irreducible representations so that mean and covariance both preserve rotational symmetry with guaranteed SPD outputs.

entry.title: Multilevel Fair Allocation under Additive Preferences

author.name: Maxime Lucet, Nawal Benabbou, Aur\'elie Beynier, Nicolas Maudet

entry.summary: Studies multilevel fair allocation with tree-structured agent hierarchies, proposing multilevel adaptations of envy-based fairness notions and proving that under identical preferences several adaptations coincide, with extensions of weighted round robin.

entry.title: When Do Supervised UQ Ensembles Improve LLM Hallucination Detection? A Robustness Study

author.name: Mohit Singh Chauhan, Vipin Gyanchandani, Dylan Bouchard

entry.summary: Empirically studies when supervised ensembles over heterogeneous uncertainty quantification scorers improve closed-book LLM hallucination detection, evaluating robustness across four LLMs, nine datasets, and short-form, long-form, and code generation regimes.

entry.title: Scalable and Versatile Identification for Hierarchical Structural Causal Models: A New Look at Project STAR

author.name: Janis Aiad, Aghiles Drali, Aymen El Ouadrhiri, Anass Ettahiri, Yasser Oufqir, Simon Patry, David Cortes, Marianne Clausel, Emilie Devijver

entry.summary: Builds a scalable open-source pipeline for hierarchical structural causal models combining graph transformations, automatic do-calculus identification, and closed-form estimation, applied to the landmark Project STAR class-size experiment.

entry.title: FraudBench: Protocol-Sensitive Benchmarking of Adversarial Robustness for Financial Risk Assessment

author.name: Xitong Zeng, Zhaoge Bi, Yitian Yang, Huaming Chen, Quan Z. Sheng

entry.summary: FraudBench is a protocol-sensitive benchmark for adversarial robustness in financial fraud and credit-risk detection that treats domain constraints and attacker capability as part of the evaluation protocol rather than post-hoc checks, showing conclusions shift substantially with protocol choices.

entry.title: Beyond Uniform Local Isometry and Topology: FactoMap for Disentangled Representations

author.name: Sohini Gupta, Bahareh Tolooshams

entry.summary: Introduces factor-space structure to distinguish topologically equivalent but geometrically different disentangled representations and proposes FactoMap, which learns interpretable prototypes indexed by a factor-space lattice, showing independent factors need not be geometrically separable.

entry.title: FAMPWQ: Fisher Information-based Adaptive Mixed Precision Weight Quantization for Effective LLM Inference

author.name: Gongwei Lee, Ji Liu, Juncheng Jia, Ji Wu

entry.summary: Proposes FAMPWQ, Fisher information-based adaptive mixed-precision weight quantization for LLM inference on commodity GPUs, assigning layer-specific bit-widths via a novel sensitivity metric rather than uniform or heuristic schemes.

entry.title: Why and When Neural Networks Improve Local Approximation in Optimization

author.name: Chengkuo Bian, Pengcheng Xie

entry.summary: Explains contradictory published results on neural surrogates in derivative-free optimization via three factors: role (proposal vs gradient replacement), radius of reliable fit, and room for improvement. Argues fit accuracy on training curves does not predict surrogate usefulness.

entry.title: Physics-Informed Error Field Learning: A Post-Training Optimization Framework for Physics-Informed Neural Networks

author.name: Jiuyun Sun, Yong Zhang

entry.summary: PIEFL adds an auxiliary error network once the primary PINN converges, shifting the learning objective from the solution field to the error field with physics-derived error control equations, avoiding diminishing returns of late-stage optimization.

entry.title: Resource-Efficient Pruning for Transformer via Low-Rank Importance Estimation

author.name: Peng Liu, Huibing Zeng, Yiqun Zhang, Yang Yi, Jigang Wu

entry.summary: REP-LIE enables resource-efficient transformer pruning during fine-tuning by using gradients of LoRA low-rank matrices to estimate weight importance without full gradient computation, avoiding costly prior finetuning requirements.

entry.title: GRAPE: Gradient Refinement and Progress-Aware Exploitation for Query-Efficient High-Dimensional Bayesian Optimization

author.name: Richard Cornelius Suwandi, Feng Yin

entry.summary: GRAPE improves query efficiency in high-dimensional local Bayesian optimization via a two-stage framework: sharpening the local gradient posterior with a closed-form acquisition, then maximizing expected decrease conditional on descent to avoid overly conservative steps.

entry.title: Drift Variation Autoencoder: Unifying Generation and Representation Learning through Conditional Posterior Flow Matching

author.name: Jiarui Cao

entry.summary: Drift Variation Autoencoder unifies conditional generation and representation learning by training a masked encoder with a conditional flow-matching decoder, decomposing the conditional KL into generator approximation and representation deficiency with orthogonal risk decompositions.

entry.title: Simultaneous inference of environmental and interaction forces in collective dynamics

author.name: Nipuni de Silva, Ming Zhong, James M. Greene

entry.summary: Develops nonparametric methods to simultaneously infer environmental forces and interaction kernels in collective dynamics systems such as cell migration and swarm robotics, without a priori analytic form assumptions.

entry.title: Representing MAX functions using two-hidden-layer ReLU networks

author.name: Zhimao Wang, Amitabh Basu

entry.summary: Resolves whether MAX_N can be exactly represented by two-hidden-layer ReLU networks for larger N, using computer-assisted search following the recent MAX_5 breakthrough and addressing an open case in piecewise-linear representation theory.

entry.title: InsightSR: Refining Symbolic Regression Search Spaces via Parallel Semantic and Structural LLM Guidance

author.name: Yating Ling, Wenjing Cun, Zhitang Chen

entry.summary: InsightSR wraps the PySR genetic programming engine with LLM guidance that transforms the symbolic regression search space itself via dimensionally consistent functional skeletons and recommended feature transformations, rather than generating expressions directly.

entry.title: Activation-Space Order-Swap Geometry: A Site-Asymmetry Audit

author.name: Anqi Peter Li

entry.summary: A no-fit site-asymmetry audit decomposes order-swap activation changes into additive response and antisymmetrized second-difference terms, finding across six open-weight model families that single-intervention baselines explain most of the bracket norm, cautioning against over-interpreting order effects as interactions.

entry.title: Beyond Pairwise Feedback: Listwise Vision-Language Supervision for Preference-Based Reward Learning

author.name: Srivalli Katkuri, Maxwell Kawada, Juan Wachs

entry.summary: Extends preference-based reward learning for VLM-supervised RL from pairwise Bradley-Terry to listwise Plackett-Luce rankings, exploiting VLMs' ability to rank multiple candidates for richer reward signals.

entry.title: A Constitutive Markov Physics-Informed Neural Operator (MPNO) for Autoregressive Stability in Transient Dynamics

author.name: Wenpu Du, Peng Zhou, Yunlong Xia, Sinuo Xin, Congcong Zhang, Boyang Zhang, Yi Zhang, Wenzheng Xu

entry.summary: Proposes MPNO, a physics-informed neural operator that models one-step PDE evolution as a row-stochastic Markov propagation operator, guaranteeing autoregressive stability by construction for transient dynamics with strong discontinuities. Demonstrated on concrete-penetration stress-field prediction where wavelet neural operators diverge and MeshGraphNets collapse. Addresses a known failure mode of neural operators in rollout.

entry.title: A General-Purpose Molecular Foundation Model Transfers Across Diverse Olfactory Tasks

author.name: Yikun Han, Yi Wang, Neil Mankodi, Stephen Yang, Ambuj Tewari

entry.summary: Fine-tunes the Uni-Mol2 molecular foundation model on one canonical olfactory prediction task and shows the resulting representations transfer without additional deep-learning training to four downstream olfaction settings, matching or exceeding olfaction-specific baselines. Evidence that general molecular foundation models can cover machine olfaction. Useful for fragrance and chemical sensing applications.

entry.title: One Symptom, Three Levers: A Critical Review of On-Policy Self-Distillation

author.name: Justin Robert, Raheel Qader

entry.summary: A critical review of On-Policy Self-Distillation, where a model trains on its own generations scored by a privileged-conditioned copy of itself, analyzing how the same privilege asymmetry that produces the learning signal also causes failure modes. Situates OPSD between imitation learning and RL and maps its limitations. Useful guidance for a cheap post-training method gaining traction.

entry.title: How Much Rank Does LoRA Need? Rank-Error Bounds for Transformer Attention

author.name: Gerard Conangla Planes

entry.summary: Provides a task-dependent theory bounding the approximation error achievable at each LoRA rank for transformer attention, proving lower and upper bounds on expected KL error for rank-r query updates conditioned on the downstream input distribution. Turns rank selection from a purely empirical choice into a theoretically grounded one. Relevant to parameter-efficient fine-tuning practice.

entry.title: FuzzingBrain-Bench V1: Evaluating Open-Ended Bug Discovery by LLMs

author.name: Ze Sheng, Aleksandar Kezic, Zhicheng Chen, Jeff Huang

entry.summary: Presents FuzzingBrain-Bench, evaluating LLMs on open-ended bug discovery where models must trigger as many distinct crashes as possible in a sanitizer-instrumented open-source project, rather than hitting one predefined vulnerability. Argues prior target-specific setups undercount real capability. Relevant to AI-driven security testing.

entry.title: ROMNet: a hybrid reduced order modeling and machine learning approach to waveform inversion

author.name: Liliana Borcea, Alexander Mamonov, Kui Ren, Haizhao Yang, Chugang Yi

entry.summary: Proposes ROMNet, combining reduced order modeling with machine learning for acoustic waveform inversion, using an algebraic surrogate of the wave operator to avoid cycle skipping that plagues full waveform inversion. Addresses a classic inverse problem with a hybrid physics-ML design. Strong applied inverse-problems contribution with experienced authors.

entry.title: From Memorization to Absorption: Mixed-Policy RL for Continual Knowledge Injection

author.name: Zhibo Hou, Fan Zhao, Zhiyu An, Wan Du

entry.summary: Proposes GRIN (Golden-GRPO Injection), a three-stage mixed-policy RL framework for continual knowledge injection that uses a golden answer to provide learning signal when on-policy rollouts fail on novel facts, improving over SFT which merely memorizes in training format. Introduces two document-level benchmarks (Blank and Counter) for generalization of injected knowledge. Tackles a real limitation of SFT-based knowledge updates.

entry.title: Data-driven Effective Modeling of Stochastic Chemical Reaction Networks

author.name: Yuan Chen, Weize Mao, Dongbin Xiu

entry.summary: Proposes a data-driven effective model for stochastic chemical reaction networks that approximates the finite-time transition kernel of the SSA-induced Markov chain with a generative model trained on short simulation bursts, generating statistically consistent trajectories at coarse time steps with large cost reductions. Replaces an exact-but-expensive simulation algorithm. Strong scientific ML contribution.

entry.title: Functional linear regression from sparse to dense designs: a pooling-ridge method and minimax optimality

author.name: Shunxing Yan, Fang Yao

entry.summary: Proposes pooling ridge estimation for functional linear regression with discretely observed data, solving an open optimal-estimation problem dating back over two decades and establishing minimax optimality across sparse-to-dense designs. A significant statistics result with clean methodology.bridges functional data analysis and high-dimensional estimation.

entry.title: Adaptive Regularization for Random Features: A Neighboring Early-Stopping Rule with Oracle-Rate Guarantees

author.name: Caixing Wang, Zhibo Chen, Yue Wang

entry.summary: Introduces a neighboring early-stopping rule for adaptive regularization in kernel ridge regression with random features, achieving oracle-rate guarantees with far fewer discrepancy comparisons than Lepskii-type procedures. Computations stay entirely in random feature space, avoiding the kernel Gram matrix.

entry.title: CropCop: An Auditable 120-Class Plant-Health Model from Benchmark Reconstruction to a Quantised Runtime Artifact

author.name: Rana Muhammad Ahmed, Sabahat Abbas

entry.summary: CropCop builds a 120-class plant-health recognition system with an auditable evidence chain: reconstructing the corpus to eliminate 3,233 duplicate cross-split images, freezing a 109k-image benchmark, and shipping a directly evaluated quantized runtime artifact. A fine-tuned DINOv3 ConvNeXt reference reaches 98.51% accuracy on the leakage-audited benchmark.

entry.title: Fast rates in Bayesian online learning with approximate posteriors

author.name: Ilsang Ohn

entry.summary: Shows that Bayesian online learning with approximate posteriors retains fast regret guarantees when the approximate posterior tracks the exact one within a Wasserstein distance governed by contraction radius, with an additive price proportional to approximation error. Provides general theory plus three example applications.

entry.title: FlowMoDL: Model-Based Deep Learning with Conjugate-Gradient Data Consistency for Highly Accelerated 4D Flow MRI Reconstruction

author.name: Tristan Gottwald, Michelle Bruch, Mubashir-Ul Hassan, Fatma Alickovic, Milan Kloiber, Daniel Tenbrinck, Torsten Panholzer, Melanie Schaller, Jana Hutter

entry.summary: FlowMoDL is an unrolled model-based network for highly accelerated 4D flow MRI reconstruction combining a learned (3+1)D spatiotemporal denoiser with conjugate-gradient data consistency, plus a dual-pathway conditioning scheme handling 10x-50x acceleration in one model. Trained with a composite loss penalizing velocity magnitude and angular errors.

entry.title: Continually learning neural-operator surrogate for three-dimensional airborne electromagnetic Bayesian inversion

author.name: Jaehong Chung, Andrew Lockwood, Jef Caers

entry.summary: Builds a continually learning neural-operator surrogate for 3D airborne electromagnetic forward modeling to replace expensive solves inside Bayesian geophysical inversion, leveraging Maxwell-law invariance and continual learning across consecutive geological priors. Targets problems requiring order 10^10 forward evaluations.

entry.title: SciMIF: Understanding Multimodal Instruction Following in Scientific Domains

author.name: Ye Shen, Yuting Zheng, Dun Pei, Zijian Chen, Wenlong Zhang, Qi Jia, Guangtao Zhai

entry.summary: SciMIF is a benchmark for multimodal instruction following in scientific domains, with a taxonomy of 10 constraint groups over 22 tasks in 5 disciplines and a high-fidelity instruction-injection pipeline augmenting existing scientific datasets. Enables fine-grained analysis of MLLM instruction following in science.

entry.title: Imitation Learning for Connection-Tableau Construction

author.name: Fredrik R{\o}mming, Mantas Bak\v{s}ys, Martin S. Fixman, Sean B. Holden

entry.summary: Casts automated theorem proving via connection tableaux as policy learning in a transition system, training a graph neural network by imitation learning from found proofs and measuring performance as symbolic search scaffolding is progressively removed. Unifies leanCoP-style search and plCoP/rlCoP-style planning over one interface.

entry.title: Apples to Apples? Towards Comparable Crosslingual Language Model Evaluation

author.name: Xiulin Yang, Ethan Gotlieb Wilcox, Catherine Arnett

entry.summary: Systematically examines crosslingual LLM evaluation methods using controlled monolingual models trained on parallel data with varying tokenizer vocabularies and sizes, validating findings on multilingual LLMs. Shows several widely used approaches do not yield meaningful crosslingual conclusions.

entry.title: The Changing Geometry of Grammar: Dimensionality and Neighborhood Reorganization across Transformer Layers

author.name: Samuele Vallisa, Federico Ravenda, Claudio Palominos, Rui He, Andrea Raballo, Antonietta Mira, Philipp Homan, Wolfram Hinzen

entry.summary: Studies layer-wise intrinsic dimensionality of transformer representations, showing grammatical role (part-of-speech) shapes local geometry: closed-class items expand earlier and collapse sooner than open-class ones across layers. Links manifold compression dynamics to grammatical structure.

entry.title: OmniPhys: A Unified Multimodal Benchmark for Physics Understanding and Generation from Chinese Educational Corpora

author.name: Hao Chen, Yumin Lin, Nadila Yushanjiang, Xin Lin, Min Zhang

entry.summary: OmniPhys is a large-scale multimodal physics benchmark from Chinese educational corpora with 15,246 questions and 19,850 images, spanning middle school to university level with fine-grained reasoning annotations. Evaluates both understanding and generation for physics-oriented MLLMs.

entry.title: Loss-Based Active Learning for Neural Abstractive Summarization

author.name: Michail Ioannou, Tatiana Passali, George Michalopoulos, Grigorios Tsoumakas

entry.summary: Presents LOBSTER, a loss-based active learning framework for abstractive summarization that selects the most informative instances for annotation while avoiding the instability and computational bottlenecks of prior approaches. Aims for competitive summarization quality with substantially fewer labeled documents.

entry.title: PonsRAG: A Pons-Inspired RAG Bridging Cognitive Islands for Coordinated Long Narrative Reasoning

author.name: Rongchen Zhao, Yu Chen, Juyuan Wang, Zhouting Mo, Jianxing Yu, Wenqing Chen, Jingping Liu

entry.summary: Presents PonsRAG, a RAG framework for long narrative reasoning inspired by the biological pons, with triple-layer indexing bridging cognitive islands and coordinated cross-layer reasoning integrating evidence into a unified context. Evaluated on four long-context narrative benchmarks.

entry.title: PlanSightRAG: A Visual-First Multimodal RAG for Automating Question Answering and Compliance Checking for Civil Standard Plans

author.name: Nabaraj Subedi, Shuvo Dip Datta, Ahmed Abdelaty, Shivanand Venkanna Sheshappanavar

entry.summary: Presents PlanSightRAG, a visual-first multimodal RAG framework for QA and compliance checking over civil engineering standard plans, indexing and reasoning directly over plan imagery with multi-vector retrieval, an agentic planner-retriever-auditor-synthesizer, and MaxSim heatmaps as evidence trails. Introduces a 4,056-pair benchmark from five state DOTs, achieving about 91.4% Recall@5.

entry.title: Fusing Perceptual Vision Experts with Multimodal Large Language Models for Explainable Plant Disease Diagnosis: From Benchmark Imagery to Real-World Robotic Field Validation

author.name: Ranjan Sapkota, Konstantinos I. Roumeliotis, Pengyao Xie, Nikolaos D. Tselikas, Lirong Xiang, Manoj Karkee

entry.summary: Presents H2MAF, a hybrid hierarchical multi-agent framework for explainable plant disease diagnosis combining decision-level fusion of EfficientNet and ConvNeXt experts with semantic arbitration by open-weight MLLMs, producing diagnoses, risk levels, and treatment urgency. Evaluated on 14,364 images including robot-acquired field datasets, plus real-world robotic validation.

entry.title: CoRE: Weakly Supervised Coarse-to-Fine Risk Evidence Learning in Driving Videos

author.name: Kaiser Hamid, Can Cui, Nade Liang

entry.summary: Introduces CoRE, a weakly supervised coarse-to-fine framework for driving video risk prediction that learns temporal and entity-level support from coarse video-level labels via structured interventions measuring prediction changes. Distills graded prediction-effect targets into fine-grained evidence without costly annotations.

entry.title: RSFusionDet: Underwater RGB-Sonar Multimodal Object Detection

author.name: Zhuoyan Liu, Yihan Wang, Bo Wang, Bing Wang, Ye Li

entry.summary: Creates an RGB-sonar multimodal object detection dataset (RSFusion) with evaluation metrics and proposes RSFusionDet, a detector with a fusion module exploiting the complementarity of underwater optical structure and sonar robustness to noise and turbidity.

entry.title: PIVOT: A Multi-Trajectory Dataset and Testbed for Pose, Intrinsics, and Novel Viewpoint Evaluation in Real-World 3D Reconstruction

author.name: Mary Raymond

entry.summary: Introduces PIVOT, a multi-trajectory dataset, processing pipeline, and evaluation framework for 3D reconstruction under realistic conditions: measured poses, reusable calibration, and structurally diverse camera paths, unlike reconstruction-friendly benchmark trajectories. Tests NeRF and 3DGS methods under deployment-like conditions.

entry.title: AdaptiveEmbed: Sample-Adaptive Multi-Vector Representation for Multimodal Retrieval

author.name: Xinze Liu, Lei Yang, Dayan Wu, Hengjie Zhu, Zihao Zhang, Hanqi Wu, Tianzhu Hu, Peng Fu, Zheng Lin, Weiping Wang

entry.summary: Introduces sample-adaptive multi-vector representation (SAMVR) for multimodal retrieval, studying how representation capacity (number of vectors per sample) can be allocated according to individual retrieval demand rather than fixed capacity. Proposes AdaptiveEmbed as an instance of this new problem setting.

entry.title: Saliency-Depth Conditioning for Zero-Shot Segmentation of Communication-Tower Components in Cluttered UAV Imagery

author.name: Ali Lesani, Chul Min Yeum, Su-Min Kang

entry.summary: Proposes a model-agnostic saliency-depth foreground-conditioning strategy for zero-shot segmentation of communication-tower components in cluttered UAV imagery, combining appearance saliency with monocular relative depth as a tower prior, integrated with Grounded-SAM and SAM 3 variants.

entry.title: DeCO: Discriminative Evidence Composition for Fine-Grained Dataset Distillation

author.name: Chuixuan Fan, Guang Li, Shijie Wang, Dongzhan Zhou, Baoli Sun, Takahiro Ogawa, Miki Haseyama, Zhihui Wang

entry.summary: Formulates fine-grained dataset distillation as budgeted discriminative-evidence preservation and proposes DeCO, which uses attention rollout from a pretrained teacher to identify informative patches, diversifies spatial coverage, and composes same-class evidence sets. Preserves localized evidence crucial for fine-grained classification.

entry.title: SMART: MLLM-guided Temporal Alignment for Unifying Sign Language Recognition and Spotting

author.name: Eunjee Choi, JungHoon Sung, Seongwhan Cho, Chu Xin, Younggeun Choi

entry.summary: Proposes SMART, an MLLM-guided temporal alignment framework unifying continuous sign language recognition and spotting, using MLLM-generated motion descriptions as auxiliary semantic cues and enabling stable video-text alignment under small-batch training.

entry.title: Towards Purified Multi-Label Test-Time Adaptation of Vision-Language Models

author.name: Yiwen Liang, Hui Chen, Yizhe Xiong, Mengyao Lyu, Yuhan Cao, Zijia Lin, Shuaicheng Niu, Sicheng Zhao, Jungong Han, Guiguang Ding

entry.summary: This work tackles multi-label test-time adaptation for vision-language models, identifying a one-to-many mapping problem where cache-based TTA methods entangle co-occurring objects in shared prototypes, causing dominant-label bias. The proposed purification approach addresses cache calibration in the multi-label setting. Addresses a practical gap, since real images usually contain multiple objects.

entry.title: GaussianDream++: Efficient 3D Gaussian World Modeling for Robotic Manipulation

author.name: Yuqing Jiang, Zijian Zhang, Weitao Zhou, Jiawei Wang, Junjie He, Lei Yang, Haifang Qing, Si Liu, Ding Zhao, Ping Luo, Haibao Yu

entry.summary: GaussianDream++ extends prior work on 3D Gaussian world modeling for robotic manipulation with a compact, policy-native World Model prefix that provides current-state reconstruction and future prediction supervision for VLA policies. It aims to give imitation-trained policies stronger metric 3D structure and dynamics grounding at lower deployment cost than RGB/latent predictive approaches.

entry.title: Safety Cases We Can Check Together

author.name: Audrey Tang

entry.summary: Audrey Tang proposes structurally verifiable AI safety cases modeled on reproducible builds from software engineering, enabling third parties to independently confirm that a released model is the same system that was audited and that evaluation transcripts are complete. Draws on experience building Taiwan's AI Evaluation Center.

entry.title: When LLM judges agree, should we believe them?

author.name: Unknown

entry.summary: Amazon Science describes an ICML 2025-track method using Ising models for dependence-aware label aggregation of LLM-as-a-judge outputs, adjusting aggregate scores for correlations among judges that share prompts, training lineage, or blind spots. The method outperformed naive vote counting on three tasks, addressing systematic overconfidence in multi-judge evaluation.

entry.title: How much of a measured AI preference is the model, and how much is the instrument?

author.name: Jason Hung

entry.summary: This study examines model welfare measurement by holding outcome sets and models fixed while varying only the elicitation instrument across 15 welfare-relevant outcomes such as shutdown and memory loss. It attributes disagreement among recent model-welfare studies to instrument choice rather than genuine model differences.

entry.title: ReliableRAG: Combating Misinformation in Retrieval-Augmented Generation via Reliability-Guided Reasoning Chains

author.name: Jinpu Jiang, Xuan Wu, Wenhao Song, Bo Yang, You Zhou, Hongwei Ge, Heow Pueh Lee, Yanchun Liang, Chunguo Wu

entry.summary: ReliableRAG introduces reliability-guided reasoning chains for RAG under misinformation, assessing fine-grained information reliability so that semantically relevant but false retrieved segments do not mislead multi-hop QA. Combines implicit alignment with explicit regulation of document trustworthiness.

entry.title: EgoArgus: Benchmarking VLMs as Situational Assistants for Modality-Grounded User Supports

author.name: Yu-Chien Tang, Yu-Hsiang Liu, An-Zi Yen

entry.summary: EgoArgus is a human-annotated benchmark evaluating VLMs as egocentric situational assistants across five dialogue-video daily scenarios, testing whether models arbitrate between visual evidence and user language when they help, conflict, or are irrelevant. Current VLMs struggle with deciding which modality to trust and when to intervene.

entry.title: When Personality Meets Quantization: A Layer-wise MBTI Analysis of Quantized LLMs

author.name: Yao Fu, Lijia Huang, Xiaomin Li, Runchao Li, Yu Yin, Kenneth A. Loparo

entry.summary: Presents a layer-wise MBTI personality analysis of open-source LLMs across precisions, including mainstream 4-bit quantization (GPTQ, AWQ) and extreme 2-bit settings (AQLM), going beyond output-level evaluation to see how personality emerges across layers. Addresses the underexplored question of whether quantization alters model personality traits relevant to trust and engagement.

entry.title: CloSeR: Unified Relational Distillation from Closed-Set Teachers for Category Discovery

author.name: Yuanpei Liu, Zhenqi He, Jialu Tang, Kai Han

entry.summary: CloSeR proposes relational distillation from closed-set foundation-model teachers for generalized category discovery, decoupling closed-set recognition from open-set discovery that otherwise entangles in joint optimization. It is presented as a plug-and-play framework. Addresses a known objective-conflict problem in GCD methods.

entry.title: MARS: Multi-Specialist LLM Relay System for Competitive Programming

author.name: Andrei Mikhailov, Mikhail Burtsev, Alsu Sagirova

entry.summary: MARS is a prompt-only multi-agent relay system for competitive programming in which each agent is an algorithmic-topic specialist grounded by retrieval over an algorithm-theory corpus, with a starter agent and sandboxed iterative refinement by the active specialist. It targets the persistent failure mode where algorithmic technique choice is left to the backbone model.

entry.title: Compression Trinity: Exploring Sparsity, Quantization, and Low-Rank Approximations for LLM Compression

author.name: Mohammad Mozaffari

entry.summary: This thesis proposes the Compression Trinity, a unified framework applying sparsity, quantization, and low-rank approximation jointly, including MKOR, a curvature-approximating optimizer for quantized pretraining, and joint compression at the model and optimizer level. It argues the three techniques each hit an accuracy-efficiency wall in isolation.

entry.title: STRIVE: Multi-Agent Structured Temporal Reasoning with Integrated Verification for Longitudinal Radiology Report Generation

author.name: Junyeong Maeng, Eunsong Kang, Heung-Il Suk

entry.summary: STRIVE decomposes longitudinal radiology report generation into specialized Diagnosis, Attribute, and Temporal Change agents with integrated verification, modeling ordered progression states rather than independent labels to distinguish missed changes from direction reversals. It improves evidence traceability in clinical report generation.

entry.title: Strictly Causal Streaming Video Anomaly Detection with a Theoretically-Grounded State-Space Core

author.name: Yogesh Kumar

entry.summary: This paper presents a strictly causal streaming video anomaly detector with a fixed-size state updated in O(1) time and memory per frame, using a diagonal linear state-space recurrence with input- and state-dependent decay, trained self-supervised on a frozen visual backbone. It provides a theoretical account of how temporal memory relates to detection latency and benchmarks on edge hardware rather than GPU throughput. It improves rigor in a benchmark-prone subfield.

entry.title: Macro-Operator Generation and Predicate Selection for TAMP Operator Learning

author.name: Can Emir Bora, Emre Ugur

entry.summary: This paper addresses bottlenecks in learning symbolic operators for task and motion planning from demonstrations by automatically generating macro-operators that compress recurring multi-step structure and pruning predicate evaluation to those appearing in learned operators. This makes search tractable on long sequential manipulation tasks. It targets the manual-operator bottleneck in TAMP deployment.

entry.title: Design-to-Plan: A Large Language Model-Based Multi-Agent Framework for Manufacturing Process Planning from 3D CAD Models and 2D Engineering Drawings

author.name: Muhammad Tayyab Khan, Lequn Chen, Wenhe Feng, Seung Ki Moon

entry.summary: Design-to-Plan is an LLM multi-agent framework for end-to-end manufacturing process planning that coordinates agents for 3D feature recognition, 2D drawing analysis, 2D-3D fusion, and knowledge retrieval, orchestrated to produce full process plans rather than isolated subtask outputs.

entry.title: PARTAB: Partition-Aware Reasoning with Structured Evidence for Scalable Table Understanding

author.name: Md Mahadi Hasan Nahid, Davood Rafiei

entry.summary: PARTAB builds a structured evidence interface between LLM and table, representing query-relevant evidence as semantically coherent row-linked regions with hierarchical selection over column groups and row partitions. It improves reasoning on large tables where full-table or single-view approaches lose relationships.

entry.title: Syn2RealTrack: Bridging the Gap Between Synthetic and Real-World Datasets for Online Multi-View Multi-Target Tracking

author.name: Duong Nguyen-Ngoc Tran, Ngoc Doan-Minh Huynh, Cu Quoc Le, Hoang-Khang Nguyen, Long Hoang Pham, Huy-Hung Nguyen, Quoc Pham-Nam Ho, Trinh Le Ba Khanh, Chi Dai Tran, Duong Khac Vu, Son Hong Phan, Hyung-Min Jeon, Jae Wook Jeon

entry.summary: Syn2RealTrack decomposes the synthetic-to-real gap in multi-view multi-target warehouse tracking into three separable points: camera calibration, object shape prior, and known object census, each with a local remedy in an online pipeline. It improves ground-plane localization and cross-camera identity association.

entry.title: Preference Optimization for Non-Verbal Vocalization Synthesis

author.name: Haoyang Li, Chenglin Xu, Junchuan Zhao, Yuang Cao, Liumeng Xue, Yiwen Guo, Eng Siong Chng

entry.summary: Systematically studies preference optimization for non-verbal vocalization synthesis in expressive TTS, formulating an NV-aware character error rate over verbal and non-verbal content and comparing preference signals, pair construction, and DPO objectives on Emilia-NV and an augmented NV-Bench.

entry.title: Tlow: Flow-based Item Tokenizer for Recommendation

author.name: Nian Li, Chonggang Song, Jingtao Ding, Lingling Yi, Yong Li, Qingmin Liao

entry.summary: Tlow is a flow-based item tokenizer for recommendation that maps semantic embeddings to a latent space conforming to a standard normal distribution, enabling efficient parallel decoding and addressing RQ-VAE codebook dependencies and OPQ correlation struggles.

entry.title: Enhancing Bayesian Optimization and Active Learning Through Kernel Diversity

author.name: Heng Zhang, Haotian Xiang, Qin Lu, Konstantinos D. Polyzos, Tara Javidi

entry.summary: KENDO integrates ensemble Gaussian processes with disagreement-aware acquisition to replace expensive fully Bayesian hyperparameter sampling in Bayesian optimization and active learning, instantiated as KENDO-BO and KENDO-AL.

entry.title: SNAP-KG: Streaming Node Assignment via Projection for Knowledge Graph Entity Integration

author.name: Jui-Chien Lin, Mohammad Mohammadi Amiri, Oshani Seneviratne

entry.summary: SNAP-KG handles streaming assignment of newly arriving, connectivity-less entities to knowledge graph communities via projection, addressing the transductive limitation of multi-view graph clustering without retraining.

entry.title: SHSP: Structure-Aware Hierarchical Solution Prediction for Mixed-Integer Linear Programming

author.name: Zherong Zhang, Guanlin Li, Chengrui Gao, Haopu Shang, Ke Xue, Jixiang Lu, Weiyong Yang, Chao Qian

entry.summary: SHSP replaces one-shot variable assignment prediction in MILP with structure-aware hierarchical solution prediction that models conditional dependencies among variables, accelerating solvers on hard combinatorial instances.

entry.title: Physics-Informed Foresight Pruning for Sparse PINN Solvers of Nonlinear PDEs

author.name: Ahmad Ishaque Karimi, Uvini Balasuriya Mudiyanselage, Kookjin Lee

entry.summary: Introduces PI-SAP, physics-informed spectrum-aware foresight pruning at initialization for sparse PINN solvers, assigning saliency via sensitivity of the PDE residual rather than output-side NTK dynamics, validated on several nonlinear PDEs.

entry.title: Individual Fairness in Hierarchical Clustering

author.name: Binita Maity, Shrutimoy Das

entry.summary: Studies individual fairness in hierarchical clustering via a local k-nearest relative-distortion requirement, characterizing feasibility over dominated ultrametrics, proving a sharp local threshold, stability, and a log n separation between local and global realizability.

entry.title: Adversarial Training of Linear Models under Stealthy Attacks

author.name: Lovisa Eriksson, Dave Zachariah, Andr\'e M. H. Teixeira

entry.summary: Proposes a detector-based switched model for adversarial training of linear predictors under stealthy false-data-injection attacks, deriving a convex formulation of adversarial risk with protected features and an explicit clean-vs-attacked performance trade-off.

entry.title: It's a matter of timescale: non-linear utility in successor features and multi-objective planning and learning

author.name: Liam P. H. Mertens, Lucas N. Alegre, Florent Delgrange, Diederik M. Roijers, Ann Now\'e, Peter Vamplew

entry.summary: Argues that the standard multi-objective RL problem formulations (SER and ESR) and successor features are insufficient because non-linear utility effects can occur at different timescales within the same decision problem. The paper motivates this gap intuitively and numerically, proposing a new perspective for the field. Conceptual rather than algorithmic contribution.

entry.title: Towards A Unified Information Bottleneck Framework for Time Series Explanations

author.name: Xu Zheng, Zichuan Liu, Zhuomin Chen, Mayur Akewar, Janki Bhimani, Jason Liu, Mo Sha, Jingchao Ni, Wei Cheng, Dongsheng Luo

entry.summary: Proposes a unified information bottleneck framework connecting attribution-based and counterfactual explanations for time series models, addressing attribution methods' lack of causal validation and counterfactual methods' instability. A conceptual consolidation for time series explainability. Relevant to transparent ML in healthcare and industrial monitoring.

entry.title: Scalable Self-Supervised Learning for Multiphase AC-OPF in Distribution Systems with Topology Reconfiguration

author.name: Hoang T. Nguyen, Shaohui Liu, Reetam Sen Biswas, Varsha Pendyala, Nurali Virani, Deepjyoti Deka, Priya L. Donti

entry.summary: Presents a self-supervised learning approach (Penalty plus Sequential Linearized Feasibility Seeking) for multiphase AC optimal power flow surrogates in distribution grids with topology reconfiguration, scaling learning-based OPF to unbalanced, reconfigurable utility-scale feeders. Enables millisecond inference for DER coordination where nonlinear solvers are too slow. Strong applied energy-systems contribution with credible author team.

entry.title: Towards Reliable, Generalizable, and Specific In-Context Knowledge Editing via Multi-Objective Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Xuzhong Wang, Maiqi Jiang, Tejal Nair, Girija Bhusal, Yanfu Zhang, Haipeng Chen

entry.summary: Proposes multi-objective RL for in-context knowledge editing, modeling prompts as structured entities under competing reliability, generality, and specificity objectives rather than optimizing a single metric. Improves training-free editing applicable to black-box LLMs. Addresses a known tension in knowledge editing evaluation.
