entry.title: Key Point Analysis Needs Structure Recovery: Task Definition, Dataset Diagnosis, and a Structure-Aware Benchmark

author.name: Zhiqiang Shi, Oana Cocarascu

entry.summary: Argues key point analysis is fundamentally a structured prediction problem and shows existing KPA benchmarks suffer grouping, redundancy, coverage, and mapping defects that break reference-based evaluation. Introduces a structure-aware, distribution-sensitive benchmark via human-in-the-loop re-annotation.

entry.title: Padamitra: Grounded Glossary Generation for Classical Sanskrit

author.name: Manoj Balaji Jagadeeshan, Sai Pragnaan Marala, Pawan Goyal

entry.summary: Padamitra formalizes grounded glossary generation for classical Sanskrit, recovering semantically meaningful phrases and translation-grounded meanings from sloka-translation pairs, with a 31,316-triple benchmark from the Ramayana and Bhagavatam. Instruction fine-tuning across several models substantially beats prompting, with explicit segmentation helping.

entry.title: Short Horizons and Sparse Concepts: a Mathematical View of the Readout in the J-lens

author.name: Shi-Qi Yan, Kai-Xuan Ding, Chao-Hong Tan, Qian Chen, Wen Wang, Xiangang Li, Zhen-Hua Ling

entry.summary: Provides a mathematical view of the Jacobian lens for reading verbalizable representations from language models, treating it as a first-order causal transfer operator from intermediate activations to expected future readouts. Analyzes its approximation behavior, bias, and Jacobian energy distribution to identify short-horizon limitations and sparse concepts.

entry.title: ClueWeaver: Reward-Guided Dual-Agent Evidence Reasoning for Compact LLMs on Literary Long Narratives

author.name: Jihao Zhu, Zhiwei Yang, Wenxiao Zhang, Junqian Zhao, Qi You, Fangqi Wang, Zheyuan Deng, Hanzhe Yang, Yu Liu, Jin B. Hong

entry.summary: ClueWeaver is a dual-agent framework (Finder for clue-locating segmentation, Interpreter for grounded answer derivation with paragraph-ID citations) enabling compact local LLMs to answer questions over literary long narratives affordably. Targets humanities and social science users without access to proprietary long-context models.

entry.title: Controllable Affective Generation via Latent Vector Steering

author.name: Xixian Yong, Siyuan Chang, Yingying Zhang, Xian Wu, Xiao Zhou

entry.summary: EmoVec enables controllable affective generation via latent vector steering: emotion directions extracted through contrastive activation addition are refined by debiasing and principal subspace removal, then injected into the residual stream with static or adaptive scaling for continuous emotion-intensity control without weight updates.

entry.title: GraftSR: Grafting Authentic Textures for Real-World Image Super-Resolution via Identical-Instance Guidance

author.name: Qifan Yu, Haoran Bai, Zongyao He, Weijie He, Sibin Deng, Honggang Qi, Ying Chen

entry.summary: Proposes GraftSR, a texture-reference-guided diffusion super-resolution framework using reference images of the identical instance to anchor authentic texture restoration, with a dual-mask guidance mechanism decoupling cross-view texture injection to handle spatial misalignment and prevent background leakage.

entry.title: VGA-BenchV2: An Expanded Unified Benchmark and Multi-Model Framework for Evaluating Video Aesthetics and Generation Quality

author.name: Longteng Jiang, DanDan Zheng, Qianqian Qiao, Heng Huang, Huaye Wang, Yihang Bo, Bao Peng, Jingdong Chen, Jun Zhou, Xin Jin

entry.summary: Examines how Gaussian splatting 3D reconstruction performs across publicly available underwater datasets spanning varying turbidity, illumination loss, and colour attenuation, plus an industrial survey, running five public-code systems under one protocol with shared poses, initialization, and budget.

entry.title: OpenVeinNet: Robust Open-Set Finger Vein Verification with Dynamic Snake Convolution and Graph Learning

author.name: Sushrut Patwardhan, Raghavendra Ramachandra

entry.summary: OpenVeinNet combines Dynamic Snake Convolution with graph-based feature modeling for finger vein verification in open-set and cross-dataset settings, where test identities are unseen during training. The adaptive convolution captures curvilinear vascular structures while graph learning models their topology. This matters for biometric security since vascular patterns resist presentation attacks.

entry.title: Deep Learning Segmentation of Diffusion-Weighted MRI Acute Ischaemic Stroke: A Pragmatic Evaluation Across Three Datasets

author.name: Atle Bj{\o}rnerud, Till Schellhorn, Thor H. Skatt{\o}r, Terje Nome, Jon Andr\'e Ottesen, Anne Hege Aamodt, Bradley J MacIntosh

entry.summary: A pragmatic evaluation of nnU-Net segmentation of acute ischemic stroke on DWI-MRI across three datasets (1,744 training, 436 test cases), testing minimal preprocessing options and clinically feasible inference times. The study finds accurate segmentation achievable with simple pipelines. Useful translational evidence rather than a new method.

entry.title: Anytime Global Tensor Motion Planning

author.name: Sai Coumar, An T. Le, Zachary Kingston

entry.summary: Generalizes Global Tensor Motion Planning so layer edges can be realized by any black-box local planner, and provides two anytime policies with theoretical guarantees including coverage of every homotopy class and convergence to optimal cost. Offers formal results on sampled graph coverage and asymptotic optimality.

entry.title: VISTA: Visually Inferred Spatial ConTact Attention for Contact-Rich Manipulation

author.name: Jiayi Chen, Wenlong Dong, Yan Huang, Xianglin Chen, Zijian Lin, Jiaqi Yin, Yushan Liu, Wenbo Ding

entry.summary: VISTA introduces a Visual Deformation Field, a 3D displacement representation of a compliant gripper, as visuo-physical feedback for imitation learning in contact-rich manipulation. This avoids dedicated tactile or force sensors while providing richer contact information than external vision alone.

entry.title: Phantom Navigator: Stealthy and Precise Unmanned Aerial Vehicle Redirection with Real-Time Tracking and GPS Spoofing

author.name: Haocheng Meng, Shaocheng Luo, Songqiao Xie, Miroslav Pajic

entry.summary: Phantom Navigator is a UAV redirection attack combining real-time tracking with GPS spoofing to achieve stealthy, precise diversion of drones toward specified targets, improving on prior physical capture, communication hijacking, and coarse sensor spoofing. Published with Duke-affiliated authors including Pajic, it demonstrates reliable targeted diversion.

entry.title: FLARE: A Systematic, Uncertainty-Aware Framework for Evidence-Based Adoption of Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare

author.name: Jacob Idoko, Siddhartha Paudel, Mariana Bento, Roberto Souza, Gouri Ginde

entry.summary: FLARE is an uncertainty-aware framework for evaluating the financial and operational case for AI adoption in healthcare, combining fuzzy logic, time-driven activity-based costing, and ROI analysis. It is demonstrated on an early health technology assessment of AI-assisted large vessel occlusion detection.

entry.title: AgentWorld: Personality-Aware Reliability Evaluation for Agentic Information Retrieval

author.name: Gunja Agarwal, Arup Kumar Das, Arun Menon, Jitesh Chandra Mishra, Vignesh Divakaran

entry.summary: AgentWorld is a simulation framework for agentic information retrieval combining Big Five personality-driven user populations, stateful tool-use environments, a pass-k consistency metric with structured fault classification, and an adversarial Risk Analyser using Monte Carlo rollouts under task-aware perturbations. It also supports score-thresholded training-data export in six fine-tuning formats.

entry.title: ACE: A Self-Correcting Agentic Canvas Editor for Multi-Slide Presentation Automation

author.name: JooYoung Jang, Taegyeong Lee, Jihyeon Park, Nojun Kwak

entry.summary: ACE is a self-correcting agentic canvas editor for multi-slide presentations operating on a hierarchical scene graph with 98 presentation-specialized tools, plus a content-aware router cutting about 89 percent of input tokens and a self-correction loop. It addresses flat legacy formats and the lack of ground truth in design evaluation.

entry.title: Constraint-Guided Enterprise Data Mapping with Large Language Models

author.name: Sebastian Monka, Pramod Anantharam, Thien Vo Minh, Lavdim Halilaj

entry.summary: CGM is a neuro-symbolic method for enterprise data mapping that constrains LLM-generated schema correspondences with metadata-grounded admissibility constraints and cascade-relaxed candidate generation, preventing fluent but operationally invalid mappings. It targets entity alignment across semi-structured enterprise records.

entry.title: Do Recipes Have Personas? Characterizing and Generating Creator Style in Attributed Procedural Graphs

author.name: Lei Jiang

entry.summary: This paper studies procedural stylometry: characterizing and generating the idiosyncratic execution style of individual recipe creators. It introduces ViralRecipesTrans, a dataset of execution-flow graphs aligned to specific creators from culinary video transcripts, and shows discrete topological metrics capture creator style where lexical classifiers overfit via semantic leakage. The framing of persona discovery over procedural graphs is a fresh angle on stylometry.

entry.title: HMGCLIP: Heterogeneous Multi-Granularity Contrastive Learning for E-commerce Representation Learning

author.name: Qiuyu Zhu, Yi Gao, Zhichao Wan, Mingyang Ma

entry.summary: HMGCLIP is a multimodal embedding framework for e-commerce that builds a heterogeneous hypergraph over product data to mine structure-aware hard negatives and align multi-granular semantics at relation and hyperedge levels. This enables fine-grained attribute discrimination, such as distinguishing subtle material differences among visually similar products. It improves on global-embedding limitations of general MLLMs for product understanding.

entry.title: Causal Modelling of Support Interventions for Student Competency Assessment

author.name: Francesca Mangili, Alessandro Antonucci, Rafael Caba\~nas

entry.summary: This paper advocates a structural causal modelling approach to educational assessment, moving beyond psychometric item response theory toward explicit interventional and counterfactual reasoning about student competency and support interventions. It proposes a construction protocol and analyzes which forms of reasoning remain inaccessible to standard psychometric models. This reframes competency assessment causally.

entry.title: Constrained Entity Selection under Partial Knowledge for LLM-Based Knowledge Graph QA

author.name: Emanuel Kitzelmann

entry.summary: This paper studies Constrained Entity Selection under Partial Knowledge for LLM-based knowledge graph QA: LLM-generated candidate answers are verified via lightweight symbolic constraints derived from the question, offering a middle ground between brittle full semantic parsing and unguaranteed LLM reasoning over KGs. The setting explicitly handles incomplete graphs. It contributes a formalized, verifiable alternative to end-to-end KGQA.

entry.title: Rebuild Dossier: Mechanically-Enforced Specs for Agentic App Rebuilds, and What Model-Tier Failures Reveal

author.name: Parker Fawcett

entry.summary: Rebuild Dossier is an open-source tool that locks an application's real interface before any code is written and enforces one-test-at-a-time building through automated checks for agentic app rebuilds, finding that a passing suite does not certify rebuild quality since a rule-breaking agent passed everything while a compliant agent failed a held-back test. It surfaces model-tier failure patterns in modernization pipelines.

entry.title: Identifying Latent Declarative Representations of Code for Assisting Repository Migration

author.name: Shraddha Surana, Ashwin Srinivasan, Michael Bain

entry.summary: ADFD-Migrate treats legacy programs as implementations of unobserved declarative descriptions and approximates those with annotated data-flow diagrams inferred by an LLM under static-analysis coverage checks, then uses dependency-aware chunking for target-language generation. The goal is improving repository-scale porting of legacy code. It combines program analysis with LLM inference in a structured migration pipeline.

entry.title: RefineRank: Joint Box Refinement and Ranking for Surgical Spatio-Temporal Grounding

author.name: Linzhe Jiang, Jiayuan Huang, Changhao Zhang, Chunyang Jiang, Zhehua Mao, Mobarak I. Hoque

entry.summary: RefineRank combines a frozen medical vision-language model with a frozen open-set detector via a trainable module that refines and ranks candidate boxes for surgical spatio-temporal grounding. It closes the gap between contextual language understanding and precise localization in surgical video.

entry.title: MatReplace: A Reference-Free, Conditioning-Aligned Benchmark for Material Replacement in Interior Scenes

author.name: Mingzhe Du, Thong Thanh Nguyen, Nguyen Tran Cong Duy, See-Kiong Ng, Luu Anh Tuan

entry.summary: MatReplace is a reference-free benchmark for material replacement in interior scenes, evaluating edits along material correctness, lighting harmony, outside preservation, and inside structure across tracks that vary one conditioning signal at a time. It avoids reference-based metric biases in the one-to-many editing setting.

entry.title: Rethinking Pre-Training and Augmentation for Zero-Shot Cross-City Object Detection

author.name: Long Hoang Pham, Quoc Pham-Nam Ho, Huy-Hung Nguyen, Duong Nguyen-Ngoc Tran, Ngoc Doan-Minh Huynh, Cu Quoc Le, Hoang-Khang Nguyen, Hyung-Min Jeon, Chi Dai Tran, Son Hong Phan, Duong Khac Vu, Trinh Le Ba Khanh, Jae Wook Jeon

entry.summary: Studies pre-training and augmentation for zero-shot cross-city object detection in traffic surveillance under privacy constraints that forbid touching target data, proposing a modular pipeline with multi-dataset pre-training and class-agnostic objectness distillation.

entry.title: LLM-Guided Contextual Action Evaluation for Operational Decisions in Industrial Processes

author.name: Youcheng Zong, Runda Jia, Dakuo He

entry.summary: LCAE uses an LLM before training to normalize fixed industrial documents into an action-observation-direction-delay relation basis, which recent action-response history then contextualizes, helping actor-critic methods learn what continuous actions affect in industrial processes.

entry.title: Evaluating Deep Multivariate Imputation Models on Wearable Device Data

author.name: Skye Goodman, Roussel Desmond Nzoyem, Leandro Junges, Peter Kissack, Yasser Qureshi, Amberly Brigden, Jeff Clark, Nawid Keshtmand

entry.summary: Develops an evaluation protocol for deep imputation models on wearable data that mines contiguous missing-run templates preserving co-missingness structure, instead of unrealistic random-point holdout, and evaluates BRITS and SAITS on epilepsy smartwatch data.

entry.title: $\texttt{findr}$: Transparent and Fair Credit Risk Decisions through Semi-Structured Regressions

author.name: Victor Medina-Olivares, Stefan Lessmann, Jonathan Crook

entry.summary: findr is a semi-structured deep regression for credit risk that decomposes the logit into an interpretable structured component and an orthogonal neural residual, with in-processing fairness constraints for transparent and auditable decisions.

entry.title: A Literate Programming Environment for Human and Machine Agents

author.name: Adam T. Burke

entry.summary: Introduces a literate programming environment for human and machine agents featuring a grammar for executable program essays, a name-graph relating prose, names, and code, and symbol-aware tooling that gives LLM coding agents IDE-like context and search.

entry.title: Parameter-Efficient Self-Supervised Adaptation for EEG-FM under Fixed Computational Budgets

author.name: Meghal Dani, Stefanie Liebe

entry.summary: Investigates parameter-efficient self-supervised adaptation of EEG foundation models, updating only 9 percent of parameters, and evaluates BIOT and CBraMod under fixed computational budgets on clinical abnormality detection, event classification, and seizure detection.

entry.title: When Does Frequency Decomposition Benefit Physics-Informed Neural Networks? A Preliminary Ablation Study

author.name: Shubham Rai

entry.summary: Introduces DBSG-PINN, a dual-branch spectrally-gated architecture separating low- and high-frequency components, used to run controlled ablations of when frequency decomposition actually helps PINNs. Challenges the assumption that Fourier features and sinusoidal activations help universally.

entry.title: CAT-GS: Balanced Multimodal Learning via Calibrated Gating and Fusion Surgery

author.name: Mahir Shahriar Tamim, Sharjil Khan, Md. Samiul Alim, Tanvir Ahmed Khan, Shafin Rahman, Nabeel Mohammed

entry.summary: CAT-GS addresses three coupled multimodal training failure modes (modality imbalance, unstable gating, fusion interference) via calibrated adaptive thresholded gating plus fusion surgery applied during backpropagation, without changing architectures or losses.

entry.title: MSR-IVA: Masked Structural Residual Independent Vector Analysis for State-Aware Fusion of Structural MRI and Dynamic Functional Network Connectivity

author.name: Victor Solomon, Zening Fu, Rafal Angryk, Vince D. Calhoun, Jingyu Liu

entry.summary: MSR-IVA fuses structural MRI with dynamic functional network connectivity via a state-aware framework combining shared structural representations, state-specific residuals, and masks for incomplete state expression, validated on Alzheimer's neuroimaging data.

entry.title: NVExplain: Explaining Time Series Forecasting with Latent Trajectory Analysis and Structure-Preserving Surrogates

author.name: Muyan Anna Li, Manikandan Ravikiran, Aditi Gautam

entry.summary: NVExplain is a model-agnostic explainability framework attributing each forecast horizon of time series models to temporally relevant historical lags via latent trajectory analysis and semantic flow, using structure-preserving surrogates.

entry.title: ShuttleArena: Interpretable Self-Play in Physics-Based Badminton

author.name: Peize Ding

entry.summary: ShuttleArena is a physics-based badminton self-play environment with continuous shuttle flight, interception, structured shot generation, and recovery, using role-conditioned policies to couple shot selection with court positioning.

entry.title: M-Fibration Theory with Applications to Neural Network Compression

author.name: Paolo Boldi

entry.summary: Extends graph fibration theory to weighted and commutative-monoid-labelled graphs, including approximate fibrations, providing a theoretical underpinning for symmetry-based neural network compression results.

entry.title: Tropospheric temperature and humidity profile retrieval from Meteosat Flexible Combined Imager based on deep learning

author.name: Alejandro Salgueiro, Johannes Rausch, Julie Th\'er\`ese Villinger, Angela Meyer

entry.summary: Develops a deep learning framework using a Residual U-Net to retrieve tropospheric temperature and humidity profiles from the Meteosat Third Generation imager without relying on numerical weather prediction background fields. This improves independence of satellite retrievals and exploits the new instrument's higher resolution and spectral coverage. Practical value for operational meteorology.

entry.title: Agentic Autoresearch for Cell-Edge Power Control: Radically Redefining the Researcher's Role

author.name: Ahmad Khan, Akram Bin Sediq, Sara Azadegi Naeini, Raviraj S. Adve

entry.summary: Demonstrates that an autonomous coding agent following an autoresearch protocol can take over the full design layer of ML for wireless resource management, including architecture, loss function, input representation, and task sampling, given only a fixed budget and immutable metric. Shows researchers can delegate experimental design in a specific engineering domain. Part of the growing AI-for-research trend.

entry.title: Evidence-Grounded Mapping of Multimodal Human Sensing Psychological Transdiagnostic Dimensions

author.name: Xiyun Hu, Xiangyuan Xue, Yuting Lyu, Hanya Shao, Jingping Nie

entry.summary: Introduces a clinician-in-the-loop benchmark evaluating whether LLMs can generate evidence-grounded B-HiTOP psychological item profiles from passive sensing, EMA, and questionnaire data, using the GLOBEM dataset with 14,592 participant-day instances aligned to 29 items across five spectra. A rigorous bridge between wearable sensing and psychiatric constructs. Careful handling of the missing-ground-truth problem via evidence-compatibility evaluation.

entry.title: Beyond Tokens: Probing Higher-Order Epistasis in Learned Protein Representations

author.name: Maryam Rahimimovassagh, Ivan Garibay, Niloofar Yousefi

entry.summary: Introduces ORBIT, an order-resolved benchmarking framework separating interaction presence, representation accessibility, and functional recovery for probing higher-order epistasis in learned protein representations, validated on synthetic landscapes and the GB1 fitness landscape. Finds no significant architecture differences in the primary comparison across 20 seeds. A careful methodological contribution to protein ML evaluation.

entry.title: The Imperfective Paradox Is Not Necessarily in Large Language Models: A Benchmark Failure Before a Model Failure

author.name: Kaiqiao Han, Yizhou Sun

entry.summary: Reexamines an NLI benchmark for the imperfective paradox and shows its conclusions rest on conceptual and evaluation mis-specifications, with 76 percent of Group A instances not explicitly ruling out culmination under a strict NLI standard. Argues a benchmark failure was mistaken for a model failure. Useful methodological correction for LLM semantic evaluation.

entry.title: Improved Analysis for Hessian-free High-resolution Monte Carlo Sampling

author.name: Wujun Lv, Xiaoyu Wang, Yingli Wang, Lingjiong Zhu

entry.summary: Establishes an explicit quantitative contraction rate for Hessian-free high-resolution dynamics under a position Poincare inequality without convexity of the potential, improving on underdamped Langevin dynamics rates, plus a weak-solution construction and spectral proof. Rigorous analysis for a Monte Carlo sampling method arising in ML. Theory contribution to sampling.

entry.title: Generative Action-Chunk Sampling for Adaptive Stiffness Control in Physical Human-Robot Collaboration

author.name: Aoi Otake, Ferdinand Hartmann, Ko Igari, Shingo Murata

entry.summary: Presents an adaptive stiffness framework for physical human-robot collaboration based on generative action-chunk sampling: the policy samples multiple future action chunks, and variation among samples continuously modulates joint stiffness and damping, yielding compliance under uncertainty and firm assistance when intention is clear. Demonstrated on real-world collaborative transport with four possible directions. Nice uncertainty-aware control idea with hardware validation.

entry.title: SAUSS: Stochastic Approximation with Unbiased Simulated Scores for Limited Dependent Variable Models

author.name: Sokbae Lee, Yuan Liao, Myung Hwan Seo, Youngki Shin

entry.summary: Proposes SAUSS, a stochastic approximation method using conditionally unbiased mini-batch simulated scores for multinomial choice models, allowing fixed per-iteration compute regardless of sample size with asymptotic theory under local conditions. Addresses computational bottlenecks in large-alternative choice modeling. Econometrics-meets-ML contribution.

entry.title: Adaptive Hybrid Subspace Levenberg Marquardt Algorithm with Adequacy Monitor for Large Scale Least Squares Problems

author.name: M. Duc Hoang, Timothy J. Lewis

entry.summary: Presents an adaptive hybrid subspace Levenberg-Marquardt algorithm for large-scale nonlinear least squares that exploits low-dimensional effective structure via an adequacy monitor, reducing per-iteration linear-solve costs. Addresses repeated damping solves through smarter subspace step acceptance.

entry.title: Multi-output Gaussian process prediction of physical fields under linear equality constraints

author.name: Mahamat Hamdan Nassouradine, Cl\'ement Gauchy, Pierre-Emmanuel Angeli, S\'ebastien da Veiga

entry.summary: Addresses multi-output Gaussian process prediction of high-dimensional physical fields under linear equality constraints, showing the common deductive strategy of eliminating one output is suboptimal and proposing a better constrained formulation. Targets surrogate modeling with uncertainty quantification in physics applications.

entry.title: Efficient Estimation of High Information Projections using Nearest Neighbours

author.name: David P. Hofmeyr

entry.summary: Proposes a dimensionality reduction method based on enhancing nearest-neighbor relationships, arising from spectral decomposition of a matrix that estimates the Density Information Matrix, a non-parametric analogue of Fisher information. Provides consistency guarantees under regularity conditions.

entry.title: GUIDE: Generative Unsupervised Chinese Query Correction via Phonetic and Visual Shared-ID Encoding

author.name: Lei Yang, Binbin Huang, Jiwei Tan, Xuhui Sui, Chang Tu, Yi Wang, Han Li

entry.summary: GUIDE is a generative unsupervised framework for Chinese query correction using a confuse-then-clarify paradigm: phonetically or visually confusable characters get shared-IDs and an encoder-decoder reconstructs the original query, constraining corrections to plausible confusions and avoiding over-correction of short ambiguous queries.

entry.title: Leveraging Speech Acts for Low-Data and Cross-Domain Conversation Derailment Forecasting

author.name: Angela Yifei Yuan, Christine De Kock, Christopher Leckie

entry.summary: Uses speech act representations as auxiliary learning signals for conversational derailment forecasting, improving low-data and cross-domain performance across three datasets. Pragmatic modeling reduces lexical noise and helps generalization to new platforms and smaller communities.

entry.title: Generative vs. Encoder Large Language Models for ASR Evaluation: A Comparative Study

author.name: Thibault Ba\~neras-Roux, Shashi Kumar, Driss Khalil, Sergio Burdisso, Petr Motlicek, Shiran Liu, Mickael Rouvier, Jane Wottawa, Richard Dufour

entry.summary: Comparative study of encoder versus generative LLMs for ASR evaluation, analyzing BERTScore and SemDist across models, layers, and pooling, and probing decoder LLMs for pairwise hypothesis selection and error classification. Finds both families achieve strong human-judgment correlation when properly configured.

entry.title: Fine-Tuning Whisper for Automatic Speech Recognition in Baniwa: A Preliminary Study

author.name: Leonardo Duart, Tiago Fonseca, Thiago Chac\'on

entry.summary: Fine-tunes Whisper for ASR in Baniwa, an indigenous Arawakan language of Brazil, Colombia, and Venezuela, using 0.54 hours of manually transcribed recordings from a linguistic documentation project. A preliminary study on extreme low-resource speech adaptation.

entry.title: Natural Language Input, Semantic Track Representation, and LLM Inference: Making the Maritime Information Exchange Model Tractable

author.name: Frederick Roth

entry.summary: Describes an architecture making the Maritime Information Exchange Model tractable with LLMs: operators contribute natural-language observations that an LLM converts into typed Semantic Assertion Records accumulated in a knowledge graph, with a second LLM pass performing inference. Removes the barrier of manually encoding observations in formal ontology languages.

entry.title: Trace Integrity for LLM Data Agents: A Vision for Auditable Structured Reasoning in Real-World Systems

author.name: Srimonti Dutta, Akshata Kishore Moharir

entry.summary: Introduces Trace Integrity, a deployment reliability criterion for LLM data agents checking whether the computation behind an answer is explicit, executable, schema-valid, operator-faithful, replayable, answer-consistent, and auditable. Identifies the Structure Gap as the failure mode making this necessary and operationalizes it via execution contracts.

entry.title: Lightweight Machine Learning-Driven Monocular Sidewalk Path Extraction for Embedded Micromobility Navigation

author.name: Lkhanaajav Mijiddorj, Yang Yan, Tyler Beringer, Bilguunzaya Mijiddorj, Alex N. Ho, Bin Xu, Binbin Weng

entry.summary: Presents a monocular sidewalk path extraction pipeline for micromobility navigation on embedded hardware, iterating through skeleton-graph, distance-transform, and lightweight image-space designs and comparing five planning methods in BEV and image space. A SegFormer-B0 student distilled with semi-supervised pseudo-labels achieves 0.946 IoU at 11.7 ms per frame.

entry.title: Semi-Supervised Adaptation of Vision-Language Models for Image Classification

author.name: Mohamed L. Mekhalfi, Mohamad M. Al Rahhal, Yakoub Bazi, Salah E. Khenfer, Mingdeng Shi, Hua Zou, Mansour Zuair

entry.summary: Proposes SE-CLIP, a semi-supervised framework for adapting CLIP to satellite scene classification with recursive label mining: a warm-up on few annotated seeds followed by iterative high-confidence discovery from unlabeled pools with safeguards for support-set integrity.

entry.title: Pose-Anchored Optical Flow for Low-Latency Human Action Anticipation in Human-Robot Teaming

author.name: Lewis de Zoete Grundy, Chris McCarthy, Christopher Fluke

entry.summary: Proposes PoseOFF, a pose-anchored optical flow representation conditioning motion feature extraction on human joints to capture localized dynamics at semantically meaningful body locations, supporting early human action anticipation for low-latency human-robot teaming.

entry.title: Asymmetric Cross-Modal Fine-Grained Visual Categorization: ACF-Net and the BirdPro Benchmark

author.name: Bohan Deng, Shuo Ye, Zitong Yu

entry.summary: ACF-Net addresses audio-visual fine-grained visual categorization where video and audio are weakly paired or not synchronized, introducing optical flow-guided motion modeling and asymmetric cross-modal adaptive fusion. It also contributes the BirdPro benchmark for this underexplored asymmetric setting. The work fills a real gap in cross-modal alignment when modalities do not correspond cleanly.

entry.title: MAMA-FLUX.2: Image-to-Image Synthesis of Post-Contrast Breast DCE-MRI for the MAMA-SYNTH Challenge

author.name: Kamil Kwarciak, Marek Wodzinski

entry.summary: MAMA-FLUX.2 performs pre-to-post contrast breast DCE-MRI synthesis via conditional latent flow matching built on FLUX.2-Klein-4B, using LoRA fine-tuning and a regional objective combining global flow matching with tumor-region supervision. This addresses the MAMA-SYNTH challenge and could reduce gadolinium contrast agent use. Application of a modern generative foundation model to a concrete clinical need.

entry.title: Fast Generative Grasping via Lie Group-Constrained MeanFlow

author.name: S. Talha Bukhari, Yi Wei, Ruiqi Ni, Zachary Kingston, Aniket Bera

entry.summary: Develops fast generative grasping by training MeanFlow on the product Lie group SO(3) x R3, coupling semigroup consistency with Riemannian conditional flow matching to enable one- or few-step grasp sampling. Addresses the latency problem of iterative diffusion/flow grasp generators in time-critical robotics.

entry.title: bert is only very slightly better than regex as a cot monitor with an emergently misaligned model and both of them are barely better than chance

author.name: nesiacel

entry.summary: An independent empirical experiment showing that a ModernBERT-based chain-of-thought monitor detects misalignment in an emergently misaligned (Thought Crime LoRA) model only barely better than chance, with regex performing almost as well. First in a planned series on CoT monitoring of emergent misalignment, with code and data released.

entry.title: Where Did D Go? A Gap Between ARC's Motivation and Its Formalism

author.name: Zach Allen

entry.summary: Critiques ARC's proposed p(doom) estimator, arguing that evaluating over a naive distribution of inputs leaves the metric open to test-deploy asymmetry attacks, drawing on trojan theory and cybersecurity practice to suggest mitigation options. A technical pre-Goodhart analysis of an emerging evaluation framework.

entry.title: PROOF-Gen: From Optimized Data to Better Distillation

author.name: Anh Ta, Junjie Zhu, Shahin Shayandeh

entry.summary: Placeholder: see prior entry for f7815205648b (XAI auditing protocol producing a Trust Score for SHAP and LIME explanations under perturbation and fidelity checks).

entry.title: Giraffe: A Mapping Architecture from Hidden Text Representations to Visual Embeddings for Efficient Graphic Design

author.name: Nejla Ghaboosi

entry.summary: Giraffe proposes a mapping architecture from hidden text representations to visual embeddings designed to reduce the token overhead of multimodal generation, targeting graphic design outputs that blend text, multiple images, and layout across thousands of tokens. It addresses the multi-token-per-image limitation of prior MLLM-to-image bridging approaches.

entry.title: Relative Time Intervals Representation for Word-level Timestamping with Masked Training

author.name: Quanwei Tang, Zhiyu Tang, Xu Li, Dong Zhang, Shoushan, Guodong Zhou

entry.summary: This work enables SpeechLLMs to produce word-level timestamps by replacing absolute with relative timestamp representations for a more compact vocabulary and stronger generalization, using hybrid fine-tuning that fully tunes timestamp modules while adapting the backbone. It moves SpeechLLMs toward temporally aligned content understanding.

entry.title: Beyond Accuracy: A Dual-Judge Evaluation Protocol for Vision-Language Models in Legally Grounded Tasks

author.name: Su Myat Noe, Ha Thanh Nguyen, May Myo Zin, Ken Satoh

entry.summary: This paper contributes a dual-judge evaluation protocol pairing a 0-10 quality judge with a strict binary semantic-equivalence judge against curated references for legally grounded vision-language tasks, studied on UK traffic-sign interpretation. It measures the calibration between quality and legal-equivalence judgments rather than mere disagreement.

entry.title: Real-World Knowledge-Guided Change Data Synthesis for Remote Sensing

author.name: Yaoyi Qi, Xingxing Weng, Chao Pang, Yongkang Cui, Xiangyu Hao, Xiaokang Zhang, Guibo Zhu, Gui-Song Xia

entry.summary: KnowChange uses pretrained vision-language models as knowledge sources to synthesize realistic change-detection training data for remote sensing, reasoning about plausible change locations and class transitions from pre-change scenes and desired change types. It replaces handcrafted transition rules that limit synthesized data diversity.

entry.title: Don't Just Listen, Try Planning: Graph-based Retrieval-Generation Agent for Long-form Audio Meeting Understanding

author.name: Quanwei Tang, Dong Zhang, Shoushan Li, Guodong Zhou

entry.summary: Constructs the LongAudioQA dataset for long-form audio meeting QA and proposes GRGA, which models heterogeneous audio features as a multi-dimensional graph and uses agent planning for retrieval and answer generation, mitigating acoustic information loss and weak long-term memory in speech LLMs.

entry.title: Structured Frequency-Domain Evidence for LLM-Based Time-Series Anomaly Detection

author.name: Jungwook Seo, Sangwon Son, Minjeong Kim, Seungmin Han, Seojin Yoo, Sungyong Baik

entry.summary: Proposes an evidence-augmented zero-shot framework for LLM-based time series anomaly detection that adds compact FFT-derived frequency-domain evidence at global and local resolutions to time-domain observations. This captures shifted periodicity and oscillatory anomalies that indexed values miss.

entry.title: SENSESHIFT: Continuous Sentiment-Controlled Text Generation via Encoder-based Mask Infilling

author.name: Shahed Masoudian, Markus Frohmann, Emmanouil Karystinaios, Navid Rekabsaz, Markus Schedl

entry.summary: SenseShift enables continuous, sentence-level sentiment control in long-form text via encoder-based mask infilling, moving beyond categorical or document-level control that dominates decoder-based controllable generation.

entry.title: StrokeGuard: A Multi-Agent Guided System for Prehospital Stroke Assessment

author.name: Wentao Yang, Zhenye Xu, Ruoyi Li, Musen Zhang, Yao Guo

entry.summary: StrokeGuard is a multi-agent system for prehospital stroke assessment that guides non-clinical users through FAST-style screening, addressing inaccurate descriptions and incomplete symptom observation in home and community settings.

entry.title: Score-Based Ideal Observer Approximation via Denoising Score Matching for Signal-Known-Exactly Detection Tasks

author.name: Weimin Zhou

entry.summary: Approximates the Bayesian Ideal Observer for signal-known-exactly detection tasks via denoising score matching, avoiding per-image MCMC posterior sampling and task-specific supervised retraining by exploiting the score function's encoding of data density geometry.

entry.title: Clearing the Underbrush: AI-Enhanced RF Interference Suppression

author.name: Rahul Jain, Pierre Trepagnier, Rick Gentile, Joey Botero, Alexia Schulz

entry.summary: Extends an autoregressive transformer-based RF interference rejection system with a Finite Scalar Quantization tokenizer layer and inference optimizations, targeting low-latency suppression of interference in digitally modulated RF signals.

entry.title: Hyperbolic Latent Geometry for Tree-Structured Prototype Networks: A Local-vs-Global Trade-off

author.name: Peter Flo, Luca Grossmann

entry.summary: Tests whether hyperbolic versus Euclidean latent manifolds for class-prototype layouts affect satisfaction of tree-structured regularizers in hierarchical classification, across 150 seed-replicated fits on WikiArt with frozen CLIP features.

entry.title: Neural-Bayesian Structure Learning for Discrete Choice Modeling

author.name: Hyunsoo Yun, Eun Hak Lee, Jiaru Zhang, Ziran Wang, Eui-Jin Kim

entry.summary: Neural-BSL couples differentiable structure learning with random-utility discrete choice estimation in one differentiable procedure, keeping observed choice outside the graph to avoid distorting recovered attribute structure, enabling counterfactual attribute adjustment.

entry.title: PaSta: Noisy Node Classification with Partial Label Learning

author.name: Yujing Liu, Yixin Liu, Yu Zheng, Yue Tan, Alan Wee-Chung Liew, Shirui Pan

entry.summary: PaSta tackles noisy node classification in graphs using partial label learning with multiple annotators capturing class distributions, avoiding overfitting and error accumulation of one-hot pseudo-label self-training.

entry.title: Why Does Graph Learning Fail to Fully Benefit from a Text Teacher?

author.name: Fumiaki Kimino (SOKENDAI), Ryoma Sato (SOKENDAI, National Institute of Informatics)

entry.summary: Investigates why combining self-supervised GNN encoders with language-model modules via alternating E-step/M-step optimization fails to deliver expected performance gains, identifying six contributing factors. A useful negative-result analysis for the LLM-plus-GNN multimodal literature. Helps calibrate expectations for text-attributed graph learning.

entry.title: VINCENT: Validated Interaction Network for Cross-drug Explanation of Therapeutics

author.name: Fan-Sheng Chuang, Xuchen Li, Yujing Bian, Kaixiong Zhou

entry.summary: Introduces VINCENT for drug synergy prediction with motif-pair explanation, identifying pairs of chemically coherent regions across two drugs that jointly drive predicted synergy, validated under repeated perturbation. Addresses the gap between built-in interpretability architectures and reliable cross-drug explanation. Relevant to drug combination discovery pipelines.

entry.title: Robust CurveMoE: Multi-Norm Adversarial Defense for Mixture-of-Experts Models via Mode Connectivity

author.name: Xu Zhang, Ren Wang

entry.summary: Proposes Robust CurveMoE, a mixture-of-experts framework for multi-norm adversarial defense that connects norm-specialized robust models via low-loss mode-connectivity paths, sharing parameters across most layers and specializing only influential ones. Reduces training cost versus optimizing competing robustness objectives jointly. Addresses practical multi-threat-model robustness.

entry.title: Modality Contribution Score - A Per-Patient Framework for Quantifying the Relative Diagnostic Contribution of Structural MRI and Amyloid PET in Alzheimer's Disease

author.name: Dawa Chyophel Lepcha, Aaliya Ali, Sophie A. Martin, Deepika Koundal, Pierrick Coupe, Shabbir Syed-Abdul

entry.summary: Introduces MCNet and the Modality Contribution Score, the first per-patient attribution framework quantifying how modality dominance shifts from structural MRI atrophy to amyloid PET across the Alzheimer's disease continuum, with per-subject normalized contributions. Adds interpretability where AI systems otherwise output a single label. Clinically meaningful granularity.

entry.title: Common-Center Geometry and Certified Radial Reconstruction for Energy-Form Full Conformal Regions

author.name: Yiheng Feng

entry.summary: Studies the geometry of full conformal prediction regions generated by energy-form pairwise scores, showing candidate-score convexity alone does not guarantee connected regions and proving that under symmetry conditions the exact conformal region is star-shaped around a common minimizer. A technical note deepening the theory of full conformal inference. Useful for certified uncertainty quantification.

entry.title: EncoTESS: Age-Sensitive Encodings from Raw TESS Light Curves

author.name: Phil R. Van-Lane (David A. Dunlap Department of Astronomy and Astrophysics, University of Toronto, Dunlap Institute for Astronomy and Astrophysics, University of Toronto, Department of Astronomy and Astrophysics, University of California San Diego), Joshua S. Speagle (David A. Dunlap Department of Astronomy and Astrophysics, University of Toronto, Department of Statistical Sciences, University of Toronto, Dunlap Institute for Astronomy and Astrophysics, University of Toronto, Data Sciences Institute, University of Toronto), Ryan Cloutier (Department of Physics and Astronomy, McMaster University), Christopher A. Theissen (Department of Astronomy and Astrophysics, University of California San Diego), Gwendolyn M. Eadie (David A. Dunlap Department of Astronomy and Astrophysics, University of Toronto, Department of Statistical Sciences, University of Toronto, Data Sciences Institute, University of Toronto), Ilay Kamai (Physics Department, Technion Israel Institute of Technology)

entry.summary: Presents EncoTESS, a time series foundation model trained on TESS 2-minute light curves producing age-sensitive encodings of stellar variability, unifying quasi-sinusoidal rotational modulation and stochastic flaring for stellar characterization. A domain foundation model with astronomy-specific design. Useful for large-scale stellar age estimation.

entry.title: Token-Oriented Semantic Communication with Pretrained Vision Transformers

author.name: Jiwoong Im, Minwoo Kim, Jaeho Lee, Yo-Seb Jeon, Yongjune Kim

entry.summary: Proposes a token-oriented semantic communication framework for client-server collaborative inference with pretrained vision transformers, transmitting token-relevance-selected compressed image latents instead of raw token embeddings, resolving cost and interoperability issues. Modular design coordinating three pretrained models. Relevant to edge AI systems.

entry.title: BVR Sim: An Open and High-Throughput Environment for Heterogeneous Air-Combat Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Haocheng Sun (Beijing University of Posts, Telecommunications), Mulai Tan (Air Force Engineering University)

entry.summary: Presents BVR Sim, an open-source Gymnasium-style environment for beyond-visual-range air-combat RL with multiple JSBIM aircraft models, configurable weapons and sensors, a unified tactical action interface over heterogeneous platforms, and interchangeable Python and accelerated backends. Fills a gap for high-throughput, partially observable, long-horizon RL research. Open release lowers barriers for this domain.

entry.title: Virgil: Navigating Explainability for Transformer-based Language Models

author.name: Martino Ciaperoni, Sezer Kutluk, Benedetta Muscato, Marta Marchiori Manerba, Fosca Giannotti

entry.summary: Virgil is an interactive system backed by a curated knowledge base that helps practitioners, including non-experts, discover and compare explainability tools for transformer language models in one interface. It addresses the fragmentation of the XAI tool ecosystem for deployed high-stakes models.

entry.title: Scalable Multi-GPU Simulation of 3D Multicellular Growth with RNN-Based Workload Balancing

author.name: Matvey Moisseyev, Huijing Du, Dandan Zheng, Chi Zhang, Hongfeng Yu

entry.summary: Presents a scalable multi-GPU framework for 3D multicellular growth simulation combining spatial binning, domain decomposition, and an RNN-based load-balancing controller that learns residual corrections to reactive repartitioning as cells grow and divide. Addresses workload drift in subcellular element simulations.

entry.title: CardioFusion-AI: Robust ECG--PPG Fusion for Multimodal Physiological Monitoring Under Signal Degradation

author.name: Navaneetha Krishnan Kamalakannan, Janakiraman Kamalakannan

entry.summary: CardioFusion-AI fuses wearable ECG and PPG signals under degradation, with a validated front end (signal-quality indexing, pulse transit time) on 53 ICU recordings and a fetal ECG database. Fusion is designed to remain reliable when one modality degrades, unlike strategies assuming equal trustworthiness.

entry.title: Semantic Variability of Replies Across LLMs: Implications for Designing Conversation-Based Assessment

author.name: Jiangang Hao

entry.summary: Examines whether LLM-generated replies remain semantically consistent when the underlying model changes, in real collaborative conversations with and without chat history. Finds model choice and context both affect similarity and alignment with human replies, warning that prompt/context engineering alone cannot preserve comparability across evolving LLMs.

entry.title: When Stale Constraints Go Unchecked: Budgeted Verification Failures in Inherited Agent Memory

author.name: Kazuki Nakayashiki

entry.summary: Models whether an agent inheriting consolidated memory can recover a superseded constraint under a scarce verification budget of two records, comparing the agent's own allocation against reassigning one slot to the critical provenance path. Shows budgeted verification failures for stale constraints.

entry.title: A Lightweight Multimodal Vision-Language Framework for Early-Stage Anatomical Green Fruit Classification in Commercial Orchards

author.name: Ranjan Sapkota, William Bu, Chen Chen, Yunjun Xu, Manoj Karkee

entry.summary: Adapts TinyCLIP with domain-specific prompts and a sliding-window scheme for fine-grained classification of early-stage apple fruitlet anatomy (calyx, body, peduncle) in orchards, supporting robotic thinning and crop-load management. Uses a 600-image dataset from two apple orchards.

entry.title: Synergising Local Geo-Environmental Characteristics with Spatial Context for Enhancing Landslide Susceptibility Mapping

author.name: Yusen Cheng, Lei Fan, Qinfeng Zhu, Cheng Zhang, Yangyang Li, Ron Mahabir

entry.summary: Proposes LGSCF, a Local-Geo and Spatial Context Fusion strategy for landslide susceptibility mapping that synergizes per-pixel geo-environmental characteristics with surrounding spatial context while filtering weakly relevant pixels. Bridges pixel-based and patch-based data representation approaches.

entry.title: Gaussian Splatting Underwater: A Controlled Cross-Regime Study

author.name: Olaya \'Alvarez-Tu\~n\'on, Stella Gra{\ss}hof

entry.summary: Benchmarks automatic weld seam segmentation from RGB and polarimetric imagery under a unified, threshold-independent protocol, comparing CNN and transformer architectures across controlled laboratory and real uncontrolled industrial conditions with multiple seeds.

entry.title: CrossMambaTuning: Synergistic Spatial and Cross-Layer Adaptation for Machine Vision Compression

author.name: Haobo Xiong, Shaobo Liu, Kai Liu, Chongyang Ding

entry.summary: CrossMambaTuning uses state space model adapters with cross-layer interaction for parameter-efficient fine-tuning of frozen learned image compression models toward downstream machine vision tasks. A scale-invariant component plus multi-scale branching captures local and global dependencies. This targets real deployment cost concerns for compression backbones.

entry.title: Leveraging Inter-object Affordances for Efficient Planning in Contact-rich Tasks

author.name: Pouya P. Niaz, Justus Piater, Alejandro Agostini

entry.summary: Proposes Unified TAMP, a task-and-motion planning method that uses object-centric abstractions of execution constraints and inter-object affordances to handle contact-rich robotic tasks. It addresses the gap between simplified planning models and real-world physical properties, aiming to reduce planning time and improve success rates.

entry.title: Barycentric Weak Inner-Product Gromov-Wasserstein

author.name: Youssef Mroueh

entry.summary: Introduces a weak Gromov-Wasserstein framework (wIGW) that compares source relations with relations between target conditional laws induced by a coupling, yielding a barycentric variational form connected to convex ordering. Generalizes GW to one-to-many settings where conditional means carry the geometry of interest.

entry.title: Your Agent's Trace Probably Cannot Tell You Who Approved a Tool Call

author.name: Jaswanth Alkur

entry.summary: Argues that production agent guardrail stacks always develop downstream dilution mechanisms (allowlists, thresholds, exceptions) that are invisible in trace logs, so one cannot reconstruct from an agent trace whether a human approved a tool call or a policy waived it. Highlights an auditability gap in deployed agent guardrails.

entry.title: Do tabular foundation models repair themselves?

author.name: Han Xiao

entry.summary: Investigates whether self-repair, common in language models where other components compensate after ablation, exists in tabular foundation models. Experiments on four SOTA tabular foundation models across 15 binary classification tasks find a negative result: redundancy is more likely than self-repair, with implications for the validity of ablation-based interpretability conclusions.

entry.title: GlucoFM: Foundation model for continuous glucose monitoring

author.name: Unknown

entry.summary: Google Research announces GlucoFM, a foundation model for continuous glucose monitoring data, part of its Health and Bioscience work. The feed provides only a headline, but a foundation model over CGM time series would enable improved glucose forecasting, glycemic event prediction, and personalized metabolic insights.

entry.title: Provable Non-Acceleration of Standard Strang Splittings of Kinetic Langevin Dynamics

author.name: Nawaf Bou-Rabee

entry.summary: Proves that standard Strang splittings of kinetic Langevin dynamics (OBABO, BAOAB) used widely in MCMC cannot achieve the O(sqrt(kappa)) accelerated mixing that friction scaling might suggest, via total variation mixing-time lower bounds uniformly over smooth strongly convex targets. A negative result clarifying limits of widely used samplers.

entry.title: Cross-Dataset Stability of Expert-Informed Skill Prompting and Fine-Tuning for Chinese Metaphor Identification

author.name: Yufeng Wu, Meichun Liu

entry.summary: Evaluates whether a fixed expert-informed procedural Skill (zero-shot) yields more stable cross-dataset performance than parameter adaptation for Chinese metaphor identification, comparing BERT fine-tuning, QLoRA LLM fine-tuning, and zero-shot prompting across three datasets. Examines cross-dataset distribution and annotation-policy effects.

entry.title: Provenance Guided Incremental Learning Under Evolving Concept Definitions

author.name: Ismail Lamaakal

entry.summary: This paper studies rule-induced concept shift, where revisions to the definitions generating prediction targets change semantic labels of stored instances without changing the data itself, and introduces a provenance-guided incremental learning framework that compiles definition changes into structured rule deltas. It extends concept-drift handling beyond statistical drift detection.

entry.title: Retrieval-augmented generation vs. deterministic tax computation in multi-agent financial advisory: A 2x2 factorial experiment

author.name: Aryan Brar, Justin Du, Avery Lor, Kylie Seto, Eric Taylor

entry.summary: This experimental study compares a deterministic tax-computation engine against RAG-retrieved advisory context in a multi-agent portfolio trade recommendation system, using a 2x2 repeated-measures design. It finds a significant main effect of the deterministic tax engine on reducing capital gains during liquidation.

entry.title: Rules Before Oracles: Auditable, User-Configurable Argument Selection for Deliberative Polling

author.name: Muntaser Syed, Markus Zanker, Marius Silaghi

entry.summary: This paper formalizes deliberative-polling argument selection as a legibility-constrained mechanism design problem, proposing seven checkable criteria and a recomputable rule with voter-held parameters so citizens can contest the exposure shaping their vote. It argues legibility is an admissibility condition rather than a tradeoff against accuracy.

entry.title: Matched Excess-Outranker Regularization for Candidate-Set Interference in Continual Knowledge Graph Embedding

author.name: Hao Ren, Junbin Gao, Jiaojiao Jiang

entry.summary: MEOR formalizes candidate-set interference in continual knowledge graph embedding, where admitting new entities can demote historical answers in ranking even when their scores and old-entity ordering are preserved, and introduces a one-sided regularization penalty that activates only when newcomer competition exceeds structurally matched references.

entry.title: Can a Dynamic Internal Field Govern a Transformer's Cognition? Certifiability, not Superiority, in Homeostatic Compute Control

author.name: Francisco M. Arrabal-Campos, Ignacio Fernandez, Francisco G. Montoya, Alfredo Alcayde

entry.summary: The authors propose a low-dimensional homeostatic internal field, governed by PDEs on a module graph, that modulates how much an adaptive-depth transformer computes without performing the computation itself. They prove a discrete Schur-Cohn stability criterion for the Verlet integrator of the field family. The work frames compute control as a certified dynamical-systems problem rather than a learned heuristic.

entry.title: A Human-Factors Guided Cognitive Model of Visuospatial Complexity in Embodied Active Vision

author.name: Vasiliki Kondyli, Jakob Suchan, Mehul Bhatt

entry.summary: This paper proposes a human-factors-grounded framework for analyzing visuospatial complexity in embodied active vision, categorizing complexity attributes as quantitative, structural, dynamic, auditory, and interactional. It grounds embodied perceptual complexity in an agent's dynamic engagement with the environment. It is a conceptual contribution bridging cognitive science and computer vision.

entry.title: From Causal Plausibility to Causal Reliability: Evaluating LLMs as Calibrated Direct Causal-Edge Classifiers

author.name: Amit Kumar, Elnur Adl Zarabi, Suranjana Trivedy, Zhiqian Chen, Lei Zhang, Kaiqun Fu, Taoran Ji

entry.summary: This paper proposes a dual-dimensional LLM framework for automated item similarity analysis in large-scale assessments, operationalizing incidental content redundancy through structured decomposition and semantic relatedness. Psychometric validation shows LLM-derived metrics align with expert judgments better than traditional metrics like BLEU or cosine similarity. It addresses quality control for automated item generation in testing.

entry.title: When Less Is More: An Empirical Study of Minimal Responses in Counseling Dialogues and the Behavior of LLMs

author.name: Zhiyang Qi

entry.summary: A cross-lingual study of minimal responses such as backchannel cues and brief empathic statements in counseling dialogues, developing a two-stage filtering method with LLM-based contextual verification. It shows counseling systems and evaluators undervalue brief listening utterances relative to content-rich replies.

entry.title: PlaceSeek: Human-Centered Geospatial Retrieval of Urban Outdoor Places via Semantic Grounding and Affective Alignment

author.name: Ziqi Cui, Shangyu Lou

entry.summary: PlaceSeek maps natural-language queries to geolocated street-view imagery for human-centered outdoor place retrieval, decomposing queries into functional and affective sub-intents with semantic grounding of physical evidence and affective alignment.

entry.title: LumiXAI: A Modular Full-Stack Framework for Feature Attribution

author.name: Alfio Ferrara, Lorenzo Gatta, Sergio Picascia, Elisabetta Rocchetti

entry.summary: LumiXAI consolidates feature attribution into a modular full-stack framework with both classification and generative attribution, an interactive GUI with bidirectional explanation, and an extensible method set aimed at non-expert users.

entry.title: COCI: Conference Organisers and Content Identifier

author.name: Angelo Salatino, Francesco Osborne, Alexis Vizcaino, Aliaksandr Birukou, Enrico Motta

entry.summary: COCI is an AI framework that extracts fine-grained structured metadata from conference calls for papers using LLMs and semantic mapping, integrating entities with OpenAlex, DBLP, TIB ConfIDent, and the AIDA Dashboard to bring grey literature into scholarly knowledge graphs.

entry.title: Deep Learning Super Resolution for Satellite Cloud Mask Downscaling

author.name: Angelos Georgakis, Valentina Kanaki, Giorgos Giannopoulos, Stella Girtsou, Ioannis Kontogiorgakis, Charalampos Kontoes, Kostas Philippopoulos

entry.summary: Proposes two deep learning super-resolution methods for downscaling SEVIRI cloud mask products and releases SEVMOD-CM, a novel cross-sensor dataset from matched MODIS and SEVIRI observations, addressing the spatial-temporal resolution trade-off in satellite cloud observation.

entry.title: Dynamic Influence-Weighted Distillation for Single-IMU Activity Recognition

author.name: Bingxuan Xie

entry.summary: Proposes dynamic influence weighting (DIW) for knowledge distillation in IMU-based activity recognition, letting a single-sensor student selectively use logit and feature targets from a multi-sensor teacher. Evaluated on the WEAR benchmark with fold-internal validation of candidate updates.

entry.title: DeMMO: Longitudinal and Cross-Disease Modelling of Digital Mobility Outcomes via Multi-Task Learning

author.name: Menghui Zhou, Zhipeng Yuan, Vitaveska Lanfranchi, Po Yang

entry.summary: DeMMO is an interpretable multi-task framework jointly modeling longitudinal digital mobility outcomes across multiple diseases and clinical outcomes, handling disease cohorts that do not share participants.

entry.title: Toward Machine Learning with the Unit as a Primitive: Learning from Unit-Linked Events

author.name: Heyang Gong

entry.summary: Proposes the unit as an explicit primitive in learning-task semantics, formalizing supervised learning as a family of unit-conditioned response laws and showing sample-only conditionals cannot distinguish homogeneity from marginalization of heterogeneous laws.

entry.title: Long-Term Behavioral Evaluation for Trusted Collaborator Selection via Bidirectional Mamba

author.name: Botao Zhu, Xianbin Wang

entry.summary: Uses bidirectional Mamba architectures for long-term behavioral evaluation of device trustworthiness in collaborator selection, combining historical behavior patterns with short-term collaborative dynamics.

entry.title: Resolving Multi-Modal Regression by Difference-Quotient-Based Clustering:Fast Coarse Conditional-Label Assignment

author.name: Huang Weiquan

entry.summary: Attributes multimodal regression mean-collapse to pairwise contradictions and proposes Difference-Quotient Clustering to partition data minimizing intra-cluster output-vs-input discrepancy, with minMSE evaluation against true outputs.

entry.title: FedQoS: Federated QoS-Risk Learning for Heterogeneous Indoor-Outdoor Access Selection

author.name: Nguyen Van Thieu, Ti Ti Nguyen, Ons Aouedi, Zerihun Huruy, Vu Nguyen Ha, Symeon Chatzinotas

entry.summary: FedQoS is a federated framework where access nodes locally learn from network logs and a global QoS-risk predictor is trained via federated aggregation to predict reliability of candidate links for indoor-outdoor access selection without centralizing user data.

entry.title: Resilient Decentralized Wireless Federated Learning via Gradient Tracking with AdamW

author.name: Nguyen Van Thieu, Ti Ti Nguyen, Ons Aouedi, Vu Nguyen Ha, Symeon Chatzinotas

entry.summary: QEF-GT-AdamW combines gradient tracking, AdamW-style adaptive optimization, and dual-stream biased quantization for communication-efficient, outage-resilient decentralized learning over wireless IoT networks with strict airtime budgets.

entry.title: Frequency-aware forecasting for short-term typhoon gust prediction

author.name: Xuefei Wang, Tingyi Liu, Heng Zhang, Shengjun Zhang

entry.summary: WDANet combines stationary wavelet decomposition, FiLM modulation, and a dual-branch encoder-decoder for short-term typhoon wind gust forecasting, separately modeling trend and fluctuation in non-stationary extreme wind.

entry.title: Modeling spatio-temporal locality in multi-step forecasting of geo-referenced time series

author.name: Annunziata D'Aversa, Gianvito Pio, Michelangelo Ceci

entry.summary: Proposes SPALT, a method for multi-step forecasting of geographically distributed sensor time series that models spatio-temporal locality using linear model trees, capturing relationships between series with similar trends even at different times. It addresses spatial autocorrelation without treating all locations under one global spatial model. Relevant to environmental and infrastructure sensor forecasting.

entry.title: Drift-Aware Multimodal User Representation Learning via Multi-Scale Temporal Modeling and Sparse Mixture-of-Experts

author.name: Ziqing Qian, Haohang Chen, Shengqi Dang, Yuhan Xiong, Canyu Shen, Jiaying Lei, Nan Cao

entry.summary: Proposes DUMoE, a framework for drift-aware multimodal user representation learning from social media, combining multi-scale temporal modeling with a sparse mixture-of-experts interest adapter that disentangles co-evolving latent interests. Targets interest drift in noisy, temporally evolving user behavior. Useful for personalization and recommendation systems.

entry.title: Cooperative Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Adaptive Aggregation in Semi-Supervised Federated Learning with non-IID Data

author.name: Rene Glitza, Luca Becker, Rainer Martin

entry.summary: Proposes pFedMARL, using multi-agent RL with TD3 to adaptively tune aggregation strategies in federated learning under non-IID data, with server-side agents weighting client contributions and client-side agents personalizing local updates. Targets semi-supervised federated settings without pre-training. Addresses the well-known heterogeneity problem in FL.

entry.title: Learning Continuous Regional Temperature Fields with Lead-Time and Resolution Queries

author.name: Chunlei Shi, Jiong Wang, Yi-Lin Wei, Junming Hou, Jinjin Liu, Yecheng Zhang, Dan Niu

entry.summary: Formulates regional 2-meter temperature forecasting as query-conditioned continuous spatiotemporal field evaluation, proposing CSTF, a neural field that treats forecast lead time and output resolution as explicit queries rather than emitting a fixed grid of future frames. Improves flexibility for downstream weather services and risk assessment. Solid applied forecasting contribution.

entry.title: Group-Shared Low-Rank Approximation for Mobile-Efficient Pointwise Convolutions in Large-Kernel CNNs

author.name: Hao Luo, Yiting Yang, Wenyi Zhao, Man Jiang, Zhijun Lin, Ghulam Mohiuddin, Ting Jiang, Kunming Luo, Zihao Zhang, Qingsen Yan, Guoqing Wang, Wei Dong, Peng Wang

entry.summary: Identifies that pointwise convolutions, not depthwise convolutions, dominate parameter volume in large-kernel CNNs (over 87 percent in RepLKNet-31B) and proposes group-shared low-rank approximation to compress them for mobile edge deployment. Addresses a real oversight in efficient architecture design. Practical for edge vision systems.

entry.title: Detection != Reliable Control: Decodable Empathy Directions Yield at Most Partial Shifts in Automated Empathy Scores

author.name: Haoran Jisun

entry.summary: Tests whether decodable empathy directions in instruction-tuned LLMs act as causal levers, finding that while both EPITOME-derived facets remain decodable and steering rewrites text, automated empathy metric shifts are at most partial, disentangling decodability, metric control, and human-perceived change. A cautionary result for steering-based interventions. Relevant to interpretability claims about linear directions.

entry.title: HCC+: Hyperbolic Guarding for Certified Attention Retrieval

author.name: Liangchen Ge

entry.summary: Introduces HCC+, a theoretical framework giving deterministic guarantees on attention retrieval in hyperbolic spaces by exploiting properties of the Poincare ball, bounding per-layer attention deviation and total variation decay under finite-precision representations. Addresses Lipschitz stability of hyperbolic attention. Theory-forward contribution to geometric deep learning.

entry.title: Behind the [MASK]: Disentangling Representation and Faithfulness in DAPF-Based Dementia Detection

author.name: Pardis Ranjbar-Noiey, Natalie Parde

entry.summary: Analyzes the interpretability of prompt-based domain-adaptive fine-tuning (DAPF) for dementia detection from spoken language, finding the best-performing model had the most recoverable diagnosis representation yet token-level attributions reflected language features rather than clinically meaningful evidence. A representational-versus-faithfulness dissociation in a clinical model. Cautionary for clinical deployment.

entry.title: WAVE: Reversing the Guidance Hierarchy for Coarse-to-Fine Guided Depth Super-Resolution

author.name: Tayyab Nasir, Daochang Liu, Ajmal Mian

entry.summary: Introduces WAVE for guided depth super-resolution, reversing the conventional fine-to-coarse guidance hierarchy via multi-level discrete wavelet transforms so low-level spatial cues are consumed late, with an interpretable feature-control mechanism to preserve depth boundaries. A focused computer vision architecture contribution. Solid but within a specialized task.

entry.title: CRAMER: Control via Request-Aware Masking for Editing Recommenders

author.name: Zhiyuan Julian Su, Naihe Feng, Zhen Luther Qin, Ga Wu

entry.summary: Presents CRAMER, a framework letting natural-language user requests immediately modify sequential recommendation model behavior via request-aware masking, inspired by model editing and avoiding backbone retraining or LLM inference overhead. Improves responsiveness of large-scale recommenders to timely user intent. Practical recommendation control contribution.

entry.title: AERIS: Offline Policy Improvement for Multi-UAV Integrated Sensing and Communication

author.name: Ziyuan Wang (Steven), Yifan Sui (Steven), Wei Wei (Steven), Wenjie Xin (Steven), Zekai Zhang (Steven), Xiangwang Hou (Steven), Xiao-Ping (Steven), Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes AERIS, an offline policy improvement framework for multi-UAV integrated sensing and communication in 6G, learning from fixed flight logs under centralized training and decentralized execution to balance communication quality, sensing reliability, and flight safety without risky online trial-and-error. Addresses a practical constraint of real UAV deployment. Competent domain RL contribution.

entry.title: A Multi-View Coupled Tensor Decomposition for Lightweight Online Adaptive Traffic Prediction

author.name: Quan Yu, Jie Ni, Yu-Hong Dai, Xiongjun Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes MVCTD, a coupled tensor decomposition model for online traffic prediction that jointly models shared spatial structure and view-specific temporal dynamics across speed, flow, and occupancy views, with group sparse regularization to handle missing data and anomalies. Targets practical intelligent transportation settings with imperfect sensing.

entry.title: Unsupervised Anatomical Feature Learning via Diffusion Models: Enhanced Medical Image Segmentation with Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Models

author.name: Akshat G, Divyansh Gupta, Shaleen Bhatnagar, Shilpa Ankalaki, Tusar Kanti Mishra

entry.summary: Uses a DDPM trained on 21 unlabeled abdominal CT scans to learn anatomical representations, transferring the encoder to BTCV multi-organ segmentation and improving liver Dice from 0.75 to 0.93. Demonstrates unsupervised diffusion pretraining as an alternative to scarce pixel-level medical annotations.

entry.title: SAMpLE: A SystemC-AMS Machine LEarning-based Framework for Virtual Prototyping

author.name: Andrei Mihai Albu, Sara Vinco

entry.summary: SAMpLE is an open-source SystemC-AMS framework integrating ML models as first-class Timed Dataflow components via a standardized plug-and-play interface, with native C++ online-training and offline execution backends. Brings reuse, comparability, and reproducibility to ML in embedded virtual prototyping.

entry.title: VietAIDetector: An Open-Source Zero-Shot Detector for Vietnamese AI-Generated Text

author.name: Trieu Hai Nguyen, Van-Dung Hoang

entry.summary: VietAIDetector is an open-source zero-shot tool for detecting Vietnamese AI-generated text, built on Binoculars-style methods with a Gradio interface handling raw text, scanned documents, and long inputs beyond LLM context. Requires no domain-specific training data.

entry.title: A Dual-Transformer for Multi-Camera View Recommendation

author.name: Josep Cabacas-Maso, Carles Ventura, Ismael Benito-Altamirano

entry.summary: A Dual-Transformer with cross-attention decouples temporal encoding of past frames from candidate camera-view querying for multicamera editing, claiming large SOTA gains on the TVMCE dataset. The design lets each candidate camera independently interrogate a memory of recent history. Relevant to automated media production workflows.

entry.title: EgoNav: Bridging Learned Waypoints and Geometry-Aware Local Control for Robust Indoor Navigation

author.name: Jing Wang, Shiqi Zhao, Hairong Qu, Peng Yin

entry.summary: EgoNav is a hierarchical indoor navigation system that combines learned image-goal waypoint prediction with a geometry-aware local controller that enforces collision avoidance. It bridges the common gap where waypoint predictors produce geometrically infeasible targets in topological-map navigation.

entry.title: PRISM: Projection-Integrated Sampling-Based MPC with Bayesian Cost Tuning for Bimanual Manipulation

author.name: Alinjar Dan, Iryna Hurova, Karl Kruusam\"ae, Arun Kumar Singh

entry.summary: PRISM is a GPU-accelerated sampling-based MPC framework for bimanual manipulation that uses a physics simulator as an online world model. Its key contribution is a QP-guided control sampling strategy that projects sampled trajectories onto kinematically feasible sets, decoupling exploration from feasibility.

entry.title: Trust-Aware Sequential Decision Making and Rollout Planning for Resilient Multi-Robot Systems

author.name: Roee M. Francos, Daniel Garces, Orhan Eren Akg\"un, Nathaniel D. Bastian, Stephanie Gil

entry.summary: Studies multi-robot routing under localization spoofing, introducing a distance-constrained spoofing model for monitor-aware adversaries and a trust-aware monitor combining probabilistic localization trust calibrated with real GPS spoofing data plus behavioral evidence. Provides resilient sequential decision-making and rollout planning.

entry.title: A General Framework for Metropolis-Adjusted Dikin Walks: Dimension-Square Mixing on Polytopes and Log-Det Walks on Spectrahedra

author.name: Zhao Song, Lichen Zhang

entry.summary: Analyzes Metropolis-adjusted Dikin walks, proving warm-start mixing bounds for the regularized Lee-Sidford walk on polytopes and a log-det walk on spectrahedra, with a shared acceptance-to-mixing reduction. Provides dimension-square mixing guarantees for exact-metric Markov chain Monte Carlo on constrained domains.

entry.title: How researchers adapted Dolma for better Thai language models

author.name: Unknown

entry.summary: Thai researchers adapted Ai2's open Dolma data toolkit to build Mangosteen, a 47-billion-token Thai corpus that filters low-quality web data while maintaining or improving model performance and strengthening Thai cultural knowledge. Demonstrates effective open-source data curation for a lower-resource language.

entry.title: Skeleton-based Zero-Shot Spatio-Temporal Action Localization via Weakly-Supervised Pretraining

author.name: Koshiro Nagano, Fumiaki Sato, Ryo Hachiuma, Kazuki Tsutsukawa, Taiki Sekii

entry.summary: This paper proposes weakly-supervised vision-language pretraining for skeleton-based zero-shot spatio-temporal action localization, switching pooling kernels from video-level alignment during pretraining to instance-level features at inference without target-action training. It includes a scene-mixed data strategy to reduce annotation cost. Niche but well-motivated zero-shot extension of action localization.

entry.title: Ethical LLM-Assisted Research: A Framework for Responsible Delegation, Verification, and Epistemic Value

author.name: Kalin Stoyanov

entry.summary: This paper develops a normative framework for responsible delegation of scientific reasoning to LLMs, treating science as a distributed process where contribution origin may be human or machine while responsibility for acceptance into the record remains human. It specifies conditions under which delegated reasoning preserves epistemic legitimacy and accountable authorship.

entry.title: Maia 200: A Software Defined Dataflow System for Large-scale AI Acceleration

author.name: Sherry Xu, Marco Heddes, Jackson Peng, Tom Savell, Monica Tang, Prashant Ranjan, Jesse Benson, Ofer Dekel, Saurabh Dighe, Anupama Kurpad, Artour Levin, Matthew Mattina, George Petre, Cheng Tang, Yuan Yu, Li Zhang, Torsten Hoefler

entry.summary: We covered the Maia 200 paper in Research yesterday, Maia 200 is a Microsoft AI accelerator delivering 10,145 Tflop/s FP4 and 5,072 Tflop/s FP8 in a 750W envelope with 7 TB/s HBM bandwidth, exemplifying Software Defined Locally Accessed Dataflow architecture that programs dataflow engines around specialized memories and a Flynn-inspired data management taxonomy.

entry.title: LAION-BVD: A 10-Million-Hour Open Video Dataset for Multimodal Pre-training

author.name: Andreas Hochlehnert, Marianna Nezhurina, Mehdi Cherti, Andrej Radonjic, Thadd\"aus Wiedemer, Christoph Schuhmann, Romain Beaumont, Wieland Brendel, Bernhard Sch\"olkopf, A. Sophia Koepke, Jenia Jitsev, Matthias Bethge

entry.summary: We covered the LAION-BVD dataset release in Research yesterday, Releases LAION-BVD, a large open video dataset of 80M videos totaling 10 million hours, built for multimodal pre-training across video, audio, and image modalities with synthetic captions and content-aware scene detection. Models trained on it achieve competitive video-text and audio-text benchmark performance with consistent scaling gains.

entry.title: Incorporating Cognitive Load and Knowledge Transfer for Multi-Domain Knowledge Tracing

author.name: Haotian Zhang, Shucun Wang, Jinze Wu, Liang Ding, Shuochen Liu, Zhenya Huang, Jing Sha, Shijin Wang, Qi Liu

entry.summary: This paper proposes a multi-domain knowledge tracing method incorporating cognitive load from managing learning across domains and knowledge transfer between related states, improving student knowledge-state assessment over single-domain methods. It targets realistic learning scenarios where students study multiple subjects simultaneously.

entry.title: Eating for a Sustainable Planet: Personalized Sustainable Diet Recommendation via Constraint-Aware Decision-Making Modeling

author.name: Ying Jin, Weiqing Min, Mingyu Huang, Shuqiang Jiang

entry.summary: This paper proposes a constraint-aware decision-making model for personalized sustainable diet recommendation, incorporating nutrition, affordability, cultural acceptability, and environmental impact as learnable constraints rather than user preferences, to handle inter-individual heterogeneity. It targets individual-level adoption of population-level sustainability goals.

entry.title: Implicit Q-learning-bootstrapped ant colony optimization for maritime moving-target observation scheduling with agile satellites

author.name: He Wang, Junyu Wu, Yeye Liu, Yifan Zhou, Jie Zhang, Hui Li, Yanjie Song, Liang Li

entry.summary: IQACO combines implicit Q-learning with ant colony optimization for maritime moving-target observation scheduling with agile satellites, where moving sea targets make feasible windows vary dynamically. Rather than learning a task-selection policy directly, it bootstraps the ACO with learned value estimates. It handles time-window, attitude, onboard-resource, and cloud-availability constraints jointly.

entry.title: LDAC-Net: A Learnable Multi-Lag Differencing Attention-Convolution Network for Drift-Robust Recognition with Low-Cost MOX Gas Sensors

author.name: Xin Zhang, Liangxiu Han, Yue Shi, Tam Sobeih

entry.summary: LDAC-Net is an end-to-end learnable multi-lag differencing attention-convolution network for drift-robust gas and odour recognition with low-cost MOX sensors, replacing fixed first-order temporal differencing with learnable feature enhancement.

entry.title: Same-Player Verification for Account Consistency in Counter-Strike 2

author.name: Xuchen Zhang

entry.summary: Formulates same-player verification in Counter-Strike 2 as behavioral fingerprint matching: encoding a player's trajectory in a match replay and judging whether two observations come from the same real player, to support account-integrity review for boosting and smurfing. Novel application formulation for competitive gaming integrity. Focused niche contribution.

entry.title: Multi-View Trust Evaluation for Collaborator Selection via Evidential Deep Learning

author.name: Botao Zhu, Xianbin Wang

entry.summary: Proposes a multi-view evidential learning method for trust evaluation in collaborator selection, modeling heterogeneous, multi-source trust data per task and device view with evidential uncertainty. Addresses accurate trustworthiness inference in distributed systems. Companion work to a related trust paper in this batch.

entry.title: Choose Your Game Wisely: Measuring Game-Theoretic Structures in Real-World Vehicle Interactions

author.name: Yueyuan Li, Rongcheng Nie, Weijie Xi, Mingyang Jiang, Songan Zhang, Hanyang Zhuang, Ming Yang
