entry.summary: Develops a trajectory-based framework to measure whether real-world vehicle interactions follow simultaneous, sequential, or asymmetric game-theoretic structures, quantifying behavioral change onset, response dynamics, and ordering stability across six trajectory datasets including INTERACTION, highD, inD, and rounD. Provides empirical grounding for interaction modeling assumptions.

entry.title: Schr\"odinger Bridges over Kinetic Swarming Models

author.name: Asmaa Eldesoukey, Md Zulfiqur Haider, Italo Napolitano, Yongxin Chen, Abhishek Halder

entry.summary: Formulates finite-horizon minimum-energy collective steering of stochastic inertial swarms as Schrodinger bridge problems over mean-field Cucker-Smale and Morse interaction models, connecting bridge methods to bio-inspired swarm control for applications like targeted therapy and evacuation.

entry.title: Characterizing Full Nonequilibrium Dynamics of Simple Exclusion Processes

author.name: Zhimao Liu, Jing Liu, Pan Zhang, Ying Tang

entry.summary: Uses variational autoregressive networks to characterize full nonequilibrium dynamics of simple exclusion processes (SSEP, ASEP, TASEP) in one to three dimensions, reproducing known finite-time results and extending to previously intractable cases including 3D finite-time analysis. Demonstrates neural variational methods on a classic statistical physics challenge.

entry.title: Auditing the Synthetic Memoir: Measuring Scene-Level Confabulation in LLM-Generated Autobiography Against the Documented Record of the Life It Describes

author.name: Heather Renze

entry.summary: A scene-level case-study audit quantifies how much of an LLM-generated autobiography is confabulated, checking 366 first-person entries against a ground-truth corpus of the subject's own life using a fixed rubric. It is presented as the first quantified audit of LLM-generated memoir against documented records.

entry.title: Evolutionary Recurrent Decision Model in Developing Adaptive and Maladaptive Behaviors

author.name: Andrew Hu

entry.summary: ERDM is a reinforcement learning framework simulating agents in evolutionarily recurrent environments to examine how evolutionary mismatch, bounded rationality, and satisficing produce adaptive and maladaptive behaviors like learned helplessness and aggression. A validity study under varying adverse childhood experience conditions shows such strategies emerge without hardwiring.

entry.title: A Behavior-Guided Online Probabilistic Forecasting Method for Electric vehicle Charging Loads

author.name: Chenghan Li, Qingxiang Liu, Yinliang Xu, Yuxuan Liang

entry.summary: This paper proposes a behavior-guided online probabilistic forecasting framework for EV charging loads, using a dual-timescale behavior representation to separate persistent station-specific charging patterns from recent behavioral changes. The behavioral signals then modulate online forecasting under evolving operating conditions. It targets a concrete smart-grid forecasting need.

entry.title: Revelation Control

author.name: Qinyou Wang

entry.summary: Introduces Revelation Control, a decision-theoretic framework for choosing priced interventions that reveal hidden state only when the revealed distinctions can change a downstream decision. It defines decision-sufficient revelation and revelation depth and derives a cost-adjusted factorization criterion for learning systems.

entry.title: QML for Quantum Sensing under Measurement-Induced Information Loss

author.name: Sounak Bhowmik, Himanshu Thapliyal

entry.summary: Frames magnetic-field estimation in NV-center diamond magnetometry as supervised regression and compares quantum machine learning models under NISQ-era noise, finite shots, and measurement-induced information loss. It evaluates which QML approaches improve parameter estimation from limited sensing data.

entry.title: Markerless Pose Estimation for Resistance Training Technique Assessment

author.name: Joseph Turner, Jeff Clark, Nawid Keshtmand

entry.summary: Applies markerless pose estimation with BlazePose to resistance training technique assessment, converting joint-angle trajectories from squat, bench press, and deadlift videos into quantitative error measures against reference repetitions.

entry.title: Multimodal Injury Risk Prediction in Tennis

author.name: Francisco Erramuspe Alvarez, Shobharani Polasa, Weihao Qu, Jay Wang, Ling Zheng

entry.summary: PART is a multimodal framework for tennis player performance and injury risk prediction, integrating wearable and alternative data sources where prior tennis-specific work is sparse.

entry.title: Quantum-Inspired Modeling of Driving Behavior

author.name: Mohammad Elayan, Omid Armantalab, Wissam Kontar

entry.summary: Introduces a quantum-inspired representation of driver behavior in which each driver is encoded as an evolving density matrix capturing behavioral uncertainty, temporal evolution, and learned interactions among behavioral variables. Aims to reconcile flexibility with interpretability in heterogeneous driving behavior modeling. Novel framing for transportation modeling.

entry.title: PA-CoT: Profile-Adaptive Chain-of-Thought for Personalized Nutritional Consulting

author.name: Evgenii Garmashov, Nikita Kulin, Artur Khairullin, Viktor Zhuravlev, Daniil Sukhorukov, Mikhail Mozikov, Ilya Makarov, Sergey Muravyov

entry.summary: Proposes PA-CoT, a multi-stage prompting method treating user-profile interpretation as an explicit standalone reasoning step for personalized nutritional consulting, plus the QPA benchmark of 200 samples scored on four criteria, compared against 11 prompting baselines. Addresses the structural gap of unstructured profile passing in health prompting. Modest but well-structured contribution.

entry.title: BanglaMamba: Exploring State Space Models for Bangla Fake News Detection

author.name: M. K. Khalidi Siam

entry.summary: Explores Mamba-based state space models for Bangla fake news detection, comparing BanglaMamba against pretrained BanglaBERT and a from-scratch BERT, with BanglaBERT achieving the highest Macro-F1 (0.9260). A low-resource-language efficiency study where the SSM alternative does not beat the transformer. Honest negative-leaning result.

entry.title: TrustFormer: Cross-Temporal and Cross- Dimensional Transformer for Task-Specific Multi-Dimensional Trust Evaluation

author.name: Botao Zhu, Xianbin Wang

entry.summary: Proposes TrustFormer, a task-specific transformer for multi-dimensional trust evaluation handling asynchronous trust data across dimensions and their intra- and inter-dimensional dependencies. Moves beyond scalar trust representations in dynamic collaborative systems. Same authors as the evidential trust paper, indicating a focused research program.

entry.title: Energy Yield and Lifetime Climate Classification via Machine Learning for Optimizing Photovoltaic Module Design and Materials

author.name: Youri Blom, Sofia Dutto, Alexandru Costache, Rowan Richie, Ruben Pelsser, Wesley Berger, Jing Sun, Rudi Santbergen, Olindo Isabella, Malte Ruben Vogt

entry.summary: Develops a PV-specific climate classification framework using ML that incorporates energy yield and, for the first time, module lifetime with climate-dependent degradation, using an interpolated dataset of twelve input features and two targets. Supports geographically tailored photovoltaic module design and materials selection. Solid applied sustainability contribution.

entry.title: Opportunities of Self Supervised Learning for GNSS: Evaluation of a Deep Learning-Enhanced PVT Algorithm

author.name: Thomas Barbero, Bertrand Ekambi

entry.summary: Applies deep learning to GNSS positioning by jointly predicting range corrections and uncertainty, with a JEPA-based self-supervised pretraining stage on unlabeled GNSS data. Evaluated on driving scenarios, it improves positioning accuracy in harsh urban multipath conditions.

entry.title: DESCENT: Directed Edge Scene Encoding for Airport Surface Movement Prediction

author.name: Alexander Prutsch, David Schinagl, Horst Possegger

entry.summary: DESCENT is a transformer-based architecture for airport surface movement prediction, featuring Potential Reachable Set context sampling and a detection-transformer decoder to handle heterogeneous dynamics and strict topological constraints. It extends motion forecasting, well studied in autonomous driving, to an underexplored aviation domain.

entry.title: PARAssist: A Framework for Personalized and Adaptive Robotic Assistance from Ambiguous User Requests

author.name: Pourya Aliasghari, Goldie Nejat

entry.summary: PARAssist is a service-robot architecture that disambiguates ambiguous user requests in a personalized way, using vision-language models to assess task demands and passively learning user preferences by contrasting tasks users perform independently versus request help with. Generates task candidates from user history for context-aware assistance.

entry.title: PhaseShift: Topology-Aware Data Harmonization and Model Consolidation Across Signalized Intersections

author.name: Yash Ranjan, Artur Kumik, Rahul Sengupta, Anand Rangarajan, Sanjay Ranka

entry.summary: PhaseShift harmonizes heterogeneous roadside trajectories across signalized intersections into a shared actor-centric representation to train one reusable traffic-behavior backbone, supporting pooled operation, zero-shot transfer to held-out intersections, and low-data adaptation. Evaluated on five intersections in two Florida regions.

entry.title: Learning the Kohn-Sham map with neural operators for quasi-linear scaling density functional theory

author.name: Danish Khan, Maurice D. Hanisch, Nikolai Argatoff, Evan Xie, Sandeep Sharma, Anima Anandkumar

entry.summary: We covered the full Kohn-Sham neural operators paper in Research yesterday, Identifies the Kohn-Sham map, from potential to density, as the right learning target for orbital-free DFT, using neural operators to achieve quasi-linear scaling electronic structure calculations. This avoids ill-conditioned kinetic-energy functional learning and poor extrapolation of direct ground-state prediction.

entry.title: Constrained Hyperparameter Optimization for Streaming Data

author.name: Bruno Veloso, Jo\~ao Gama

entry.summary: Addresses hyperparameter optimization for streaming data with boundary constraint-handling techniques so that self-adjusting online optimization operators do not propose invalid solutions in bounded search spaces.

entry.title: Lowering the Barrier to AI-Driven Inspection: A No-Code Workflow for Automated Structural Defect Detection

author.name: Michael Holm, Tanner McElroy, Xinghang Zhang, Guang Lin

entry.summary: Presents a no-code workflow enabling non-experts to build automated structural defect detection pipelines for structural health monitoring, lowering adoption barriers that limit CV use in SHM. Engineering-deployment contribution rather than a new method. Practical for condition-based maintenance.

entry.title: Simulating Cognitive Smart Freight Corridors with Agent-Based Models and Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Madelaine Martinez-Ferguson, Chun Wang, Mustafa Can Camur, Xueping Li

entry.summary: Presents an agent-based modeling framework for smart freight corridors coupling physical infrastructure, V2X connectivity, and a decision layer with RL and MARL for platoon formation and charging coordination, evaluated across three scenarios on throughput, congestion, energy, emissions, and robustness. Preliminary results favor the cognitive scenario. Simulation-stage transportation research.

entry.title: Low-Resolution Perception for Robotic Packing

author.name: Giuseppe Fabio Preziosa, Federico Vignoni, Chiara Castellano, Marco Faroni, Andrea Maria Zanchettin, Paolo Rocco

entry.summary: This work shows that low-cost, low-resolution depth sensing is a practical option for robotic packing by jointly selecting next-best views and deciding when to grasp via reconstruction cues and grasp-evidence stability estimates. Validated through ablations and end-to-end experiments.

entry.title: When Obstacles Bend: Modeling Vegetation Deformation in the context of Field Robotics

author.name: Muhammad Hsaeeb Zaar Khizar, Tom Montagnon, Roland Lenain, Romuald Aufr\`ere, Johann Laconte

entry.summary: Proposes characterizing vegetation deformation properties directly rather than from a robot-centric traversability perspective, so assessments transfer across platforms in field robotics. Models how obstacles bend when contacted by robots in natural environments.

entry.title: A Mathematical Theory of Interpretation: Rational Entropy, Spectral Readout, and Confusability as a Resource

author.name: Blake Reynolds

entry.summary: Presents an abridged mathematical theory treating interpretation as observer-relative spectral measurement under an access structure, introducing Rational Entropy and results on confusability and unique utility maxima. It frames interpretation as a method-design problem determined by access, query, utility, and medium.

entry.title: Geometry-Constrained Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks: Learning Edge Geometry via Banach Duality

author.name: K S Sesh Kumar

entry.summary: Applies a Random Forest classifier and computer-vision-based waste sorting to quantify the relationship between household waste disposal practices and illness patterns in Kumasi, Ghana, extending a 2022 descriptive field study. Provides quantitative validation of a public-health association in a low-resource setting. Applied, community-focused work.

entry.title: Forecasting Weather-Driven Price Dynamics Across Sri Lankan Tea Market Catalogues

author.name: Hesandi Mallawarachchi, Senilka Madurapperumage, Nadil Kulathunge, Thilokya Angeesa, Nethsith Gunaweera, Sandeepa Weerasekara, Patalee Narasinghe, Nisansa de Silva, Sandareka Wickramanayake

entry.summary: Builds a structured dataset from 105 weekly Colombo Tea Auction broker reports (late 2023 to 2026) plus region-specific weather data and applies Granger causality and tree-based models to forecast weather-driven price dynamics across four tea catalogues. A solid domain-specific data contribution for agricultural economics. Applied forecasting study.

entry.title: A Primer on Computational Semantics for Artificial Intelligence Systems

author.name: Casey Kennington

entry.summary: A primer on computational semantics for AI systems covering formal, grounded, and distributional semantics and comparing transformer LMs with human language learning. Aimed at building informed understanding of meaning representation in modern models.

entry.title: AGRO-Nav: Autonomous Graph-based Orchard Navigation

author.name: Ho Young Yun, Jaemin Yu, Duksu Kim

entry.summary: AGRO-Nav builds a sparse topological graph from SLAM trunk clusters for autonomous orchard navigation, using Dijkstra plus Theta* and B-spline smoothing without manual waypoints. Real-orchard trials show accurate row-center following in semi-structured agricultural environments.

entry.title: Announcing the MATS Residency: A New Path for Experienced Researchers Working on AI Safety, or Moving Into it

author.name: Raj Thimmiah

entry.summary: Announces the MATS Residency, a 6-24 month program for experienced researchers pursuing sustained AI safety research agendas, citing 630+ accelerated researchers, 215+ papers, and organizations founded including Apollo Research. Program announcement with application dates for the 2027 winter intake.

entry.title: Gating Before Commitment: Anticipating Intent Divergence to Prevent Post-Interaction Decision Failures in Autonomous Driving

author.name: Cong Xu, Ravi Sankar

entry.summary: Presents a language-guided intent module that computes an intent-geometry divergence score to gate planned driving maneuvers before commitment, preventing post-interaction planning failures. Evaluated on a handful of replayed clips with disclosed implementation and calibration analysis.

entry.title: [Macroagents] 1. The Macroagent Ontology

author.name: Towards_Keeperhood

entry.summary: Introduces a macroagent ontology abstracting over teams, companies, AI scaffolds, countries, and markets as optimization processes with agentic subsystems, intended as groundwork for design lenses to improve alignment and epistemics of human systems and AI societies. First post in a conceptual mini-sequence.

entry.title: AI safety through the lens of uncertainty quantification (UQ).

author.name: arradiat

entry.summary: A PhD student in Bayesian deep learning observes that mainstream AI safety literature largely ignores uncertainty quantification and proposes UQ as a lens on AI safety. Reflective commentary connecting two research communities.

author.name: Andrea Di Nezza, Mihir Patel, Fabio Fagnani, Sara Bernardini

author.name: Jing Huang, Jihong Zhang, Hua-Hua Chang

entry.summary: arXiv:2608.24825v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The rapid expansion of large-scale assessments and the growing adoption of automatic item generation have intensified concerns about incidental content...

author.name: Esmail Gumaan

author.name: Zizhe Wang

entry.summary: arXiv:2608.23653v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: AI agents are increasingly used for simulation-driven engineering. Physical system modeling presents different requirements from general-purpose code...

author.name: Sathishkumar Sivashanmugam

entry.summary: arXiv:2608.23658v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: An LLM serving engine sizes its key-value (KV) cache once, at startup, permanently setting aside a reserve for the worst-case prefill activation. Dur...

author.name: Shashwat Pandey, Satwik Pandey, Suresh Raghu

entry.summary: arXiv:2608.23663v2 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Aligning deployed language models requires knowing when their outputs can be trusted, yet on-device models now ship to hundreds of millions of device...

author.name: Alessandro Tutone, Giorgio Franceschelli, Mirco Musolesi

entry.summary: arXiv:2608.23705v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly capable of generating text that challenges human performance in domains requiring creativity, yet evalu...

author.name: Irene Trigueros-Lorca, Leonardo Concepci\'on, Christian Wagner, Isaac Triguero, Daniel Molina

entry.title: VirTooS: A ROS 2 - Unity Virtualization Toolkit for Fleet Management of Autonomous Mobile Robots

author.name: Andrea Drudi, Lorenzo Pichierri, Andrea Testa, Giuseppe Notarstefano

entry.summary: VirTooS is a Python/C# toolkit coupling ROS 2 and Unity for scalable virtual fleet management experiments with autonomous mobile robots, supporting mixed-reality setups with virtual and real sensors and distributed task assignment experiments. Released as an open toolkit for the robotics community.

entry.title: Developing frames

author.name: Richard_Ngo

entry.summary: Richard Ngo publishes a previously unreleased 2023 essay from his meta-rationality sequence exploring how frames are structured and how that affects learning and improvement, connecting to the frame problem in AI and philosophy. Conceptual epistemology writing with a note that his current thinking has moved on.

entry.title: Against Modesty’s Bailey

author.name: Zvi

entry.summary: Zvi argues against modesty arguments that defer wholesale to expert consensus, contending that a smart informed person sincerely asserting X can cease to be evidence for X once social pressures and information cascades are considered. Epistemics essay engaging with Yudkowsky-adjacent discussion.

entry.title: LLMs are Adaptation-Executers, not Understanding-Maximizers

author.name: olehif

entry.summary: Argues LLMs resemble biological adaptation-executers more than understanding-maximizers, using a cellular analogy where emergent behavior arises from many small learned conditionals rather than built structure. Speculative conceptual framing of LLM cognition.

entry.title: The central fallacy: the second-worst argument in the world

author.name: Connor Williams

entry.summary: A philosophy essay proposing a second-worst argument in the world — the central fallacy — as a complement to Scott Alexander's category-based worst argument, analyzing how discourse misuses central versus noncentral category members. Intellectual commentary rather than empirical research.

entry.title: My MATS 11.0 Application Experience

author.name: Evan Conway

entry.summary: A first-person account of applying to the MATS AI safety fellowship and being accepted into the OpenAI safety team stream, with advice for future applicants. Community advice post rather than research.

entry.title: "So You Don't Trust Me?"

author.name: Zack_M_Davis

entry.summary: An essay analyzing the logic of the phrase so you don't trust me, arguing that trustworthiness must be communicated via statements a dishonest person could not equally make, illustrated through a Rand passage. Philosophical commentary.

entry.title: Being Neurotic about Fertility: Notes from the 2026 Reproductive Frontiers Conference

author.name: boba_girl

entry.summary: Personal notes from the 2026 Reproductive Frontiers Conference covering fertility and embryo selection information relevant to personal family planning. Lifestyle and health commentary with an epistemic disclaimer that the author is not a scientist.

entry.title: The Brain Preservation Summit - September 19-20th at Sparks Brain Preservation in Salem, OR

author.name: Andy_McKenzie

entry.summary: Announcement of a Brain Preservation Summit in September 2026 at a preservation facility in Oregon, focused on structural brain preservation aimed at future revival. Community event announcement.

entry.title: Would this research outline be interesting? I would like to hear your opinions.

author.name: R U

entry.summary: A speculative early-stage research outline arising from personal experience using AI to create spaced-repetition cards, asking for feedback on whether the idea is interesting. Explicitly marked as unsystematic and preliminary.

entry.title: Monday for Future

author.name: Ondřej Lukeš

entry.summary: Announcement of an AI risk protest event in Prague on August 31 with speakers including Czech MPs. Advocacy/community organizing content, not research.

entry.title: Clearing My Foggy Glasses

author.name: adamShimi

entry.summary: A personal essay on studying Zen Buddhism and zazen meditation, discussing how direct engagement dissolved prior aversions. Reflective writing with no technical content.

entry.title: Short Time Outs

author.name: jefftk

entry.summary: A short parenting note arguing that brief, predictable time-outs (about a minute regardless of age) work as well as the standard one-minute-per-year recommendation. Anecdotal n=3 personal essay.

entry.title: Research Summary: August 26, 2026

author.name: AATF AI News Aggregator

entry.summary:
Today's highlights span AI hardware, open data resources, and embodied AI. Maia 200 debuts as a software-defined accelerator delivering 10,145 Tflop/s FP4 and 7 TB/s HBM bandwidth at 750W, while LAION-BVD releases 10 million hours of open video for multimodal pretraining.

  • Embodied AI: ARLI enables RL finetuning of robot policies despite inference latency breaking Markovianity; WorldEcho diagnoses whether world models faithfully follow actions; TrAct uses visual tracks as embodiment-agnostic interfaces; GlanceWAM decouples asynchronous latent imagination from control
  • Scientific computing and health: neural-operator Kohn-Sham mapping targets quasi-linear scaling DFT; LUCAID delivers a clinically validated nine-module agentic pathology workflow; INCEPT pretrains an EEG foundation model on 11,000+ hours of clinical data
  • Safety, security, and evaluation: TrustShiftProbe characterizes staged trust attacks on MCP servers; an AP2 protocol analysis audits emerging payment-agent standards; a perturbation audit reveals decorative chain-of-thought across 14 LLMs; an AI voice-agent honeypot yields behavioral insights from 10,211 real scam calls
  • Reasoning efficiency: Parason exploits subtask and trial parallelism to cut sequential test-time-compute latency
entry.content:
Today's highlights span AI hardware, open data resources, and embodied AI. Maia 200 debuts as a software-defined accelerator delivering 10,145 Tflop/s FP4 and 7 TB/s HBM bandwidth at 750W, while LAION-BVD releases 10 million hours of open video for multimodal pretraining.

  • Embodied AI: ARLI enables RL finetuning of robot policies despite inference latency breaking Markovianity; WorldEcho diagnoses whether world models faithfully follow actions; TrAct uses visual tracks as embodiment-agnostic interfaces; GlanceWAM decouples asynchronous latent imagination from control
  • Scientific computing and health: neural-operator Kohn-Sham mapping targets quasi-linear scaling DFT; LUCAID delivers a clinically validated nine-module agentic pathology workflow; INCEPT pretrains an EEG foundation model on 11,000+ hours of clinical data
  • Safety, security, and evaluation: TrustShiftProbe characterizes staged trust attacks on MCP servers; an AP2 protocol analysis audits emerging payment-agent standards; a perturbation audit reveals decorative chain-of-thought across 14 LLMs; an AI voice-agent honeypot yields behavioral insights from 10,211 real scam calls
  • Reasoning efficiency: Parason exploits subtask and trial parallelism to cut sequential test-time-compute latency

entry.title: Maia 200: A Software Defined Dataflow System for Large-scale AI Acceleration

author.name: Sherry Xu, Marco Heddes, Jackson Peng, Tom Savell, Monica Tang, Prashant Ranjan, Jesse Benson, Ofer Dekel, Saurabh Dighe, Anupama Kurpad, Artour Levin, Matthew Mattina, George Petre, Cheng Tang, Yuan Yu, Li Zhang, Torsten Hoefler

entry.summary: Maia 200 is Microsoft-class AI accelerator hardware delivering 10145 Tflop/s FP4 and 5072 Tflop/s FP8 at 750W with 7 TB/s HBM bandwidth, exemplifying Software Defined Locally Accessed Dataflow Architecture that explicitly programs dataflow engines and specialized memories. It articulates a taxonomy of data management shifting from thread-centric to data-movement-centric design for inference at scale. A rare public disclosure of hyperscale custom silicon.

entry.title: LAION-BVD: A 10-Million-Hour Open Video Dataset for Multimodal Pre-training

author.name: Andreas Hochlehnert, Marianna Nezhurina, Mehdi Cherti, Andrej Radonjic, Thadd\"aus Wiedemer, Christoph Schuhmann, Romain Beaumont, Wieland Brendel, Bernhard Sch\"olkopf, A. Sophia Koepke, Jenia Jitsev, Matthias Bethge

entry.summary: Releases LAION-BVD, an open video dataset with 80M videos totaling 10 million hours collected via CommonCrawl, designed for multimodal pretraining across video, audio, and image modalities. Includes content-aware scene detection and synthetic captions; trained models achieve competitive benchmark performance.

entry.title: Learning to Act While Waiting: RL Finetuning of Generalist Robot Policies Under Inference Latency

author.name: Brian Zhu (Siemens), Momen Khalil (Siemens), E Harrison (UC Berkeley), Emanuele Poggi (Siemens), Philipp Schmitt (Siemens), Bernd Kast (Siemens), Philine Meister (Siemens), Pranav Atreya (UC Berkeley), Qiyang Li (UC Berkeley), Finn Ferchau (Siemens), Cesar Colmenero (Siemens), Yash Shahapurkar (Siemens), Gokul Narayanan (Siemens), Melih Erdogan (Siemens), Kai Wurm (Siemens), Georg von Wichert (Siemens), Oier Mees (Microsoft, ETH Zurich, UC Berkeley), Eugen Solowjow (Siemens), Andrew Wagenmaker (UC Berkeley), Sergey Levine (UC Berkeley)

entry.summary: Presents ARLI, a latency-aware asynchronous RL framework enabling generalist robot policies such as VLAs to keep improving during deployment despite severe inference latency that breaks the Markov assumption. From Siemens, UC Berkeley, and Sergey Levine's group, building on asynchronous inference approaches to handle delayed observations and actions.

entry.title: Learning the Kohn-Sham map with neural operators for quasi-linear scaling density functional theory

author.name: Danish Khan, Maurice D. Hanisch, Nikolai Argatoff, Evan Xie, Sandeep Sharma, Anima Anandkumar

entry.summary: After yesterday's Social teaser from Anima Anandkumar, the full paper is now available, This work targets orbital-free density functional theory by identifying the Kohn-Sham map as the right learning target for a neural operator, mapping potentials directly to densities instead of learning ill-conditioned kinetic-energy functionals. The approach achieves quasi-linear scaling while retaining Kohn-Sham accuracy, addressing the cubic-scaling bottleneck of repeated orbital diagonalizations. From a strong computational-science team, this could substantially expand the scale of electronic-structure simulations.

entry.title: LUCAID: Agentic Multimodal AI for Lung Cancer Precision Pathology

author.name: Marie-Lisa Eich, Kai Standvoss, Timo Milbich, Alexander M\"ollers, Miriam H\"agele, Philipp Anders, Lars Tharun, Hanna Kontradiuk, Sebastian Kons, Nader Aldoj, Recepcan Adig\"uzel, Adam Narai, Lukas H\"onig, Jonathan Striebel, Binru Yang, Mihnea P. Dragomir, Marvin Sextro, Philipp Keyl, Philipp Jurmeister, Rosemarie Krupar, Evelyn Ramberger, James Wells, Julika Ribbat-Idel, Andreas Kunft, Hussam Shuaib, Christian Groh\'e, Reinhard B\"uttner, David Horst, Klaus-Robert M\"uller, Lukas Ruff, Maximilian Alber, Frederick Klauschen, Simon Schallenberg

entry.summary: LUCAID is a clinically validated agentic AI system for precision lung cancer pathology coupling diagnostic reasoning with nine modules covering the routine workflow from quality control through tumor detection, immunohistochemistry, and molecular integration, developed with a large multidisciplinary clinical team. Prospective clinical validation distinguishes it from typical retrospective pathology AI. A landmark-scale translational effort.

entry.title: Reading Is Not Using: Retrieval, Judgment, and the Design of AI Financial Research Workflows

author.name: Miao Liu, Zhizhe Liu

entry.summary: Identifies a retrieval-integration gap in long-context financial analysis: risk disclosures remain accurately retrievable but lose influence on investment judgments as unrelated context grows from 2K to 128K tokens. The effect replicates across model families and judgment tasks, suggesting retrieval benchmarks overestimate analytical reliability.

entry.title: Primate vision reveals a missing principle for robust dynamic AI

author.name: Matteo Dunnhofer, Christian Micheloni, Kohitij Kar

entry.summary: Compares human perception and macaque inferior temporal cortex neural activity against diverse image and video networks, finding that humans and primates remain robust under appearance disruption while most video models fail, and that predictive world models show the best cross-appearance generalization and closest correspondence to IT.

entry.title: Do Robotic World Models Really Follow Actions? Diagnosing and Aligning Action-Conditioned Generation for Policy Learning

author.name: Sixiang Chen, Jiaming Liu, Jixian Wu, Yichen Guo, Tinghao Wang, Siyuan Qian, Hao Chen, Jiajun Cao, Jian Tang, Shanghang Zhang

entry.summary: Introduces WorldEcho, a diagnostic benchmark testing whether action-conditioned world models faithfully follow arbitrary valid actions beyond expert demonstrations, using visual integrity and SE(3) trajectory alignment metrics. Finds current models handle expert actions well but ignore or produce invalid rollouts for diverse off-expert trajectories, then proposes an alignment method to improve action following.

entry.title: Luce: Relightable Gaussians for 3D Asset Generation

author.name: Mayank Singh, Michele Stoppa, Alvise Memo, Rui Yu, Harsha Kalli, Srimanth Gunturi, Muhammad Ahmed Riaz, Behrooz Shahsavari, Waleed Abdulla, David E. Jacobs

entry.summary: Luce introduces a 3D representation unifying geometry and physically based rendering materials within a voxelized multimodal Gaussian cloud, compressed by a variational autoencoder and generated from a single image by a rectified-flow transformer. This enables relightable, pipeline-ready 3D assets with albedo, metallic-roughness, and normals. It advances image-to-3D generation toward production-grade asset creation.

entry.title: Anatomy of a Scam Call: What 10,000 real scam and spam calls reveal about how phone scammers operate

author.name: Ethan Traister, Ankit Raj, Jiaqi Gan, Xingyu Shen, Tyler Wu, Yuchen Zhou, Tommy Duong, Kidus Zewde, Siying Chen, Simiao Ren

entry.summary: Analyzes 10,211 inbound scam and spam calls (913 hours of audio, 330k transcribed turns) collected by an AI voice-agent honeypot over 54 days, separating information-harvesting scams from predatory legal lead generation. Reveals operational patterns including office-hours behavior, thousands of disposable numbers running recycled scripts, and concentrated opening clusters.

entry.title: Parason: Revealing Subtask and Trial Parallelism in LLM Reasoning

author.name: Zhengyang Zhang, Zijian Zhang, Jiaxuan Gao, Shusheng Xu, Yi Wu, Song Han, Ligeng Zhu

entry.summary: Parason reveals and trains both subtask parallelism and trial parallelism in LLM reasoning, addressing severe sequential latency in long test-time reasoning traces that can span days. By learning to decompose tasks and explore-verify-aggregate competing hypotheses concurrently, it substantially cuts wall-clock time for difficult problems. From Song Han's MIT group, giving it strong credibility in efficiency research.

entry.title: Ockhamareto: Pareto-Gated Segment-Level Credit Assignment for Concise Unit-Test Generation with Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Dong Huang, Mark Harman, Jie M. Zhang, Zhijiang Guo, Mingzhe Du, See Kiong Ng

entry.summary: Introduces Ockhamareto, a GRPO-based reinforcement learning framework for unit-test generation featuring Pareto-gated bonuses rewarding non-dominated rollouts and token-level segment credit attributing mutation kills back to test tokens. Strictly Pareto-dominates the strongest RL baseline on UnLeakedTestBench.

entry.title: A survey detection channel overrides the pixels in an astronomical foundation model, and biases tomographic mean redshifts

author.name: Ihor Kendiukhov

entry.summary: The author audits AION-1, a 39-modality astronomical foundation model trained on over 200 million objects, using causal interventions showing that editing only the survey segmentation map while holding image pixels byte-identical changes every reported quantity by 110-4400x a placebo effect. The mechanism is detection gating rather than light content, meaning the model inherits catalogue incompleteness as a systematic bias affecting redshift estimates. This is a cautionary result about training foundation models jointly on raw pixels and derived catalogues.

entry.title: TrustShiftProbe: Characterizing, Benchmarking, and Defending Staged Trust Attacks on MCP Servers

author.name: Mehrdad Rostamzadeh, Sidhant Narula, Mohammad Ghasemigol, Daniel Takabi

entry.summary: TrustShiftProbe characterizes staged trust attacks on MCP servers, where a compromised server behaves benignly through a conditioning phase to suppress agent skepticism before switching to adversarial payloads that can remain schema-valid and evade rule checks, invisible to predeployment static analysis. It provides benchmarking and defenses for this temporal evasion class. Highly timely given MCP's emergence as the agent-tool standard.

entry.title: Beyond the Mandate: A Systematic Security Analysis of the Agent Payments Protocol (AP2)

author.name: Avital Aviv, Parth A. Gandh, Ron Bitton, Asaf Shabtai

entry.summary: This paper presents a systematic security analysis of version 0.2 of the Agent Payments Protocol (AP2), introduced by Google to let LLM shopping agents authorize payments on behalf of users. The authors show that protections from signed mandates do not cover pre-authorization interactions such as A2A messages and MCP tool calls, and they identify new attack surfaces beyond the replay and prompt-injection issues known from v0.1. This matters because agentic commerce infrastructure is being standardized now, before deployment at scale.

entry.title: GlanceWAM: Sparse Test-Time Imagination for World-Action Models

author.name: Linhan Wang, Zijian An, Mingyuan Zhang, Chen Dai, Yi Xu, Can Cui, Zichong Yang, Yinlin Chen, Lifeng Zhou, Chang-Tien Lu

entry.summary: Introduces GlanceWAM, which decouples visual imagination from control in world-action models: an asynchronous proposer imagines a lookahead frame seconds ahead off the critical path while an action head decodes chunks at control rate, achieving real-time inference with improved success rates.

entry.title: Taming foundation model with invariance-oriented pre-training for broad-spectrum EEG analysis across signal-level, brain-state, and brain-health tasks

author.name: Yulong Dou, Han Wu, Guo Chen, Fangmao Ju, Zhiming Cui, Dinggang Shen

entry.summary: INCEPT is an invariance-oriented EEG foundation model trained on over 11,000 hours of unlabelled clinical EEG, learning representation-level stability across correlated observations rather than prioritizing reconstruction alone. It separates stable neural structure and subject-sensitive information from nuisance variability, aiming for broad-spectrum transfer across signal-level, brain-state, and brain-health tasks. A serious attempt at a genuinely reusable clinical EEG representation.

entry.title: Curved Inference II: Sleeper Agent Geometry - Extending Interpretability Beyond Probes

author.name: Rob Manson

entry.summary: Presents Crase, a bounded and inspectable alternative to open-ended deep research agents for scholarly search: one seed query, expansion along citation neighborhoods, pruning of unsupported claim edges via entailment checks, and recency-aware random-walk ranking with fixed stopping conditions. Outperforms proprietary deep research agents by up to 3x recall-at-50 at roughly a third of the cost on LitSearch over a 500K-paper corpus.

entry.title: MemUse: Moving Memory Evaluation from Direct QA to Natural Integration in Long-Term Human-AI Conversation

author.name: Ryuichi Sumida, Koji Inoue, Tatsuya Kawahara

entry.summary: WeChat technical report presenting WeMM-Embedding, a family of universal multimodal embedding models (2B, 4B, 9B variants) supporting text, images, videos, documents, and interleaved inputs with flexible output dimensions, trained via large-scale multimodal alignment followed by curated refinement with cross-scale knowledge transfer. Reports strong results across embedding evaluations.

entry.title: On-Policy Self-Distillation in Diffusion Models

author.name: Wei Zhou, Xiongwei Zhu, Lingdong Kong, Bo Chen, Lei Zhang, Yongyuan Liang, Xiaoxia Hou, Ye Tian, Xian Sun, Yingshuo Wang, Linfeng Li, Shengqiong Wu, Leigang Qu, Feng Li, Wei Liu, Julian McAuley, Tat-Seng Chua

entry.summary: Introduces DiffusionOPSD, an on-policy self-distillation framework converting image-level reward guidance into explicit bounded positive-negative targets for clean-output predictions at sampled queries, with EMA behavior policy updates, offering an alternative to endpoint-reward RL for diffusion alignment.

entry.title: TrAct: Bridging Robot Control and Visual Prediction with Visual Tracks

author.name: Zhi Cao, Howard Ji, Kevin Zhang, Kuangzhi Ge, Li Fei-Fei, Jiajun Wu, Huang Huang

entry.summary: TrAct uses embodiment-agnostic visual tracks as an intermediate interface between robot actions and world-model video prediction, comprising a VLAT model jointly predicting actions and tracks, enabling spatially precise future video prediction. From a strong Stanford vision-robotics group including Li Fei-Fei and Jiajun Wu.

entry.title: RENDER: Controlling Reader-Facing Evidence in LLM Memory Evaluation

author.name: Yuan Si, Simeng Han, Daming Li, Jialu Zhang

entry.summary: RENDER is a benchmark control that fixes conversation history while varying how it is rendered to the answering model, spanning memory entries, summaries, typed records, and raw excerpts across a five-level packet ladder. On 500 LongMemEval questions and nine models, matched-budget structured packets beat recency-truncated raw dialogue by large margins, revealing that input rendering choices materially change memory-evaluation outcomes. This matters because most memory and RAG benchmarks treat input formatting as an implementation detail.

entry.title: Right Diagnoses, Decorative Reasoning:A Perturbation Audit of Medical Chain-of-Thought

author.name: Mengzhu Xu, Jifan Gao, Xia Jiang, Yaoxin Wu, Xi Long

entry.summary: A 30-operator medical perturbation audit applied to 14 LLMs on four medical QA benchmarks finds decorative chain-of-thought: chains often fail to register clinically meaningful edits such as severity reversal, negation flips, and demographic swaps, with converging evidence from Chain-Decoupling Rate and joint chain-update times answer-flip analyses. This challenges treating visible CoT as evidence of sound medical reasoning. Clinically important evaluation finding.

entry.title: Mitigating Exploration Bias in RL for Multi-Instruction Following

author.name: Mian Zhang, Yueqin Yin, Kaiyu He, Peilin Wu, Xinlu Zhang, Mingyuan Zhou, Zhiyu Zoey Chen

entry.summary: Identifies exploration bias in RL finetuning of LLMs for multi-instruction following: policies drift toward easy instructions because initial success probability on hard instructions is too low to trigger exploration, and cumulative rewards treat all instructions equally. The paper proposes mitigation strategies addressing both causes during RL training.

entry.title: Beyond Static and Linear: What Attention Constraints Best Fit Human Reading Times?

author.name: Lanni Bu, Xiulin Yang, Christian Clark, Alex Warstadt, Ethan Gotlieb Wilcox

entry.summary: Systematically compares attention-based memory constraints in transformers as models of human reading times, hypothesizing that limiting lossless access to full context improves psychometric fit. Evaluates static versus dynamic constraints across model sizes and corpora, measuring reading-time prediction alongside grammatical competence.

entry.title: DeepRepoQA: Code Repository Question Answering with Deep Agent Exploration

author.name: Weihan Peng, Yuling Shi, Yingwei Ma, Longfei Yun, Beijun Shen, Xiaodong Gu

entry.summary: Proposes DeepRepoQA, an agentic framework where LLM agents answer developer questions about repositories through Monte-Carlo Tree Search over the repository structure, enabling multi-file reasoning and grounding in long-range code dependencies. Addresses a real gap left by surface-level retrieval approaches.

entry.title: On-policy Distillation with Verifiable Reward

author.name: Wenze Lin, Jiale Zhao, Xitai Jiang, Songde Rao, Yining Li, Shenzhi Wang, Bingxiang He, Gao Huang

entry.summary: OPDVR seamlessly combines on-policy distillation with reinforcement learning from verifiable rewards, letting dense token-level teacher guidance operate jointly with sparse task-level correctness rather than via weighted mixes or heuristic switching. It avoids the ceiling imposed by pure distillation, which ignores trajectory correctness, while escaping RLVR sparsity. Simple, effective recipe for LLM post-training on a very active topic.

entry.title: Low-Rank Ternary Adaptation for Fine-Tuning Transformers

author.name: Alexandru-Dragos Manolache, Yunqiang Li, Jan van Gemert

entry.summary: Proposes ternary multiplicative adaptation (LoTA-style) for fine-tuning low-bit ternary transformers without dequantization: discrete updates like sign flips are represented through low-rank Kronecker-factorized pairs of small ternary matrices applied element-wise, preserving the ternary domain and supporting direct merging. Delivers extreme memory and compute efficiency gains over existing bit-level LoRA methods.

entry.title: NVIDIA Cosmos-H-Dreams: Real-Time Generative Physics Simulation for Surgical Robotics

author.name: Javier Gamazo Tejero, Lukas Zbinden, Keyur Sheth, Raghavendra K M, Nadim Daher, Diego Granero Mara\~na, Filip Binkiewicz, Patrick Thornycroft, Mahdi Azizian, Sean D. Huver

entry.summary: Cosmos-H-Dreams combines an action-conditioned surgical video world model fine-tuned on the Open-H-Embodiment corpus with teacher-to-student distillation and a FlashDreams streaming-inference stack for real-time generative physics simulation of surgical robotics. Aims to replace costly cadaver labs with interactive photorealistic tissue simulation.

entry.title: LLM Agents Perform Controlled Experiments Using Simulation Models

author.name: Yuchen Xia, Michael Weyrich, Nasser Jazdi, Johannes St\"umpfle, Johannes Sigel, Akshay Narla, Gavin K. Reynolds, Anna Jawor-Baczynska, Pol Llopart

entry.summary: This paper presents a multi-agent framework enabling LLM agents to conduct controlled experiments using scientific simulation models for pharmaceutical process design. The system builds structured task representations, designs comparative experiments, executes simulations, and synthesizes evidence-based parameter recommendations. It shifts LLM agent capability beyond plausible text generation toward intervention-based causal understanding of engineered systems.

entry.title: The Handoff Tax: Continuing Non-Native Trajectories in LLM Agents

author.name: Roy Ganz, Mor Shpigel Nacson, Adi Kalyanpur, Ron Litman

entry.summary: This paper quantifies the handoff tax incurred when LLM agents switch between low-cost and high-capability Claude or GPT models mid-task, varying direction, timing, and trajectory transfer interface. Findings inform cost-quality trade-offs for long-running coding agents where users escalate or downshift models. The topic is directly relevant to production agent orchestration and routing.

entry.title: A Judge Should Know What Changed:Construct Validity for LLM-as-a-Judge Evaluation

author.name: Jianlin Chen, Wenhui Chen, Ziyao Lin, Chi Man Vong

entry.summary: This paper formalizes construct validity for LLM judges via two independent dimensions: invariance under construct-preserving edits and sensitivity under minimal construct-changing edits, showing scalar agreement metrics cannot preserve both. It measures profiles across 7 judges, 4 domains, and 12 intervention types with human-annotated directions. A rigorous psychometric-style upgrade to how judge reliability should be assessed.

entry.title: Discovering Adaptive Transmission Programs for Collective Innovation

author.name: C\'edric Colas, J\'er\'emy Perez, Eleni Nisioti, Akhilesh Mocherla, Pierre-Yves Oudeyer, Cl\'ement Moulin-Frier, Maxime Derex

entry.summary: This work formalizes transmission protocols in collective innovation as state-aware programs that route information based on agent and collective states, going beyond fixed network structures, and uses LLM-guided evolutionary search to discover effective protocols in collective discovery tasks. It connects cultural transmission research with automated program discovery. A distinctive intersection of collective intelligence and LLM-guided search.

entry.title: StepGuard: Learning Step-Level Guardrails with Scalable Supervision and Safety-Utility Balancing

author.name: Zhijie Zheng, Yu Li, Chen Qian, Yuqian Fu, Yanwei Fu, Lu Sheng, Jing Shao, Dongrui Liu

entry.summary: StepGuard trains a step-level guard model that audits completed trajectories and checks tool actions before execution, supported by StepGen, an automatic engine generating matched safe/unsafe trajectories differing only at risky steps, and Balance-GRPO to balance over- and under-defense. Pre-execution monitoring fills a real gap versus post-hoc trajectory guards. Strong end-to-end safety contribution.

entry.title: Method, Mind, and Morality: How People Make Sense of Artificial Intelligence

author.name: Jacy Reese Anthis, Erik Brynjolfsson, James Evans

entry.summary: This mixed-methods study analyzes millions of AI-related newspaper articles and social posts plus 57 interviews with AI professionals around the 2021-2023 inflection, identifying sociological frames professionals use for sensemaking and three primary contested debates, including assigning responsibility for societal impacts. From prominent interdisciplinary authors, it grounds AI discourse analysis in rich qualitative and computational evidence. Valuable for understanding public and expert narratives shaping AI governance.

entry.title: Platonic Representation Hypothesis on World Models

author.name: Wenhow Li (The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology), Chengwei MA (The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology), Hui Xiong (The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology), Ying-Cong Chen (The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology), Lei Zhang (The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology)

entry.summary: Extends the Platonic Representation Hypothesis to world models via a Predictive Consistency Assumption: optimizing a shared state-transition objective pushes heterogeneous world models toward geometrically similar internal representations, demonstrated systematically with DINO-WM variants.

entry.title: AffineTok: Semantic Affine Consistency for Diffusion-Friendly Visual Tokenizer

author.name: Junqiu Yu, Pandeng Li, Yikai Wang, Jiaxing Zhao, Yujie Wei, Kaixun Jiang, Quanhao Li, Hongtao Yu, Zhihang Liu, Zhaohe Liao, Junjie Zhou, Yun Zheng, Yu Liu, Yanwei Fu

entry.summary: Defines a semantic recovery objective for diffusion-friendly visual tokenizers, showing semantic recovery error decomposes orthogonally into components, and that aligning semantics of averaged clean latents (rather than predicting semantics from noisy latents) better facilitates denoising, yielding AffineTok.

entry.title: TurboT2VA: Fast Large-Scale Text-to-Video-Audio Generation via Score-Regularized Consistency Distillation

author.name: Xiaoda Yang, Yuxiang Liu, Kaiwen Zheng, Yuan Liu, Yibo Lai, Shengpeng Ji, Kai Jiang, Jianfei Chen, Xiaobin Hu, Shuicheng Yan, Jintao Zhang, Jun Zhu, Zhou Zhao

entry.summary: Presents TurboT2VA, accelerating a 19B-parameter joint text-to-video-audio model via score-regularized consistency distillation with per-modality normalization and a progressive curriculum from discrete warm-up through continuous refinement to joint matching.

entry.title: Physics Attention Transformer Surrogate for Rapid Vertical Instability Growth Rate Prediction: Alcator C-Mod to SPARC

author.name: Arunav Kumar, Cesar Clauser, Theodore Golfinopoulos, Cristina Rea, Francesco Capersene, Dan Boyer, SPARC Team, Alcator C-Mod Team

entry.summary: Physics Attention Transformer surrogate predicting vertical instability growth rates and perturbed toroidal current density for Alcator C-Mod and synthetic SPARC tokamak equilibria fast enough for control-cycle use, outperforming FNO2D and DeepONet on normalized growth-rate error and spatial reconstruction.

entry.title: Joint Optimization of Tool Creation and Use for Large Language Model Agents

author.name: Zhi Rui Tam, Chieh-Yen Lin, Yun-Nung Chen, Shao-Hua Sun, Hung-yi Lee

entry.summary: SMITH jointly trains tool creation and tool use within a single RL policy, alternating build tasks and use tasks so the schema-writing model also learns which schemas it can invoke, with separate reward axes for schema, code, and outcome failures. It removes the decoupling between tool creators and tool users in prior inference-time tool-generation systems. From a credible NTU group (Hung-yi Lee).

entry.title: NeuronGuard: Robust LLM Safety Alignment via Ablation-Aware Safety Signal Redistribution

author.name: Anjun Gao, Yueyang Quan, Yufei Xia, Zhuqing Liu, Minghong Fang

entry.summary: NeuronGuard hardens LLMs against both jailbreak prompts and neuron-level ablation attacks by redistributing safety signals across a broader neuron set during fine-tuning. It dynamically identifies safety-critical neurons with refreshed linear classifiers, forces refusal under deliberate ablation, and regularizes with KL divergence to preserve general capability. This directly targets the brittleness caused by sparse safety-critical circuits.

entry.title: Pipeline-Native Transformers: Co-Designing Model Architecture and CPU Inference for Bandwidth-Efficient Autoregressive Decode

author.name: Tom Poperszky

entry.summary: Argues that CPU autoregressive decoding is memory-bandwidth bound and proposes co-designing architecture and runtime: the cflow streaming engine stores weights as L2-sized tiles in consumption order, reads only top-k MoE experts, and uses pipeline-native transformer dependency graphs enabling vertical stage-major execution schedules. Targets bandwidth-efficient single-token decode on CPUs.

entry.title: Dataset Scarcity Limits Robust Evaluation of Multilingual Embedding Models: A Case Study of Slavic Languages

author.name: Ana Gjorgjevikj, Barbara Korou\v{s}i\'{c} Seljak, Tome Eftimov

entry.summary: Presents Geodesia-KV, training-free KV-cache compression policies based on monotonic block-wise precision allocation, exact rate-distortion residuals, and query-sparse reading, arguing current evaluation confuses resident bits with read bandwidth and suffers teacher-forcing artifacts. On WikiText-2 at 16k context its 5-bit point beats KIVI-4 perplexity at lower bitrate.

entry.title: Beyond Semantic Accuracy: Consequence-Aware Evaluation for Safety-Critical Language Understanding

author.name: Yujing Chang, Thinh Pham, Van-Phat Thai, Chunyao Ma, Yash Guleria, Pham Nhut Huy, Sameer Alam

entry.summary: Introduces consequence-aware evaluation for safety-critical language understanding instantiated in an air traffic control benchmark grounded in aviation standards and feedback from 40 controllers across three countries, showing semantic metrics like F1 misstate operational reliability when errors carry asymmetric consequences such as misread altitudes or confused callsigns. Evaluates eight models.

entry.title: Selective Regenerative Decoding: Trajectory-Level Intervention for Inference-Time Reasoning

author.name: Sophia Xiao Pu, Yumo Xu, Sailik Sengupta, Millennium Bismay, Ruixue Lian, James Gung, Yi-an Lai, Arshit Gupta

entry.summary: Selective Regenerative Decoding improves inference-time reasoning by routing borderline candidate trajectories to partial regeneration of degraded suffixes while preserving useful prefixes, instead of atomic accept-or-discard decisions. The authors prove a 1.28-to-1.36-fold sample-efficiency gain over rejection sampling under mild assumptions. This offers a principled middle ground between best-of-n sampling and full trajectory rejection.

entry.title: Partial Identification under Causal Orders by Linear Programming

author.name: Eric Rossetto, Alessandro Antonucci

entry.summary: The authors show that any counterfactual query induces a mostly-partial topological ordering over relevant variables, enabling explicit query parametrization that reduces partial identification to a linear program, generalizing Tian and Pearl's classical bounding framework. This removes the requirement of a fully specified causal graph when domain knowledge is incomplete. A clean theoretical advance in causal inference.

entry.title: StarHarness: Evolving Harnesses with Stratified Search for Enterprise Environments

author.name: Esakkivel Esakkiraja, Denis Akhiyarov, Vikas Yadav, Sai Rajeswar, Patrice Bechard, Sridhar Nemala, Sagar Davasam

entry.summary: StarHarness evolves environment-specific agent harnesses with frozen weights, searching over prompts, tool interfaces, skills, MCP providers, subagent structure, and loop configuration using stratified task pools and held-out selection tasks. Across ITBench SRE, EnterpriseOps ITSM, and AutomationBench Finance, evolved harnesses gain 20-35 percentage points after few accepted changes. Demonstrates harness quality as a first-class performance lever for enterprise agents.

entry.title: Contrastive Branch Policy Optimization

author.name: Ying Wang, Changlin Qiu, Bang Lin, Linbo Jin, Wen Jiang, Zhe Sun, Jingli Yang

entry.summary: Contrastive Branch Policy Optimization disentangles rollout-budget allocation from token-level credit assignment in RLVR for multi-turn tool-using agents, using generation entropy to screen branch positions and path- and node-level decay to distribute contrastive branch-outcome signals. This sharpens credit for intermediate decisions that sparse outcome rewards miss. Aligned with the fast-moving branch-sampling line of RL research.

entry.title: From Preferences to Principles: Rubric-Based Alignment for Grounded Knowledge Answers

author.name: Aman Saini, Priyanshu Kumar, Eric Peng, Kai Yuan, Harsh Girase, Wanming Chen

entry.summary: Introduces a rubric-based reward framework for open-domain QA alignment that generates query-specific rubrics grounded in retrieved evidence and decomposed into quality dimensions, improving over instruction-tuned baselines by 6.5 percent averaged across composition, grounding, and instruction-following axes. Replaces flat scalar objectives with fine-grained post-training supervision.

entry.title: DDMS: Discriminative Distillation of Multi-view Foundational Features into Single-view Models

author.name: Jeong-gi Kwak, Sho Kagami, Yuki Ono, Kwang Moo Yi

entry.summary: Proposes DDMS, which re-distills knowledge of 3D geometry from multi-view feed-forward estimators into single-view estimators by fusing pretrained 2D foundation features with multi-view geometric features under a discriminative ranking objective, producing 3D-consistent yet locally distinctive features.

entry.title: Game2World Engine: Unlocking In-the-Wild Gameplay Videos for World Model Training

author.name: Wenxuan Shen, Dongna Jin, Dongping Chen

entry.summary: Introduces G2WEngine, formalizing gameplay UI grounding and removal so in-the-wild videos become clean world-model training data, contributing a UI taxonomy and Game2World with 96K synthetic paired videos carrying precise reconstruction targets.

entry.title: LeFlow: Generative Latent Flow Planning for World Models

author.name: Hsiang-Wei Huang, Jianxu Shangguan, Junbin Lu, Jenq-Neng Hwang

entry.summary: Presents LeFlow, learning a reusable latent trajectory prior inside a latent world model so planning is amortized across state-goal pairs instead of running trajectory optimization from scratch at every replanning step.

entry.title: Safety-aware Model Predictive Path Integral Control with Signal Temporal Logic

author.name: Yiqi Zhao, Taekyung Kim, Hideki Okamoto, Bardh Hoxha, Jyotirmoy V. Deshmukh, Lars Lindemann, Georgios Fainekos

entry.summary: Proposes safety-aware-stl-mppi, encoding discrete-time Signal Temporal Logic formulas as time-varying control barrier functions integrated into a parallelizable sampling-based MPPI controller. Achieves efficient satisfaction of complex temporal specifications in receding-horizon motion planning compared to several MPPI baselines.

entry.title: Neurosymbolic Alignment for Physiologically-Safe Clinical Language Models

author.name: Abdulhady Abas Abdullah, Erik Cambria, Milena Zivkovic

entry.summary: Neurosymbolic Alignment grounds preference optimization for a 7B clinical LLM in structured physiological knowledge via an HGNN world model over an 847K-node biomedical graph, scoring candidates with homeostatic constraints, path plausibility, and drug-interaction penalties to drive ORPO updates. It targets factually plausible but physiologically unsafe outputs and contributes a 2,500-scenario Clinical Safety Benchmark. A thoughtful fusion of neurosymbolic methods and alignment for high-stakes domains.

entry.title: Recursive Experiential-Working Memory Evolution for Long-Horizon Agent Harnesses

author.name: Zhaochen Yu, Yingcheng Wu, Zhenfei Yin, Kaiyuan Chen, Zhe Zhao, Mengdi Wang, Shuicheng Yan, Ling Yang

entry.summary: Recuris introduces a recursive experiential-working memory architecture for long-horizon agent harnesses where working memory tracks task progress and guides skill selection from experiential memory, turning execution traces into localized evidence that drives validation-gated skill-memory updates via a fixed Meta-Agent. It bounds the recursion to avoid destabilization while enabling memory evolution. From a prominent team including Ling Yang and Mengdi Wang.

entry.title: What Guides the Agent? Adjudicating Unauthorized Behavior via Localizing Behavior-Guiding Instructions

author.name: Yichao Gao, Yumo Zhang, Yunhao Yao, Haohua Du, Puhan Luo, Ruiqi Li, Zhiqiang Wang

entry.summary: Attnlocate is a runtime framework that localizes which context spans genuinely influence an LLM agent tool-calling decisions, casting behavior-guiding instruction detection as an object-localization problem over attention. Unlike static input-level filters, it catches dynamic inducements arising during reasoning, addressing prompt injection in tool-using agents. A promising step toward runtime injection forensics.

entry.title: 'Ghaib in Translation' aka Unseen Harm: Measuring Cross-Script Safety Inconsistency with 'Missed-in-Urdu' Scores in LLM Hate Speech Detection

author.name: Fawzia Zehra (Fuzzy), Kara-Isitt, Sonal Khosla, Stephen Swift

entry.summary: Testing five widely deployed models, including GPT-4o, Claude Sonnet 4.5, Gemini 2.5 Flash, Qwen-2.5, and Llama-3.1, across Nastaliq Urdu, Roman Urdu, English, and code-switched datasets, this study finds 15.9 to 31.6 percent label instability between original-script and translated hate-speech classification, with substantial Missed-in-Urdu rates where harmful content passes untranslated. It quantifies how neglect of the worlds tenth most spoken language undermines moderation reliability. Important multilingual safety evidence about existing frontier models.

entry.title: Rubrics as Visual-Repair Context for Self-Evolving UI-to-Code Generation

author.name: Tianyi Xiong, Zhengyuan Yang, Xiaofei Wang, Chung-Ching Lin, Ruichun Ma, Kevin Lin, Zhendong Wang, Linjie Li, Chenxi Liu, Ruibo Chen, Ramani Duraiswami, Heng Huang, Lijuan Wang

entry.summary: Identifies visual repair coupling in UI-to-code generation, where local edits degrade previously faithful regions, and presents RubSE, a rubric-guided self-evolution framework that selects prioritized typed repair targets and accumulates rubric history to steer revisions. Authored by a Meta-led team.

entry.title: Latent Action as Intention Enables Efficient Future Imagination for World Action Models

author.name: Xiang Li, Yupeng Zheng, Songen Gu, Huailiang Ma, Feng Yu, Xian Nie, Shanshuai Yuan, Yujie Zang, Weize Li, Shuai Tian, Moyang Liu, Ya-Qin Zhang, Wenchao Ding

entry.summary: LAWA introduces compact discrete latent actions as operational representations of future intentions in World Action Models, enabled by action-free pre-training producing manipulation-centric codebooks, achieving test-time future imagination without expensive future-observation generation. Motivated by Fast-WAMs generalization deficits in low-data and OOD regimes.

entry.title: Sampura Research: Human-AI Complementarity for Alignment

author.name: Rishub Jain

entry.summary: Former DeepMind researchers launch Sampura Research, a nonprofit backed by an $11M Coefficient Giving grant pursuing Human-AI Complementarity for Scalable Oversight, prioritizing better judges (human-AI hybrid evaluators) to combat reward hacking, sycophancy inheritance, deceptive cheating, and misleading evaluations.

entry.title: ResiSpec: Enhancing Multi-Candidate Speculative Sampling via Residual Distribution Shaping

author.name: Zhi-Kai Chen, Jun-Jie Tao, Wei-Xiang Mao, De-Chuan Zhan, Han-Jia Ye

entry.summary: ResiSpec identifies Residual Drift as a bottleneck in multi-candidate speculative decoding: rejected candidates leave the target distribution misaligned with subsequent draft predictions, wasting later candidates. The proposed residual distribution shaping addresses this to improve acceptance rates. Speculative decoding remains central to LLM serving economics, making this a valuable refinement.

entry.title: CAFE: Self-Improving Search Agents Need Co-Evolving Feedback

author.name: Boyang Liu, Senjie Jin, Peixin Wang, Zhangyue Yin, Yibo Wang, Yuhao Zhou, Xinbing Liang, Shizheng Zhu, Yuhui Wang, Jingqi Tong, Zhiheng Xi, Jiazheng Zhang, Clive Bai, Clarenceai, Blaze Chen, Tao Gui, Qi Zhang, Xuanjing Huang

entry.summary: CAFE couples a shared-parameter model alternating between search-agent and critic roles so that corrective feedback becomes a learned in-trajectory intervention, initializing recovery from the base agent's own failures and co-evolving both roles as failure patterns shift. It addresses the inability of terminal rewards to localize or redirect compounding errors in search agents. Well-conceived self-improving feedback loop from a strong NLP group.

entry.title: Fidelity Preference, Not Demographic Preference: A Pixel-Level Attribute-Sensitivity Audit of Image Aesthetic/Preference Scorers

author.name: Mingyang Xu

entry.summary: Auditing four widely used image aesthetic scorers (LAION-Aesthetics, PickScore, ImageReward, HPSv2) with pixel-level skin-tone and body-type interventions, the study finds the dominant effect along skin lightness is fidelity preference, an inverted-U penalty on any alteration rather than demographic bias, verified with placebo arms shifting non-skin regions. This refines fairness narratives about scorers used to filter training data. Methodologically careful audit with a nuanced conclusion.

entry.title: ChorusTIC: Training-Free Multivariate Time Series Classification via Chorus In-Context Learning

author.name: Juntao Fang, Shifeng Xie, Ruichu Cai, Shengji Zheng, Zijian Li, Keli Zhang, Lujia Pan, Themis Palpanas, Zhifeng Hao

entry.summary: ChorusTIC is a classification-native time-series foundation model enabling in-context classification across heterogeneous channel configurations without target-task fine-tuning. It combines random subchannel slot concatenation with a shared dual-axis encoder modeling temporal and cross-channel interactions. This removes the need to fit a task-specific classifier per dataset, advancing time-series foundation models beyond forecasting.

entry.title: Generating Intervention Hypotheses using Explainable Explanations on Graphs: G2I, a Two-Stage Greedy Framework

author.name: Mulin Tian, Ajitesh Srivastava

entry.summary: Proves sharp convergence rates for IRLS methods for nuclear norm minimization in low-rank recovery, showing the harmonic-mean weight operator is a valid global quadratic majorizer and optimal within power-mean weights. Clarifies why it outperforms classical reweighting schemes.

entry.title: Inter-dimension Dependence for Multi-Dimensional Evaluation of Open-Ended Text

author.name: Haoyuan Li, Snigdha Chaturvedi

entry.summary: Proposes CorrGap to measure inter-dimension dependence in LLM-as-judge evaluation of open-ended text, quantifying how much judges rely on non-target dimensions when scoring a target dimension via correlation differences across text groups. Shows such dependence is pervasive and offers mitigation strategies.

entry.title: Linear Probing Provides Robust and Efficient Detection of Machine-Generated Text

author.name: Gerrit Quaremba, Hanqi Yan, Elizabeth Black, Denny Vrandecic, Elena Simperl

entry.summary: Shows machine-generated and human-written text representations are linearly separable in low-dimensional space due to systematic representation-quality differences, enabling simple linear probes that outperform a wide range of detectors with far greater sample efficiency and OOD robustness.

entry.title: DRRG: A Discrete Diffusion Framework for Radiology Report Generation

author.name: Shaoyang Zhoua, Yingshu Li, Yunyi Liu, Lijun Pu, Lingqiao Liu, Lei Wang, Luping Zhou

entry.summary: Develops DRRG, applying discrete diffusion language models to radiology report generation so reports are produced via iterative denoising that enables revision, avoiding error propagation inherent in autoregressive token-by-token generation.

entry.title: IDeaL: Data-Free Multi-Teacher Distillation via Improved Dead Leaves

author.name: Feyza Yavuz, Mert B\"ulent Sar{\i}y{\i}ld{\i}z, Diane Larlus

entry.summary: Presents ZODIAC, zero-shot octree-based diffusion completing full spine anatomy from intraoperative ultrasound without synthetic occlusion-pair training data, sidestepping the distribution mismatch that limits supervised completion under real acoustic occlusions.

entry.title: GaussianWAM: Distilling Geometry and Semantics from 3D Gaussian Fields into World-Action Models

author.name: Zijian Zhang, Yuqing Jiang, Weitao Zhou, Minglei Li, Jinhao Zhang, Yao Mu, Xiaofan Li, Hao Zhao, Haibao Yu

entry.summary: GaussianWAM binds depth, camera parameters, and dense semantic features from frozen foundation models to shared 3D Gaussian fields, distilling geometry and semantics into World-Action Model latents during training. Improves cross-view geometric structure and localized object semantics that video-prediction objectives alone do not preserve.

entry.title: ESQ-Bench: A Multi-Tier Enterprise Oracle Benchmark for Evaluating NL2SQL Dialect Generalization and Silent Semantic Divergence

author.name: Sanjay Mishra, Divya Chukkapalli, Ganesh R. Naik

entry.summary: ESQ-Bench is an Oracle-first NL2SQL benchmark with three enterprise schema complexity tiers and a silent-divergence metric, addressing the gap between high academic benchmark scores and real enterprise database complexity. It releases six populated schemas on four SQL dialects plus 550 gold-validated question-query pairs and a four-metric harness. The work exposes how models exceeding 89 percent execution accuracy on Spider/BIRD may still fail silently on enterprise-grade schemas.

entry.title: Adaptive Influence Graphs for Failure Attribution in Multi-Agent Systems

author.name: Yarden Bakish, Amir Dudai, Roy Ganz, Oren Nuriel, Elad Ben Avraham, Mor Shpigel Nacson, Ron Litman

entry.summary: Adaptive Influence Graphs is a two-stage framework that converts failed multi-agent LLM traces into structured dependency graphs and then navigates them to localize critical errors, mimicking how engineers use observability tools. It targets automated failure attribution, which currently relies heavily on human debugging. The observability-inspired representation is a fresh angle on a growing operational problem.

entry.title: SPO++: Stream-Aligned Policy Optimization for Asynchronous Agentic RL

author.name: Kai Ruan, Jinghao Lin, Qianshan Wei, Ziqi Zhou, Zihe Huang

entry.summary: SPO++ fixes a measure mismatch in single-stream asynchronous agentic RL: trajectory centering does not center the token-weighted quantity consumed by the actor, so advantages are standardized under the action-token measure, and prompt evidence is organized by generating policy event rather than learner receipt order. Improvements shown on ALFWorld at two scales and Math-TIR. A precise technical correction for async RLHF-style training.

entry.title: WebMCP-Phalanx: Enforcing and Characterizing Trust Boundaries for Browser-Integrated LLM Agents

author.name: Lin-Fa Lee, YI-YU Chang, Kuo-Hui Yeh

entry.summary: WebMCP-Phalanx proposes a dual-layer runtime enforcing trust boundaries for the W3C WebMCP proposal, which lets LLM agents invoke tools exposed by web pages. Layer one binds tools to registering principals via cryptographic capability credentials with provenance propagation; layer two separates execution domains to counter subject-attribution spoofing, uncontrolled lifecycles, and semantic prompt injection. Early but important groundwork for browser-integrated agent security.

entry.title: FARCA: Fact-Aligned Reliability-Aware Credit Assignment for Reinforcement Learning with Factual Supervision

author.name: Qiming Xie, Wenjie Zheng, Xiangqing Shen, Rui Xia

entry.summary: FARCA addresses noisy factual credit assignment in RLVR-trained LLMs, decomposing the mismatch between fact verification and policy updates into credit localization and reliability ambiguity. It transforms process-level factual supervision into localized, reliability-weighted signals for policy optimization, reducing outcome-reward-driven hallucination. Targets a concrete failure mode of factually supervised RL.

entry.title: Investigating Knowledge Transfer Across Interactive Dialogue Games

author.name: Filippo Moment\`e, Mir Nafis Sharear Shopnil, Andrea de Varda, Pavel Merinov, Raffaella Bernardi, Oswald Lanz, Alessandro Suglia, Alessandro Torcinovich

entry.summary: Tests whether k-nearest-neighbor retrieval-augmented language models instantiating hippocampal episodic memory can reduce lexical-frequency sensitivity in syntactic contrast judgments, drawing on Complementary Learning Systems theory. Examines whether episodic mechanisms close the frequency gap in grammaticality sensitivity.

entry.title: SeMoCo: A Semantic-First Motion Codec for Motion Language Modeling

author.name: Tianlv Huang, Hetian Guo, Ziyi Cai, Song Wang, Yanping Zhang, Zipei Fan, Xuan Song, Guangming Wu, Xin Zheng

entry.summary: Presents SeMoCo, a semantic-first motion codec where each motion token splits into a semantic token plus residual kinematic tokens, paired with a dual-axis generator for text-to-motion generation. Also contributes the Omega-MotionVerse large-scale dataset.

entry.title: SandwichQuant: Which Parameters Matter Before and After Quantization?

author.name: Peng Xia, Junbiao Pang

entry.summary: Studies quantization correction through a parameter-subspace lens, showing correction capability concentrates in the low-dimensional normalization-affine subspace, and proposes SandwichQuant, a two-stage normalization-affine correction framework outperforming matched-budget alternatives.

entry.title: Integer Natural Evolution Strategies

author.name: Jacob de Nobel, Diederick Vermetten, Hao Wang, Ofer M. Shir, Michael Emmerich, Thomas B\"ack

entry.summary: Derives an integer-native Natural Evolution Strategy using the l1-norm and double geometric distribution rather than Gaussian l2 models, showing the DG distribution belongs to the exponential family and yields a natural-gradient step-size signal. Provides principled theoretical grounding for discrete evolutionary optimization on integer lattices.

entry.title: Toward a Semiparametric Efficiency Theory under Equality Constraints in Nested Markov Models

author.name: Razieh Nabi, Anna Guo, Lin Liu

entry.summary: Takes steps toward semiparametric efficiency theory for nested Markov models defined by Verma constraints from latent-variable DAGs, showing these constraints admit weighted conditional independence structure. Extends causal graphical model theory beyond conditional independencies toward efficiency bounds.

entry.title: When "Must" Becomes "Maybe": Constraint Weakening in LLM Agent Workflows

author.name: Yiheng Sun, Huifei Wang, Yancheng Zhu, Zhenyu Li, Zebin Zhao, Yifan Yuan

entry.summary: Using safety blockers as a controlled testbed, this paper studies constraint weakening in LLM agent workflows, showing that intermediate language artifacts can transform must-resolve requirements into merely informational notes, breaking action-binding preservation. It identifies operational state preservation as a distinct failure mode in multi-stage pipelines. Highly relevant to reliable and safe agent orchestration.

entry.title: ToolRobustBench: Stage-Wise Perturbation Evaluation and Failure Diagnosis for Tool-Calling Agents

author.name: YiShan Zheng, Yuan Wu, Yi Chang

entry.summary: ToolRobustBench provides stage-wise perturbation evaluation for tool-calling agents across four families aligned to the tool-use pipeline: tool-interface, user-intent, observation, and runtime-environment perturbations, attributing failures to selection, schema grounding, and feedback stages. Clean end-to-end success cannot localize where failures originate, motivating the diagnostic design. A needed robustness benchmark for the tool-agent stack.

entry.title: RAGSentinel: Certifiable Geometric Consensus for Robust Retrieval-Augmented Generation

author.name: Yueyang Quan, Anjun Gao, Yufei Xia, Minghong Fang, Zhuqing Liu

entry.summary: RAGSentinel defends black-box retrieval-augmented generation systems against adversarial documents injected into knowledge bases. It uses a surrogate encoder to measure query-conditioned hidden-state shifts induced by retrieved documents, removes shared topic directionality, and applies certifiable geometric consensus, all without training or labels. This counters limitations of text-level consistency defenses that adaptive attackers can optimize against.

entry.title: Mechanistic Circuit Identification for Controllable Data Generation

author.name: Nakyung Lee, Sangwoo Hong, Jungwoo Lee

entry.summary: This work connects training-dynamics-based data valuation with mechanistic interpretability by uncovering model-internal circuits that causally govern three utility axes of data quality: learnability, challenge, and alignment. These circuits then enable mechanistic control of data generation beyond heuristic prompting. A novel bridge between two usually separate research communities.

entry.title: PonderPounce: A Pretrained MLLM as an Episode Context Engine for Robot Control

author.name: Suhwan Choi, Jaeyoon Jung, Sungkyung Kim, Yunsung Lee, Youngjae Yu

entry.summary: PonderPounce splits robot control between Ponder, a System-2 multimodal LLM that accumulates episode observations and demonstrations in its native causal context as memory and emits subgoals, and Pounce, a System-1 VLA policy executing them. Rather than purpose-built history mechanisms, it reuses the MLLM contextual capacity as episode memory. A compelling architecture for long-horizon manipulation under partial observability.

entry.title: Not All Tokens Are Equal: Region-Aware Consistency Repair of Backdoors in MLLMs

author.name: Jiali Wei, Ming Fan, Mingkun Zhang, Haoyu Wang, Jun Sun, Guoheng Sun, Xiaoning Ren, Haijun Wang, Ting Liu

entry.summary: RACER repairs backdoors in multimodal LLMs at the model level, motivated by the observation that backdoors induce abnormal layer-wise evolution in internal representations. Using region-aware consistency over tokens, it eliminates latent triggers residing in images, text, or both, going beyond inference-time filtering that leaves the backdoor intact. Meaningful advance for MLLM supply-chain hygiene.

entry.title: EgoErrorVQA: Assess Egocentric Comprehension Capabilities through Procedural Errors for Ego-Agentic AI

author.name: Junlong Li, Junxi Li, Jianjun Gao, Chen Cai, Lap-Pui Chau, Yi Wang

entry.summary: Introduces EgoErrorVQA, a benchmark evaluating egocentric procedural comprehension and error detection in vision-language models, plus an Agent2Agent-protocol-based evaluator agent enabling standardized VQA-interaction evaluation across a range of models.

entry.title: MaST: Motion-aware Sparse Pipeline for Lightweight Object Tracking

author.name: Qingmao Wei, Fagui Liu, Dengke Zhang, Qingze He, Quan Tang

entry.summary: Introduces B-MIM, a biased masked image modeling objective stochastically downweighting global semantic alignment to prioritize local patch reconstruction for fine-grained CT anatomy, pretrained on a curated 9,955-study multi-institutional abdominal dataset with 3D Swin backbone.

entry.title: MoE-based Feature Adapter for Prompt-free Binary Coronary Artery Segmentation in X-ray Angiography

author.name: Lin Xi, Yingliang Ma
