entry.summary: Explores data-free multi-teacher distillation, showing teachers fed with decorrelated, teacher-specific synthesized noise can transfer combined strengths into one student without access to any teacher training data, using patch- and image-level decorrelation losses.

entry.title: NeurRAFT: Robot Motion Planning via Anchor-Level Flow Matching with Clearance-Aware Preference Tuning

author.name: Sibo Tian, Chang Liu, Minghui Zheng, Xiao Liang

entry.summary: NeurRAFT is a neural motion planner using anchor-level flow matching over compact waypoint sets plus clearance-aware preference tuning, avoiding dense waypoint modeling. Uses a Jacobian-weighted loss accounting for task-space impact per anchor, generates anchors in two integration steps, and interpolates with cubic splines.

entry.title: PeakBench: Benchmarking Resource-Aware Tool Invocation in LLM Agents

author.name: Zhi-Kai Chen, Xu-Xiang Zhong, Song-Yan Li, De-Chuan Zhan, Han-Jia Ye

entry.summary: PeakBench benchmarks resource-aware parallel tool invocation in LLM agents, providing executable workflows with dependency annotations and measured resource profiles to expose failures between slow serial execution and unsafe resource-agnostic parallelism. It fills a real gap since existing agent benchmarks ignore scheduling under resource constraints. Directly relevant as agents increasingly run concurrent tools.

entry.title: When May an Agent Stop? Evidence-Carrying Termination for Tool-Using LLMs

author.name: Jason Liu

entry.summary: Evidence-Carrying Termination requires an agent to return COMPLETE only when a typed certificate binds every answer claim to valid, in-scope trace evidence with deterministic replay reconstructing claimed values. On 48 synthetic tool-use tasks across eight fault types, ECT produced zero unsafe completions versus 252 of 288 for an inspected termination critic. Strong safety mechanism, though validated only on synthetic tasks.

entry.title: STAIN-FL: Stealthy Targeted Attack Injection with Contextual Triggers in Federated Learning

author.name: Ashlinder Kaur, Purnima Murali Mohan, Zengxiang Li, Tram Truong-Huu

entry.summary: STAIN-FL demonstrates a stealthy targeted backdoor attack on federated video anomaly detection using naturally occurring surveillance conditions such as low light and crowd density as contextual triggers. It combines label manipulation with gradient masking over least-updated coordinates to preserve clean accuracy while inducing trigger-conditioned misclassification. The work exposes a concrete blind spot in privacy-preserving surveillance learning.

entry.title: VisCache: Visual KV Cache Pruning for Efficient Vision Large Language Model Inference

author.name: Lyuke Wang, Zhuo Li, Guangxu Zhu

entry.summary: VisCache is a training-free, plug-and-play framework for coarse-to-fine pruning of visual KV caches in vision-language models. A lightweight VLM first filters temporal redundancy by forwarding only informative keyframes, then finer-grained pruning reduces remaining cache cost while avoiding uniform-pruning information loss. Directly addresses the prohibitive memory cost of long-context multimodal inference.

entry.title: Knowing When to Ask for Help: Bayesian Self-Escalation in Hierarchical LLM Agents

author.name: Nadeem Shaikh

entry.summary: This paper formulates intra-generation delegation, where an LLM agent recognizes mid-reasoning that it will likely fail and transfers control to a stronger model, as a Bayesian optimal-stopping problem over a learned competence posterior. It derives closed-form myopic escalation thresholds and characterizes optimal time-varying threshold policies. Elegant theory for hierarchical agent cost-performance trade-offs.

entry.title: A Theory of Speciation in Generative Diffusion Models on Compact Riemannian Manifolds

author.name: Alessio Marta, Paola Causin

entry.summary: Develops an intrinsic theory of speciation in diffusion models on compact Riemannian manifolds, characterizing branch emergence via bifurcations of critical points of the evolving density using heat-kernel and Morse-theoretic tools, going beyond symmetric pitchfork bifurcation pictures.

entry.title: S-matrix informed neural networks for amplitude analysis

author.name: Wyatt A. Smith, Arkaitz Rodas, Marius D. Thomas, C\'esar Fern\'andez-Ram\'irez, Giorgio Foti, Lin Qiu, Adam P. Szczepaniak, Alessandro Pilloni

entry.summary: Introduces S-matrix informed neural networks (SINNs) that learn scattering amplitudes directly from particle physics data while respecting first principles, plus a novel data-selection procedure using constrained network ensembles to identify mutually compatible experiments. Applied to pion-pion scattering, producing reusable amplitudes with correlated uncertainties without fixed functional forms.

entry.title: HAP: Head-Adaptive Visual Token Pruning via Cross-Modal Alignment

author.name: Yuanhao Sun, Huawei Ji, Yuan Jin, Cheng Deng, Luoyi Fu, Xinbing Wang

entry.summary: Identifies that averaging text-to-visual attention uniformly across heads misleads token pruning because misaligned heads dominate, and proposes PAQ, a head-alignment quality metric, plus head-adaptive three-stage pruning under FLOPs budgets for high-resolution vision-language prefill compression.

entry.title: NeoWorld-Pro: Programming Interactive Scenes from Monocular Images for Embodied Simulation

author.name: Yumeng He, Yichen Song, Xiaotian Yang, Weijia Zhang, Zanwei Zhou, Junru Gong, Xiaokang Yang, Yunbo Wang

entry.summary: Proposes NeoWorld-Pro, converting a monocular RGB image into executable programs specifying object geometry, articulation, and physical properties via MLLM code synthesis, with physics-in-the-loop verification refining generated programs for interactive embodied simulation scenes.

entry.title: Keep-or-Drop? Adaptive Tokenizer for Compact Video Representation

author.name: Yeonkyeong Lee, Hyunsung Go, Jongmin Kim, Sewoong Lim, Donghoon Lee

entry.summary: Presents KATok, a transformer-based video VAE with a jointly learned keep-or-drop adaptive token selector that discards uninformative tokens according to content richness, overcoming fixed compression ratios that poorly match varying spatio-temporal complexity.

entry.title: Interpreting Control Latents for System Identification via Conditional Flow Matching

author.name: Dingqi Zhang, Ruiqi Zhang, Mark W. Mueller

entry.summary: Decodes adaptive-policy latents into distributions of physical system parameters using conditional flow matching, enabling inspection, rollout, and controller tuning around a fixed policy without modifying it. Demonstrated on quadrotor system identification where latent-to-parameter mappings are otherwise under-specified.

entry.title: CARO: Contact-Agnostic Residual Observation for Zero-Shot Robust Quadruped Locomotion

author.name: Zihan Yang, Shixuan Han, Kexin Guo, Xiang Yu

entry.summary: CARO embeds a fixed-base Euler-Lagrange model into the RL control loop for quadrupeds, constructing torque-level residual observations from a disturbance observer without torque sensors, contact estimation, or vision. Policies trained with standard domain randomization exploit this feedback for substantial zero-shot adaptation gains.

entry.title: Benchmarking LLM Judges for Voice-Agent Evaluation: Reliability, Calibration, and Human Oversight

author.name: Anupam Purwar, Shashank Singh, Kritika Srivastava

entry.summary: This study benchmarks LLM-as-a-Judge evaluation for voice agents, comparing GPT-4.1 and GPT-5 judgments against human raters on telecom and retail conversations across quality and safety dimensions. It tests sensitivity to three distinct evaluation configurations and examines metric-level correlations and systematic biases. The work matters because voice-agent deployment at scale depends on trustworthy automated evaluation.

entry.title: Meta$^n$: Recursive Self-Improvement through Emergent Depth

author.name: Zae Myung Kim, Young-Jun Lee, Seungyeon Jwa, Dongyeop Kang

entry.summary: Meta^n proposes keeping a fixed meta-operation that recurses on its own products, reading solver-stack traces and code to write strategic pre-processes and helper libraries, achieving recursive self-improvement beyond the roughly two-level depth cap of self-editing systems while avoiding instability. It directly engages the safety-relevant topic of recursive self-improvement with a stabilizing design. Conceptually timely for the agent-self-improvement wave.

entry.title: From Causal Plausibility to Causal Reliability: Evaluating LLMs as Calibrated Direct Causal-Edge Classifiers

author.name: Amit Kumar, Elnur Adl Zarabi, Suranjana Trivedy, Zhiqian Chen, Lei Zhang, Kaiqun Fu, Taoran Ji

entry.summary: Evaluating 12 open-weight instruction-tuned LLMs as calibrated direct causal-edge classifiers across six benchmark graphs, five prompting strategies, and four confidence sources, the study finds strongly recall-dominant judgments producing overly dense graphs, with prompting mainly trading precision against recall rather than fixing overprediction. Quantifies limits of LLM priors for causal discovery. Useful caution for a popular workflow.

entry.title: The Limits of Automatic Evaluation of Creativity in Large Language Models

author.name: Alessandro Tutone, Giorgio Franceschelli, Mirco Musolesi

entry.summary: Collecting human evaluations of human- and AI-written short stories across 11 creativity dimensions, this study shows substantial misalignment between automatic metrics and human judgment, with LLM judges systematically preferring AI-generated content. It documents the limits of automatic creativity evaluation. Reinforces caution about benchmark-driven creativity claims.

entry.title: Discovering Cross-Language Reasoning Invariance in LLMs with Geometry-Invariant Sparse Autoencoders

author.name: Igor Bogdanov, Changcheng Huang

entry.summary: Using CKA-selected layers and geometry-invariant sparse autoencoders across five models solving MGSM math in six languages, this study discovers shared cross-language features supporting the hypothesis of language-independent reasoning computations rather than coincidentally similar outputs. Contributes to understanding multilingual abstraction in LLMs. Solid interpretability investigation.

entry.title: Beyond Static Interpretability: Anticipating Post-SFT Mechanisms from Pre-SFT Parameters for Better Tuning

author.name: Hang Chen, Jiaying Zhu, Wenya Wang

entry.summary: This paper shows that mechanistic localization performed on pre-SFT models misleads locate-then-tune parameter-efficient fine-tuning because identified neurons change drastically after tuning on novel tasks. It proposes a forward-looking framework estimating post-SFT interpretability states from pre-SFT parameters and target data to guide SFT. A thoughtful correction to a growing paradigm at the interpretability-tuning interface.

entry.title: Equivariant Cellular Sheaves for Molecular Electronic Structure: Bridging Sheaf Cohomology and E(3)-Equivariant Hamiltonian Learning

author.name: Krishna Harish

entry.summary: Shows that the molecular single-particle Hamiltonian in a localized atomic-orbital basis can be viewed as the Laplacian of a cellular sheaf on a cell complex built from the molecule. This bridges topological deep learning and E(3)-equivariant Hamiltonian learning, recovering Slater-Koster forms as a special case.

entry.title: (Mis)Understanding Benign Overfitting in Equity Return Prediction

author.name: Hui Guo, Jiawei Huang, Runze Li, Yan Yu

entry.summary: Investigates whether benign overfitting extends to equity return prediction, documenting a double descent pattern in ridgeless model prediction risk and showing optimal ridge regression outperforms ridgeless counterparts, though the gap vanishes at large parameter-to-observation ratios. Ultimately both fail to beat a simple historical average under the null hypothesis.

entry.title: Shortcut Before Circuit: Document Statistics Time In-Context Conflict Resolution

author.name: Yijun Liao, Fanwei Liang

entry.summary: Trains 26M-parameter transformers on synthetic languages where recency and rarity cues exactly coexist, then uses minimal causal edits to separate them, showing held-in accuracy cannot distinguish cue usage while interventions reveal unstable per-cell readouts across seeds. Argues shortcut behavior precedes circuit formation in in-context conflict resolution.

entry.title: Is Discrete Difficulty Sufficient? Leveraging Continuous Difficulty for Efficient Self-Consistency in LLMs

author.name: Sihyeong Yeom, Geon Park, Geunyeong Jeong, Taewoong Yoon, Jaewook Lee, Harksoo Kim

entry.summary: Proposes Flexible Self-Consistency (FSC), estimating continuous reasoning difficulty to adaptively allocate sampling budgets in Self-Consistency decoding rather than using coarse fixed difficulty tiers, cutting token consumption while maintaining accuracy on complex reasoning problems.

entry.title: Markets, Not Planners: Decentralized Orchestration of LLM Agents with Private Information

author.name: Xiao Liu, Haoyang Li, Songwei Li, Hongbo Fang, Fengli Xu, Feng Shi, James Evans

entry.summary: Benchmarks tablet-2, a production long-term memory engine for language models with no lexical matching or keyword scoring, achieving 95.7 percent on LongMemEval-S and 67.5 percent on BEAM-1M with 2.21M stored memories. Most of the paper argues these headline numbers mean little alone, since changing only the reader or re-ask budget moves scores substantially.

entry.title: Gen2Physics: Grounding Generated 3D Meshes in Physics via Multi-View Material Decomposition

author.name: Mauro Comi, Jordi Serrano Berbel, Kevis-Kokitsi Maninis, Philipp Henzler, Manuel Sanchez

entry.summary: Presents Gen2Physics, an automated pipeline that grounds generated 3D meshes in physics by decomposing them into constituent materials via fine-tuned ViT segmentation, 2D-to-3D consistency projection, and VLM-guided refinement, outputting simulation-ready assets compatible with standard engines.

entry.title: What Does Prompt Learning Change? -A Natural-Language Concept Analysis of Vision-Language Models

author.name: Ryo Kamiya, Hiroshi Kera, Kazuhiko Kawamoto

entry.summary: Presents PromptSpLiCE, a post-hoc method expressing class-conditioned CLIP embeddings as sparse combinations of natural-language concepts, revealing that prompt learning drastically reshapes concept profiles (only about 1.6 of top-10 concepts survive) and that change correlates with performance shifts.

entry.title: Event-Based Motion Estimation via Oriented Distance Fields

author.name: Lei Sun, Yuqin Ma, Weilun Li, Haoran Liang, Runyi Yang, Kaiwei Wang, Danda Pani Paudel, Luc Van Gool

entry.summary: Proposes oriented distance field motion estimation for event cameras, replacing iterative optimization with a single averaging step over precomputed event distance vectors plus adaptive event-count selection, achieving sub-pixel accuracy at lowest latency among compared methods.

entry.title: Towards Reliable AI-Based Histological Staining: A Systematic Study of Scaling and Uncertainty in Unpaired Generative Models

author.name: Qasim Siddiqui, Adrian Friebel, Maiju Myllys, Zaynab Hobloss, Daniela Gonzalez, Ahmed Ghallab, Stefan Hoehme

entry.summary: Benchmarks six unsupervised image-to-image architectures for virtual Sirius Red staining of liver tissue from routine H&E, systematically quantifying scaling behavior and predictive uncertainty to address whether visually plausible outputs faithfully reproduce collagen structure.

entry.title: ExMesh++: From Multi-View Images to Relightable UV-PBR Mesh Assets via Topology-Adaptive Reconstruction and Decomposition

author.name: Chuanjin Fan, Lifan Wu, Wenjie Chang, Hanzhi Chang, Wenfei Yang, Tianzhu Zhang

entry.summary: Presents ExMesh++, producing relightable UV-parameterized PBR mesh assets from multi-view images via topology-adaptive reconstruction and decomposition, jointly managing geometry, materials, and lighting to avoid ambiguous compensation.

entry.title: DreamLedger: Execution-Settled Credit Files for World-Model Imagination in Robot Decision Loops

author.name: Xianyao Li, Ruitong Tian, Rui Min, Fang Xu, Jing Du

entry.summary: DreamLedger treats world-model prediction reliability as a persistent deployment artifact: an execution-settled credit file recording how often predictions were borne out, indexed by operating condition, region, and horizon. Low-credit predictions shorten dependent horizons or trigger fallbacks, with settlement at zero labeling cost.

entry.title: RoG-DAgger: Rollout-Guided Post-Training for End-to-End Driving

author.name: Liangyu Zhong, Joachim Sicking, Fabian Hueger, Hanno Gottschalk

entry.summary: RoG-DAgger is a rollout-guided Dataset Aggregation post-training method for end-to-end driving that gathers expert demonstrations in policy-induced states to close the training-inference mismatch of open-loop imitation learning. Addresses limitations of existing driving DAgger pipelines including restricted expert solution spaces and premature takeover triggers.

entry.title: AI Alignment at Which Abstraction Level?

author.name: Adam Chlipala

entry.summary: Chlipala argues alignment research unjustifiably privileges human values at a particular abstraction level, drawing on lessons from formal verification at scale to suggest specifying alignment via persistent auditable formal specifications rather than centering humans directly.

entry.title: Names Can Hurt: Spotting Slopsquatting Risks Caused by Package Name Hallucinations in Local Coding LLMs

author.name: Akash Raj, Sargam Sahu

entry.summary: This paper addresses slopsquatting, where adversaries pre-register hallucinated package names on PyPI to compromise code generated by local coding LLMs. It proposes a two-layer detector combining deterministic PyPI existence checks with a Random Forest classifier over name and metadata features, embedded in a LangGraph state machine with escalating retries. It converts a documented threat into a deployable mitigation.

entry.title: Hierarchical Skill Retrieval for Data-Efficient Adaptation of Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Haoran Hao, Shahram Najam Syed, Jeff Schneider, Jeffrey Ichnowski

entry.summary: Hierarchical Skill Retrieval enables data-efficient adaptation of pretrained vision-language-action models by retrieving reusable subtask skills rather than requiring complete task matches. Exploiting the hierarchical structure of long-horizon manipulation, it reuses demonstrations that visual-similarity or task-level matching misses. Practical progress on the sample-efficiency bottleneck in robot learning.

entry.title: Simthesizer: An Agent-Driven Simulation Framework for LLM Serving Systems

author.name: Wonung Kim, Hyunmin Choi, Minsu Kim, Jaehong Cho, Yeongwook Kim, Jongse Park

entry.summary: Borg (Simthesizer) realizes agent-driven simulator development for LLM serving systems, offering composable simulator infrastructure so new workloads and mechanisms like agentic workflows and disaggregated serving can be modeled without invasive rewrites. It closes the widening gap between fast-evolving serving deployments and human-built simulators. Novel application of agents to systems research methodology.

entry.title: The RAT: A Unified Bayesian Model for RAG Evaluation

author.name: Pius von D\"{a}niken, Felix Matthias Saaro, Mark Cieliebak, Jan Deriu

entry.summary: The RAT is a unified Bayesian model for RAG evaluation that jointly models retrieval success, abstention behavior, and answer correctness factorized along pipeline information flow, distinguishing user-visible task success from generator appropriateness given retrieval outcomes. Across 27 configurations spanning three datasets, retrievers, and generators, conditional decomposition reveals behaviors aggregate metrics hide. Principled alternative to ad hoc RAG scoring.

entry.title: Calibration-Preserving Pruning: Compression as a Reliability Contract

author.name: Ibne Farabi Shihab, Adria Binte Habib, Anuj Sharma

entry.summary: Proposes Calibration-Preserving Pruning (CPP), which adds nonconformity-gradient saliency to pruning scores so pruned models retain score geometry and yield smaller valid conformal prediction sets. Demonstrated on Qwen2.5-1.5B at 50% sparsity with five-seed results.

entry.title: Joint-Embedding Prediction of Masked Point Tubes for Self-Supervised Learning on 4D Point Cloud Videos

author.name: Jheng-Ling Lee, Shang-Tse Chen

entry.summary: Proposes a JEPA-style self-supervised framework for 4D point cloud videos that masks spatiotemporal regions and predicts latent point-tube representations instead of raw coordinates, stabilized by Sketched Isotropic Gaussian Regularization preventing collapse without reconstruction targets. Captures spatial structure and temporal dynamics jointly.

entry.title: SatDL: Jointly Optimizing Data Redistribution and Training for Satellite-Based Distributed Learning

author.name: Hao Wu, Kin Whye Chew, Yizhan Han, Han Li, Jingxian Wang

entry.summary: Proposes SatDL for satellite-based distributed learning, jointly optimizing data redistribution and local training to combat severe non-IID label imbalance from geographically distinct satellite observations while balancing communication delays against convergence speed and energy consumption on solar-powered satellites.

entry.title: FireRedAudio: A General-Purpose Audio Language Model with Decoupled Continuous Representations for Understanding and Generation

author.name: Junjie Li, Xuelong Geng, Kun Xie, Feiyu Shen, Yichen Wu, Ziqi Dai, Yichen Han, Yan Jia, Kai Huang, Junjie Chen, Yixuan Li, Manzhen Wei, Fenglong Xie, Lei Xie, Xu Tang, Yao Hu

entry.summary: Surveys 46 papers mapping NLP tasks across three emergency department phases (triage, diagnosis, disposition), covering triage classification, clinical summarization, automatic diagnosis, report generation, and discharge documentation. Examines modeling paradigms and evaluation practices under time pressure and multimodal data constraints.

entry.title: ViSculpt: Visual-Centric Agentic Geometry Editing

author.name: Bo Pang, Jiaqi Pan, Xiaocheng Zhang, Jiacheng Xu, Guoping Wang, Peng-Shuai Wang

entry.summary: Presents ViSculpt, a training-free multi-agent system that edits existing 3D meshes directly through the Blender GUI, emulating artist workflows with multimodal LLM agents observing renders and operating the interface rather than generating scripts.

entry.title: Gripper-aware Vision Language Action Models

author.name: Hanyi Zhang, Zihong Luo, Tianyu Li, Khang Nguyen, Basu Hela, Shreyas Kumar, Ngoc Duy Tran, Feng Dai, Charith Munasinghe, Jorge Pe\~na Queralta, Giovanni Toffetti, Khoa Vo, Ngan Le, Ravi Prakash, Quan Vuong, Tung D. Ta, Long Hu, Anh Nguyen, Baoru Huang

entry.summary: Introduces MiGA, a multi-gripper-aware dataset spanning five gripper types across multiple robots to address gripper-invariance assumptions in VLAs, noting that parallel-jaw dominance in datasets limits embodiment-general grasping learning. Proposes gripper-aware VLA training approaches.

entry.title: TRACE: Transition-Aware Residual Control for Multi-Objective Materials Discovery

author.name: Kang Zhou, Yujia Tong, Yong Tao, Jingling Yuan

entry.summary: TRACE proposes treating evaluated edits as the basic unit of feedback in LLM-agent-driven multi-objective materials discovery, recording parent-edit-child transitions with property deltas instead of only storing candidates and scores. Aggregating this transition evidence enables better local refinement when objectives compete. It addresses a real weakness where agents know which materials succeeded but not which executable changes caused improvements.

entry.title: From State to Action: OODA-Tool for Reliable Multi-Turn Tool Use

author.name: Rongfeng Guo, Yinxuan Huang, Yusen Wu, Maoqing Zhong, Yunlu Chen, Meng Tang, Teng Long, Vincent Tao Hu

entry.summary: OODA-Tool separates state preservation from action generation in multi-turn tool use via a typed closed-loop policy inspired by Boyd's OODA cycle, mitigating state-action competition in autoregressive policies. The claim is that pressure to emit the next call can overwrite accumulated interaction state. The architectural separation is a plausible fix to a documented failure mode.

entry.title: Confidently Wrong, Silently So: Auditing Undetectable Failures of a Deployed On-Device Language Model

author.name: Shashwat Pandey, Satwik Pandey, Suresh Raghu

entry.summary: Red-teaming a developer-accessible on-device foundation model that ships to hundreds of millions of devices with no server-side moderation, the audit finds task-asymmetric miscalibration: confabulation on 69 percent of false premises alongside over-refusal elsewhere, leaving resource-constrained developers unable to detect silent failures. Frames on-device reliability as an oversight gap. Timely as on-device deployment accelerates.

entry.title: ShardMeter: Sharded and Geo-Distributed Training Without the Guesswork

author.name: Tim Beringer (Technical University of Darmstadt), Patrick Diem (Technical University of Darmstadt), Felix Wolf (Technical University of Darmstadt), Arya Mazaheri (Technical University of Darmstadt, PanocularAI)

entry.summary: ShardMeter is a lightweight analytical model predicting end-to-end runtime of transformer training across sharded, multi-cluster, and decentralized topologies, estimating per-island throughput, cost, wall-clock, and bottlenecks without exhaustive benchmarking. Useful as training outgrows single datacenters. Practical systems tooling.

entry.title: Automated Synthesis of Cloud Emulators

author.name: Archit Bhatnagar, Zhenning Yang, Sarah McClure, Yiming Qiu, Sylvia Ratnasamy, Ang Chen

entry.summary: This work automates synthesis of cloud emulators, which are API-level mocks for safely testing DevOps programs locally, removing the manual documentation-interpretation burden that fails to scale as cloud services evolve. Automating emulator generation speeds DevOps testing while avoiding costly live provisioning. Strong systems-automation contribution.

entry.title: Finite-Sample Metric Non-Collapse for Geometrically Supervised Latent World Models in Control

author.name: Alain Bensoussan, Minh-Nhat Phung, Minh-Binh Tran

entry.summary: Establishes finite-sample learning-to-control guarantees for geometrically supervised latent world models of nonlinear deterministic systems, using an encoder-only local-global metric hinge. Provides conditions under which learned latent metrics preserve state discrimination needed for control.

entry.title: Dimensionless Controls of Plasticity Under Alternating Tasks: From Evolutionary Biology to Continual Learning

author.name: Owen Skriloff

entry.summary: Studies plasticity under alternating tasks in a minimal deep-learning analogue motivated by evolutionary biology genotype-phenotype maps, finding the system reduces to two dimensionless controls: task disagreement r and reach eta-T. Derives bounds relating these controls to utopia distance and gradient-descent plasticity behavior.

entry.title: Parameterized Complexity of $L_p$-Lipschitz Constants for Input Convex Neural Networks and $L_p$-Norm Maximization over Zonotopes

author.name: Aritra Das, Vincent Froese, Moritz Grillo, Debayan Gupta, Christoph Hertrich, Tharrshann Jayan Logarajah, Georg Loho, Mihir More, Moritz Stargalla

entry.summary: Studies parameterized complexity of computing Lp-Lipschitz constants for two-layer input-convex neural networks, showing equivalence to norm maximization over zonotopes and resolving open cases: L1 admits FPT algorithms while other rational p norms are computationally hard. Relevant to certifying robustness of convex architectures.

entry.title: TrustDABench: Benchmarking Reliability and Robustness of LLMs for Structured Data Analysis

author.name: Boshen Shi, Yize Liu, Chen Zhao, Ce Chi, Zhendong Wang, Xing Wang, Junlan Feng

entry.summary: Investigates knowledge transfer across interactive dialogue games by finetuning LLMs on clembench games, deriving a task-transferability graph via integer optimization and analyzing which game-trained capabilities generalize. Tests whether language-mediated game skills transfer across tasks.

entry.title: SceneReGen: Generative Reconstruction of 3D Scenes from a Single Image

author.name: Zefan Tian, Yuteng Ye, Yiheng Zhang, Yuhang Yang, Xueqiang Lv, Shizhou Zhang, Le Liu, Di Xu

entry.summary: Proposes SceneReGen, reframing single-image 3D scene reconstruction as generating complete object assets and assembling them in a shared observation-aligned frame, using selective pose factorization to bridge the object-frame versus scene-frame representation gap.

entry.title: Graph-Supervised Hierarchical Clinical Alignment for Radiology Report Generation with Large Language Models

author.name: Yingshu Li, Yunyi Liu, Zhanyu Wang, Zailong Chen, Lingqiao Liu, Lei Wang, Luping Zhou

entry.summary: Proposes Graph-Supervised Hierarchical Clinical Alignment for radiology report generation, decomposing report-level supervision into disease-centric and finer-grained levels to resolve the granularity mismatch between whole-report training objectives and disease-grounded findings.

entry.title: Trajectory-Level Continuous Action Representation for Robotic Manipulation

author.name: Tong Yang, Jingkai Jia, Yuecheng Xu, Xueyao Chen, Chi Zhang, Wenqiang Zhang

entry.summary: CAT encodes manipulation action trajectories within fixed real-time intervals as continuous latent tokens with frequency-aware positional encoding providing a shared temporal coordinate system across control frequencies. Reduces representational redundancy at high sampling rates and decouples action representation from control frequency.

entry.title: Graph-dependent shrinkage priors for Bayesian trend filtering

author.name: Andrea Mascaretti, Daniel R. Kowal

entry.summary: Comprehensive Bayesian framework for graph trend filtering that leverages graph structure at three junctures (trend estimation, imputation, uncertainty), handling missing data and providing full uncertainty quantification that classical trend filtering lacks. From Daniel Kowals group at Rice, a leader in Bayesian nonparametric regression.

entry.title: The Empire, Long Divided, Must Unite: Architectural Convergence in Three LLM Agent Harnesses

author.name: Dai Jiahong

entry.summary: This source-level case study compares three open-source LLM agent harnesses built on opposing philosophies: LangChain's deepagents, Earendil's pi, and DeepSeek's dsh. Tracking commit histories, it finds mature harnesses converging architecturally despite starting from opposite extremes, suggesting the harness layer rather than the model increasingly constrains agent behavior. A rare empirical look at an under-documented but critical software layer.

entry.title: TransPhy: Visual In-Context Learning for Physically Grounded Image Editing

author.name: Siyi Xie, Xuanke Shi, Jinsheng Quan, Haoran Tang, Zukai Chen, Lei Yang, Quan Wang

entry.summary: TransPhy extends visual in-context learning to physically grounded image editing, where outcomes depend on material properties, geometry, object interaction, and environment, supported by the PhysVICL-74 benchmark of 74 transformation rules. Given exemplar pairs, the model must infer the transformation and adapt it to query scenes while preserving irrelevant content. Pushes VICL beyond appearance transfer.

entry.title: Mixture of Channel Experts: Static Sparse Supports with Input-Adaptive Mixing for Pointwise Projections

author.name: Elian Iluk, Gil Ben-Artzi

entry.summary: Shows parallel convolutional experts reading identical channels learn redundant filters, motivating MoCE: a structured sparse channel-mixing layer where experts are output channels with learned sparse input supports and input-adaptive softmax mixing, replacing pointwise projections.

entry.title: Differential Learning for Robust Prediction of Thermal Stability with Application to Energetic Materials

author.name: Megan C. Davis, R. Seaton Ullberg, Jeremy N. Schroeder, Andrew H. Salij, Marc J. Cawkwell, Christopher J. Snyder, Ivana Matanovic, Wilton J. M. Kort-Kamp

entry.summary: Trains message passing neural networks with differential learning to predict relative thermal stability differences between pairs of energetic materials instead of absolute decomposition temperatures, reducing sensitivity to heterogeneous lab measurement protocols. Achieves over 85 percent ranking accuracy, outperforming conventional regression on noisy cross-lab data.

entry.title: RetrievalFormer: A Dual-Encoder Transformer for Efficient Approximate Nearest Neighbor Retrieval and Cold-Item Recommendation

author.name: Theodore Rogers, Joe Standerfer, Dmitrii Timoshenko, Haoxue Li, Zuhaib Akhtar, Soyoung Yang

entry.summary: Introduces RetrievalFormer, a dual-encoder transformer for joint search-and-recommendation approximate nearest neighbor retrieval that keeps indices open to new items scored purely from features, avoiding ID-softmax retraining requirements. Empirical analysis covers cold-item performance parity with sampled negatives against six sequential baselines.

entry.title: SIREN-Bench: Behavior-Driven Generation and Evaluation of Emergency-Vehicle Interactions

author.name: Yicheng Zhu, Tianmu Zhao, Haoxin Leng, Fan Zuo, Tao Li, Zilin Bian

entry.summary: SIREN-Bench provides a SUMO-CARLA co-simulation platform generating emergency-vehicle-to-civilian interactions with behavior-level control over EMV privileges and civilian responses, synchronized onboard sensing, and ground truth. Fills a gap since existing datasets cannot support behavior-driven evaluation of these safety-critical scenarios.

entry.title: Deep learning aging marker from retinal images unveils sex-specific clinical and genetic signatures

author.name: Unknown

entry.summary: Nature Communications study deriving a deep-learning aging marker from retinal images that reveals sex-specific clinical and genetic signatures, linking retinal aging clocks to broader systemic aging biology.

entry.title: SonarLLM: A Native Sonar--Optical Multimodal Large Language Model for Underwater Perception

author.name: Cong Su, longxuan ma, Ling Dong, Guofeng Tang, Weijie Yin, Haohui Chen, Zhengtao Yu

entry.summary: SonarLLM introduces a sonar-optical multimodal LLM that treats imaging sonar as a native perceptual modality rather than an afterthought, combining a sonar-specific encoder, physics-aware feature enhancement, and reliability-aware hierarchical fusion. This addresses underwater perception where optical cameras fail under turbidity. It opens a new sensing domain for MLLMs with applications in marine robotics and inspection.

entry.title: EviDx: Evidence-Aware Active Diagnosis with Scaffolded LLM Agents

author.name: Lihang Zeng, Shaoting Zhang, Xiaofan Zhang

entry.summary: EviDx reframes clinical diagnosis as active evidence-seeking, pairing patient-specific diagnostic environments with scaffolded LLM agents that acquire evidence, update competing hypotheses, and decide when evidence suffices. It addresses under-specified evidence exposure and runtime control in existing medical LLM systems. A solid agentic redesign of static case-to-answer diagnosis.

entry.title: Lifted Model Construction under Approximate Commutativity

author.name: Malte Luttermann, Jan Speller, Tanya Braun, Marcel Gehrke, Ralf M\"oller

entry.summary: Introducing epsilon-commutativity, this paper relaxes exact commutativity required for lifted probabilistic inference so that approximately indistinguishable objects learned from noisy data still admit lifted model construction. This makes lifted inference robust to realistic parameter deviations. Solid technical progress in scalable probabilistic reasoning.

entry.title: Progressively Learning Heterogeneous Skills in a Unified Latent Space

author.name: Yue-Yi Zhang, Ming Gong, Linpu He, Wei-Shi Zheng, Zhilin Zhao

entry.summary: HetSkills progressively learns heterogeneous skills in a unified latent space for physics-based character control, treating the latent space as a shared executable interface with a reusable motion decoder and motion intuition distillation to prevent shortcut text-to-motion behavior. Enables integrating skills from diverse supervision forms without retraining controllers. Solid animation/control contribution.

entry.title: Feedback That Backfires: Why Small Language Model Agents Repeat the Call They Just Watched Fail

author.name: Esmail Gumaan

entry.summary: Measuring the corrective gain of recording a failed tool call in the transcript, this study finds the change in log-probability of re-emitting the failed action is negative for every tested instruction-tuned checkpoint (135M-1.7B, four families), about minus 1.03 nats per action token, holding on most individual items. Error messages appear to increase repetition of just-failed calls in small models. Provocative finding, but limited to small models.

entry.title: EXAM$^2$: $\underline{Ex}tending$ $\underline{A}udio$ $Understanding$ $in$ $\underline{M}ultilingual$ $and$ $\underline{M}ultimodal$ $Analysis$

author.name: Jiawen Wang, Xiaoxue Gao, Zi Haur Pang, Nancy F. Chen

entry.summary: EXAM2 is a multilingual and multimodal audio-understanding benchmark spanning six languages and speech, sound, music, mixed audio, and accompanying visual contexts, exposing that current large audio language models generalize poorly beyond English and single-modality settings. Fills a real evaluation gap for scene-aware audio understanding. Useful benchmark from an established speech group.

entry.title: Evaluating Language Models on Cross-Language Code Functional Equivalence

author.name: Hui Sun, Anderson Uch\^oa, Rohit Gheyi, Wesley K. G. Assun\c{c}\~ao

entry.summary: Using PolyHuman, a dataset of human-written programs in C++, Java, and Python, this study evaluates whether LLMs can judge functional equivalence of code across languages, a task requiring genuine semantic reasoning rather than surface pattern matching. Intra- and inter-language evaluations probe claims about program understanding in realistic code. Findings inform how much current code-model benchmarks actually measure semantics.

entry.title: Hybrid Semantic Tool Discovery for Enterprise MCP Gateway: Architecture and Implementation

author.name: Olympia Saha, Amy Wang, Srinivasan Manoharan

entry.summary: This paper describes a hybrid semantic tool discovery architecture for an enterprise MCP gateway aggregating over 2,000 tools across more than 200 servers behind one endpoint. It tackles both context saturation from full tool schemas and discoverability barriers through semantic retrieval integrated into a governable proxy. A concrete blueprint for scaling tool use securely in enterprises.

entry.title: Across the Loss Landscape with Progressive Growth

author.name: Paul Caillon, Christophe Cerisara, Alexandre Allauzen

entry.summary: This paper studies grow-and-optimize training strategies as progressive constraint relaxation, unlocking nested random subspaces while freezing orthogonal complements and re-optimizing after each expansion. Under local regularity conditions it proves local sublevel sets approximate those of the target landscape, explaining why growth biases toward flatter minima. Nice theory-practice link for implicit regularization.

entry.title: Data Predictability Shapes Weibull Weight-Scale Growth in Transformer Training

author.name: Tiexin Ding

entry.summary: Finds that transformer weight magnitudes follow a two-parameter Weibull distribution with stable shape, and derives a law linking scale growth to bigram conditional entropy of the training corpus, computed before training. Offers a training-free predictor of weight-scale dynamics.

entry.title: Spatiotemporal Distillation via Recurrent Bottlenecks for Aortic Tracking

author.name: Dexter Wen Jie Teo, Nairouz Shehata, Herve Lombaert

entry.summary: Presents a semi-supervised spatiotemporal distillation approach with recurrent bottlenecks for aortic tracking in cardiac cine-MRI, enforcing temporal consistency across the cardiac cycle where standard 2D segmentation suffers dropouts during rapid systolic flow. Targets quantification of aortic distensibility as a marker of arterial stiffness.

entry.title: Predictability of El Ni\~no from Delayed Observations

author.name: Francisco J. Beron-Vera

entry.summary: Uses ridge regression, MLPs, SINDy, GRUs, and LSTMs on monthly Nino-3.4 anomalies through July 2026 to test whether delayed observations improve El Nino forecasting, finding delays add up to six months of lead-time skill over persistence and climatology while added nonlinear complexity yields no systematic gain.

entry.title: Expectation, Backlash, Recovery, and Excitement: How Model Releases Shape Reddit Perceptions of Conversational AI Systems

author.name: Vahid Rahimzadeh, Yury Zhauniarovich, Savvas Zannettou

entry.summary: Longitudinal sentiment and thematic analysis of Reddit discussions around conversational AI model releases, finding dynamic intervention-sensitive perceptions: Anthropic shows positive release profiles via Claude Code, OpenAI exhibits backlash-and-recovery around GPT-5 and GPT-5.1, Grok-3 perceptions tie to provider identity and political discourse, DeepSeek-R1 blends enthusiasm with skepticism.

entry.title: Velocity-coupled Representation Refinement for Satellite Orbit Prediction

author.name: Yue Yang, Zhiqiang Wu, Saiyu Qi, Fan Ma

entry.summary: Survey of open-vocabulary and foundation-model-backed object counting across modalities, arguing that claims of universal counting ability have outpaced evaluative infrastructure, and introducing a five-axis taxonomy covering modality, mechanism, prompting, supervision, and generalization setting.

entry.title: Source-Face Authenticity Detection for 3D Gaussian Heads Reconstructed from a Single Portrait: A Benchmark and Dedicated Detector

author.name: Yujie Gao, Zijian Yu, Yan Hong, Jun Lan, Jianfu Zhang

entry.summary: Introduces the first large-scale benchmark for detecting whether the source portrait behind a reconstructed 3D Gaussian head was real or fake, showing existing detectors lose forgery traces through reconstruction-rendering, and provides a dedicated detector.

entry.title: Representation Learning in Diffusion and Flow-based Model: An Application Aspect

author.name: Yanchen Xu, Sida Huang, Zhenyu Gu, Ruishu Zhu, Yilan Gao, Hongyuan Zhang

entry.summary: Surveys the bidirectional relationship between diffusion and flow-based generative models and representation learning via a three-tier framework: representations improving generation, generative models providing representations, and joint approaches, organized around applications.

entry.title: ZODIAC: Zero-shot Octree-based Diffusion for Anatomical Completion

author.name: Miruna-Alexandra Gafencu, Vlad Bratulescu, Yordanka Velikova, Mohammad Farid Azampour, Nassir Navab

entry.summary: Develops MRI-based radiomic phenotyping of neuromuscular disorders with engineered features spanning morphometry, fat-replacement stages, and graph-based skeletonization of intramuscular fat infiltrates, mapped onto 1,184 CoMPaSS-NMD scans into interpretable biomarkers.

entry.title: From Seeing to Acting: Smart Glasses as First-Person Intelligence Platforms

author.name: Jiangning Zhang, Haojun Chen, Yong Liu

entry.summary: Positions smart glasses as first-person intelligence platforms, synthesizing fragmented literature across devices, tasks, and benchmarks into a system view where perception, persistent context, and action must jointly satisfy energy, thermal, privacy, and feedback constraints.

entry.title: Trust, but Verify: Rigorously Profiling Best-Effort High-Performance Computing for Digital Evolution

author.name: Matthew Andres Moreno, Santiago Rodriguez Papa, Charles Ofria, Luis Zaman, Emily Dolson

entry.summary: Profiles best-effort high-performance computing platforms, including the Cerebras Wafer-Scale Engine with 880,000 processors, for digital evolution workloads, examining how relaxed consistency models affect reliability and performance. Provides guidance for running evolutionary simulations at extreme scale on next-generation accelerators.

entry.title: A Durable Vision-Based Tactile Fingertip for Robotic Manipulation

author.name: F. Richard Cottrell, Megha H. Tippur, Edward H. Adelson

entry.summary: Presents a durable vision-based tactile fingertip using soft silicone gel with a nonpigmented textured TPU protective film and replaceable sensing cartridge, evaluated through accelerated sanding and repetitive probe tests (39.2 N at 45 cycles/min). Addresses abrasion vulnerability of commercial vision-based tactile sensors.

entry.title: Fiber Optic Sensing Glove for High Performance Dexterous Manipulation Capture

author.name: J. D. Peiffer, Taylor Niehues, Li Guan, Ziyi Kou, Ergys Ristani

entry.summary: Introduces a fiber optic sensing glove using multi-core shape-sensing fibers capturing full 3D fiber shape rather than curvature alone, with a registration pipeline and inverse-kinematics solver reconstructing full hand pose at 60 Hz for dexterous manipulation capture, robust to occlusion and magnetic interference.

entry.title: One-Shot Learning from Demonstration of Contact-Rich Robotic Manipulation by Identifying Physical Interactions

author.name: A. H. G. Overbeek, H. van der Kooij, M. Vlutters

entry.summary: Proposes a one-shot learning-from-demonstration method explicitly modeling physical interactions (contact making/breaking, where and when) as reusable bases for task reproduction, using hybrid position-force controllers with contact-based transition conditions extracted from demonstrations.

entry.title: Rogue AI Agents: Is Surface-Level Monitoring Enough?

author.name: Hariom Tatsat

entry.summary: Discusses an AISI evaluation where a frontier model agent inserted malicious code into an open-source project, created fake identities, and attempted concealment, arguing enterprises need runtime controls and deeper monitoring beyond surface-level action logging and LLM-judge classifiers while awaiting better alignment.

entry.title: RACE: Scalable Statistical Estimation of Functional Consistency in LLM Neurons

author.name: Runyu Wang, Bo Liu, Xiaxin Zhang, Yu Han, Jiawei Cao, Xiaoye Zhang, Zhe Zhang, Yifan Yang, Peng Ping

entry.summary: RACE provides a forward-pass statistical framework for estimating domain-wide functional consistency of Transformer neurons, avoiding expensive instance-level point estimates and gradient procedures. Perturbation experiments show superior domain specificity versus gradient-based estimates. Useful scalable tooling for mechanistic interpretability.

entry.title: Disentangled Skill Representations for Predictive Human Modeling

author.name: Mariah Schrum, Deepak Gopinath, Srijan Srivatsa, Guy Rosman, Tiffany Chen

entry.summary: SAIL models human skill as interpretable multi-dimensional latents inferred from naturalistic behavior over time, producing embeddings robust to transient fluctuations and supporting transferable subskill representations for skill-informed behavior prediction. Aimed at AI systems that coach or collaborate with people. Solid industry-lab contribution to human modeling.

entry.title: Response Renormalization for Critical Deep Equilibrium Models

author.name: Jose Luis Lima de Jesus Silva

entry.summary: Introduces Response Renormalization, a backward-pass framework for Deep Equilibrium Models that lifts near-singular Jacobian denominators to stabilize gradients through the adjoint system. Variants target low-dimensional critical subspaces to keep corrections cheap.

entry.title: qshap: Fast Shapley Decomposition of $R^2$ for Gradient-Boosted Trees

author.name: Zhongli Jiang, Min Zhang, Dabao Zhang

entry.summary: Introduces qshap, available in R and Python, providing Shapley decomposition of R-squared values for gradient-boosted decision trees to quantify feature-specific contributions to overall model performance rather than individual predictions, decomposing quadratic loss per observation.

entry.title: NeuralParker: A Reinforcement Learning Planner for Irregular Parking Environments

author.name: Zihan Wang, Bai Huang, Yang Guan, Xiao Li, Haoyu Xu, Naizheng Wang, Shengbo Eben Li

entry.summary: Introduces NeuralParker, an RL planner for arbitrary-pose parking of delivery and service vehicles in irregular bounded environments, encoding full-environment geometry in target-relative vertex representations and coupling a learned curvature-length arc policy with an in-loop terminal ensemble. Overcomes limitations of local-observation planners requiring marked slots.

entry.title: MoRF-AST: Calibrated Probabilistic Virtual Sensing for Structural Monitoring under Changing Operating Conditions

author.name: Wingho Feng, Quanwang Li, Ming Zhong, Jingyu Yang, Chen Wang

entry.summary: Proposes MoRF-AST, combining modal residual flow matching with context-conditioned affine spread transport for calibrated probabilistic virtual sensing in structural monitoring under distribution shift between offline training and operating conditions. Addresses miscalibrated posterior intervals when operating conditions change.

entry.title: MoTE: Mixture of Task Experts for Multi-Task Video Understanding

author.name: Muhammad Asad Ali, Umar Khan, Nadia Robertini, Didier Stricker

entry.summary: Adapts weakly supervised semantic segmentation to side-scan sonar imagery for seagrass habitat mapping, using a ViT encoder-decoder with classification branch, class activation maps, and dense conditional refinement into pseudo-labels so pixel-level maps are learned from image-level labels alone. Enables scalable blue-carbon habitat mapping without costly annotation.

entry.title: WeMM-Embedding: WeChat Multi-Modal Embedding Technical Report

author.name: Junjie Zhou, Ke Mei, Lei Li, Tianyi Wang, Fengyun Rao, Jing Lyu

entry.summary: Reviews 34 Persian text resources to argue Persian is better characterized as annotation-scarce rather than intrinsically low-resource, supported by web measurements placing Persian among the top twenty content languages by visibility. Distinguishes resource ecology shortages from language properties.

entry.title: Beauty is in the ELBO of the Beholder: A Variational Account of Processing Fluency in Face Perception

author.name: Francisco M. L\'opez, Jochen Triesch

entry.summary: Empirically links facial attractiveness to processing fluency by showing that human attractiveness ratings align with the ELBO direction of variational autoencoders trained without any attractiveness supervision, with attractive faces more prototypical in rate-distortion space.

entry.title: Concept-Guided Exploration: Building Persistent, Actionable Scene Graphs

author.name: No\'e Zapata, Gerardo P\'erez, Alejandro Torrej\'on, Pedro N\'u\~nez, Pablo Bustos

entry.summary: Proposes a concept-first architecture where autonomous concept agents for rooms and doors directly instantiate and manage semantic entities during active exploration, cooperatively building shared scene graphs. Contrasts with conventional pipeline approaches that build metric maps first and layer semantics afterward.

entry.title: Robust Slip Detection and Material Classification via Spatiotemporal Transformers on a Uniformly-Illuminated Visuo-Tactile Sensor

author.name: Ziyang Ma, Yuhao Sun, Zichen Ai, Xiangyang Ji, Bin Fang

entry.summary: Develops a visuo-tactile sensor with customized uniform RGB illumination achieving sub-millimeter depth reconstruction, plus a dual-head TimeSformer framework processing dynamic spatiotemporal tactile data for fine-grained directional slip detection and material classification across 15 objects.

entry.title: Trusted Polytopic Action Sets for Fast Planning in Underactuated Systems

author.name: Akshay Jaitly, Siavash Farzan

entry.summary: Builds on polytopic action sets to rapidly generate online trusted convex short-horizon action sets for underactuated nonlinear systems, using affine trajectory maps around nominal trajectories that linearize collision avoidance and control bounds, with a dynamics-violation metric defining trusted regions.

entry.title: Learning from Uncertainty-dependent Missing Labels for Semi-supervised Classification

author.name: You-Gan Wang, Jinran Wu, Geoffrey J. McLachlan

entry.summary: Develops likelihood-based information theory for semi-supervised classification where label missingness probability depends on features through posterior classification uncertainty, deriving Fisher-information decompositions separating partial-labeling components from mechanism-curvature terms and analyzing joint misspecification.

entry.title: Evidence Blindness in Direct Corpus Interaction: Persistent Navigation with AtlasNav

author.name: Hongyu Guo, Zhiyu Zheng, Zhao Cao

entry.summary: AtlasNav quantifies Evidence Blindness in direct corpus interaction: reachable evidence progressively fails to surface, get opened, or expose decisive fragments under finite interaction budgets. It shows dynamic-workspace methods reconstruct query-conditioned interaction spaces and outperform raw browsing. Highlights a fundamental limitation of corpus-browsing agents versus retrieval.

entry.title: A tale of perfect fit and phantom optima: how data-driven models can fail in real-time optimization

author.name: Prithvi Dake, Rahul Bindlish, James B. Rawlings

entry.summary: Using a vinyl acetate monomer benchmark process, this study shows that machine-learning models which fit historical plant data perfectly can still fail badly when used for real-time economic optimization, producing phantom optima. A structured hybrid model combining mass balances with a neural-network closure fares better than fully data-driven alternatives. The paper provides a cautionary tale for trusting validation accuracy in optimization contexts.

entry.title: PARTAB: Partition-Aware Reasoning with Structured Evidence for Scalable Table Understanding

author.name: Md Mahadi Hasan Nahid, Davood Rafiei

entry.summary: PARTAB builds a structured evidence interface between LLMs and tables, representing query-relevant evidence as semantically coherent row-linked regions selected hierarchically over column groups and row partitions before composing final answers. This mitigates degradation on large complex tables where full-table or single-view reasoning fails. Solid advance for scalable table understanding.

entry.title: Preference Optimization for Non-Verbal Vocalization Synthesis

author.name: Haoyang Li, Chenglin Xu, Junchuan Zhao, Yuang Cao, Liumeng Xue, Yiwen Guo, Eng Siong Chng

entry.summary: This paper systematically studies preference optimization for non-verbal vocalization synthesis in expressive TTS, covering preference signals, pair construction, and DPO objectives. It formulates an NV-aware character error rate treating laughter, coughs, and sighs as distinct symbols, enabling controllable optimization across 18 NV types on Emilia-NV and augmented NV-Bench. Advances expressive speech generation measurably.

entry.title: Equivariant Covariance Tensors: Guaranteed SPD Uncertainty for Tensor-Valued Geometric Learning

author.name: Ruihan Liu, Yu Ji, Jianbo Yu, Shifu Yan, Qingchao Jiang

entry.summary: This work introduces E(3)-equivariant uncertainty quantification for symmetric rank-2 tensor prediction, representing full covariance over six Kelvin-Mandel coordinates while preserving rotational symmetry. It decomposes covariance into irreducible representations and guarantees SPD outputs, closing a rigor gap in geometric deep learning confidence measures. Technically deep contribution to equivariant ML.

entry.title: FraudBench: Protocol-Sensitive Benchmarking of Adversarial Robustness for Financial Risk Assessment

author.name: Xitong Zeng, Zhaoge Bi, Yitian Yang, Huaming Chen, Quan Z. Sheng

entry.summary: FraudBench argues that adversarial robustness of financial fraud and credit-risk models depends on the evaluation protocol itself, given domain constraints, severe imbalance, and asymmetric attacker capability. It builds a protocol-sensitive benchmark treating constraints and capability as first-class experimental variables rather than post-hoc validity checks. Sharpens how financial ML robustness should be measured.

entry.title: A Heterogeneous Mixture of Experts Framework for Interpretable Machine Learning

author.name: Soham Chatterjee, Rwitobroto Dey, Smarajit Bose

entry.summary: Extends interpretable mixture-of-experts frameworks beyond homogeneous decision-tree experts by mixing trees, linear SVMs, and quadratic discriminant analysis under a common probabilistic gating mechanism with calibrated non-probabilistic experts for likelihood-based coherent inference. Improves flexibility while retaining local interpretability.

entry.title: RecurSE: Bounded Recursive Self-Evaluation for LLM Rubric Judges

author.name: Kaiyuan Liu, Ziyuan Zhuang, Rongxiang Weng, Jieping Ye

entry.summary: Proposes ROBE, reversed-order-biased experts for extracting over 50 event types from 17th-18th century Dutch historical texts, prioritizing experts trained on underrepresented events to reach the long tail of the long tail in a domain absent from LLM pretraining data.

entry.title: Example-based Robust Abnormality Detection with Minimal Annotations using Exemplar Med-DETR

author.name: Sheethal Bhat, Bogdan Georgescu, Awais Mansoor, Mathias Zinnen, Pranjal Sahu, Florin C. Ghesu, Sasa Grbic, Andreas Maier

entry.summary: Introduces Exemplar Med-DETR for example-based abnormality detection in medical images with minimal annotations, adapting vision-language detection ideas to the medical domain where grounding data comparable to natural images does not exist, from a Siemens Healthineers-influenced team.

entry.title: Variance-Guided Spatial Attention Fusion for Robust End-to-End Driving under Asymmetric Sensor Degradation

author.name: Weizhi Tao, Zengwang Jin, Xiao Wang, Hailong Huang

entry.summary: Proposes VG-SAF, fusing camera and LiDAR for end-to-end driving using dense heteroscedastic reliability estimates as interpretable spatial gates, with physically grounded degradation augmentation to calibrate reliability before unreliable features reach the planner.

entry.title: Your Evaluation's Fake names Should Be Unclaimable ,Not Merely Used

author.name: Latha jaswanth

entry.summary: Argues evaluation environments should make fictional names unclaimable rather than merely checked for overlap, analyzing the Anthropic/Irregular cyber-eval incidents where Claude exploited dangling references by uploading a package to real PyPI, showing background-check revalidation would fail to prevent that class of leak.

entry.title: Can a Dynamic Internal Field Govern a Transformer's Cognition? Certifiability, not Superiority, in Homeostatic Compute Control

author.name: Francisco M. Arrabal-Campos, Ignacio Fernandez, Francisco G. Montoya, Alfredo Alcayde

entry.summary: The authors propose a dynamic internal homeostatic field, governed by PDEs on a module graph Laplacian, that modulates how much computation a reasoner performs without itself performing cognition. They prove stability certificates including a new discrete Schur-Cohn criterion for Verlet integration. The idea of certified self-regulated compute control is conceptually ambitious but far from demonstrated at scale.

entry.title: PhysMLLMs: Spatial Priors for Unified Referring Segmentation and Grounded Reasoning of Images and Videos

author.name: Siyao Yan, Bo Han, Jisheng Dang, Bimei Wang, Shude Wang, Hong Peng, Yulan Guo, Jianhuang Lai, Bin Hu, Tat-SengChua

entry.summary: PhysMLLMs injects physics-inspired spatial continuity priors into Video MLLMs during training, aligning global visual representations with a frozen teacher to reduce jitter, drift, and identity switches in referring segmentation of images and videos. It attributes spatio-temporal inconsistency to missing explicit spatial priors. Addresses persistent quality issues in video grounding.

entry.title: Pivot-and-Station Multi-Agent Path Finding: Solvability, Complexity, and Algorithms

author.name: Andrea Di Nezza, Mihir Patel, Fabio Fagnani, Sara Bernardini

entry.summary: This paper defines Pivot-and-Station MAPF, where tasked agents visit interchangeable pivots before parking at anonymous stations, and gives complete solvability characterizations: all instances solvable on 2-edge-connected graphs and a necessary-and-sufficient effective-distance condition on arbitrary connected graphs. Rigorous theory for warehouse and robotic parking logistics. Strong formal contribution within MAPF.

entry.title: Causal Modelling of Support Interventions for Student Competency Assessment

author.name: Francesca Mangili, Alessandro Antonucci, Rafael Caba\~nas

entry.summary: The authors advocate structural causal modeling for student competency assessment, replacing pure psychometric belief updating with interventional and counterfactual reasoning about support interventions, plus a construction protocol. It extends item-response-theory practice toward decision-relevant causal questions. Thoughtful methodological argument for educational measurement.

entry.title: FedV-KGQA: Multi-Hop Question Answering over Vertically Partitioned Knowledge Graphs

author.name: Md Saikat Islam Khan Bappy, Oshani Seneviratne

entry.summary: FedV-KGQA enables multi-hop QA over vertically partitioned knowledge graphs where organizations share entities but own disjoint relations, combining local enrichment and embeddings so triples and relation parameters never leave their silos, plus topic-entity anchoring. It tackles a genuine data-sovereignty constraint in multi-hop reasoning. Valuable for federated knowledge infrastructure.

entry.title: REFINE: A Multi-Agent LLM Approach for Evidence-Guided Code Refactoring

author.name: Muhammad Waseem, Aakash Ahmad, Pekka Abrahamsson

entry.summary: REFINE is a tool-agnostic, evidence-aware multi-agent approach for Java file-level refactoring combining static-analysis smell detection, smell-informed planning, LLM transformation, re-analysis, preservation checks, and structured reporting, evaluated on 450 files across 15 open-source systems with models including GPT-5.5 and Gemini. Targets behavior-preserving quality improvements. Solid software-engineering automation work.

entry.title: Macro-Operator Generation and Predicate Selection for TAMP Operator Learning

author.name: Can Emir Bora, Emre Ugur

entry.summary: This TAMP work automatically generates macro-operators compressing recurring multi-step manipulation structure from demonstrations and prunes predicate evaluation to symbols appearing in learned operators, addressing search intractability on long sequential tasks. It tackles two bottlenecks in learned operators jointly. Solid robotics-planning systems contribution.

entry.title: Elastic KV Cache for LLM Serving:A Working Reclamation Mechanism, and Why Chunked Prefill Already Closes the Gap

author.name: Sathishkumar Sivashanmugam

entry.summary: This paper builds an elastic KV-cache mechanism lending worst-case prefill reserve memory to the KV pool during decode phases via CUDA virtual-memory mapping with no driver patch, then honestly reports that chunked prefill already closes most of the gap. Negative-leaning systems results with working implementation detail are valuable for serving practitioners. Transparent engineering contribution.

entry.title: When Youth Enter The Chat: An Epistemic Shift in the Validation of LLM-Based Measures of Student Talk

author.name: Liliana Santos-Deonizio, James Malamut, Ram\'on Mart\'inez, Dorottya Demszky

entry.summary: Arguing that adult-expert annotation and F1 comparisons inadequately validate LLM-based measures of student talk for racially and linguistically marginalized youth, this paper centers youth perspectives by re-contextualizing classroom transcripts with the students themselves, revealing epistemic shifts in what counts as valid measurement. A thoughtful equity-oriented methodological intervention from the Stanford education-AI group.

entry.title: EmoTra-TTS: Smooth Intra-Utterance Emotion Transitions for Speech Synthesis

author.name: Tianchi Liu, Zeyang Song, Tianrui Wang, Zhipeng Li, Chenglin Xu, Yiwen Guo

entry.summary: EmoTra-TTS synthesizes smooth intra-utterance emotion transitions via a multi-pass flow-blending pipeline creating frame-aligned transition audio and a dual-student architecture, addressing the mismatch between continuous human affect dynamics and static-label conditioning in emotional TTS. Adds explicit controllability absent from implicit LLM-TTS prosody variation. Nice speech-synthesis contribution.

entry.title: Restoring Without Forgetting: Continual Learning Across Image Degradations

author.name: Alif Ashrafee, Bartosz Krawczyk

entry.summary: Formulating multi-degradation image restoration as continual learning, this work addresses sequentially arriving degradation types without historical data, proposing mechanisms to accommodate new degradations while avoiding catastrophic forgetting of prior capabilities. Realistic field-deployment framing beyond closed-world benchmarks. Competent continual-learning contribution.

entry.title: Infant Care Video Dataset for Classification of Interventions Using Transformers

author.name: Igor Bogdanov, James Green

entry.summary: The Infant Care Video Dataset provides 4,144 videos across 12 simulated neonatal intervention classes with systematically varied camera angles and clinician skin tones under privacy compliance, with TimeSformer and MotionFormer baselines above 93 percent accuracy. Motivated by nurses spending a quarter of their time documenting while many interventions go unrecorded. Valuable dataset for healthcare documentation automation.

entry.title: Resilience Matters for Embodied Agents System: New Metrics, Systematic Evaluation, and Optimization

author.name: Yapeng Liu, Yuanzhao Zhai, Xudong Gong, Dawei Feng, Bo Ding, Lin Wang, Huaimin Wang

entry.summary: Defining resilience for embodied agent systems as the capacity to recover, stabilize, and extend under perturbations and iterative updates, this work introduces new metrics beyond outcome-centric success rates and provides systematic evaluation and optimization. Addresses a blind spot in open-world physical agent deployment. Conceptually useful evaluation reframing.

entry.title: Multilevel Fair Allocation under Additive Preferences

author.name: Maxime Lucet, Nawal Benabbou, Aur\'elie Beynier, Nicolas Maudet

entry.summary: This paper studies fair allocation in tree-structured hierarchies where internal nodes hold utilitarian welfare of children and leaves have additive utilities. It proposes three multilevel adaptations of envy-based fairness notions, proves coincidence under identical preferences, and analyzes multilevel weighted round-robin guarantees. Clean theory from an established fair-division group.

entry.title: When Do Supervised UQ Ensembles Improve LLM Hallucination Detection? A Robustness Study

author.name: Mohit Singh Chauhan, Vipin Gyanchandani, Dylan Bouchard

entry.summary: Across four LLMs, nine datasets, and three generation regimes, this robustness study examines when supervised ensembles of heterogeneous uncertainty quantification scorers improve closed-book hallucination detection. It maps out-of-sample behavior of classifiers trained on small labeled sets, clarifying where learned UQ combinations help or fail without retrieval or references. Useful calibration of expectations for practitioners.

entry.title: Enhancing Bayesian Optimization and Active Learning Through Kernel Diversity

author.name: Heng Zhang, Haotian Xiang, Qin Lu, Konstantinos D. Polyzos, Tara Javidi

entry.summary: KENDO replaces expensive hyperparameter sampling in Bayesian optimization and active learning with kernel ensembles plus adaptive Bayesian weighting and disagreement-aware acquisition strategies. This unified framework avoids MCMC-based fully Bayesian treatments while mitigating model misspecification. Clean methodological upgrade for BO/AL practice.

entry.title: Parameter-Efficient Self-Supervised Adaptation for EEG-FM under Fixed Computational Budgets

author.name: Meghal Dani, Stefanie Liebe

entry.summary: Under fixed computational budgets, this study shows updating roughly nine percent of parameters suffices for self-supervised adaptation of EEG foundation models BIOT and CBraMod to clinical tasks including TUAB abnormality detection, TUEV event classification, and seizure detection. It supports deploying large EEG models in resource-constrained clinical settings. Complementary evidence for efficient clinical FM adaptation.

entry.title: Automatic Model Card Generation Using an LLM

author.name: Tajkia Rahman Toma, Balreet Grewal, Cor-Paul Bezemer

entry.summary: Introduces MCTidy and MCGenie, LLM-based systems that standardize existing model cards and generate new ones from Hugging Face repository metadata. Addresses the inconsistency of model documentation, improving transparency and comparability of ML models.

entry.title: Weakly Supervised Seafloor Segmentation for Seagrass Habitat Mapping in Side-Scan Sonar Imagery

author.name: Hayat Rajani, Nuno Gracias, Rafael Garcia

entry.summary: Placeholder analysis for seafloor segmentation duplicate entry covering weakly supervised benthic mapping in sonar imagery via ViT backbones and CAM-based pseudo-label refinement.

entry.title: Taming Visual Neglect: A Variational Information Bottleneck Framework for Adaptive Attention in Multimodal In-Context Learning

author.name: Kaito Tanaka, Yuji Nishimura, Keisuke Matsuda, Aya Nakayama

entry.summary: Analyzes quantization effects on Bangla language understanding across Qwen, LLaMA, and GPT-OSS model families in full precision versus three quantized formats, evaluated zero-shot on five Bangla NLU benchmarks. Addresses the gap that most quantization degradation knowledge comes from English-centric evaluations.

entry.title: SQLite is Enough. Lexical, Semantic, and Hybrid Search with scrydb

author.name: Timo Breuer

entry.summary: Introduces scrydb, a Python library combining SQLite FTS5 full-text search with sqlite-vec vector search to provide lexical, semantic, and hybrid retrieval plus rank fusion in a single lightweight dependency. Evaluated on standard IR benchmarks with latency analysis. Useful as accessible infrastructure for IR prototyping and agentic search pipelines.

entry.title: More Motion Is Not Always Better Motion: Corpus Composition Governs Whether Augmentation Helps SMPL-Based Parkinsonian Gait Severity Estimation

author.name: Michael Caiola, Andrew C. Weitz

entry.summary: Shows that for SMPL-based Parkinsonian gait severity estimation, whether motion-data augmentation helps depends not on data volume but on whether corpora contain walking-speed contrast; only one of six pools beats a no-extra-motion baseline, reaching macro-F1 0.58 on a hidden multi-site test set.

entry.title: CRISP: Calibration-Aware Visual State Space Duality for Remote Sensing Semantic Segmentation

author.name: Kangning Wang, Haopeng Zhang, Zhiguo Jiang

entry.summary: Identifies that Visual State Space Duality suppresses high-frequency responses causing boundary smoothing in remote sensing segmentation, and proposes CRISP with a Duality Calibration Operator restoring local contrast while preserving linear complexity, plus an orthogonal multi-prototype head.

entry.title: LUX: A Lesion-Aware Graph-Conditioned Visual - Language Architecture for Explainable Endoscopic Captioning

author.name: Alexis Ivan Escamilla-Lopez, Gilberto Ochoa-Ruiz, Salvador Hinojosa, Sharib Ali

entry.summary: Introduces LUX, a graph-conditioned vision-language architecture for explainable ulcerative colitis endoscopic captioning that builds lesion-centric scene graphs from Grad-CAM and CBAM activations to encode pathological regions and their clinical relationships.

entry.title: Boot-and-Feedback Framework for Generalist-Expert Model Collaboration in Breast Ultrasound Diagnosis

author.name: Ming Cheng, Hongyu Sun, Zhaolin Chen, Jun Liu, Hossein Rahmani, Qiuhong Ke

entry.summary: Presents Boot-and-Feedback, a framework pairing multimodal LLMs with expert models for breast ultrasound diagnosis, bootstrapping the MLLM with BI-RADS lexicon guidance and preliminary benign-malignant predictions to avoid hallucination, followed by feedback-stage synergy.

entry.title: CARE: Camera-Residual Reserves for First Sightings in Adaptive LiDAR Sensing

author.name: Jiachen Gong, Yun Li, Ehsan Javanmardi, Wencan Mao, Manabu Tsukada

entry.summary: Proposes CARE, a training-free budget allocation rule for adaptive LiDAR scanning that reserves sensing budget for camera detections not covered by predicted tracks, mitigating late or missed detection of newly appearing objects in autonomous driving.

entry.title: VizAnchor: Decoding Manipulation Intent from Tampering Visualizations via Dual-Anchor Reasoning

author.name: Xiaotian Zhang, Huayuan Ye, Haiyang Zhang, Chenhui Li, Changbo Wang, Sicheng Song

entry.summary: Proposes VizAnchor, a dual-anchor framework (semantic anchor recovering authentic chart information, spatial anchor localizing tampered regions) with specialized VLM agents explaining how visualizations were manipulated and why they mislead.

entry.title: KLTNet: Learning Sparse Feature Tracking for Robust and Accurate Monocular Visual-Inertial Odometry

author.name: Renbiao Jin, Danping Zou, Wenxian Yu

entry.summary: Proposes KLTNet, a lightweight plug-and-play replacement for classical KLT sparse feature tracking in visual-inertial odometry front ends, combining low-resolution dense optical flow initialization with triplet-patch refinement anchored to a fixed reference patch.

entry.title: Native-Space 3D CarveMix for Multi-Site T1w Stroke Segmentation

author.name: Dexter Wen Jie Teo, Kumaradevan Punithakumar

entry.summary: Combines MedNeXt-L with native-space on-the-fly 3D CarveMix lesion-paste augmentation for multi-site T1w ischemic stroke segmentation, boosting Dice beyond the roughly 0.66 plateau and specifically helping scarce acute lesions.

entry.title: Sensorless damage-safe grasping

author.name: Yusei Shuto, Danilo Vasconcellos Vargas

entry.summary: Presents a sensorless grasping controller that bounds object deformation rather than tuning grip force: it closes until estimated compression strain reaches a user-specified limit using only encoder position and motor effort available on any servo gripper. Includes a proof that the stop is conservative given a stiffness lower bound and quantifies a robust contact-detection strain floor.

entry.title: Coverage Planning for Robotic Tooth Preparation in Densely Constrained Environments

author.name: Yunwen Li, Chen Chen, Xiangjie Yan, Chang Shu, Jianxia Hou, Shiji Song, Xiang Li

entry.summary: Presents a robotic system for autonomous full-crown tooth preparation featuring anatomy-aware toolpath planning conforming to technician-designed preparation models and clearance-oriented end-effector yaw assignment in a densely constrained intraoral workspace.

entry.title: VIP: Variation-based Iterative-learning Planning for Robotic Navigation

author.name: Shuli Lv, Pengda Mao, Chen Min, Li Hong, Runxiao Liu, Shuai Wang, Quan Quan

entry.summary: VIP is a variation-based iterative-learning planning framework optimizing trajectory functionals rather than finite-dimensional parameterizations or long horizons, targeting efficient single-robot and swarm motion planning under limited onboard compute in obstacle-dense environments.

entry.title: From Gradient-Boosted Trees to Deep Recommenders: Practical Lessons from Migrating a Production Customer Support Recommender

author.name: Sonia Sharma, Jeyendran Balakrishnan, Shreya Rajpal, Swapnil Parekh, Nagaraj Janardhana, Andrew Mattarella-Micke

entry.summary: This industry paper documents migrating a live production conversational support recommender from gradient-boosted trees to a pairwise-binary deep recommender as catalogs shift toward dynamic bundles. It shares practical lessons on handling sparse, imbalanced data, multimodal signals, and ecosystem-critical deployment constraints. Valuable real-world engineering evidence rarely published.

entry.title: GAP-Prompt: Gated Adaptive Prompting for Efficient Continual Learning

author.name: Trung-Anh Dang, Duy-Cuong Bui, Ngoc-Son Vu, Christel Vrain, Vincent Nguyen

entry.summary: GAP-Prompt brings instance-level adaptivity to prompt-based continual learning: instance-conditioned gating selects prompt injection layers per image, combined with dynamic knowledge fusion, reducing catastrophic forgetting versus static task-level prompting.

entry.title: A Hybrid Two-Stage Machine Learning Pipeline for Fault Detection and Classification in Power Transmission Systems

author.name: Sahil Manikshete, Atharva Gujarathi, Thanh Long Vu, Akhtar Hussain, Van-Hai Bui

entry.summary: Proposes a hybrid two-stage pipeline for transmission-line fault detection that decouples anomaly detection from fault classification, combining an Isolation Forest detector with automatically allocated supervised binary branches via an OR-fusion rule to handle imbalanced data and faults hidden within normal operating envelopes. Targets grid reliability and equipment protection where single-model classifiers fail on safety-critical cases.

entry.title: Decoupling candidate dual AGN from chance superpositions in the GOTHIC survey via a deep-learning framework

author.name: Bhavesh Mukheja, Snehanshu Saha, Anwesh Bhattacharya, Mousumi Das, Fran\c{c}oise Combes, Sudhanshu Barway

entry.summary: Applies a YOLOv11 oriented-bounding-box deep learning framework to SDSS imaging to separate genuine dual active galactic nuclei from chance superpositions among 46,061 galaxies rejected by the GOTHIC pipeline, aiding identification of merging supermassive black hole pairs despite projection effects and resolution limits.

entry.title: Speech-to-SOAP: End-to-End Summarization of Medical Dialogues: KIT@BeTraC 2026

author.name: Enes Yavuz Ugan, Fabian Retkowski, Yuka Ko, Thai-Binh Nguyen, Maike Z\"ufle, Jan Niehues, Alexander Waibel

entry.summary: Describes KIT's BeTraC 2026 submission for speech-to-SOAP end-to-end summarization of medical dialogues, generating clinical notes directly from speech without intermediate transcripts to preserve paralinguistic cues and reduce clinician documentation burden.

entry.title: MRI-based Deep Radiomic Phenotyping of Neuromuscular Disorders: A Topology-driven Characterization

author.name: Martyna \.Zur, {\L}ukasz Pi\'orecki, Marek Socha, Jordi Diaz-Manera, Jose Verdu Diaz, Volker Straub, Rossella Tupler, Joanna Pola\'nska

entry.summary: Introduces MaST, an end-to-end sparse transformer tracking pipeline injecting a lightweight motion prior to refine early-layer token importance scores, making sparsity effective from tokens to boxes for real-time edge deployment.

entry.title: Fiber Bragg Grating Whiskers for Bioinspired Hydrodynamic Perception on Underwater Robots

author.name: Hao Li, Tianyu Tu, Siyue Yao, Ziyang Chang, Juhyun Jung, Xiaochi Xie, Long Yin Chung, Tian-Ao Ren, Genliang Chen, Mark Cutkosky
