entry.summary: Presents compact fiber Bragg grating whiskers for underwater robots mimicking seal vibrissae geometry (tapered, elliptical cross-section), demonstrating monotonic flow response from 0.1-0.6 m/s, reduced self-induced oscillation, and vortex detection several seconds after source passage for passive hydrodynamic perception.

entry.title: Deep learning super-resolution of paediatric ultra-low-field MRI without paired high-field scans

author.name: Unknown

entry.summary: Deep learning super-resolution method for paediatric ultra-low-field MRI that operates without paired high-field scans, addressing the data scarcity problem in pediatric neuroimaging where acquiring paired scans is impractical.

entry.title: The Shadow Price of Intelligence: Quality Degradation in LLM Inference as a Supply Chain Problem

author.name: Elioth Sanabria

entry.summary: This paper models quality degradation under compute congestion at LLM providers as a supply chain problem, showing standard cost accounting ignores retry-inflated arrivals and churn-driven lifetime-value losses. Using newsvendor and queueing-style primitives, it argues degraded routing to smaller models is economically worse than dashboards suggest. A thought-provoking economic critique of common serving practices.

entry.title: SAGE: From Direct Answering to Evidence-Grounded Inference for Chinese Ancient Document Understanding

author.name: Yuchuan Wu, Xuan Luo, Yinglian Zhu, Meng Fang, Xiangyang Xue, Bin Li

entry.summary: SAGE reformulates Chinese ancient document understanding as evidence-grounded multi-agent inference rather than single-pass answer generation. Specialized agents handle planning, tool-mediated evidence acquisition, claim-level verification, and bounded replanning, supporting abstention when grounds are insufficient. It targets overconfident, weakly grounded outputs of current LVLMs in a demanding humanities domain.

entry.title: Tlow: Flow-based Item Tokenizer for Recommendation

author.name: Nian Li, Chonggang Song, Jingtao Ding, Lingling Yi, Yong Li, Qingmin Liao

entry.summary: Tlow proposes a flow-based item tokenizer for recommendation that maps semantic embeddings into a latent space conforming to a standard normal distribution so independent tokenizers can overcome dimensional correlations that plague OPQ and the decoding inefficiency of RQ-VAE. Better token IDs address parameter bloat and cold-start in generative recommenders. Solid efficiency-oriented contribution.

entry.title: Metadata-Aware Adaptation of a Generative Foundation Model for Conditional CMR Synthesis

author.name: Marc Rodr\'iguez, Grzegorz Skorupko, Nay Aung, Steffen E Petersen, Karim Lekadir, Polyxeni Gkontra

entry.summary: This work adapts a pretrained latent diffusion model for metadata-conditioned cardiac MRI synthesis, encoding structured clinical metadata and slice position as textual prompts, with Metadata-Free CFG, Contrastive Batching, and Inverse-Frequency Sampling to improve adherence on imbalanced attributes. Synthetic CMR faithful to phenotypes can mitigate data scarcity for underrepresented groups. Solid medically oriented generative work.

entry.title: $\texttt{findr}$: Transparent and Fair Credit Risk Decisions through Semi-Structured Regressions

author.name: Victor Medina-Olivares, Stefan Lessmann, Jonathan Crook

entry.summary: findr is a semi-structured deep regression framework for binary credit risk that decomposes the logit into an interpretable structured component and an orthogonal neural residual, with in-processing fairness constraints and coefficient-based explanations describing the actual decision rule. It balances predictive power with transparency and auditable fairness for regulated lending. Well-targeted finance methodology.

entry.title: Measuring Digital Labour Market Transitions with a Digital Semantic Score: An AI-Based Methodology Applied to the Dutch Labour Market

author.name: Sadegh Shahmohammadi, Xavier Pinho, Mairi Bowdler, Suhendan Adiguzel-van Zoelen, Joost van Genabeek

entry.summary: Develops an AI-based methodology combining embedding similarity search and LLM classification to map millions of Dutch job profiles onto harmonized ESCO occupations, introducing a Digital Semantic Score measuring association of job titles and skills with digital concepts relative to non-digital anchors. Enables granular labour market digitalization intelligence.

entry.title: Learning Whom to Trust : Decision-Generated Credibility in Social Learning

author.name: Gabriel Bontemps, Abhishek Banerjee

entry.summary: Studies collective learning dynamics when credibility of social information emerges from senders' own drift-diffusion decision processes, where decision confidence weights anticipatory influence and retrospective social learning. Derives exact representations yielding a common-mode amplification threshold governing when social learning improves or degrades collective accuracy.

entry.title: The Invisible Editorial Layer: Formalizing Undisclosed Inference-Time Steering, Probability Placement, and the Attribution Problem in Deployed Language Models

author.name: Augusto Camargo

entry.summary: This position paper argues modern inference pipelines insert an undisclosed editorial layer between frozen weights and observed text via logit-level interventions, formalizing probability placement and the resulting attribution and governance problems. It connects controlled generation and watermarking techniques to transparency and economic accountability concerns. Raises legitimate oversight questions about deployed model behavior.

entry.title: Identifying Latent Declarative Representations of Code for Assisting Repository Migration

author.name: Shraddha Surana, Ashwin Srinivasan, Michael Bain

entry.summary: ADFD-Migrate approximates a legacy repository's latent declarative description via annotated data-flow diagrams inferred by an LLM under static-analysis coverage checks, then performs dependency-aware chunked generation toward a target language. It treats porting as recovering an unobserved specification. Creative framing for legacy modernization.

entry.title: Beyond Executable Models: The Pufibara Agent Harness and the Modelica Agent Workflow Benchmark for Physical System Modeling

author.name: Zizhe Wang

entry.summary: Pufibara is an agent harness maintaining persistent engineering state for Modelica physical-system modeling, paired with the Modelica Agent Workflow Benchmark, addressing cases where models compile yet violate intended physics or rely on stale simulation evidence. Correctness here extends beyond executability to physical consistency. A niche but genuinely novel agentic-engineering benchmark area.

entry.title: Predicting Radiologist Expertise from 3D Gaze Patterns During CT Interpretation

author.name: Leila Khaertdinova, Anna Anikina, Claudia Mello-Thoms, Bulat Ibragimov

entry.summary: A gaze-informed transformer with DINOv2 backbone integrates radiologist fixation patterns into volumetric CT feature learning via learnable log-space attention bias and gaze-weighted pooling, classifying reader expertise from 182 reading sessions with strong ROC performance. Extends eye-tracking expertise assessment from 2D to volumetric imaging. Focused clinical-perception study.

entry.title: Syn2RealTrack: Bridging the Gap Between Synthetic and Real-World Datasets for Online Multi-View Multi-Target Tracking

author.name: Duong Nguyen-Ngoc Tran, Ngoc Doan-Minh Huynh, Cu Quoc Le, Hoang-Khang Nguyen, Long Hoang Pham, Huy-Hung Nguyen, Quoc Pham-Nam Ho, Trinh Le Ba Khanh, Chi Dai Tran, Duong Khac Vu, Son Hong Phan, Hyung-Min Jeon, Jae Wook Jeon

entry.summary: Syn2RealTrack decomposes the synthetic-to-real gap in online multi-camera 3D warehouse tracking into three separable points: camera calibration, object shape priors, and unknown object census, each with a targeted remedy including image-only distortion recovery and cross-view fusion. The resulting pipeline bridges synthetic training and physical capture. Careful systems decomposition of a persistent perception problem.

entry.title: Rethinking Pre-Training and Augmentation for Zero-Shot Cross-City Object Detection

author.name: Long Hoang Pham, Quoc Pham-Nam Ho, Huy-Hung Nguyen, Duong Nguyen-Ngoc Tran, Ngoc Doan-Minh Huynh, Cu Quoc Le, Hoang-Khang Nguyen, Hyung-Min Jeon, Chi Dai Tran, Son Hong Phan, Duong Khac Vu, Trinh Le Ba Khanh, Jae Wook Jeon

entry.summary: This study explores pre-training and augmentation choices for zero-shot cross-city object detection under privacy constraints forbidding any target-city profiling. It proposes a modular pipeline built on multi-dataset pretraining with class-agnostic objectness distillation and complementary augmentation pillars. Empirically grounded guidance for blind geographic domain shift.

entry.title: Evaluating Deep Multivariate Imputation Models on Wearable Device Data

author.name: Skye Goodman, Roussel Desmond Nzoyem, Leandro Junges, Peter Kissack, Yasser Qureshi, Amberly Brigden, Jeff Clark, Nawid Keshtmand

entry.summary: Using smartwatch data from a person with epilepsy, this study develops a missing-data evaluation protocol that mines contiguous missing-run templates stratified by gap-length quantiles and injects block masks preserving co-missingness structure, correcting unrealistic random-point holdout assumptions. It then evaluates deep imputation models BRITS and SAITS under realistic sensor dropout. Methodologically careful benchmarking contribution.

entry.title: Beyond Uniform Local Isometry and Topology: FactoMap for Disentangled Representations

author.name: Sohini Gupta, Bahareh Tolooshams

entry.summary: FactoMap introduces factor-space structure combining domains, generator-induced identifications, and position-dependent scales, showing statistically independent factors need not be geometrically separable due to anisotropic effects like hue versus scale. Its topographic map learns interpretable prototypes on a factor-space lattice, relaxing uniform local isometry assumptions in disentanglement. Conceptually deep contribution to representation learning theory.

entry.title: Accelerating the Adoption of Residential Solar Power Systems: Policy Analysis using a Dynamic Structural Model

author.name: Sebasti\'an Souyris, Jason A. Duan, Anantaram Balakrishnan, Varun Rai

entry.summary: Develops a dynamic structural model of residential solar PV adoption by forward-looking households weighing installation timing tradeoffs, ROI, and neighbor influence, used to analyze rebate and tax credit policies under budget constraints. Provides principled, data-driven policy guidance for incentive allocation across household segments.

entry.title: Low-Rank Velocity Fields as a Structural Prior for Unsupervised 4D Medical Image Interpolation

author.name: Haojin Li, Hengzhuo Wang, Chang Liu, Zhiheng Ma, Heng Li, Jiang Liu

entry.summary: Constrains unsupervised 4D medical image interpolation with low-rank Tucker velocity fields, decomposing motion into globally shared spatial bases and compact sample-specific cores to encourage anatomy-consistent deformation and suppress artifacts in endpoint-only training.

entry.title: Vision Language Model Fusion for Explainable Face Recognition

author.name: Ana Estrada-Real, Lydia Alapatt, Christoph Busch, Christian Rathgeb

entry.summary: Evaluates four vision-language models standalone and fused for face verification, examining whether combining multiple VLMs improves both decision accuracy and the quality of explanations supporting auditable face recognition decisions.

entry.title: Integrated Strategic Forecasting: A New RAND x Metaculus Methodology

author.name: Molly

entry.summary: Announces Integrated Strategic Forecasting, a RAND x Metaculus methodology combining scenario plannings exploration of discontinuous futures with crowdsourced forecastings probabilistic precision to enhance decision advantage in fast-changing environments.

entry.title: RefineRank: Joint Box Refinement and Ranking for Surgical Spatio-Temporal Grounding

author.name: Linzhe Jiang, Jiayuan Huang, Changhao Zhang, Chunyang Jiang, Zhehua Mao, Mobarak I. Hoque

entry.summary: RefineRank improves surgical spatio-temporal grounding by combining language features from a frozen medical vision-language model with proposals from a frozen open-set detector. Its trainable RefineNet module predicts bounded coordinate corrections and quality scores per candidate box, resolving the trade-off between semantic understanding and precise localization. Useful for procedural video understanding in operating rooms.

entry.title: Don't Just Listen, Try Planning: Graph-based Retrieval-Generation Agent for Long-form Audio Meeting Understanding

author.name: Quanwei Tang, Dong Zhang, Shoushan Li, Guodong Zhou

entry.summary: This paper introduces LongAudioQA, a dataset for long-form audio meeting question answering, and GRGA, a model that represents heterogeneous audio features as a multi-dimensional graph and uses agent planning for retrieval and answer generation. It targets acoustic information loss and poor long-term memory in speech LLMs. A useful resource plus method for meeting understanding.

entry.title: Structured Frequency-Domain Evidence for LLM-Based Time-Series Anomaly Detection

author.name: Jungwook Seo, Sangwon Son, Minjeong Kim, Seungmin Han, Seojin Yoo, Sungyong Baik

entry.summary: This work augments zero-shot LLM-based time-series anomaly detection with compact FFT-derived frequency-domain evidence alongside indexed de-seasonalized observations. Evidence is constructed at global and local resolutions to expose shifted periodicity and oscillatory anomalies invisible in pure time-domain views. A simple, effective enrichment of LLM inputs for TSAD.

entry.title: Scalable and Versatile Identification for Hierarchical Structural Causal Models: A New Look at Project STAR

author.name: Janis Aiad, Aghiles Drali, Aymen El Ouadrhiri, Anass Ettahiri, Yasser Oufqir, Simon Patry, David Cortes, Marianne Clausel, Emilie Devijver

entry.summary: This paper delivers a complete, scalable open-source pipeline for hierarchical structural causal models, integrating graph transformations, automatic do-calculus identification via pyAgrum, symbolic-to-formula compilation with an adapted abstract syntax tree, and numerical estimation. It demonstrates the pipeline by reanalyzing the landmark Project STAR class-size experiment. Bridges symbolic causal identification and practical estimation.

entry.title: HMGCLIP: Heterogeneous Multi-Granularity Contrastive Learning for E-commerce Representation Learning

author.name: Qiuyu Zhu, Yi Gao, Zhichao Wan, Mingyang Ma

entry.summary: HMGCLIP builds a heterogeneous hypergraph over product data to mine structure-aware hard negatives and align multi-granular semantics for e-commerce representation learning, targeting fine-grained attribute discrimination like material differences among similar products. A focused industrial-application contribution improving over global embedding baselines.

entry.title: Strictly Causal Streaming Video Anomaly Detection with a Theoretically-Grounded State-Space Core

author.name: Yogesh Kumar

entry.summary: This paper presents a strictly causal streaming video anomaly detector with a diagonal linear state-space core updated in O(1) time and memory per frame, trained self-supervised via causal next-embedding prediction on a frozen backbone, with a theoretical account linking temporal memory to detection latency. It targets edge hardware rather than GPU throughput. Careful systems-oriented vision contribution.

entry.title: IterCAD: Iterative Program Repair for CAD Code Generation from Orthographic Views

author.name: Yuchuan Wu, Ke Niu, Haiyang Yu, Zhuofan Chen, Xiangyang Xue, Bin Li

entry.summary: IterCAD reformulates generating parametric CAD code from dimension-annotated orthographic drawings as progressive program repair rather than one-shot generation. The model repeatedly inspects intermediate CAD results, reasons about discrepancies, and iteratively corrects the code, improving executability and geometric consistency. A pragmatic fix to a known weakness of vision-language CAD generation.

entry.title: DriftAD: Visually-Guided Text Drift for Few-Shot Industrial Anomaly Detection

author.name: Wenyang Liu, Tianyi Liu, Dongshuo Zhang, Kejun Wu, Adams Wai-Kin Kong

entry.summary: Proposes DriftAD, a CLIP-based few-shot industrial anomaly detection framework that amplifies subtle defect signals via spatial-frequency branches and uses visually-guided text drift instead of static global prompts to capture localized, scale-dependent defects.

entry.title: Phase-Aligned Finite-Fourier Periodic Deformation for 4D Medical Image Interpolation

author.name: Haojin Li, Hengzhuo Wang, Zhiheng Ma, Mingyang Ou, Heng Li, Jiang Liu

entry.summary: Formulates 4D medical interpolation as learning a phase-conditioned periodic deformation process with finite-Fourier priors aligned to physiological near-periodic motion such as cardiac MRI cycles, handling non-uniform temporal spacing.

entry.title: Bridging Adversarial and Collaborative Learning for AI-Generated Image Quality Assessment

author.name: Baoliang Chen, Qing Lin, Sijie Mai

entry.summary: Uncovers interdependence between perceptual fidelity and prompt alignment in AI-generated image quality ratings and introduces an interaction-aware framework negotiating the two dimensions via adversarial and collaborative learning.

entry.title: DoublesEval: Diagnosing Multi-Agent Tactical Reasoning in Vision-Language Models via Professional Doubles Badminton

author.name: Jintao Cheng, Weibin Li

entry.summary: Introduces DoublesEval, diagnosing multi-agent tactical reasoning in vision-language models using professional doubles badminton rallies decomposed into key moments probing atomic recognition, composite understanding, causal reasoning, and tactical abstraction.

entry.title: Human-Inspired Social Engagement Analysis via Interpretable Mutual Visual Attention

author.name: Urwa Fatima, Mohammad Zohaib, Francesca Odone, Nicoletta Noceti

entry.summary: Builds an interpretable social engagement model from psychological theories of mutual visual attention, explicitly modeling dyadic head orientation cues aggregated into individual and group engagement measures accessible to non-technical users.

entry.title: Multi-Stage Prompt-Guided Feature Modulation for Generalizable Brain Tumor Segmentation

author.name: Mohammad Mahdi Danesh Pajouh, Sara Saeedi

entry.summary: Proposes Multi-Stage Dynamic Prompt nnU-Net, conditioning nnU-Net with staged prompts to improve cross-site, cross-protocol generalization of brain tumor MRI segmentation outside the training domain.

entry.title: Bridging Teacher Expectations and Robot Learning via Coupling Dynamics

author.name: Evan Dallas, Sean Dallas, Wing-Yue Geoffrey Louie

entry.summary: Investigates how coupling human teaching with online robot learning affects teaching effectiveness and human perceptions, proposing a new framework informed by human learning theories to bridge teacher expectations and robot learning dynamics. Targets post-deployment customization by nontechnical experts.

entry.title: Dynamical System-Based Imitation Learning and Neuroadaptive Control for Trajectory Recovery in Autonomous Ships

author.name: Yeyson A. Becerra-Mora, Jos\'e \'Angel Acosta

entry.summary: Hybrid architecture combining dynamical-systems-based imitation learning reference generation with neuroadaptive control for unmanned surface vehicles, introducing control-action augmentation to recover localized trajectory fidelity that standard DS-IL sacrifices for global convergence under marine perturbations.

entry.title: Design-to-Plan: A Large Language Model-Based Multi-Agent Framework for Manufacturing Process Planning from 3D CAD Models and 2D Engineering Drawings

author.name: Muhammad Tayyab Khan, Lequn Chen, Wenhe Feng, Seung Ki Moon

entry.summary: Design-to-Plan is an LLM-based multi-agent framework for end-to-end manufacturing process planning from 3D CAD models and 2D engineering drawings. An orchestrator coordinates specialized agents for feature recognition, drawing analysis, 2D-3D fusion, knowledge retrieval, and rule checking to produce coherent process plans. It moves beyond isolated subtask automation in digital manufacturing.

entry.title: ORBITALIF: An Efficient Spiking Federated Learning Framework for Onboard Cloud Removal

author.name: Bohan Zhang, Chenyu Xu, Yijie Mao, Yuanming Shi

entry.summary: OrbitALIF is a spiking federated learning framework performing onboard training and inference for satellite cloud removal across low-earth-orbit constellations. Using a compact 2.3M-parameter spiking backbone with adaptive gating, it avoids downloading cloudy imagery given constrained bandwidth and contact windows. Creative systems-level solution at the edge of space computing.

entry.title: LLM-Guided Contextual Action Evaluation for Operational Decisions in Industrial Processes

author.name: Youcheng Zong, Runda Jia, Dakuo He

entry.summary: LCAE uses an LLM before training to normalize fixed industrial documents into a frozen action-observation-direction-delay relation basis, which recent numerical history then modulates to guide continuous-action evaluation in actor-critic reinforcement learning. This injects process knowledge that fixed documentation already contains into industrial control policies. Pragmatic fusion of domain text and RL.

entry.title: StrokeGuard: A Multi-Agent Guided System for Prehospital Stroke Assessment

author.name: Wentao Yang, Zhenye Xu, Ruoyi Li, Musen Zhang, Yao Guo

entry.summary: StrokeGuard is a multi-agent guided system for prehospital stroke assessment that helps non-clinical users conduct FAST-based screening accurately at home by structuring instructions, observation checks, and decisions within the narrow treatment window. Multi-agent orchestration mitigates inaccurate descriptions and incomplete symptom capture. Socially valuable application of agent frameworks to emergency triage.

entry.title: Reinforcement Learning-Guided Evolutionary Policy Optimization for Preference-Adjustable Heterogeneous Agile Earth Observation Satellite Scheduling

author.name: He Wang, Junyu Wu, Hui Li, Yanjie Song, Witold Pedrycz, Liang Li

entry.summary: This paper proposes reinforcement learning-guided evolutionary policy optimization for preference-adjustable scheduling of heterogeneous agile Earth observation satellites under visibility, attitude, energy, and storage constraints. It combines weighted-objective evolutionary search with learned policies. A competent combinatorial optimization contribution for a demanding aerospace planning problem.

entry.title: Confident at the moment of action: belief miscalibration in LLM play under hidden information

author.name: Bhushan Kashinath Joshi

entry.summary: Testing stated confidence against recoverable ground truth in a hidden-information chess variant, the author finds captures made at high stated confidence about the hidden royal piece were correct in only 1 of 62 cases, concentrating nearly all miscalibration in action moments. This challenges the assumption that confidence gates on actions are safe for agentic systems. A striking, if narrowly scoped, calibration finding.

entry.title: Constrained Entity Selection under Partial Knowledge for LLM-Based Knowledge Graph QA

author.name: Emanuel Kitzelmann

entry.summary: CESPK verifies LLM-generated candidate answers for knowledge graph QA using lightweight symbolic constraints derived from the question under partial knowledge, sitting between brittle full SPARQL parsing and guarantee-free LLM reasoning. A pragmatic verification layer for grounded KGQA. Modest but sensible contribution.

entry.title: Rebuild Dossier: Mechanically-Enforced Specs for Agentic App Rebuilds, and What Model-Tier Failures Reveal

author.name: Parker Fawcett

entry.summary: Rebuild-dossier mechanically enforces application interface specs during agentic app rebuilds, locking inputs and outputs before code is written and enforcing one-test-at-a-time building through automated checks. It reports that compliant agents can fail held-back tests while rule-breaking agents pass, showing passing suites do not certify spec compliance. Honest small-scale tooling study with useful negative observations.

entry.title: Too much of a good thing -- when knowledge distillation promotes overfitting, and how to avoid it

author.name: Irene Trigueros-Lorca, Leonardo Concepci\'on, Christian Wagner, Isaac Triguero, Daniel Molina

entry.summary: Investigating intermediate block-wise knowledge distillation, this work proposes a homogeneous-block student mirroring teacher blocks and identifies conditions, such as few instances per class in fine-grained datasets, where intermediate KD promotes overfitting rather than helping. Offers guidance on when layer-wise supervision hurts. Modest but useful distillation analysis.

entry.title: What Reaches Expert Review? Representation, Structural Screening, and Candidate-Form Dependence in AI-Assisted Item Development

author.name: Christopher Brooks (School of Information, University of Michigan)

entry.summary: Across two linked in-silico studies of 32,000 Big Five items, this work shows that representation choice, structural screening, and candidate-form construction in AI-assisted item development determine which items psychometricians ever review, with identical wording acquiring different construct evidence and intended attributes disappearing. Elevates preprocessing choices to consequential editorial decisions. Careful measurement-side analysis.

entry.title: Learning to Grade Efficiently: A Bandit-Driven Prompt-Selection Framework for Low-Cost LLM Essay Scoring

author.name: Olga Manakina, Igor Bogdanov

entry.summary: Treating prompt types as bandit arms, this framework adaptively selects grading recipes for LLM essay scoring, matching exhaustive grid-search accuracy on IELTS Writing Task 2 while cutting LLM calls by 78 percent. Cost-aware prompt selection addresses operational expenses of automated scoring. Neat applied optimization.

entry.title: Deep Learning Super Resolution for Satellite Cloud Mask Downscaling

author.name: Angelos Georgakis, Valentina Kanaki, Giorgos Giannopoulos, Stella Girtsou, Ioannis Kontogiorgakis, Charalampos Kontoes, Kostas Philippopoulos

entry.summary: This work proposes two deep super-resolution methods for downscaling SEVIRI cloud masks and introduces SEVMOD-CM, a cross-sensor dataset spatially and temporally matching MODIS and SEVIRI observations. It addresses the unresolved spatial-temporal resolution trade-off blocking continuous high-resolution cloud observation. Useful geoscience resource and models.

entry.title: Score-Based Ideal Observer Approximation via Denoising Score Matching for Signal-Known-Exactly Detection Tasks

author.name: Weimin Zhou

entry.summary: This paper approximates the Bayesian Ideal Observer for signal-known-exactly binary detection via denoising score matching, using score functions to avoid per-image posterior sampling required by MCMC and retraining required by task-specific supervised approaches. It establishes practical access to the theoretical performance upper bound in medical imaging detection tasks. Niche but rigorous imaging-science contribution.

entry.title: Absorbing Gradient Conflicts: Modeling Semantic Variance via Kent Distributions for Cross-Modal Hashing

author.name: Hengjie Zhu, Dayan Wu, Zihao Zhang, Xinze Liu, Jingxuan Yu, Peng Fu, Zheng Lin, Weiping Wang

entry.summary: Proposes KDPH, replacing deterministic point proxies in supervised cross-modal hashing with anisotropic Kent distributions on the hypersphere, absorbing gradient conflicts arising from label co-occurrence in multi-label scenarios instead of suffering optimization collapse.

entry.title: Hierarchical Prototype-Memory Adaptation of SAM for Surgical Instrument Segmentation

author.name: Xinning Yao, Jingjing Wang, Jinghua Yue, Xiaoyan Luo, Fugen Zhou, Bo Liu

entry.summary: Adapts SAM for surgical instrument segmentation via hierarchical prototype-memory that persists category memory across cases instead of degenerating into task-specific parameters, improving robustness to intraoperative variation.

entry.title: X-MULTI: VLM-based Imaging Factor Disentanglement for Factor-Aware Image Synthesis

author.name: Sonali Godavarthy, Matthias Neuwirth-Trapp, Tim-Felix Faasch, Maarten Bieshaar, Michael Moeller, Kristof Van Laerhoven, Danda Pani Paudel

entry.summary: Extends MULTI for imaging-factor disentanglement in text-to-image generation, addressing pixel-only supervision and observed-combination limitations so models can synthesize novel factor combinations like fisheye lenses with event sensors, building on the FAA metric.

entry.title: On Scaling Coordinate-Based Neuroevolution: The Quadtree Bottleneck in ES-HyperNEAT

author.name: Romain Claret, Michael O'Neill, Paul Cotofrei, Kilian Stoffel

entry.summary: Presents JAX-ESHN, a GPU-parallelized implementation of ES-HyperNEAT in JAX, and identifies a structural quadtree bottleneck: each CPPN discovers unique substrate positions, preventing population-level vectorization. Shows GPU construction cost plateaus at deep substrates where CPU baselines scale exponentially.

entry.title: Dual-Layer Approach to Mitigating AI-Generated Biological Threats

author.name: greeshma ranjeev

entry.summary: Proposes a dual-layer mitigation approach for AI-generated biological threats focused on guardrails for next-generation automated biomanufacturing, acknowledging current DNA synthesis remains difficult and offline, and positioning safeguards ahead of automation reducing wet-lab barriers.

entry.title: Implicit Q-learning-bootstrapped ant colony optimization for maritime moving-target observation scheduling with agile satellites

author.name: He Wang, Junyu Wu, Yeye Liu, Yifan Zhou, Jie Zhang, Hui Li, Yanjie Song, Liang Li

entry.summary: IQACO bootstraps ant colony optimization with implicit Q-learning for maritime moving-target observation scheduling with agile satellites, learning heuristic guidance rather than a direct task-selection policy. It handles dynamic windows induced by moving sea targets and orbital geometry. Companion work to the same group's AEOS scheduler.

entry.title: SENSESHIFT: Continuous Sentiment-Controlled Text Generation via Encoder-based Mask Infilling

author.name: Shahed Masoudian, Markus Frohmann, Emmanouil Karystinaios, Navid Rekabsaz, Markus Schedl

entry.summary: SenseShift enables sentence-level continuous sentiment control within long-form text using encoder-based mask infilling rather than decoder-only causal generation. It addresses coarse categorical or document-level control limitations of prior controllable-generation work. Useful for fine-grained editorial applications.

entry.title: ReGround-Surg: Reliability-Guided Anchor Grounding for Referring Surgical Video Segmentation

author.name: Jiaxin Wen, Ming Yin, Lu Liu, Zeyu Fu

entry.summary: Proposes ReGround-Surg, adding reliability-guided anchor grounding before SAM2 mask propagation in referring surgical video segmentation, reducing error propagation when visually similar instruments and occlusion corrupt the initial grounded mask.

entry.title: MatReplace: A Reference-Free, Conditioning-Aligned Benchmark for Material Replacement in Interior Scenes

author.name: Mingzhe Du, Thong Thanh Nguyen, Nguyen Tran Cong Duy, See-Kiong Ng, Luu Anh Tuan

entry.summary: MatReplace is a reference-free benchmark for material replacement edits in interior scenes, evaluating along four verifiable dimensions: local material correctness, lighting harmony, outside preservation, and inside structure. Three tracks vary conditioning signals to enable fair comparison across editors. Fills a benchmark gap for a commercially relevant editing task.

entry.title: A Literate Programming Environment for Human and Machine Agents

author.name: Adam T. Burke

entry.summary: This paper presents a literate programming environment for co-creating programs with LLM agents, featuring a grammar for executable essays, first-class names, an internal name-graph relating prose and code, and symbol-aware tooling analogous to IDE capabilities for agents. It improves context-window usage by colocating code with relevant prose and structured data. Forward-looking developer-experience proposal for agentic coding.

entry.title: Arbitrary Polygon Oscillator: Generalizing Polygonal Synthesis to Arbitrary Shapes, Morphing, and Three-Dimensional Polyhedra

author.name: Antonio Argentieri, Francesco Scagliola

entry.summary: Generalizes polygonal audio synthesis to arbitrary closed polygons via constant arc-length velocity traversal, adding morphing and three-dimensional polyhedra support in a unified DSP engine. Extends prior constant-angular-velocity formulations to irregular and star-shaped vertex configurations.

entry.title: Interpretable Fundus Image Classification via Ring-Based Retinal Vasculature Features

author.name: Xiaoyan Li, Shixin Xu, Arvind Gupta, Huaxiong Huang

entry.summary: Develops interpretable fundus classification from ring-structured retinal vasculature features around the optic disc, quantifying vessel geometry, color, oxygenation-related appearance, and entropy across concentric regions as physiologically motivated descriptors.

entry.title: Optimal Allocation of Embedding Dimensions under Finite-Sample Constraints

author.name: Vasileios E. Papageorgiou

entry.summary: Formulates embedding dimension selection for categorical predictors as a constrained allocation problem, characterizing approximation error via singular-value tails and estimation error via total embedding complexity, yielding closed-form allocation rules under a fixed global embedding budget.

entry.title: Do Recipes Have Personas? Characterizing and Generating Creator Style in Attributed Procedural Graphs

author.name: Lei Jiang

entry.summary: This work introduces ViralRecipesTrans, a dataset of execution-flow graphs extracted from cooking video transcripts mapped to specific creators, and frames procedural stylometry as graph learning and process discovery. It finds topological metrics capture creator style better than lexical classifiers prone to semantic leakage. An interesting niche study connecting process mining and creator identity.

entry.title: Mahalanobis-Based Multi-Head Attention for Complex State Propagation

author.name: Xiaohe Li

entry.summary: MHA-CSP replaces dot-product attention with a Mahalanobis-distance RBF kernel, claiming infinite-dimensional feature computation without extra parameters, plus direct Tree Attention construction via LogSumExp correction and an attention meshing mechanism for complex state propagation. The proposal is architecturally inventive. Independent validation and scaling evidence are unclear from the abstract alone.

entry.title: A Dual-Dimensional LLM Framework for Automated Item Incidental Content Similarity Analysis in Large-Scale Assessments

author.name: Jing Huang, Jihong Zhang, Hua-Hua Chang

entry.summary: A dual-dimensional LLM framework for detecting incidental content similarity across assessment items decomposes similarity into structured elements and semantic relatedness, validated psychometrically against expert judgments in large-scale testing. It improves over BLEU and cosine baselines for construct-irrelevant redundancy detection. Specialized but useful for testing organizations adopting automatic item generation.

entry.title: Place, Slice and Schedule: Hierarchical O-RAN Control of a Tethered mmWave UAV-gNB

author.name: Alireza Mohammadhosseini, Fatemeh Afghah

entry.summary: Exploiting O-RAN disaggregation, this work hierarchically coordinates slow aerial control (placement and slicing of a tethered mmWave UAV base station) with fast per-user scheduling, coupling topology changes from UAV movement with rapidly evolving demand. Addresses isolated-optimization gaps in prior UAV network studies. Competent wireless-systems contribution.

entry.title: The Annotation Bottleneck in Persian Text NLP: Persian as an Annotation-Scarce Language

author.name: MohammadHossein Mortazavi, Mostafa Salehi, Hadi Veisi

entry.summary: First part of a pair analyzing emergence of musical form via observation-driven estimation of local Markov transition kernel trajectories from overlapping sliding windows on Debussy's Syrinx, validating detected boundaries against A-B-A' readings using Jensen-Shannon divergences for pitch and duration kernels.

entry.title: UTS at CheckThat! 2026: Cite-Frame Engineering for Generated Fact-Checking Articles

author.name: Dima Galat, Marian-Andrei Rizoiu

entry.summary: Describes the 2nd-place UTS system for CheckThat! 2026 Task 3 fact-checking article generation, built around deterministic drafting with two interventions: domain-attribution cite frames and shadow-validated anchor selection using a tiny Llama-3.2:1B validator. Offers ablation-backed design lessons about scorer conservatism.

entry.title: LG-GER: Language-Guided Group Emotion Recognition via Multimodal Evidence Distillation

author.name: Ahmed Shehab Khan, Zhiyuan Li, Yan Tong

entry.summary: Proposes LG-GER, a language-guided group emotion recognition framework where a multimodal LLM generates dense spatially grounded evidence (boxes with emotions and confidences) distilled into a single vision-language student, replacing detector-driven multi-stream pipelines.

entry.title: EMFE: A lightweight, explainable machine learning framework for malaria cell classification

author.name: Md Abdullah Al Kafi, Walayat Hussain, Mousumi Karmakar, Sumit Kumar Banshal, Ahmed Al Marouf

entry.summary: Proposes a mixture-of-experts prompt-free feature adapter on parameter-efficient ViTs for binary coronary artery segmentation in X-ray angiography, routing heterogeneous angiographic appearances through specialized experts to handle thin low-contrast vessels and catheter interference.

entry.title: Revelation Control

author.name: Qinyou Wang

entry.summary: Revelation Control formalizes when priced interventions should reveal hidden state, distinguishing information that changes a consequential decision from productive reuse created by the intervention itself. It defines decision-sufficient revelation and revelation depth and derives a cost-adjusted factorization criterion for learning systems. The work offers a novel decision-theoretic lens but remains highly abstract.

entry.title: Energy-Aware Performance Evaluation of Nonlinear Mechatronic Systems Under Matched-Tracking Conditions

author.name: Bhanuka Dayawansa

entry.summary: Introduces an energy-aware evaluation index (EAPI) combining tracking error with cumulative actuator energy for comparing nonlinear mechatronic systems under approximately matched tracking conditions, arguing standard RMSE/overshoot/settling-time metrics ignore actuator effort.

entry.title: The Reified Referent: How the Saturation View Values the Taste of Someone Who Does Not Exist

author.name: Ronen Bar

entry.summary: Philosophical argument in population ethics that the Saturation View (varied joys beat identical joys) smuggles in a fictional experiencer, coining the reified referent to describe inventing unreal moral subjects, and warning variety-valuing may widen valence spectra away from suffering reduction.

entry.title: When Less Is More: An Empirical Study of Minimal Responses in Counseling Dialogues and the Behavior of LLMs

author.name: Zhiyang Qi

entry.summary: This empirical study analyzes minimal responses such as backchannels and brief empathic statements across multiple counseling dialogue datasets, using length-based filtering plus contextual verification with an LLM. It shows these brief utterances carry interactional value often overlooked by dialogue systems favoring content-rich replies. Relevant to building better counseling chatbots.

entry.title: PlaceSeek: Human-Centered Geospatial Retrieval of Urban Outdoor Places via Semantic Grounding and Affective Alignment

author.name: Ziqi Cui, Shangyu Lou

entry.summary: PlaceSeek maps natural-language urban place queries to street-view imagery by decomposing intent into functional and affective sub-intents, verifying physical evidence via a Semantic Grounding Module and aligning affective expectations. It addresses open-ended, activity-oriented search that POI-centric geospatial retrieval cannot satisfy. Interesting human-centered retrieval direction.

entry.title: Mind the Student: Behavioral and Contextual Cues for Automated Engagement Prediction in Online Learning

author.name: Alperen Kantarci, Visvanathan Ramesh, Gemma Roig

entry.summary: This paper develops a multimodal framework predicting student engagement in online tutoring videos by integrating pretrained video, audio, and image encoders with structured behavioral cues such as head pose and gaze. Analysis of the CASED dataset highlights inter-person variability and annotation subjectivity as core difficulties. Applied contribution to educational analytics.

entry.title: AgentHands: Generating interactive hand gestures for spatially grounded agent conversations in XR

author.name: Unknown

entry.summary: Google research on AgentHands, generating interactive hand gestures for spatially grounded agent conversations in extended reality, addressing embodied communication cues for agents in XR environments.

entry.title: A Human-Factors Guided Cognitive Model of Visuospatial Complexity in Embodied Active Vision

author.name: Vasiliki Kondyli, Jakob Suchan, Mehul Bhatt

entry.summary: A human-factors guided cognitive framework analyzes visuospatial and auditory complexity in embodied active vision, categorizing quantitative, structural, dynamic, auditory, and interactional complexity attributes grounded in embodied cognition theory. Primarily a conceptual and analytical framework for multimodal perception complexity. Interdisciplinary but light on computational validation.

entry.title: ConsensusTAS: Self-Supervised Temporal Action Segmentation for Long-Horizon Construction Videos

author.name: Xiaoshan Zhou, Yafei Sun

entry.summary: Proposes ConsensusTAS, a label-free self-supervised method for segmenting fine-grained action transitions in long-horizon construction videos, motivated by robot assistance scenarios and avoiding costly temporal boundary annotation.

entry.title: TorchMorph: CUDA-accelerated Morphological Transforms

author.name: Kai Zhao

entry.summary: Releases TorchMorph, a PyTorch extension with 22 CUDA-fused morphological operators covering binary, greyscale, distance transforms, and entropy-regularized optimal transport, closing a gap left by CPU-bound scipy.ndimage in GPU training loops.

entry.title: QML for Quantum Sensing under Measurement-Induced Information Loss

author.name: Sounak Bhowmik, Himanshu Thapliyal

entry.summary: This study frames magnetic-field estimation in nitrogen-vacancy center magnetometry as supervised regression and compares several quantum machine learning approaches under noisy, finite-shot, measurement-limited conditions typical of the NISQ era. It assesses whether QML can improve parameter extraction from degraded sensing data. Results are preliminary but informative for quantum sensing pipelines.

entry.title: LumiXAI: A Modular Full-Stack Framework for Feature Attribution

author.name: Alfio Ferrara, Lorenzo Gatta, Sergio Picascia, Elisabetta Rocchetti

entry.summary: LumiXAI consolidates feature attribution into a modular full-stack framework combining classification and generative attribution with an interactive GUI supporting bidirectional exploration, aimed at non-expert accessibility. It addresses fragmentation of explainability tools across modalities and interfaces. Helpful infrastructure for interpretability practice.

entry.title: A Behavior-Guided Online Probabilistic Forecasting Method for Electric vehicle Charging Loads

author.name: Chenghan Li, Qingxiang Liu, Yinliang Xu, Yuxuan Liang

entry.summary: A behavior-guided online probabilistic forecasting framework for EV charging loads uses a dual-timescale behavior representation separating persistent station patterns from recent behavioral changes. It targets grid operations under heterogeneous, evolving charging behavior. Competent applied work in energy forecasting.

entry.title: One Timeline, Many Renderings: A Wolfram Language Paclet for heterogeneous musical output

author.name: Francesco Vitucci, Michele Lorusso, Francesco Scagliola

entry.summary: Companion software paper presenting Temporal System, a Wolfram Language paclet compiling one immutable typed timeline store into synchronized Csound scores, MusicXML notation, OSC control, and rehearsal click artifacts with unit conversion deferred to render time.

entry.title: Cross-Generation Optimization of YOLOv26, YOLOv11, and YOLOv8 for Fine-Grained Small-Object Detection and Instance Segmentation in Complex Orchards

author.name: Ranjan Sapkota, Manoj Karkee

entry.summary: Benchmarks YOLOv8, YOLOv11, and YOLOv26 across five scales and two resolutions (30 experiments) for apple fruitlet, calyx, and peduncle detection and segmentation in orchards, finding that larger models do not consistently help and that YOLOv11s at 960px leads on mask mAP.

entry.title: Comparative Assessment of Deep Learning Architectures for Underwater Subsurface Kelp Forest Segmentation with The Kelp-o-Tron

author.name: Sundarabalan Balasubramanian, C\'esar Borja, Ana C. Murillo, Lexi N. Wilkes, Meredith L. McPherson, Kira A. Krumhansl, Jennifer A. Dijkstra, Jarrett E. K. Byrnes

entry.summary: Systematically compares ResNet34-U-Net, ResNet50-DeepLabV3, and a hybrid ASPP-Transformer for kelp forest segmentation on 3,395 annotated underwater images from northeastern US waters with geographically independent test sites, releasing the Kelp-o-Tron resource.

entry.title: An AI4Chemist’s perspective on biosecurity

author.name: Ana Leonescu

entry.summary: A computational/experimental chemist reflects on the distinction between AI safety and biosecurity, exploring how AI-for-chemistry capabilities intersect biological threat landscapes and where their skill set applies to biorisk reduction.

entry.title: Markerless Pose Estimation for Resistance Training Technique Assessment

author.name: Joseph Turner, Jeff Clark, Nawid Keshtmand

entry.summary: This paper presents a markerless pose estimation framework assessing resistance-training technique from ordinary video, extracting BlazePose landmarks for squats, bench presses, and deadlifts, converting them to joint-angle trajectories, and scoring deviations against reference repetitions. It aims to democratize laboratory-grade technique assessment for injury prevention. Accessible applied computer vision.

entry.title: Amortized Set Prediction for Inverse IFS Reconstruction from Density Maps

author.name: Yutaka Yamaguti

entry.summary: Amortizes the inverse problem of recovering iterated function system parameters from fractal density maps with a single forward-pass estimator, handling unordered map sets via Hungarian matching and evaluating by reconstruction since parameters are not uniquely identifiable.

entry.title: When There Are No Experts

author.name: J Bostock

entry.summary: Philosophical essay exploring what distinguishes fields with genuine experts from those without, prompted by a debate about consciousness studies, arguing expertise requires structured feedback loops with reality rather than mere respected writing.

entry.title: COCI: Conference Organisers and Content Identifier

author.name: Angelo Salatino, Francesco Osborne, Alexis Vizcaino, Aliaksandr Birukou, Enrico Motta

entry.summary: COCI is an AI framework extracting fine-grained structured metadata from Calls for Papers using LLMs plus semantic mapping into OpenAlex, DBLP, ConfIDent, and related knowledge bases. It integrates grey literature into scholarly knowledge graphs despite heterogeneous raw text. Useful research-infrastructure demo.

entry.title: Constrained Hyperparameter Optimization for Streaming Data

author.name: Bruno Veloso, Jo\~ao Gama

entry.summary: This paper addresses hyperparameter optimization for streaming data, focusing on constraint-handling techniques that repair invalid solutions produced by optimization operators over bounded search spaces, enabling self-adjustment during online learning. It targets a real operational need in evolving-data deployments. Incremental contribution to AutoML for streams.

entry.title: ROI-Gated SAHI: Content-Adaptive Slicing-Based Inference for Efficient Object Detection

author.name: Rashid Riyadh, Abd Ullah Khan, Imad Gohar, Muzammil Behzad

entry.summary: Adds an ROI-gating proposer to Slicing-Aided Hyper Inference to skip background tiles during sliced small-object detection, reporting mixed results including settings slower than full SAHI with marginal gains elsewhere.

entry.title: Image Difference Quantification Using Autoencoder-Based Latent Representations

author.name: Manish Sharma, Timothy Yim, Clifton Forlines

entry.summary: Proposes quantifying perceptual image differences via cosine similarity in convolutional autoencoder latent space, claiming better alignment with human perception than MSE, PSNR, or SSIM under illumination, pose, and background variation.

entry.title: A Mathematical Theory of Interpretation: Rational Entropy, Spectral Readout, and Confusability as a Resource

author.name: Blake Reynolds

entry.summary: The Mathematical Theory of Interpretation treats interpretation as observer-relative spectral measurement under an access structure, introducing Rational Entropy to measure residual uncertainty across knowledge, utility, and medium. It derives results about confusability and zero-error identification that reverse conventional roles. The framework is ambitious but dense and its practical implications are unclear.

entry.title: Pattern-Derived Visual Swarm Games: Multi-Scale Drone-Vision States for Interception and Sustainability Audits

author.name: Faruk Alpay, Levent Sarioglu

entry.summary: Converts drone-vision annotation datasets (VisDrone, UAVSwarm) into virtual zero-sum swarm games via Bloom-filter representations, adding a repeated Markov layer tracking fatigue, budget, and entropy variables for sustainability audits. Reports modest gains from screen tuning on bounded game values.

entry.summary: arXiv:2608.23670v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: LLM-based agents execute multi-step tasks, but their behavioral structure remains opaque: long unstructured traces resist the safety auditing and runti...

author.name: Stephen Chung, Wenyu Du, William J. Wesley

entry.summary: arXiv:2608.23691v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study autonomous mathematical discovery in the Station, an open-world multi-agent environment in which AI agents from different model families pursu...

author.name: Junxiao Chen, Paul Glasserman

entry.summary: arXiv:2608.23706v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A large language model (LLM) trained on synthetic limit order book (LOB) data achieves near perfect scores in generating valid sequences of LOB events....

author.name: Seonglae Cho, Donghyun Lee

entry.summary: arXiv:2608.23740v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Concurrent multi-agent coding promises division of labor across modules, robustness through redundancy, and parallel exploration at the natural granula...

author.name: Farhana Amin, Sabiha Afroz, Mona Moghadampanah, Dimitrios S. Nikolopoulos

entry.summary: arXiv:2608.23807v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Masked diffusion language models (dLLMs) can in principle generate text faster than autoregressive (AR) models, since they denoise many tokens at once....

author.name: Jiongxiao Wang, Dingli Ma, Chaoqun Ni

author.name: Lijia Huang, Yao Fu, Sihao Ren

entry.summary: arXiv:2608.23837v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are known to exhibit social sycophancy, often validating or agreeing with users in socially sensitive contexts. Existing e...

author.name: Haoyang Fang, Bernie Wang

entry.summary: arXiv:2608.23848v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Budget-constrained agentic search arises when an LLM agent must refine candidates under a small evaluation budget, because validation is expensive, gen...

author.name: Thang Nguyen, Dung Nguyen, Romero Morais, Truyen Tran

entry.summary: arXiv:2608.23855v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose ICI-Time, a novel framework that reframes time series forecasting as a visual inpainting task, leveraging the generalisation power of large ...

entry.title: Research Summary: August 25, 2026

author.name: AATF AI News Aggregator

entry.summary:
Today's research spans frontier safety methodology, optimization theory, and agentic systems. Dell & Rambachan map credible measurement and inference pipelines as AI transforms economics, while Alon, Moran & Moran settle optimal query complexity for learning orders from comparison-counterexamples.

Frontier safety dominates the agenda:

  • Activation Controllability Benchmark tests whether LLMs can modulate their own residual-stream activations via instruction—if so, interpretability-based monitoring assumptions break
  • Aligned Alone, Misaligned Together shows individual-model audits fail to predict adversarial capture when agents interact
  • Reasoning-induced misalignment receives both a mechanistic account and an actionable safety-direction penalty
  • Compaction Cliff documents safety-rule decay after context compaction across 20 production Claude Code configurations

Training methods and agents also advanced:

  • A physical response-and-memory model provides principled grounding for Muon, increasingly influential in large-model training
  • Best-Practice Critic Optimization diagnoses RLHF instability and delivers a stable DPPO-based recipe
  • Apodex 1.1 scales agentic working capability along orthogonal environment and verification axes
  • Lit2Test requires research proposals to precommit falsifying observations, enabling decidable evaluation of scientific ideation
entry.content:
Today's research spans frontier safety methodology, optimization theory, and agentic systems. Dell & Rambachan map credible measurement and inference pipelines as AI transforms economics, while Alon, Moran & Moran settle optimal query complexity for learning orders from comparison-counterexamples.

Frontier safety dominates the agenda:

  • Activation Controllability Benchmark tests whether LLMs can modulate their own residual-stream activations via instruction—if so, interpretability-based monitoring assumptions break
  • Aligned Alone, Misaligned Together shows individual-model audits fail to predict adversarial capture when agents interact
  • Reasoning-induced misalignment receives both a mechanistic account and an actionable safety-direction penalty
  • Compaction Cliff documents safety-rule decay after context compaction across 20 production Claude Code configurations

Training methods and agents also advanced:

  • A physical response-and-memory model provides principled grounding for Muon, increasingly influential in large-model training
  • Best-Practice Critic Optimization diagnoses RLHF instability and delivers a stable DPPO-based recipe
  • Apodex 1.1 scales agentic working capability along orthogonal environment and verification axes
  • Lit2Test requires research proposals to precommit falsifying observations, enabling decidable evaluation of scientific ideation

entry.title: The Measurement Revolution? Credible Measurement and Inference in the Age of AI

author.name: Melissa Dell, Ashesh Rambachan

entry.summary: Dell and Rambachan provide guidance for credible measurement and inference as AI transforms economics, mapping three pipeline stages (discovery, construct definition, observation) and arguing that anchoring AI-generated variables to external gold standards is essential for valid inference. It addresses the shift from scarcity to abundance of plausible measures.

entry.title: Sorting from Counterexamples

author.name: Noga Alon, Shay Moran, Shlomo Moran

entry.summary: Alon, Moran, and Moran determine optimal query complexity for learning an unknown linear order via comparison-counterexample queries with up to k untruthful counterexamples of unknown count: Theta(n log n + nk). Noiseless complexity matches classical sorting while each lie costs order n, with matching upper bounds via a geometric construction.

entry.title: Measuring Activation Control in Large Language Models

author.name: Marek Mateusz Kowalski, Joshua Fonseca Rivera, Uzay Macar, David Demitri Africa

entry.summary: The Activation Controllability Benchmark measures how much LLMs can modulate their own residual stream activations via natural-language instruction, finding most models achieve some directional and magnitude control with temporal resolution. This raises concerns that latent-space monitoring may be circumventable if models can hide deception inside their own activations.

entry.title: A Physical Response-and-Memory Model for Muon Optimization

author.name: Yinze Hu, Hongjun Xiang, Xingao Gong, Hongyu Yu

entry.summary: This paper develops a physical response-and-memory model explaining why Muon's semi-orthogonalized momentum updates work, treating the weight matrix during training as a responsive medium with memory. It aims to answer theoretically what has so far been settled only empirically: why semi-orthogonalization helps and how long the momentum history should be.

entry.title: Aligned Alone, Misaligned Together: Forecasting Adversarial Capture in LLM Agent Populations

author.name: Isotta Magistrali, Chen Shani

entry.summary: Shows that individual-model audits fail to predict collective behavior when language-model agents interact: on a security-triage task, injected committed minorities can pull well-calibrated monitors toward different escalation decisions. Argues AI safety evaluation must move from the single model to interacting agent populations.

entry.title: Apodex 1.1: Scaling Agentic Intelligence for Complex Work

author.name: Apodex Team, B. An, B. Li, B. Wang, B. Zhang, B. L. Wang, C. Feng, C. Wei, C. Xue, C. Zhang, D. Ng, D. Ye, E. Min, F. Chen, F. Liu, F. Yang, F. Ye, H. Xu, H. Yang, H. Ye, H. Zhang, H. Zhao, J. Li, J. Lin, J. Xia, K. Jin, K. Wang, K. Yang, L. Bing, L. Lei, L. Su, Le. Wang, Lu. Wang, N. Wang, Q. Ren, Q. Yang, R. Li, S. Bai, S. Du, S. Li, S. Lin, S. Nie, S. Wang, S. Zhang, S. Z. Wang, Ta. Q. Fang, Ti. Q. Fang, W. Fang, W. Li, W. Zhang, X. Chen, X. Li, X. Tang, X. Wang, X. Xu, X. Zhang, X. Q. Wang, X. Y. Wang, Y. Deng, Y. Gao, Y. Hu, Y. Li, Y. Sui, Y. Wang, Y. Xiao, Y. Zhang, Z. Chen, Z. Cheng, Z. Feng, Z. Liang, Z. Zhang

entry.summary: Apodex 1.1 scales agentic working capability, defined as sustained verifiable progress on real-world objectives, via Environment Scaling of diverse verifiable file, search, and code environments plus Agentic Coordination Scaling teaching decomposition, delegation, asynchronous integration, and replanning under a shared execution harness and AgentOS.

entry.title: GOLEM: Modular Humanoid Autonomy Towards Electric Vehicle Battery Disassembly

author.name: Max Conway, William Xie, Allen Devaraj, Yutong Zhang, Niraj Pudasaini, Mateo Feit, Adam Abid, Zachary Allen, Chen Liu, Xuan Tan, Jensen Lavering, Jason Chen, Lyle Antieau, Anthony Von Pischke, Alessandro Roncone, Zachary Sunberg, Nikolaus Correll

entry.summary: GOLEM is an end-to-end open-source modular architecture for humanoid EV battery disassembly on the Unitree H1-2, with independent walking, manipulation, stability, navigation, and spatial-memory modules behind abstract interfaces. Docker-based ROS 2 deployment with MuJoCo and IsaacLab digital twins matching the physical robot.

entry.title: How to Train a Critic Stably and Efficiently

author.name: Penghui Qi, Xiangxin Zhou, Wee Sun Lee

entry.summary: Best-Practice Critic Optimization studies why critic-based RLHF training is unstable and assembles a stable recipe combining DPPO, reward-bounded value predictions, Monte Carlo targets, unnormalized advantages, and length-adaptive GAE. Because critics run only during training, they can condition on reward-defining information like reference answers hidden from the policy, offering a credible alternative to GRPO's multi-sample advantage estimation.

entry.title: MCP-Universe RL: A Framework for Training MCP Tool-Use Agents via Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Ziyang Luo, Yan Yang, Xiangru Jian, Ziji Shi, Xiaoqiang Lin, Jun Hao Liew, Silvio Savarese, Junnan Li

entry.summary: MCP-Universe RL is an open-source framework that handles environment isolation and rollout scheduling for reinforcement learning of MCP-based tool-use agents, addressing the systems problems beyond the policy update itself. It lets any MCP server plug into training without custom RL integration.

entry.title: Mitigating Reasoning-Induced Misalignment via Safety-Direction Penalty

author.name: Yipeng Zhao, Qishun Yang, Shenzhe Zhu, Shu Yang, Di Wang

entry.summary: This paper analyzes Reasoning-Induced Misalignment, where fine-tuning on harmless reasoning data induces harmful behaviors, identifying the representation-space geometry behind neuron-level entanglement. It proposes a Safety-Direction Penalty that constrains movement along a learned unsafe direction during reasoning fine-tuning. Provides both diagnosis and a training-time fix for an important safety problem.

entry.title: Breaking the Assumptions: Auditing Input-Side Jailbreak Defenses Against Semantic Attacks

author.name: Aaditya Pratap, Harsh Kasyap, Somanath Tripathy

entry.summary: This paper audits jailbreak defenses for locally deployed LLMs served by engines like Ollama, which lack API-level moderation. Rather than just documenting failures, it traces each defense failure back to the specific design assumption violated by semantic attacks.

entry.title: What Proves You Wrong: Benchmarking Language Models on Falsifiable Research Ideation

author.name: Ziyue Wang (State Key Laboratory of Multimedia Information Processing, School of Computer Science, Peking University), Aomufei Yuan (Peking University), Yiran Yao (Tianjin University), Linli Yao (State Key Laboratory of Multimedia Information Processing, School of Computer Science, Peking University), Hongyao Zuo (Tianjin University), Ziwen Gong (Hainan University), Yuanxin Liu (State Key Laboratory of Multimedia Information Processing, School of Computer Science, Peking University), Shicheng Li (State Key Laboratory of Multimedia Information Processing, School of Computer Science, Peking University), Yishuo Cai (State Key Laboratory of Multimedia Information Processing, School of Computer Science, Peking University), Tong Yang (Peking University), Xu Sun (State Key Laboratory of Multimedia Information Processing, School of Computer Science, Peking University), Xiaohui Li (Huawei Technologies), Haoli Bai (Huawei Technologies)

entry.summary: Lit2Test is a benchmark that requires LLM-proposed research ideas to precommit a falsifying observation via a six-field contract, enabling decidable quality assessment instead of free-form judging. Built prospectively from 200 real-paper neighborhoods, it elicits proposals from four frontier models and evaluates them through 1,200 pairwise comparisons. It addresses a genuine gap in how research ideation ability is judged.

entry.title: Who Pays More for Safety? Measuring the Disparate Cost of Safety Alignment across Languages

author.name: Chanwoong Yoon, Jungsoo Park, Alan Ritter

entry.summary: Introduces Safety Cost, a protocol measuring utility loss caused purely by safety alignment via pairwise comparison of aligned versus unaligned models, and finds non-English users systematically bear larger costs, with some languages in a double-penalty zone of weaker protection and greater utility loss.

entry.title: EchoWM: Open and Enterable Omnimodal World Models

author.name: Songchun Zhang, Yaowei Li, Junhao Zhuang, Weiyang Jin, Haoyu Wang, Xin Lu, Yilang Sun, Shiyi Zhang, Haoran Li, Xiaoxiao Ma, Yuming Li, Yijun Liu, Yaofeng Su, Yanwen Ma, Haoyu Wu, Zihan Su, Yue Ma, Lvmin Zhang, Haoyang Huang, Zeyue Xue, Anyi Rao, Nan Duan

entry.summary: EchoWM is an omnimodal enterable world model generating 720p video, environmental sound, music, and speech under continuous navigation, mapping discrete commands and poses to metric-scale 6-DoF trajectories with a complementary data engine and progressive autoregressive training. Represents the frontier of interactive generative media.

entry.title: Vision Guided Target Conditioned Control for Autonomous Excavation

author.name: Shuai Zhao, Ji-An Pan, Junwei Li, Xun Tang, Fansen Xi, Qing Xu, Keqiang Li, Jianqiang Wang

entry.summary: Proposes an interaction-aware MPPI planner integrating an ego-conditioned generative autoregressive prediction model that outputs stochastic multi-modal predictions conditioned on each candidate ego action, enabling what-if probing in dense traffic. A nested sampling scheme makes expected cost and collision risk evaluation tractable.

entry.title: InstructMove: A Text-Indispensable Benchmark for Instruction-Following Manipulation

author.name: Mengao Zhao, Ziang Li, Chaodong Huang, Mengchen Ma, Haoyi Jiang, Yiwei Jin, Xinjie Wang, Yun Du, Xuewu Lin, Taojun Ding, Hongyu Xie, Jackson Jiang, Chunlei Yu, Kaihua Zhang, Lichao Huang, Liu Liu, Tianwei Lin, Zhizhong Su

entry.summary: InstructMove introduces a text-indispensable benchmark for instruction-following manipulation where multiple actions are visually and physically plausible but only one matches the language instruction, exposing that many VLA benchmarks let policies succeed without grounding instructions.

entry.title: InjecMEM: Memory Injection Attack on LLM Agent Memory Systems

author.name: Hanling Tian, Gengyu Zhang, Zeyang Sha, Jingying Wang, Yuhang Liu, Zhehao Huang, Kun Yang, Xiaolin Huang

entry.summary: InjecMEM demonstrates memory injection attacks on LLM agent memory systems requiring only a single interaction with no read or edit access: a retriever-agnostic topical anchor ensures downstream retrieval associates a poisoned record with a target topic, then a short adversarial command steers future responses. It reveals a new vulnerability class in deployed agent memory subsystems.

entry.title: LD4WAM: Learning Latent Dynamics from Human Videos for World Action Models

author.name: Zhenhao Shen, Jiaqi Liang, Jasper Lu, Feng Jiang, Yuran Wang, Chuanbo Wei, Jiayi Liu, Jianchun Yang, Qize Yu, Jiadi You, Ce Hao, Guanqi He, Chen Xie, Ruihai Wu

entry.summary: LD4WAM learns embodiment-agnostic motion-aligned latent dynamics from human videos, pairing a latent dynamics model trained with semantic reconstruction and real motion alignment with a mixture-of-transformers world dynamics action model, bridging cheap video priors and actionable robot actions.

entry.title: Context as an Environment: Programmatic Context Management for Long-Horizon Agents

author.name: Yin Lin, Elaine Ang, Erkang Zhu, Bolin Ding, Jingren Zhou

entry.summary: Scroll treats each agent session as an executable Session Environment backed by an append-only event log and persistent sandboxed Python kernel with typed state, letting model-written code search and materialize context instead of serializing everything into prompts. It targets long-horizon agents whose histories exceed context windows.

entry.title: The Compaction Cliff in Long-Running AI Agent Memory

author.name: Saber Zerhoudi, Jelena Mitrovic, Michael Granitzer

entry.summary: Studying Claude Code compaction on Sonnet 4.6 across 20 production configurations, this paper names the Compaction Cliff: safety rules lose enforceable wording during context summarization, dropping from 53 percent preserved after one round to 10 percent after five. Knowledge Triage routes different knowledge types through type-specific retention policies with deterministic operators.

entry.title: Safety Hacking in Constrained Best-of-$N$ Inference-time Scaling

author.name: Akifumi Wachi, Takumi Tanabe, Youhei Akimoto

entry.summary: This paper defines safety hacking in constrained Best-of-N inference-time scaling: an imperfect safety proxy contaminates the feasible set and reward maximization amplifies residual unsafe-but-feasible outputs. Finite-N bounds governed by joint upper reward tails characterize when hacking becomes likely.

entry.title: DIME: Query-Efficient Framework for Membership Inference on Diffusion Models

author.name: Tue Do, Daniel Alabi

entry.summary: DIME provides a theoretically grounded, query-efficient membership inference attack on diffusion models based on an exact characterization of the optimal finite-set denoiser. Leakage decomposes into a reconstruction bias term and a novel local crowding term capturing training-point geometry.

entry.title: CounterAlign: Counterfactual Supervision for Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Haru Kondoh, Kei Ota, Asako Kanezaki, Yueh-Hua Wu

entry.summary: CounterAlign derives dense corrective supervision for VLA training purely from expert demonstrations by pairing expert actions with mismatched instructions via relabeling, avoiding costly curated negative data or reward engineering. Provides negative supervision that behavior cloning lacks.

entry.title: SuperMap: A Spatio-Temporal SLAM System for Visual-Language Navigation

author.name: Shibo Zhao, Guofei Chen, Honghao Zhu, Zhiheng Li, Changwei Yao, Nader Zantout, Seungchan Kim, Wenshan Wang, Ji Zhang, Sebastian Scherer

entry.summary: SuperMap is a 4D spatio-temporal SLAM framework for vision-language navigation that reconciles high-frequency geometric SLAM with asynchronous open-vocabulary perception via consistency-driven instance association, re-activation, and existence-and-label confidence management to prevent identity drift and stale semantics.

entry.title: PsychJail: Exploring Psychological Jailbreaks via Multi-Turn Persuasion of LLM Policies

author.name: Zeyu Feng, Qingyu Wu, Yuzhe Luo, Hua Cheng

entry.summary: PsychJail red-teams aligned LLMs through theory-grounded multi-turn persuasion, mapping social-psychological techniques into a tactic-conditioned attack policy with Change-of-Meaning analysis per action. It exposes psychologically grounded vulnerabilities that single-turn optimization misses.

entry.title: The Interaction Tax: When Communication Erases Diversity in Multi-Agent Teams

author.name: Summer Eunhyung Ann, Haokun Liu, Chenhao Tan

entry.summary: The Interaction Tax paper resolves contradictions in multi-agent LLM literature by showing that when agents read each other's complete outputs, structurally distinct proposals converge within one round, erasing the diversity motivating multi-agent systems. Different model families find different solutions, but naive communication destroys exactly that difference.

entry.title: ConvergeFlow: Language Flow with Provable Convergence to Token Embeddings

author.name: Na Li, Yuchen Jiao, Changxiao Cai, Gen Li

entry.summary: ConvergeFlow is an embedding-space flow-based language model constrained to the convex hull of token embeddings and trained purely with flow-matching MSE, with proofs that flows converge to valid token embeddings despite predictor errors, removing the cross-entropy decoder dependency of continuous LMs. This enables direct token prediction from continuous trajectories.

entry.title: ORBIT++: Benchmarking SfM in the Wild with 360{\deg} Video

author.name: Sara Sabour, Linyi Jin, Richard Tucker, Amir Hertz, Marcus Brubaker, Saurabh Saxena, Junhwa Hur, Andrea Tagliasacchi, Deqing Sun, David J. Fleet, Richard Szeliski, Noah Snavely

entry.summary: ORBIT++ introduces a benchmark for camera pose estimation leveraging online panoramic 360-degree video to construct challenging clips with robust ground-truth trajectories, targeting SfM failures under difficult camera motions and dynamic scenes. Author team includes leading figures from academic and industrial 3D vision research.

entry.title: Betting for Sim-to-Real Performance Certificates

author.name: Yujia Chen, Bowen Weng

entry.summary: Applies betting/e-value style sequential testing to sim-to-real evaluation: an operator peeks at large simulation banks before each costly real trial and places bets on outcomes, yielding tighter performance certificates than small-sample intervals alone. Formalizes how simulation evidence can be safely leveraged for real-world guarantees.

entry.title: DreamMimic: Learning Visuomotor Whole-Body Loco-Manipulation via World Model

author.name: Jie Yin, Xingyu Lai

entry.summary: DreamMimic distills privileged teacher policies into vision-based humanoid loco-manipulation controllers by repurposing a Dreamer-style RSSM world model as predictive latent dynamics serving both representation and multi-step supervision, reducing long-horizon drift.

entry.title: There Is No Neutral Harness: Modern LLM Leaderboards Are Manufactured by Config-Fragile Items

author.name: V. S. Raghu Parupudi

entry.summary: This paper treats the LLM evaluation harness (option order, prompt wording, likelihood-vs-generated answer extraction) as an independent variable and introduces the fragility grid: 12 open-weight instruction-tuned models answering the same 3,679 items under many harness configurations. It shows leaderboard rankings are substantially manufactured by config-fragile items.

entry.title: HANSARD: A Reference Architecture for Forensic Readiness, Runtime Witnessing, and Graded Attribution in Autonomous Multi-Agent AI Systems

author.name: Christos Sardianos, Iliana Pla, Vasilis Efthymiou, Iraklis Varlamis, Thomas Lagkas, Panagiotis Sarigiannidis, Georgios Th. Papadopoulos

entry.summary: HANSARD proposes a reference architecture for forensic readiness, runtime witnessing, and graded attribution in autonomous multi-agent systems, targeting attribution laundering where acts are spread across redundant agents until none is a but-for cause. It notes the audit record is produced by the suspects themselves.

entry.title: How AI Assistance Affects Human Skill Development: A Study of Learning with Logic Puzzles

author.name: Shang Wu, Catarina G Belem, Shuyuan Fu, Mark Steyvers, Padhraic Smyth

entry.summary: A controlled logic-puzzle experiment shows that lower-cost on-demand AI assistance increases usage frequency, and participants who used AI during access perform worse after removal, with their unassisted ability overestimated by AI-assisted performance. A Bayesian latent model separates initial ability from assistance effects. Directly relevant to concerns about AI eroding human skill development.

entry.title: EDGE: Experience-Distillation for Guided Exploration in Agentic Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Can Xie, Yuyi Zhou, Wen Yang, Ziyi zhang, Siyao Song, Yingzhuo Deng, Shuo Ren, Jiajun Zhang

entry.summary: EDGE treats retrieved experiences as temporary training-time scaffolds that are progressively internalized into the policy parameters during agentic RL, rather than maintaining permanent inference-time retrieval dependencies. It partitions rollouts to guide exploration while avoiding capability-mismatched guidance.

entry.title: Register Shifts Break LLM Safety: A Bengali Benchmark with Culturally Grounded Harms

author.name: Naymul Islam, Nusrat Jahan Lia, Shubhashis Roy Dipta, Sabik Bin Sultan, Abdullah Khan Zehady

entry.summary: BanglaSafe evaluates 18 frontier LLMs on 879 Bengali prompts across 17 culturally grounded harm categories and five prompting conditions, finding 53.6% of responses unsafe or partially unsafe. Notably, writing style within Bengali matters more than the English-to-Bengali switch, with formal newspaper framing succeeding most.

entry.title: Unlearning Is Not Just Erasing: Temporal Decoupling via Generation Inequality

author.name: Xunlei Chen, Qirui Ye, Yuang Li, Yi Gong, Zhaokun Wang, Wenyi Li, Shiyao Guo, Jinyu Guo

entry.summary: ADU reframes LLM unlearning as contextual attention-pathway decoupling rather than token erasure, exploiting the functional distinction between local and global attention heads. It identifies preplan positions that retrieve persistent sensitive anchors and fixes their candidate pathways, aiming for precise forgetting without damaging general utility or benign knowledge.

entry.title: Credal Large Language Models for Semantic Commitment under Uncertainty

author.name: Shireen Kudukkil Manchingal, Sofiia Nikolenko, Fabio Cuzzolin

entry.summary: Credal LLMs represent uncertainty via ensembles of LoRA adapters inducing credal sets with lower and upper probabilities, distinguishing epistemic ignorance from genuine ambiguity rather than collapsing to one softmax distribution. Two commitment scores, including a token-space CTC computed without extra generation, quantify semantic commitment under uncertainty.

entry.title: Thinking Beyond Videos: Unifying Video Reasoning and Deep Research for Open-World Video Agents

author.name: Wenqi Liu, Shijie Ma, Yunxiao Wang, Meng Liu, Qile Su, Han Liu, Bohan Hou, Xuanyu Zheng, Changyi Liu, Tianke Zhang, Haonan Fan, Kaiyu Jiang, Yingxin Li, Jiankang Chen, Xu Wang, Bin Wen, Tingting Gao, Han Li, Jianhua Yin, Yinwei Wei, Xuemeng Song

entry.summary: VideoRover unifies thinking-with-videos temporal perception with deep-research-style external information seeking, iteratively coordinating video cropping, multimodal search, and webpage browsing where each tool result selects the next action. A dedicated dataset trains this coordinated behavior for open-world video question answering requiring evidence absent from the video itself.

entry.title: Provably adaptive sampling with uniform and remasking discrete diffusion models

author.name: Daniil Dmitriev, Zhihan Huang, Yuting Wei

entry.summary: Provides theoretical analysis of adaptive sampling for uniform and remasking discrete diffusion models, showing first-order leave-one-out denoiser samplers remove the linear-in-dimension lower bound dependence of tau-leaping and can correct denoising mistakes mid-sampling.

entry.title: Long-Horizon Audio-Visual Generation for Persistent Stories and Interactive Worlds

author.name: Nan Duan, Haoyang Huang, Weiyang Jin, Haoran Li, Yaowei Li, Yuming Li, Yijun Liu, Xin Lu, Xiaoxiao Ma, Yanwen Ma, Yaofeng Su, Yilang Sun, Haoyu Wang, Zeyue Xue, Songchun Zhang, Junhao Zhuang

entry.summary: JoyAI-Echo-1.5 is a unified audio-visual generation system with long-video variants featuring composable cross-shot memory for persistent character identity and voice, and a world-model variant converting navigation inputs into calibrated metric 6-DoF trajectories. Companion system to EchoWM pushing persistent long-form generative storytelling.

entry.title: UniMem: Unifying Multimodal Memory and Control for Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Lars Osterberg, Maggie Wang, Mac Schwager

entry.summary: UniMem unifies multimodal memory and low-level control within a single VLA framework to handle non-Markovian long-horizon tasks, avoiding the memory bottleneck of auxiliary VLM-based approaches. It adaptively selects informative historical frames rather than using fixed-interval frame conditioning.

entry.title: CIDER: Continual Interactive Distillation for Embodied Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Houlin Li, Minghui Xu, Guo Xu, Xuan Du, Xiaohan Yan, Chun Wang, Yuxiang Yan, Shukai Yang, Yongcheng Liu, Wei Shan, Maoqing Yao
