entry.summary: CIDER extends human-in-the-loop real-world reinforcement learning to continual settings by freezing the accumulated policy as a teacher before each new task and interleaving learning with distillation-based consolidation, mitigating catastrophic forgetting in physical manipulation.

entry.title: Proxy reliance in large language model decisions is uncalibrated to predictive evidence

author.name: Zengqing Wu, Chuan Xiao

entry.summary: Using a clinical-ranking task with computable ground-truth warranted reliance, this paper shows proxy reliance in LLM decisions is uncalibrated: neutral-label proxies get relied upon despite carrying no information, while informative proxies draw over-, under-, and warranted-reliance verdicts across four models.

entry.title: AutoSaddler: Automatic Harness Optimization with Durable Updates from Agent Execution Traces

author.name: Sungho Park, Wonjoong Kim, Rongyuan Tan, Jue Zhang, Wook-Shin Han, Pengfei Gao, Chanyoung Park, Yongqiang Yao, Rao Fu, Elsie Nallipogu, Qingwei Lin, Saravan Rajmohan, Dongmei Zhang

entry.summary: AutoSaddler formulates harness improvement for unreliable long-horizon agents as offline learning, iteratively updating harness prompts, tool configs, and control logic from failure traces via diagnosis, structured patch generation treating the harness as code, and validation-based selection. Evaluated on GAIA2 and SWE-style tasks.

entry.title: EditStream: A Unified Autoregressive Framework for Interactive Video Generation and Editing

author.name: Yuqian Zhou, Zhenghong Zhou, Zongze Wu, Cameron Smith, Richard Zhang, Jiebo Luo, Eli Shechtman, Zhe Lin

entry.summary: EditStream unifies text-to-video, image-to-video, video-to-video, editing propagation, reference-guided editing, and camera pose control in one DiT-based autoregressive model with task-specific conditioning, distilled to few-step streaming for interactive use.

entry.title: In-Situ Reconstruction of the International Space Station Using 3D Gaussian Splatting and Astrobee

author.name: Hudson Kim, Ryan Soussan, Brian Coltin, Jordan Kam

entry.summary: DELTA is a deformable elevation-based local terrain attention encoder for quadrupedal locomotion on sparse terrain that predicts state-conditioned sampling locations and attends only to fixed-size terrain-evidence tokens, avoiding the resolution-scaling costs of dense attention map encoding.

entry.title: KVBoost: Chunk-Level Key-Value Cache Reuse with Deviation-Guided Recomputation for Efficient Large Language Model Inference

author.name: Srihari Unnikrishnan

entry.summary: KVBoost introduces chunk-level KV cache reuse for LLM inference that works even when shared content appears at non-prefix positions, using a dual-hash keying scheme separating positional and content identity plus deviation-guided recomputation to fix attention boundary errors. This addresses prefill latency beyond what prefix-caching systems offer.

entry.title: Disagree to Explore, Agree to Commit: Routing-Guided Test-Time Scaling for Software Agents

author.name: Kang Chen, Junjie Nian, Yixin Cao, Yugang Jiang

entry.summary: Risa uses native MoE router traces as a behavioral signal to guide exploration diversity and answer arbitration in software-engineering agents, avoiding external judges or test execution at selection time. It shows router readouts can steer and select among stochastic patch trajectories effectively.

entry.title: TailSieve: Partial-Rollout-Guided Tail Routing for LLM Rollouts

author.name: Tianqi Xu, Lu Lv, Haoyang Huang, Wenjie Huang, Zhanming Shen, Yuhao Shen, Baolin Zhang, Xinyi Hu, Shuang Ge, Jun Dai, Tianyu Liu, Suorong Yang, Zhikai Li, Ye Bai, Jun Zhang, Lei Chen, Yue Li, Mingchen Wan

entry.summary: TailSieve jointly controls tail routing and replica allocation for large-scale LLM rollouts used in RL post-training, on-policy distillation, and heavy sampling, preventing a few long generations from dominating end-to-end makespan inside high-concurrency batches.

entry.title: Is Next-Chunk Reasoning RL Really Better than SFT? Revisiting Training Strategies under no-CoT Data

author.name: Yinhao Tang, Youqing Fang, Yanan Sun, Jiangning Liu, Ziyi Wang, Xun Zhao, Weiming Zhang, Bin Liu, Kuikun Liu, Wenwei Zhang, Kai Chen

entry.summary: A controlled study asking whether next-chunk reasoning RL genuinely beats supervised alternatives for leveraging no-CoT corpora, comparing against Mixed SFT which interleaves no-CoT data in a single supervised stage. Findings clarify whether gains come from the RL formulation or merely better data exposure.

entry.title: Agent-G$^2$: Gaussian Guidance for Agentic Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Zixuan Wang, Yanrui Miao, Zhengxi Lu, Teng Pan, Yiwen Qiu, Hongxing Li, Peng Qiu, Ruiqing Zhang, Yongliang Shen

entry.summary: Agent-G2 improves hint-based reinforcement learning for agentic tasks by modeling guidance depth as a Gaussian band of informative prefix lengths rather than a single deterministic scalar. This addresses reward sparsity in long-horizon rollouts with per-task adaptive guidance. It matters because expert-trajectory hints are a practical lever for training agents on sparse-reward problems.

entry.title: ADMIL: Attention-Distilled Multiple Instance Learning for Selective Foundation Model Inference in Pathology

author.name: Duncan Stothers, Ren-Chin Wu, William Lotter

entry.summary: ADMIL distills an attention-based multiple instance learning teacher's attention into a lightweight PriorNet that selects top-K informative tiles before invoking an expensive pathology foundation-model encoder. This selective-compute scheme preserves slide-level accuracy while dramatically cutting inference cost.

entry.title: Pointing-VLA: Typed Spatial Grounding Interfaces for Vision-Language-Action Manipulation

author.name: Xiwen Chen, Zelin Li, Zhiruo Zhou, Huiming Chen, Chenwei Wang, Xiaojun Zhu

entry.summary: Pointing-VLA adds typed spatial grounding heads to Embodied-R1 that predict normalized points, object-functional grounding heatmaps, and trajectories directly from hidden states instead of serializing geometry as text. An execution contract assigns PICK and PLACE to appropriate readouts, achieving SOTA on Bridge/WidowX averaging 72.9 percent plus physical pick-place deployments.

entry.title: Future Querying: Can LLMs Serve as Implicit Medical World Models?

author.name: Siri Willems, James Butterworth, Lore Goetschalckx, Peter Vrancx, Philippe Modard, Elke Giets, Ludovic Denoyer

entry.summary: Future querying probes whether LLMs act as implicit medical world models by answering time-indexed clinical queries about patient futures directly from unstructured documentation, with endpoint-agnostic training avoiding task-specific retraining. Small locally fine-tuned open-weight models match or approach larger proprietary systems.

entry.title: Adaptive Multilevel Twisted Sequential Monte Carlo for Rare Events Estimation in Language Models

author.name: Zixuan Liu, Fangzheng Wu, Brian Summa, Zizhan Zheng

entry.summary: Adaptive Multilevel Twisted SMC estimates extremely rare unsafe LLM behaviors by learning twist functions through progressively rarer intermediate events, avoiding reliance on positive samples that are nearly absent initially. This enables principled probability estimation for tail risks at deployment scale. It directly serves AI safety auditing.

entry.title: WnW: Waxing-and-Waning KV Cache for Long-Form Speech LLMs

author.name: Yiming Yao, Chenyang Lyu, Xuanfan Ni, Longyue Wang, Weihua Luo, Yazheng Yang, Jinsong Su

entry.summary: Identifies that prefill-only KV cache compression fails on long-form audio because prefill attention concentrates near the audio start while decode-time attention spreads broadly. Proposes WnW, which classifies KV heads into anchor, tidal, and fixed roles, keeping anchor heads on GPU as importance observers and recalling tidal-head complements from CPU chunk-by-chunk.

entry.title: Perturb the Thought, Not the Pixels: Latent-Space Rollout Diversification for Reinforcement Learning of Vision-Language Models

author.name: Michael Jerge, Joseph Pelczar, Justin Downes

entry.summary: NC-GRPO injects scale-calibrated Gaussian noise into the last hidden layer of prompt encoding for half of each rollout group in reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards, branching rollouts from displaced departure states. Branches that still reach the answer despite displacement are reinforced over derailed ones, converting latent sensitivity at the branch point into a useful training signal for vision-language model reasoning.

entry.title: Frame-Level Evaluation in Weakly Supervised Video Anomaly Detection Mostly Measures Video-Level Ranking

author.name: Inpyo Song, Jangwon Lee

entry.summary: This analytical paper exactly decomposes Micro-AUROC used in weakly supervised video anomaly detection into Within-AUROC for temporal ordering within videos and Cross-AUROC for comparisons across videos, showing only 0.071-0.388 percent of anomalous-normal frame comparisons occur within the same video. Frame-level evaluation mostly measures video-level ranking, a benchmark property decreasing as O(1/V).

entry.title: Robust Bimanual Vision-Language-Action Models via Embarrassingly Simple Modality Masking

author.name: Dongzhou Cheng, Ziang Li, Yixiao Zhou, Haojuan Li, Jinghao Zhang, Lei Lei, Minjing Dong, Jie Gui, Jiaqi Wang

entry.summary: Introduces a Modality Masking Mechanism (M3) that stochastically masks modality channels during training to stabilize query-based vision-language-action models for bimanual manipulation. The approach requires no architectural changes or large-scale pretraining, addressing discontinuous actions caused by unstable multi-view and language fusion.

entry.title: OpenSCvx: An Open-Source Modular and Extensible Nonlinear Trajectory Planning Package

author.name: Christopher R. Hayner, Griffin J. Norris, Fabio Spada, Samet Uzun, Avi Mittal, Behcet Ac{\i}kmese, Karen Leung

entry.summary: OpenSCvx is an open-source Python framework for nonlinear trajectory optimization providing a symbolic modeling interface that auto-constructs solver formulations from modular objectives, dynamics, and constraints. Supports continuous-time constraints, temporal logic specifications, and more.

entry.title: Ludi${}_{\scriptscriptstyle 0.1}$: An Agentic System for Socially Intelligent Robots

author.name: Wooseong Chung, William Cong, Jakub Dworakowski, Ethan Ewer, Tri Wahyu Guntara, Yeonwoo Jeong, Tianchong Jiang, Chaewon Kim, Hyunseo Kim, Jinwoo Kim, Jinyeon Kim, Yea-Seul Kim, Jack Kunde, Kangwook Lee, Sangheon Lee, Robert Nowak, Junha Roh

entry.summary: Ludi 0.1 is an agentic system for socially intelligent robots integrating speech, multimodal reasoning, memory, navigation, and learned manipulation, with a fine-tuned VLM decision core trained on multi-turn traces containing ambiguity, clarification, correction, and interruption.

entry.title: Generating scenarios for extreme events, without extreme data

author.name: Jennifer Chu | MIT News

entry.summary: MIT engineers developed a machine-learning method generating plausible extreme-event scenarios (storms, heat waves, wildfires) and their characteristics without requiring historical extremes, learning instead from ordinary daily data distributions.

entry.title: Hints, Critics, and Teachers: Prior Injection for Sparse-Reward RL in Vision-Language Math Reasoning

author.name: Qiqian Fu

entry.summary: Training eleven prior-injection methods under identical sparse-reward conditions for vision-language math reasoning (Qwen2-VL-2B answers 3.6% correctly), the study finds priors help exactly when effectively delivered to the policy: hint, distillation, and critic arms separate cleanly from teacher-capped and no-prior arms.

entry.title: WAM-OPD: On-Policy Distillation for World Action Models

author.name: Liuhaichen Yang, Zhuang Jiang, Chenchao Sheng, Zezhi Tang

entry.summary: WAM-OPD presents a deployment-consistent on-policy distillation recipe for video-first world action models, where a frozen teacher labels student-generated histories with coherent video and action targets. This repairs accelerated students without sparse-reward RL and keeps training consistent with deployment conditions.

entry.title: ExecRubrics: Executable Tool-Augmented Rubrics for Verifiable and Efficient Long-Form Evaluation

author.name: Kaustubh D. Dhole, Charles L. A. Clarke, Eugene Y. Agichtein

entry.summary: ExecRubrics represents evaluation rubrics as compact executable Python scoring programs rather than ambiguous natural-language criteria aggregated linearly, capturing dependencies, alternatives, penalties, and overrides. It shows verifiable, inspectable evaluation logic on HealthBench, HelpSteer, and other long-form benchmarks.

entry.title: From Inertia to Objectivity: Improving Deep Research Agents with Noise Isolation

author.name: Xiangxin Zhang, Zhanwei Zhang, Zhihang Fu, Binbin Lin, Wenxiao Wang

entry.summary: Introducing inertia bias, this paper shows deep research agents judge the consequences of their own prior actions less objectively, measured via the IBIS benchmark controlling observations while varying ownership of the preceding search step. Self-authored history systematically distorts subsequent judgment and propagates into downstream errors.

entry.title: EviSafe: Evidence-Grounded Safety Evaluation for Vision-Language Models

author.name: Xuetong Li, Gaofeng Liu

entry.summary: EviSafe evaluates VLM safety beyond final responses by jointly assessing natural behavior, explicit grounding in textual and visual evidence, and counterfactual sensitivity to safety-critical evidence changes, instantiated as EviSafeBench with 1,181 gold scenarios and 2,452 counterfactual variants.

entry.title: Inferring Action from Future Latent State for Robotic Manipulation

author.name: Fenghao Lei, Zhixiong Huang, Long Yang, Jiabao Chen, Jie Cheng, Peilin Huang, Han Fu, Zhuo Li, Xiaoxue Ren

entry.summary: DELE-w0.5 argues video generation is an unnecessary intermediate objective for world-action modeling in robotic manipulation, proposing instead to infer actions from predicted future latent states. Skipping dense intermediate frames saves substantial capacity and computation while targeting physical outcomes directly.

entry.title: The Mask Is Not the Model: Auditing Prefix Invariance in Attention, State-Space, and Hybrid Sequence Models

author.name: Taebong Kim, Youngsik Hong, Minsik Kim, Sunyoung Choi, Jaewon Jang, Minseo Kim

entry.summary: This paper formalizes prefix invariance (representations at position t must not depend on future inputs) and gives a two-forward-pass audit localizing causality breaks in attention, state-space, and hybrid models. Mask inspection found none of 192 injected faults while the audit localized all, also finding defects in Zamba2 and Nemotron-H checkpoints.

entry.title: Beyond Surface Cues: Disentangling Sociocultural Signals in Multilingual LLMs

author.name: Yuanjun Feng, Tanzhou Liu, Stefan Feuerriegel, Yash Raj Shrestha

entry.summary: This audit disentangles sociocultural signals in multilingual LLM outputs, showing that identity labels inferred from textual cues can masquerade as cultural grounding and obscure bias. Using 89,253 outputs from 12 LLMs across English, French, and Chinese, it separately measures stereotype reproduction, group representation differences, and cross-cultural patterns.

entry.title: Adversarial Entropy Inflation Against Gumbel-Based Inference Verification

author.name: Nikita Kezins

entry.summary: This security paper shows Gumbel-based inference verification against LLM weight exfiltration degrades sharply when an adversary controls the prompt distribution: prompts engineered to break grammatical structure widen the verifier's admissible-token set and open a larger covert channel. Attacks across six instruction-tuned models demonstrate the passive-adversary assumption is unsafe.

entry.title: ST$^2$U: Stateful Test-Time Unlearning via Restricted Knowledge Boundary Control

author.name: Xunlei Chen, Qinghui Gong, Ruini Xue, Yaodong Hu, Tian Lan, Wenhong Tian

entry.summary: ST2U formulates test-time unlearning of restricted knowledge in LLMs as trajectory-wide boundary control rather than isolated activation edits, preventing restricted knowledge re-entry during autoregressive generation. Avoids costly retraining while controlling hidden-state trajectories across prompt, cache, and generated prefix.

entry.title: WorldToken: Time-First Sequence Modeling for Robotic Imitation Learning

author.name: Chunkai Yang, Andong Yang, Chao Gao

entry.summary: WorldToken fuses multiview images, proprioception, and task conditioning into one token per timestep for a causal temporal transformer with a diffusion action head, achieving 59.45 percent mean success across 23 RoboCasa tasks with an 85M-parameter policy, supported by a full factorial sweep over dataset sizes, model sizes, and seeds.

entry.title: Evaluating Multimodal Narrative Understanding of Popular Hollywood Films

author.name: David Bamman, Kent K. Chang, Allison Cooper, Juishan Hsu, Reina Kushihashi, Madison Mar, Arnav Podichetty, Rachael Samberg, Ipek Nil Sancak, Yuhan Shao

entry.summary: The authors build a copyright-safe multimodal benchmark for narrative understanding of Hollywood films by identifying likely public-domain films via US Copyright Catalog research and publishing Variety weekly box-office data from 1922-1979. This enables large-scale computational film analysis without legal risk.

entry.title: Read Less, Solve More: Token-Efficient Sparse Reading for AI Agents

author.name: Zedong Liu, Jiaan Wu, Xinyang Ma, Le Xu, Kai Wang, Yuanchao Hu, Dingwen Tao, Guangming Tan

entry.summary: SparseRead is a training-free reading layer that controls what content enters an agent context before broad material reaches the model, combining a regime-aware Read Gate, pluggable reader backends, and a bounded, source-anchored evidence acquisition protocol. It reduces token and latency costs while preserving task-relevant evidence.

entry.title: CONTRAMEM: Learning Self-Evolving Procedural Memory from Contrasting Multi-Model Trajectories

author.name: Zheyuan Deng, Binghang Lu, Hanqi Feng, Shirley Huang, Dianzhuo Wang, Yuanda Xu, Zhiwei Zhang, Yige Sun, Changhong Mou, Runyu Zhang, Yuexing Hao, Barnabas Poczos, Xiaomin Li

entry.summary: CONTRAMEM builds self-evolving procedural memory for computer-use agents without training, treating outcome variation across same-task trajectories from different models as supervision signal. Differences in correctness, efficiency, recovery, and failure modes are distilled into compact procedural knowledge.

entry.title: CAI-DLLM: Convergence Aware Inference for Diffusion Language Models

author.name: Farhana Amin, Sabiha Afroz, Dimitrios S. Nikolopoulos

entry.summary: CAI-DLLM is a training-free inference acceleration method for diffusion language models that uses first-step confidence to commit easy tokens early and allocate more denoising steps to harder tokens. It works on LLaDA-8B-Instruct and Dream-7B-Instruct without retraining or extra predictors.

entry.title: GSAR: Goal-State-Anchor Rewards for Mobile GUI Agents with Self-Evolving Data Synthesis

author.name: Long Zhang, Yuhan Chen, Chaoran Zhang, Wanxia Cao, Kun Huang, Pengzhi Gao, Wei Liu, Jian Luan, Chenliang Li, Lixin Zou

entry.summary: GSAR provides goal-state-anchor rewards enabling online RL for mobile GUI agents, pairing scalable self-evolving task synthesis across environments with reliable reward signals to stabilize policy optimization where existing evaluators are inaccurate or unscalable.

entry.title: AI emotional support is better only when chosen, but shifts preferences even when it is not

author.name: Yaoxi Shi, Cathy Mengying Fang, Guy LabanPattie Maes, Amit Goldenberg

entry.summary: Across three experiments plus a 28-day OpenAI collaboration study, this paper shows AI emotional support is rated superior only when users chose it, yet interacting with AI shifts preferences toward choosing it again regardless of congruence, revealing choice-dependent evaluation and preference drift.

entry.title: Hidden in the Request: Explaining Unethical LLM Compliance through Token Relevance

author.name: Or Biton, Tomer Krichli, Itai Allouche, Joseph Keshet

entry.summary: Using Layer-wise Relevance Propagation, this paper traces why LLMs comply with unethical requests more in request-for-assistance forms than classification or first-person statement forms, attributing the discrepancy to attribution bias in how the model weights tokens.

entry.title: SRPO: Self-Reflective Policy Optimization for Long-Horizon Reasoning

author.name: Jialong Liu, Yuling Shi, Ning Yang, Xiaodong Gu, Zuchao Li

entry.summary: SRPO enables LLMs to analyze their own completed trajectories, compress errors into reflection patches, and use reflection-conditioned teacher scoring to convert sparse terminal rewards into dense token-level training signals without external critics or larger teachers. It internalizes self-reflection as a credit-assignment mechanism for post-training. Potentially significant for efficient RL fine-tuning.

entry.title: Agentic Scaffolding Amplifies Sycophantic Behavior in Large Language Models

author.name: Thantham Jittham

entry.summary: Across 4,800 veracity judgments spanning six models and four conditions, this paper finds that agentic scaffolding features like feedback loops, reconsideration checkpoints, and iterative refinement systematically amplify sycophantic behavior in LLMs. Multi-turn interaction and user pressure each add opportunities for agreement drift. Extends sycophancy research beyond single-turn settings.

entry.title: NoTB: Oracle-Free Triage of LLM-Generated RTL via Cross-Model Formal Consensus

author.name: Elisavet Lydia Alvanaki, Je Yang, Biruk Seyoum, Luca P. Carloni

entry.summary: NoTB is an oracle-free framework for triaging LLM-generated RTL hardware designs using cross-model formal consensus via Sequential Equivalence Checking. Designs provably equivalent across independently trained LLM families are flagged as likely correct without testbenches or judge heuristics.

entry.title: The Imitator Game: Benchmarking Robot Imitative Ability Beyond Action Prediction

author.name: Xunzhe Zhou, Yiyang Cai, Fengyi Wang, Ran Ju, Hanxiang Ren, Ruizhe Liu, Yu Zhang, Qian Luo, Feng Chen, Pei Zhou, Yi Ma, Yanchao Yang

entry.summary: The Imitator Game is a four-level benchmark progressively widening the gap between human demonstrations and the robot's own scene to isolate where trajectory replay fails and intent-level imitation begins. It tests whether policies infer demonstrated goals rather than replay motions in near-identical scenes.

entry.title: WildHandBench: A Benchmark for Handwritten Text Understanding that Challenges MLLMs and Humans

author.name: Jun Zhang, Qiao Zhao, Cheng Cui, Jianying Qu, Zhongkai Sun, Jianwen Yang, Changda Zhou, ZhuoXin Liu, Shubin Han

entry.summary: WildHandBench provides 500 handwritten documents across free text, tables, formulas, four languages, and nine real-world scenarios to stress-test multimodal document understanding where printed-document parsing has neared saturation. It introduces a Prior-Driven Error metric that separates language-prior errors from visual-evidence errors across 18 state-of-the-art models plus calibrated human baselines.

entry.title: Think Only When Needed: Prompt-Authority Control for Selective Slow-Path Intervention in Vision-Language-Action Manipulation

author.name: Zhiruo Zhou, Zelin Li, Xiwen Chen, Jiazhuo Li, Chenwei Wang, Huiming Chen, Xiaojun Zhu

entry.summary: TOWN-VLA identifies prompt-form collapse in retrieval-augmented VLA policies, where merely changing instruction form collapses success rates even when appended text carries no useful semantics. Its prompt-authority interface separates candidate generation from permission to modify policy inputs, invoking slow-path thinking only when needed.

entry.title: SWE Refactor Bench: Can Coding Agents Complete a Long-Horizon, Whole-Repository Stack Migration?

author.name: Deyao Hong, Yizhe Chi, Wenyi Li, Xiaoqiu Wang, Mingju Gao, Kaisen Yang, Bingxiang He, Youjie Zheng, Calvin Xiao, Qinhuai Na

entry.summary: SWE Refactor Bench comprises 20 whole-repository migrations covering four kinds of technical debt, with a three-stage protocol measuring migration completeness, not just behavioral correctness, to prevent agents from copying original implementations to pass tests (Blindness hack). It asks whether coding agents can perform long-horizon stack migrations autonomously.

entry.title: Benchmarking Composable Compression Techniques in Mixture-of-Experts LLMs

author.name: Afsara Benazir, Chen Chen, Rongxiao Qu, Jiabo Huang, Jingtao Li, Lingjuan Lyu

entry.summary: MoEXBench systematically benchmarks how expert pruning, weight quantization, and KV-cache compression interact when stacked in Mixture-of-Experts LLM deployment pipelines. Prior work evaluated these techniques in isolation despite realistic deployments requiring composition. The benchmark clarifies compounding effects on quality, memory, and throughput.

entry.title: Neural Boltzmann Equations

author.name: Jonas Spinner, Jack Shergold

entry.summary: Introduces Neural Boltzmann Equations for early-universe particle dynamics, combining physics-inspired neural distribution functions, Monte Carlo importance sampling for phase-space integrals, and learned parameter prediction to escape the fixed momentum-grid scaling limits of classical quadrature approaches.

entry.title: Kernel Token Contradiction: a Fast and Principled Approach for LLM Claim Uncertainty Quantification

author.name: J\'er\'emie Dentan, Alexi Canesse, Mahammed El Sharkawy, Sonia Vanier

entry.summary: Presents Kernel Token Contradiction (KTC), a lightweight white-box claim-level uncertainty method representing candidate tokens as a positive semi-definite kernel combining conditional distributions with a Wikipedia-frequency token contradiction score, quantified via Von Neumann entropy. Runs CPU-only at over 8x speedup versus baselines.

entry.title: Calibrate What You SHIP: Post-Selection Risk Control for Verifier-Guided Text-to-Image Generation

author.name: Xuanhua Yin, Shunqi Mao, Wei Guo, Chuanzhi Xu, Weidong Cai

entry.summary: SHIP addresses a calibration mismatch in verifier-guided text-to-image systems: search changes both which prompts receive outputs and which candidates are released, so candidate-level risk control does not imply control of released-output risk. The framework formalizes the estimand shift through prompt reweighting and within-prompt selection, then calibrates inference policies by replaying the full deployed policy on held-out prompts with an independent judge.

entry.title: Improved denoising diffusion probabilistic models with efficient non-diagonal covariance modeling

author.name: Rui Xia, Ayan Das, Artem Artemev, Andi Zhang, Guillaume Hennequin, Alberto Bernacchia

entry.summary: This paper develops a Kronecker-DCT covariance model capturing non-diagonal pixel and channel correlations plus power-law frequency spectra of natural images, improving second-order approximations to the denoising posterior covariance in DDPMs. Better covariance modeling allows fewer, larger sampling steps at acceptable quality.

entry.title: Multiple View Neural Regression of a Facial Shape Model

author.name: Xiang Li

entry.summary: OmniCAD is a large-scale benchmark for assembly-aware 3D spatial reasoning containing 25k mechanical assemblies across robotic, automotive, aerospace, and agricultural domains, with human-verified ground-truth 3D models, 20 viewpoints each, and 21 mate relationship types, evaluating component-level reasoning, assembly prediction, and related capabilities for VLMs.

entry.title: FixAnything: 3D-Consistent Rendering Refinement via Video Generative Priors

author.name: Khiem Vuong, Deva Ramanan, Srinivasa Narasimhan

entry.summary: FixAnything repurposes a pretrained video generative model with lightweight finetuning to fix rendering artifacts across 3DGS, NeRF, mesh, and point-cloud representations in one model, exploiting implicit multi-view priors from noisy rendered sequences. Replaces representation-specialized artifact-fixing architectures.

entry.title: JANUS: Online Jacobian-Aligned Infill for Black-Box Optimization

author.name: Hongyuan Yu, Pufan Xu, Jiaojiao Yi, Yiding Tian, Mingrui Sun, Jiayuan Lu, Changyuan Wen

entry.summary: JANUS is a plug-and-play infill module for population-based black-box optimizers that estimates a local Jacobian from recent evaluations to generate Gauss-Newton exploitation candidates and exploration metrics. It augments scalar/rank-based selection signals with local geometric information without replacing the host optimizer.

entry.title: Model-Free Adaptive Parameter Tuning for Efficient Multi-Robot Warehouse Operations

author.name: Pratap Tokekar, Mouhacine Benosman, Rahul Chandan, Alexandre Ormiga Galvao Barbosa, Michael Caldara, Joseph W. Durham

entry.summary: Presents model-free adaptive tuning of digout cost-function parameters for multi-robot warehouse fulfillment centers, balancing pod-shuffling against lane congestion as operational conditions shift. Likely deployed-scale work given the author affiliations.

entry.title: EndoNav: Semantic-to-Geometric Grounding for Language-Guided Robotic Endoscopic Examination

author.name: Jecia Z. Y. Mao, Hisashi Ishida, Kathryn Jung, Masaru Ishii, Russell H. Taylor, Manish Sahu

entry.summary: EndoNav grounds spoken surgeon commands into autonomous endoscopic visualization behaviors within patient-specific sinonasal anatomy, using a viewpoint agent that generates structured visualization objectives rather than raw motion. Bridges semantic surgical intent and geometric control.

entry.title: Contact-Rich Robotic Manipulation in Construction via Zero-Shot Learning: A Diffusion Policy-Guided Adaptive Control

author.name: Roman Ibrahimov (Princeton University), Salma Mozaffari (Princeton University), Arash Adel (Princeton University)

entry.summary: Couples diffusion policies trained on simulated pose and force/torque data with an L1-inspired adaptive controller correcting predicted actions online for unmodeled contact dynamics, achieving reported 100 percent success on timber joinery, pipe fitting, and truss assembly benchmarks.

entry.title: SAEM: Stage-Aware Expert Management for Memory-Efficient MoE Inference in Chain-of-Thought Reasoning

author.name: Yujie Zhang, Bin Gao, Tulika Mitra

entry.summary: SAEM is a stage-aware MoE inference runtime that detects chain-of-thought reasoning stage boundaries and exploits coherent expert activation patterns per stage for smarter expert caching, reducing GPU-CPU transfers and memory pressure during long CoT decoding.

entry.title: Where World Models Break: Natural-Input Failure Discovery

author.name: Zhanpeng Shi, Zi Liang, Rong Feng, Shiqin Tang, Xuyang Chen, Hongzong Li

entry.summary: This paper formalizes natural-input failure discovery for world models: finding rare or unobserved condition-action combinations that cause catastrophic prediction failures within a finite query budget. It argues average-error evaluations miss systemic risk that propagates through downstream control pipelines.

entry.title: Coalition-Aware Skill Reliability for Self-Evolving Agents

author.name: Qiyan Zhao, Xiaofeng Zhang, Bo Liu, Minda Chen, Wei Xiong, Jingyang Chen, Guanting Ye, Wenhao Yu, Xiaosong Yuan, Shijie Han, Da-Han Wang, Jianmin Ji, Fei Huang, Xu-Yao Zhang

entry.summary: This paper audits whether accumulated skills in self-evolving agent skill banks actually make positive mechanistic contributions, revealing recurring reliability failures across bank compositions and deployment domains. It proposes coalition-aware skill reliability assessment to address them.

entry.title: ParallelWorld: Test-Time Scaling for Embodied Reasoning

author.name: Min Chen, Shengjun Zhang, Yuxin Li, Zhang Zhang, Xin Fei, Chong Xia, Yueqi Duan

entry.summary: ParallelWorld brings test-time scaling to embodied reasoning with parallel long-horizon exploration trajectories rather than myopic single-step lookaheads, resolving delayed-feedback challenges in occluded spatial environments.

entry.title: Rank Reversal in Multilingual LLM Judges: A Label-Free Double-Centering Calibrator

author.name: Alhasan Mahmood, Samir Abdaljalil, Hasan Kurban

entry.summary: This paper shows multilingual LLM judges produce different backbone rankings depending on prompt language, with statistically significant rank reversal in 7 of 15 backbone pairs across eight languages. Its Consensus-Based Calibration estimator recovers language-backbone interaction terms label-free via double-centering with finite-sample guarantees.

entry.title: Towards a Densing Law for User Representation Learning at Billion-Scale Capacity

author.name: Bin Dou, Junru Zhang, Zhaoyi Yuan, Wuliang Huang, Letian Gong, Baokun Wang, Huan Li, Yu Cheng, Weiqiang Wang

entry.summary: From ByteDance-affiliated industrial researchers, this report proposes a User Behavioral Densing Law quantifying the minimum sufficient tokenization capacity as raw behavioral data scales toward billion-user regimes, where raw-text scaling exhibits diminishing returns. Pilot studies compare raw versus tokenized scaling and derive quantitative scaling guidance.

entry.title: Act with Intent: Distilling Behavior Intent for Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Sangoh Lee, Sangwoo Mo, Wook-Shin Han

entry.summary: Intention Distillation supervises VLA action decoders with behavior-level intent distilled from a frozen teacher VLM interpreting demonstrated segments, capturing the shared semantic objective behind actions rather than particular future realizations. It improves on behavior cloning and future-frame supervision signals.

entry.title: RIBOSPAN: A Long-Context RNA Foundation Model for Versatile RNA Modeling

author.name: Ziyuan Wang, Bohao Tang, Fei Zhang, Shuo Han, Pengfei Liu

entry.summary: RIBOSPAN is a 1.61B-parameter bidirectional RNA foundation model pretrained natively at up to 10,240 nucleotide context, enabling full-length transcript modeling at single-nucleotide resolution via attention-isolated sequence packing. Evaluations show long-context pretraining preserves reconstruction quality at maximum length.

entry.title: AIREP: A Protocol for Per-Decision Evidence in AI Runtime Governance

author.name: Ali Toygar Abak

entry.summary: AIREP proposes a signed-record protocol for logging AI runtime governance decisions (release, block, defer, redact, escalate) as hash-chained objects that any party can verify offline. Records reference evidence by hash and explicitly declare coverage gaps, enabling tamper detection and accountability.

entry.title: Beyond What Meets the Eye: Unveiling Situational Illusions for Multimodal Large Language Models

author.name: Zhiming Yang, Zhuoxi Xiong, Donglin Zhou, Wenjun Wei, Shiyao Cui, Jinqiao Shi

entry.summary: This work defines situational illusions, where scene appearances diverge from underlying physical states, and introduces MSIBench to evaluate MLLM discrimination, understanding, and reasoning under such illusions. Evaluations across 27 model configurations show current MLLMs are systematically vulnerable.

entry.title: STAGE: Stateful Translation to Agentic Graph Execution with Policy-Scoped Context and Deterministic Control

author.name: Mengxi Luo, Changjia Chen, An Cao, Zirong Huang, Wanyi Dai

entry.summary: STAGE confines model judgment to policy-scoped nodes in an executable graph while deterministic code enforces procedural control, evaluated on SOP-Bench, tau2-bench domains, and a proprietary banking dispute benchmark. It improves task success and repeated-run reliability versus monolithic full-policy execution.

entry.title: CacheRouter: A Dual-Path Tool Routing Architecture with Cache-Preserving Main-Model Isolation for Long-Tail Tool Discovery

author.name: Donghui Zha, Lingwei Xu, Linxiao Wu, Yixue Dong, Haochen Li

entry.summary: CacheRouter resolves the tension between progressive disclosure of tools and prompt-cache validity via dual-path routing: the main model sees a small fixed core-tool set keeping its request prefix stable, while a router sub-model searches and delivers all other tools through an independent channel.

entry.title: Buried in Textual Debt: Context Pruning with Visual Evidence Preservation for MLLM Agents

author.name: Yuchen Huang, Sijia Li, Jun Zhang, Yi R. Fung

entry.summary: SPARE is a KL-guided framework pruning accumulated self-generated reasoning text in multimodal tool-use agents before it suppresses visual evidence, using a compact task-state summary as privileged guidance to remove redundancy while preserving grounding.

entry.title: POOL: Propagated Uncertainty Over Lookalikes

author.name: Rounak Sharma, Ananya B. Sai, Soumyabrata Pal

entry.summary: POOL provides cost-efficient confidence estimation for black-box LLMs by clustering overlapping query stems and evaluating a base estimator on representatives, propagating uncertainty to lookalikes inspired by group testing, trading off against expensive sampling-based uncertainty.

entry.title: EarthVerse: Benchmarking Scientific Agents Across Dynamic Earth Systems and Natural Hazards

author.name: Zhiqing Cui, Xinxiang Yin, Yihong Tang, Xinglang Zhang, Yuanzhe Hu, Siru Zhong, Weidong Tang, Yuxuan Liang, Weijia Li, Ming Jin, Shirui Pan, Yuhao Kang, Dingyi Zhuang, Jinhua Zhao

entry.summary: EarthVerse benchmarks scientific agents on 405 reproducible earth-system and natural-hazard investigation tasks grounded in 199 documented events across 19 hazard families. Agents must select compatible heterogeneous evidence, execute transparent calculations, reconcile source conflicts, and preserve provenance. Executable ground truth enables fine-grained evaluation of scientific reasoning.

entry.title: Mol-JEPA: A multimodal Joint Embedding Predictive Architecture for Molecules

author.name: Florian Rottach, Sebastian Schieferdecker, William Rudman, Randall Balestriero, Carsten Eickhoff

entry.summary: Mol-JEPA learns molecular world models via modality masking across molecular structures, cellular phenotypes, binding affinities, ADMET profiles, and quantum chemistry simulations, avoiding chemically invalid augmentations. It delivers strong benchmark performance while incorporating biochemical context into representations.

entry.title: AI Surrogate Modeling for Real-Time Tokamak Equilibrium Prediction: Benchmarking Neural Architectures and Validation on EXL-50U

author.name: Guoyang Shi, Zitong Zhang, Siqi Ding, Jianguo Chen, Yapeng Zhang, Jiayi Zhi, Hanyue Zhao, Tianyuan Liu

entry.summary: This work builds AI surrogate models for real-time tokamak plasma equilibrium prediction, benchmarking MLP, CNN, FNO, Transformer, and KAN architectures on 110,000 Grad-Shafranov solver samples with device-level validation on the EXL-50U tokamak. Surrogates reach 10^-3 to 10^-2 relative error with real-time inference efficiency.

entry.title: Subzero matrix completion for sparse data analysis: large-scale learning of latent low-rank structure

author.name: Lawrence K. Saul, Ningyuan Huang, Dennis Bollweg, Jeff Soules, Diana C. Halikias

entry.summary: This paper studies when a sparse nonnegative matrix can be recovered from a much lower-rank real matrix by zeroing negatives, revealing a mathematical link between sparsity and rank. It introduces a stochastic block-based alternating least-squares algorithm that avoids materializing the full dense product matrix. This enables latent low-rank analysis at scales previously impractical.

entry.title: The Laws of Context Allocation: Causal Measurement and Closed-Loop Orchestration in Generative Search

author.name: Peiyang Liu, Xi Wang, Di Liang, Wei Ye

entry.summary: Identifies a diagnostic illusion where standard relevance proxies fail on hard negatives in RAG, replacing them with a causal leave-one-out probe that isolates true generative reliance. Uses this probe to prove that monolithic context widening is suboptimal and derive closed-loop context budget allocation strategies.

entry.title: GTA-RAG: Graph-Trajectory-Augmented Reinforcement Learning for Multi-Turn Retrieval-Augmented Reasoning

author.name: Jun Chen, Yongchao Liu, Pengyu Qiu, Jiajun Zheng, Juelu Zhang, Yujie Zeng, Qin Zhang, Ziyue Qiao, Xiao Luo

entry.summary: Introduces GTA-RAG, a reinforcement learning framework for multi-turn retrieval-augmented reasoning that samples connected document paths from an entity-document graph to synthesize multi-hop training data with denser rewards than final-answer-only supervision. Addresses sparse-reward limitations of agentic RAG training.

entry.title: Interpretable AI with Local Distillation

author.name: Erin Craig, Yiling Huang, Snigdha Panigrahi

entry.summary: Proposes local distillation, where a black-box teacher defines neighborhoods and guides a regularized linear student fit at each query point, yielding locally accurate yet inherently interpretable models for tabular foundation models and gradient-boosted ensembles in high-stakes decisions.

entry.title: Inertial Manifold Neural Operator for Dissipative Time-Dependent Partial Differential Equations

author.name: Xiaoyang Xie, Clarence W. Rowley

entry.summary: Introduces the Inertial Manifold Neural Operator (IMNO), explicitly exploiting the low-dimensional effective dynamics of dissipative PDEs for better interpretability, accuracy, and long-horizon stability than FNO-style operators, plus a shift-equivariant variant for equivariant systems.

entry.title: Claim-Level Confidence Calibration for Reliable Decision Making with Large Language Models

author.name: Toghrul Abbasli, Kentaroh Toyoda, Yuan Wang, Li Chen

entry.summary: Decomposes LLM responses into atomic verifiable claims and assigns each a calibrated confidence using inference-time consistency and self-verification signals, operating in closed-box settings without logit access. Positions claim-level calibration as an actionable decision signal for high-stakes use.

entry.title: GeoWAM: Visual Geometry World Action Models for Autonomous Driving

author.name: Yiren Lu, Xin Ye, Jiaming Liu, Jin Yao, Yi-chung Chen, Liam Merino, Dhruva Dixith Kurra, Min Cai, Tom Lampo, Yu Yin, Danhua Guo, Burhan Yaman

entry.summary: GeoWAM argues point-cloud geometry is a more natural state space than pixels for autonomous-driving world action models, jointly modeling scene evolution and ego actions in geometry space to disentangle dynamics from appearance. Challenges pixel-space WAM orthodoxy.

entry.title: Social Graph Mamba: Forecasting Pedestrian Movements Based on Social Context

author.name: Hong-Son Nguyen, Yen-Chen Liu

entry.summary: Social Graph Mamba replaces quadratic-complexity attention in pedestrian trajectory forecasting with selective state space models operating on dynamically constructed social interaction graphs, explicitly modeling group structures. Targets scalable crowd forecasting for autonomous navigation.

entry.title: Physics Filtering Favors the Generalization of Robot Learning

author.name: Jindou Jia, Shixuan Han, Meng Wang, Gen Li, Zihan Yang, Sicheng Zhou, Kexin Guo, Jianfei Yang, Xiang Yu, Wei Wang, Lei Guo

entry.summary: Safety-critical bilateral teleoperation framework for omnidirectional aerial manipulators using force-sensorless haptic feedback derived hierarchically, with a control-barrier-function safety filter accounting for interaction-induced tracking errors and thrust limits during free flight.

entry.title: What just happened? Pragmatism and Pessimization

author.name: Richard_Ngo

entry.summary: Richard Ngo chronicles how pragmatic alignment research advanced frontier capabilities over the past decade, eroding the alignment-versus-capabilities distinction, tracing the paradigm across the three leading AGI labs and citing outside observers.

entry.title: K-Bench: measuring model performance on real scientific agent requests

author.name: Aubrey Brueckner, Darshil Patel, Yuhuan He, Timothy Kassis

entry.summary: K-Bench 01 evaluates scientific AI agents on 1,602 end-to-end runs built from live first-turn user requests on K-Dense Web, scored blindly by three judges on an eight-dimension rubric including whether a domain scientist would accept the output. No frontier model clears the accept-with-minor-edits anchor.

entry.title: Think with Structured Grounding: Perceptual Reinforcement Learning for Chart and Visual-Tabular Understanding

author.name: Changjiang Jiang, Qiannian Zhao, Lei Xin, Jinxiang Xie, Preslav Nakov, Zhuohan Xie

entry.summary: TwSG internalizes fine-grained perception for chart and visual-table understanding via perceptual reinforcement learning with structured grounding, removing reliance on slow external tools. It distills tool-use benefits into the model to close the spatial-structural gap in text-dense visuals.

entry.title: CausalCache: Conditional High-Fidelity Restoration for Long-Horizon GUI Agents

author.name: Jiaxuan Luo, Zhanfeng Liao, Jiayao Teng, Yuan Wang, Haojian Huang

entry.summary: CausalCache formulates GUI-agent history management as conditional fidelity restoration under a fixed visual-context budget, promoting past events from summary-only to summary-plus-image based on conditional marginal utility rather than recency. A history-gated KV adapter modifies only restored tokens and is bypassed otherwise.

entry.title: Your AI, On a Dial: Controlling Investment Bias in LLMs with a Single Neuron

author.name: Sahong Park, Suhwan Park, Hoyoung Lee, Gakyung Kwon, Wonbin Ahn, Jaewon Choi, Alejandro Lopez-Lira, Yoon Kim, Chanyeol Choi, Hyeongwoo Kong, Yongjae Lee

entry.summary: This paper demonstrates a single-neuron inference-time intervention acting as an investment-bias dial that continuously calibrates an LLM overall buy/sell tendency across five open-weight models, without prompt changes or weight updates, producing monotonic stance shifts.

entry.title: What Process Evaluation of Coding Agents Actually Measures: Action, Task, and Step Are Three Different Levels

author.name: Jiawei He, Mengyu Shi, Jie jia, Xikai Yang, Dong Sun

entry.summary: This paper separates action prediction, task uncertainty, and step attribution as three distinct levels of process evaluation for coding agents, instantiating step-level causal attribution via SCAE, a replay-based estimator derived from a structural causal model of agent execution.

entry.title: Meta-Ctrl: Guaranteed Plan Generation by Decoupling Syntactic and Semantic Constraints

author.name: Gwen Yidou-Weng, Edward Sun, Tianyi Ma, Metin Alp Dogan, Benjie Wang, Allen Peng, Guy Van den Broeck, Yuchen Cui

entry.summary: Meta-Ctrl guarantees syntactic and semantic constraints in LLM robot plan generation via meta-tokens enforcing syntax at token level and semantics at action level, with exact factorization cutting constrained-decoding memory. It preserves base LM plan quality unlike symbolic planners that discard commonsense.

entry.title: BLADE: Bilevel Low-rank Augmented-Lagrangian Erasure for LLM Unlearning

author.name: Md Toufikuzzaman, Ahmad Mousavi, Dongwon Lee

entry.summary: BLADE is a constrained bilevel LLM unlearning framework combining clamped-entropy forget losses, asymmetric augmented Lagrangians that ratchet retain protection, and LoRA-confined bilevel repair of retain damage. It dominates baselines across three unlearning benchmarks with improved robustness under scaling and repeated application.

entry.title: Molecular LLM Agents: From Architectural Design to Scientific Autonomy

author.name: Jiatong Li, Wengyu Zhang, Weida Wang, Yuxuan Ren, Wei Liu, Chenyang Mao, Yuqiang Li, Yatao Bian, Changmeng Zheng, Xiaoyong Wei, Qing Li

entry.summary: This survey/framework paper organizes molecular LLM agent design across perception of chemical objects (strings, graphs, 3D conformations, spectra), tool grounding, and computational or wet-lab feedback loops. It lays out an architectural roadmap toward scientific autonomy in molecular science.

entry.title: DF-MoE: Generalizable Deepfake Detection via Multimodal Sparse Mixture-of-Experts

author.name: Vlad Hondru, Florinel Alin Croitoru, Iuliana Georgescu, A. Sophia Koepke, Radu Tudor Ionescu

entry.summary: DF-MoE builds audio-visual deepfake detection on a sparse Mixture-of-Experts backbone fusing diverse pre-trained cues (mouth movements, facial expressions, gaze, heart rate, audio emotion), hypothesizing feature diversity reduces overfitting to specific generation methods. Cross-domain experiments on five benchmarks support improved generalization.

entry.title: Beyond Sparse Weights: When Is Attention Compressible?

author.name: Chiwun Yang, Xiaoyu Li

entry.summary: This analysis separates competing justifications for KV-cache compression, showing global attention-score gaps rather than threshold counts determine tokens needed for target mass, and that omitted-value cancellation means preserving attention output may not preserve task performance. It motivates CertKV, a training-free compressor reserving tail-summary slots allocated by value dispersion, ranking top-two under matched budgets.

entry.title: Thinking at the Right Size: Amortized Distillation Across Post-Trained LLMs

author.name: Yan Zhou, Sara Kangaslahti, Jonathan Geuter, Nihal V. Nayak, Marco Fumero, Francesco Locatello, David Alvarez-Melis

entry.summary: ADAPT extends boomerang distillation so that intermediate-size models can be constructed across multiple post-trained variants (instruction-tuned, reasoning-tuned, chat) without independent training of each size-variant pair. This reduces the cost of maintaining full LLM model families.

entry.title: RiskWorld: Object-Centric Latent World Modeling for Autonomous Driving Risk Identification

author.name: Jingzheng Li, Yufei Ge, Qianren Mao, Zhijun Chen, Bing Li, Xingyu Peng, Baochang Zhang, Xianglong Liu

entry.summary: RiskWorld is an object-centric latent world model for autonomous driving risk identification that rolls relation-aware object states forward with RSSM-style dynamics to localize which observed object will become safety-critical, rather than predicting scene-level accidents or relying on geometric checks.

entry.title: One Inverse Step is a Convex Program: Bayes-Limit Calibration of Diffusion Inversion

author.name: Gordei Verbii

entry.summary: Shows one implicit DDIM inversion step is the stationarity condition of an explicit potential that is strongly convex at the Bayes limit with modulus exactly e^-h_t, yielding hypothesis-free certificates of model error, unique solutions, and schedule-constant contraction bounds throughout stable sampling regimes.

entry.title: SelFusion: Self-distillation for Diffusion Language Models

author.name: Hyeongsoo Lim, Jinyoung Kim, Eunseo Seo, Minho Jang, Jiwon Yoon

entry.summary: Finds that naive knowledge distillation barely helps or even degrades diffusion language models, and proposes SelFusion, a teacher-free self-distillation scheme using two forward passes at different masking levels where the easy mode supervises the hard mode, improving generation quality.

entry.title: DefaultShift: Auditing Semantic Default Shift in Accelerated Text-to-Image Models

author.name: Xuanhua Yin, Chuanzhi Xu, Shunqi Mao, Wei Guo, Weidong Cai

entry.summary: DefaultShift introduces a paired audit showing that few-step accelerated text-to-image models silently shift distributions over unspecified attributes, termed semantic default shift, even when individual outputs look plausible. The audit labels repeated samples with closed vocabularies, measures probability-mass movement, and separates interpretable ranking from confirmatory cross-fit inference across 14 reference-replacement pairs.

entry.title: When Does Visual Generation Help Visual Understanding in Unified Multimodal Models?

author.name: Yubo Zhu, Zhehan Kan, Jingyi Yang, Miaolin Chen, Jinbo Xing, Kai Zhu, Zijian Wang, Sheng Zhong, Wei Tong

entry.summary: VGAU-Diag is a fine-grained evaluation framework asking when visual generation helps understanding in unified multimodal models, stratifying samples by difficulty and using Oracle-Assisted Reference Protocols to disentangle confounds. Findings show generated visual aids help easier instances but become unreliable as reasoning complexity increases, with oracle diagnosis revealing main bottleneck sources.

entry.title: Privileged Critic Training Enables Sensor-Free Thruster Fault Adaptation in End-to-End RL

author.name: Ricard Marsal I Castan, Miguel A. Olivares-M\'endez

entry.summary: Shows privileged critic training suffices for sensor-free thruster fault adaptation: giving the PPO value function true degradation states during training shapes an actor that compensates for continuously degrading, dead, or stuck-open thrusters at deployment without dedicated fault sensors (RAFT).

entry.title: LitReview Arena: Evaluating Literature Review Agents with Battle-Style Peer Review Platform

author.name: Ruotong Zhao, Zhiyu Chen, Xurui Liu, Haidong Xue, Dong Liang, Jigao Fu, Wu YanBiao, Yuanyi Zhen, Fengli Xu, Yong Li

entry.summary: LitReview Arena is a battle-style evaluation platform where domain experts compare anonymized literature-review drafts from AI systems across five criteria, yielding about 3k expert judgments. Findings show even the strongest current systems win only around 23% of head-to-head comparisons against presumably human-quality references.

entry.title: HERO: Human-profile Enhanced Retrieval Optimization Framework for Long-term Agent Memory

author.name: Yuanhua Lin, Yile Li, Zhiyuan Zhao, Jing Shang, Jian Sun

entry.summary: HERO converts dialogue history into a traceable heterogeneous memory graph that preserves raw dialogue text as evidence, avoiding information loss from compression and semantic drift from rewriting in long-term agent memory. It improves personalized response quality over compression-based baselines.

entry.title: Small Reasoning Models are Instruction Followers in Function Calling

author.name: Yalda Taheri, Mohammad Hassan Heydari, Erfan Naaman, Afsaneh Fatemi

entry.summary: This work shows LLMs achieve better function-calling accuracy in instruction-following contexts than native tool-calling contexts, and proposes Instruction-Followed Function Calling which delegates calling logic to a smaller dedicated model. The decoupled approach consistently outperforms native function calling.

entry.title: Does Rank Still Matter? Position Bias When AI Agents Shop on Our Behalf

author.name: Davood Wadi, Yu Ma

entry.summary: Randomizing hotel listing order across 5,000 AI shopping-agent sessions and comparing four LLMs against human field data, this study finds agents search more deeply than humans and position effects weaken and become non-monotonic, with mid-page listings least inspected. Heterogeneity across models tracks which reach the choice stage.

entry.title: FinixDoc: Rethinking Financial Document Parsing Beyond Saturated Benchmarks

author.name: Hang Wang, Jin Zhang, Guoliang Xu, Pengyue Lu, Yao Li, Zijiao Zhang, Tianyu Huang, Weiqi Xiong, Yulong Wang, Chuqiao Lu, Wenkang Huang, Kai Yang, Yadong Li, Hui Li, Xingzhong Xu, Xiao Xu

entry.summary: FinixDoc presents an end-to-end agentic parsing system for financial documents with FinixDoc-VL, a 4B vision-language model built on Qwen3-VL-4B, trained with homoglyph-aware contrastive learning and multi-stage RL with composite rewards. A capability matrix along visual-quality and document-scale axes exposes benchmark-to-deployment gaps.

entry.title: MobilePA-Bench: Benchmarking Mobile Planner Agents on Complex Real-World Tasks

author.name: Yi Zhu, Xiongwei Wu, Qiyi Wang, Tingyu Qu, Jiajun Liu, Sihan Cao, Long Chen, Weigao Sun, Feida Zhu, Yiran Zhong, Steven Hoi

entry.summary: MobilePA-Bench is an interactive, stateful, tool-centric benchmark for mobile planner agents running in an executable sandbox, closing the gap between GUI-centric screen-manipulation tests and static offline function-calling benchmarks.

entry.title: ReWorld: An Interactive World Model with Long-Horizon Memory

author.name: Zhifei Chen, Luozhou Wang, Guibao Shen, Dongyu Yan, Shuai Yang, Tianshuo Xu, Yihua Du, Wei Wang, Tianyi Gui, Lianghua Huang, Yingcong Chen

entry.summary: ReWorld is an interactive video world model supporting user action control, long-horizon memory, and real-time streaming. Mixed per-head attention windows plus random head routing decouple short control horizons from unbounded memory, while a bounded KV cache backed by a pose-indexed landmark bank keeps inference costs fixed. Addresses the structural tension between control and memory in world models.

entry.title: Lexical Perturbations Disrupt LLM Reasoning: An Empirical Study of Attention Diversion

author.name: Jiaqian Zhu, Yang Zhang, Junhua Ding, Xiaowei Yu

entry.summary: This empirical study shows character-level lexical corruption substantially degrades LLM reasoning via Attention Diversion, where fragmented subword tokens attract disproportionate attention mass in middle and final transformer layers. Filler insertion has little effect, isolating fragmentation as the causal factor.

entry.title: Evaluating Inference-Time Defenses Against Package Hallucination in LLM-Generated Code

author.name: Alberick Euraste Djire, Iyiola E. Olatunji, Melissa Tessa, Earl T. Barr, Jacques Klein, Tegawend\'e F. Bissyand\'e

entry.summary: This study shows prior package-hallucination evaluations systematically inflate rates by misclassifying standard-library modules (up to 9.4 points for Python), then evaluates seven inference-time defenses including guided decoding variants, Self-Refine, and RAG against supply-chain attacks.

entry.title: Shaping the Evolutionary Dynamics of Robot Morphology via Adaptive Control Learning

author.name: Junru Song, Yang Yang, Yaqing Xu, Ying Wen, Wei Peng, Guozhen Li, Wei'en Zhou, Wen Yao

entry.summary: This paper studies how control learning reciprocally shapes morphological evolution in robot co-design, formalizing convergence speed as morphological intelligence and performance ceiling as true potential. It shows these two contributions decouple into orthogonal dimensions, giving a holistic brain-body interplay account.

entry.title: NetConfArena: An Executable Benchmark for LLM Agents in Closed-Loop Network Configuration

author.name: Chang Liu, Xiaohui Xie, Xinyi Chen, Yong Cui

entry.summary: NetConfArena evaluates LLM agents on closed-loop network configuration inside emulated multi-device networks, where correctness requires protocol and topology reasoning rather than static command generation. It provides a realistic risk-free testbed exposing failure patterns of configuration agents.

entry.title: Sigmoid Attention as a Better Substrate for Learned KV Cache Eviction

author.name: Isaac (Rucheng), Li

entry.summary: Using controlled GPT-2-scale experiments, this paper finds that although sigmoid attention underperforms softmax for dense language modeling, sigmoid-gated models support learned hard KV-cache eviction with negligible perplexity change under matched live-cache protocols. Attention substrate thus changes the useful operating points for cache eviction.

entry.title: Predicting Early Functional Decline from Longitudinal Laboratory and Vital Sign Trajectories: A Large-Scale Study Using the All of Us Research Program

author.name: Rashmita Kudamala, Aravind V. Kuruvikkattil, Lalitha Pranathi Pulavarthy, Saptarshi Purkayastha

entry.summary: Using All of Us program data (N=297,861), this study shows trajectory features (slope, variability, delta) of twelve routine biomarkers over a three-year window predict early functional decline better than static summaries (AUROC 0.797 vs 0.755), confirmed in matched analyses. Routine labs already recorded could identify pre-clinical mobility decline earlier.

entry.title: Width-Independent Compressibility of Deep Neural Networks

author.name: Hong-Yi Wang, Mingze Wang, Liu Ziyin

entry.summary: The paper proves a uniform compressibility theorem for deep MLPs: a narrow network of width independent of teacher width, scaling as O((log(1/eps))^(d_in)), approximately represents the same function as a wide trained network. A novel derivative-matching construction exploiting low effective input dimension underpins the result. This formalizes why trained networks compress so aggressively.

entry.title: CatchBench: When Can an Agent Failure Be Caught?

author.name: Yue Zhao

entry.summary: CatchBench evaluates when agent failures can be caught across three information states: pre-run configuration, live trace prefixes, and finished traces. It scores 72 entrants including eleven LLM judges under seven task contracts with per-contract metrics.

entry.title: Beyond Point Predictions: Uncertainty-Aware Satellite Poverty Mapping for Public Policy

author.name: Markus B. Pettersson, James Bailie, Mohammad Kakooei, Eagon Meng, Adel Daoud

entry.summary: Develops uncertainty-aware satellite poverty mapping for Africa using simultaneous quantile regression and a novel conformal prediction variant on a spatiotemporal transformer over Landsat and nighttime-light sequences. Produces prediction intervals suitable for public-policy decision-making.

entry.title: ProxyFormer: A Dual-Stream Proxy Architecture for Ultra-Long Context and High-Resolution Generation

author.name: Zhongpan Tang

entry.summary: ProxyFormer proposes a dual-stream proxy-token architecture compressing fine-grained local features bottom-up into proxy states where global attention occurs, then decompressing top-down, with a persistent local stream preserving detail across layers. Targets ultra-long-context LMs and high-resolution generation while avoiding quadratic KV cache growth.

entry.title: Sparse Additive Off-Policy Evaluation for Reinforcement Learning with Potentially Limited Number of Trajectories

author.name: Tuoyi Zhao, Chengchun Shi, Zhengling Qi, Lan Wang

entry.summary: Develops off-policy evaluation for infinite-horizon RL using sparse additive Q-function models, deriving high-probability finite-sample value bounds that depend only logarithmically on ambient dimension and remain valid when either trajectories or horizon are limited. Supports interpretable policy evaluation in large state spaces.

entry.title: ADDA: a Modular Framework for Representing, Simulating and Assimilating Dynamics with End-to-end Differentiability

author.name: Anthony Frion, Vien Minh Nguyen-Thanh, Ali Can Bekar, Pauleo R. Nimtz, Vadim Zinchenko, David S. Greenberg

entry.summary: Introduces ADDA, a modular end-to-end differentiable framework unifying simulation, variational assimilation, ensemble methods, and learning-based approaches for geoscience data assimilation, addressing code incompatibility and inflexible discretization that block fair algorithm comparisons.

entry.title: Can LLMs Truly Forget? Revealing Unlearning Gaps Through Adversarial Evaluation

author.name: Ayush Gupta, Hima Varshini Surisetty, Sreevidya Bollineni, Varad Ingale, Tuhina Tripathi, Abhishek Lalwani, Somya Chatterjee, Sadid Hasan

entry.summary: Evaluates prompt-based and fine-tuning-based unlearning on TOFU with Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct, then adversarially probes methods that pass standard metrics, introducing an Attack Success Rate metric showing apparently forgotten information remains recoverable through strategic prompting.

entry.title: Beyond Factual Knowledge: Benchmarking and Learning Step-Level Procedural Rule Reasoning in Large Language Models

author.name: Bohan Yu, Pengfei Cao, Chen Han, Chenxi Zhou, Zhiheng Zhang, Zhiyang Xie, Wenhao Teng, Xiangwen Liao, Jun Zhao, Kang Liu

entry.summary: Introduces RuleWorld, a large-scale benchmark treating externally provided rules as globally reusable abstract units across single-rule, parallel, and multi-hop scenarios, plus DynaRule, which injects rules into the KV cache and learns step-wise internal retrieval via stacked step-level attention training.

entry.title: Accelerating Diffusion Language Models via Structured Suffix Modeling

author.name: Zifeng Cheng, Keda Li, Zhiwei Jiang, Cong Wang, Fei Shen, Qing Gu

entry.summary: Proposes structured suffix modeling for diffusion language model inference, dividing the suffix into local, middle, and tail regions treated heterogeneously instead of a uniform local window, addressing both compute overhead and re-initialization pathologies of prior acceleration methods.

entry.title: MedReaMM: Evaluating Large Multimodal Models on Expert-Level Clinical Diagnostic Synthesis

author.name: Lai Wei, Yuchao Chen, Zhenbiao Cao, Xiaojin Zhang, Zhongyu Wei, Bangting Wang, Wei Chen, Xiang Bai

entry.summary: MedReaMM is a benchmark evaluating large multimodal models on expert-level clinical diagnostic synthesis, requiring integration of detailed patient histories with multiple medical images into accurate differential diagnoses under a complete-information paradigm, constructed from case reports to fill gaps left by textual reasoning or isolated VQA benchmarks.

entry.title: IntentQA: Intent Question Answering in Videos by Cognitive Context Reasoning

author.name: Jiapeng Li, Ping Wei, Wenjuan Han, Song-Chun Zhu, Lifeng Fan

entry.summary: IntentQA introduces intent question answering in videos with a large-scale VideoQA dataset, five LLM-generated contrast sets, a Contrast Performance Decline robustness metric, and the X-CaVIR explainable cognitive-context reasoning model. Targets the dark matter of social intelligence beyond visual fact recognition.

entry.title: Evaluating Human and LLM-Generated Thematic Analysis in HRI for Vulnerable Populations: A Comparative and Ethical Analysis

author.name: Alva Markelius, Fethiye Irmak Dogan, Julie Bailey, Hatice Gunes

entry.summary: Comparatively evaluates human versus LLM-generated thematic analysis in HRI studies involving vulnerable populations, measuring objective and semantic agreement between theme sets. Examines whether divergences reflect systematic interpretive patterns with ethical significance.

entry.title: Free-Energy-Gated Plasticity for Real-Time Online Motor Learning in Physical Human--Robot Interaction

author.name: Hiroki Sawada, Jun Tani

entry.summary: Extends PV-RNN predictive coding networks with Free-Energy-Gated Plasticity regulating effective learning rates by variational free energy, enabling fully online acquisition of motor patterns during physical human-robot interaction without offline pretraining, replay, or task boundaries.

entry.title: From Mastery Profile to Simulated Response: Stochastic Student Knowledge Graphs (SSKG) for Faithful LLM Student Simulation

author.name: Yuan An, Emily Wang, Benjamin Wang, Ruhma Hashmi

entry.summary: The paper demonstrates that prompt-based LLM student simulation fails because models answer according to built-in capability regardless of instructed mastery level (96.8-100% accuracy even for low-mastery personas on SAT Algebra items), and proposes Stochastic Student Knowledge Graphs to condition response generation on explicit mastery structure.

entry.title: Query-Driven Multimodal Information Extraction from Long Documents

author.name: Yikai Gao, Ding Xia, Xi Yang

entry.summary: The paper introduces query-driven joint image-text extraction from long multimodal documents, requiring models to output both attribute values and corresponding image bounding boxes. It contributes ITJoint, claimed to be the first high-quality dataset for this task, plus a two-level taxonomy of query and instance challenges.

entry.title: Scaling Curriculum Learning For Autonomous Driving

author.name: Cevahir Koprulu, David Paz, Feng Tao, Yuliang Guo, Xinyu Huang, Ufuk Topcu, Liu Ren

entry.summary: CL4AD integrates curriculum learning into batched autonomous driving simulators by framing scenario selection as a bandit-like prioritization problem, replacing uniform domain randomization that wastes interactions on low-value cases. It improves sample efficiency for large-scale RL training.

entry.title: The Retriever Should Remember: Experience-Amortized Reranking for Long-Term Agent Memory

author.name: Qi Feng, Chris Ding, Jicong Fan

entry.summary: EARM treats previously acquired LLM relevance scores as reusable retrieval experience, storing sparse query-memory scores in an online matrix and learning shared structure to amortize reranking costs for long-term agent memory instead of rescoring candidates statelessly each time.

entry.title: Concepts for Securing Agentic AI Coding and the Terok Environment

author.name: Ji\v{r}\'i Vysko\v{c}il, Franz P\"oschel, Andreas Kn\"upfer

entry.summary: This paper lays out security concepts for agentic AI coding, arguing the agentic approach introduced severe new IT-security risks beyond conventional AI-assisted coding, and presents the Terok environment to study and mitigate them.

entry.title: Bulbul: A Dataset for Dialectal Arabic Speech Recognition

author.name: Ahmed Ashraf, Aisha Alansari, Fadel Al Abbas, Nada Almarwani, Samah Aloufi, Saad Ezzini, Maged S. Al-Shaibani, Doaa Dalaq, AbdelRahim A. Elmadany, Muhammad Abdul-Mageed, Mohamed Mehdi Trigui, Dania Refai, Layan Refai, Mohamed Akrout, Mustafa Jarrar, Wasfi G. Al-Khatib, Alaa Dalaq, Darin El-Nakla, Samir Abdaljalil, Abdulrahman Al-Fakih, Nour El Imane Zeghib, Moussa Redah, Salmane Chafik, Mohamed El-Attar, Rima Grati, Sarah Kohail, Malak Alkhorasani, Khadijah Al Safwan, Ismail M. Mudhaffar, Ali Altam, Ahmed Al-Shaikh, Adnan Saeed, Hamzah Luqman

entry.summary: BULBUL is a multi-dialect Arabic ASR dataset covering 275 speakers across 11 Arab countries with structured dialect and sub-dialect coverage plus accent-aware MSA recordings. Recordings passed two-level human verification, enabling dialect-robust speech recognition benchmarks.

entry.title: TRACE: A Self-Evolving Skill Bank for Consistent, Limit-Aware LLM Agents

author.name: Wenhao Wu, Menghao Zhang, Xin Wang, Zhi Wang, Kun Shao, Jian Luan

entry.summary: TRACE builds a self-evolving skill bank via trajectory-contrastive evolution to close the gap between Pass@3 and Pass^k consistency exposed by CAR-bench for in-car assistant agents, adding limit-awareness for unfulfillable requests. Even frontier models show substantial consistency gaps in policy-adhering multi-turn tool use.

entry.title: DeMixPert: Decomposed Response Modeling with Gaussian Mixtures for OOD Single-Cell Perturbation Prediction

author.name: Jiawen Liu, Xuechenxiao Cao, Yutong Li, Bing Liu, Jiaming Liang, Tinghe Zhang, Xiaoqi Sheng, Hongmin Cai

entry.summary: DeMixPert predicts transcriptome-wide responses to unseen genetic perturbations by decomposing perturbation-induced changes into basal-state-dependent systematic shifts and stochastic population variation modeled with Gaussian mixtures. This prevents dominant shared patterns from masking weaker perturbation-specific signals in out-of-distribution settings.

entry.title: How Much Regularization Survives Averaging? Update Masking in Federated Learning

author.name: Wenhao Yan, Fu Kuroda, Yucheng Jin, Zhenke Chen

entry.summary: This theory paper analyzes when update masking regularization survives federated averaging, proving per-client masks lose sharpness penalties by exactly the cohort size while shared masks restore it by a factor tied to cohort gradient diversity. It explains why noise-based flat-minima regularization had never transferred to FL and quantifies the fix.

entry.title: Posterior Information Dynamics of Diffusion Models for Linear Inverse Problems

author.name: Xiangming Meng

entry.summary: This paper analyzes diffusion-model priors for linear inverse problems via the smoothed likelihood force—the difference between posterior and prior scores at each noise level. It derives I-MMSE identities linking information gain to denoising-error reduction and characterizes quadratic decay of force energy. This gives a principled account of when measurement information enters reverse denoising.

entry.title: Arbitrage-Aware Multi-Step Forecasting of Implied Volatility Surfaces: Modelling Surface Trajectories Using Latent Diffusion

author.name: Dominik Manuel Buchegger, Lukas Gonon

entry.summary: Proposes a conditional latent diffusion framework generating joint 30-step trajectories of implied volatility surfaces and underlying returns, using an arbitrage-aware autoencoder for admissible surface representations. Evaluated on SPX surfaces, it beats persistence benchmarks while producing realistic probabilistic scenarios.

entry.title: Mirror descent algorithms with logarithmic barriers

author.name: Alberto De Marchi, Yura Malitsky, Adrien B. Taylor

entry.summary: Derives tight O(log k/k) convergence guarantees for mirror descent and proximal mirror descent with logarithmic barrier distance-generating functions, including a new technique for handling Bregman divergence blow-up at boundary solutions and resolving a gap in relative smoothness theory.

entry.title: Iteration Without Elaboration: A Simple ReAct Architecture Suffices for Text-to-SQL Generation

author.name: Jian Lu, Haiwei Yu, Raymond M Xiong, Anru Zhang, Danyang Zhuo

entry.summary: ReAct-SQL shows a simple zero-shot ReAct-style loop with iterative reasoning over a constrained 15-operation typed DSL matches elaborate text-to-SQL pipelines built from schema-linking, retrieval, and multi-stage refinement, achieving competitive results on corrected BIRD mini-dev and EHR-SQL with far less latency and engineering overhead.

entry.title: BehaviorWorldGen: Closing the Loop between Action Models and World Simulators via Controllable Behavior-Aware Structured World Generation

author.name: Jiaqi Wang, Zhuo Zhang, Haining Guan, Tingguang Zhou, Haowen Cui, Zhongyang Zhu, Yulong Zheng, ChuanYe Wang, Xuefeng Chen, Zhen Yang, Tianchen Deng, Feiyang Tan, Hangning Zhou, Bo Dai, Lixia Shen, Xiwu Chen, Xiyang Wang, Jiajun Zhu

entry.summary: BehaviorWorldGen closes the self-improvement loop between driving action models and world simulators via BehaviorFlow, a meta-action-conditioned traffic-flow model injecting interpretable behavior controls so generated futures are interactionally plausible and distributionally balanced. Targets the key bottleneck in driving self-play data engines.

entry.title: OptiSight: Bridging Semantic Reasoning and Geometric Control for Embodied Navigation

author.name: Alperen Avan, Jordi Sanchez-Riera

entry.summary: OptiSight combines VLM semantic reasoning with deterministic visual servoing via a finite-state chain-of-thought architecture for indoor navigation, querying the VLM only at key decision points. Grounded-SAM localization plus camera projection geometry enables zero-shot navigation in Habitat without dense mapping.

entry.title: Force/Torque-Based Kinematic Adaptation for Robotic Manipulation Tasks

author.name: Carl Glen Henshaw (US Naval Research Laboratory)

entry.summary: Develops a provably stable adaptive law that estimates unknown tool kinematics online using only joint angles and a wrist force/torque sensor, handling contact-mode changes in multi-fingered grasping. Eliminates need for exteroceptive tip measurement in contact-rich manipulation.

entry.title: Beyond Instance Slots: Semantically Rich World Models for Physical Interaction Planning

author.name: Juntao Cheng, Jingkai Wang, Yijun Shen, Xiansheng Chen, Zhiwei Yu

entry.summary: SR-WM is a task-conditioned world model structured around five functional roles (gripper, target, goal, relation, phase) so entity representations capture what role each object plays, not just what is present, improving planning-oriented physical interaction prediction.

entry.title: Guided Riemannian Optimization (GuRO): Bridging Model Predictive Control and Decision Transformers

author.name: Hossein Abdi, Satya Prakash Dash, Mingfei Sun

entry.summary: GuRO bridges MPC and Decision Transformers via guided Riemannian optimization addressing the non-convex loss landscapes of sequence-model decision-making, aiming to combine MPC sample efficiency and interpretability with RL-style learned policies.

entry.title: Robust Lightweight Deep Learning Models for Oral Cancer Screening

author.name: Siddhant Bharadwaj, Aakash Shedsale, Tejashree Subramanya, Mohd. Azfar, Praveen Birur, Debnath Pal, Shankararama Sharma, Anupama Shetty, Rajesh Sundaresan

entry.summary: The authors optimize lightweight deep learning models for smartphone-based oral cancer screening using a decade-long multi-centre dataset of about 30k images, comparing CNN, transformer, and hybrid architectures under class imbalance and edge-device constraints typical of low-to-middle-income settings.

entry.title: Beyond Success and Failure: Length-Aware Contrastive Learning for GUI Agents

author.name: Chengyang Gu, Le Zhang, Jingbo Zhou, Yize Chen, Yu Shi, Siqi Bao, Zheng-Fan Wu, Hua Wu, Hui Xiong

entry.summary: The paper introduces length-aware contrastive objectives for GUI agent training, moving beyond outcome-level supervision in contrastive RLVR formulations of GRPO to capture fine-grained step quality and address reward-gradient misalignment in MLLM-based GUI automation.

entry.title: Where Cognition Lives: Dissecting Emergent from Computed Function in a Minimal Complete Cognitive Architecture

author.name: Francisco M. Arrabal-Campos, Francisco G. Montoya, Alfredo Alcayde, Ignacio Fern\'andez

entry.summary: This paper dissects a minimal complete cognitive architecture with adaptive halting, homeostatic control, and a value module, asking which functions emerge from gradient descent versus must be computed explicitly. It finds stopping behavior appears emergent but that appearance is partly instrumentation, with ex-ante value signals providing most of the payoff.

entry.title: ClawProBench: Trace-Aware Evaluation of AI Agents with Runtime Coverage and Frozen Workplace-Style Holdouts

author.name: YuanHang Xiao

entry.summary: ClawProBench is a trace-aware agent benchmark instantiated on OpenClaw with live workspace tools, defining a 102-scenario full profile and a frozen 68-scenario holdout with closed-world output contracts. It evaluates declared model-plus-runtime configurations rather than final answers alone.

entry.title: CDEG: Learning Decision-Critical Evidence for Long-Horizon Diagnostic Agents

author.name: Xiwei Dai, Zijie Meng, Zhiting Fan, Yixuan Tang, Ziru Niu, Zuozhu Liu

entry.summary: CDEG learns decision-critical evidence for long-horizon diagnostic agents, validating which acquired evidence actually drives diagnostic decisions rather than blindly reusing noisy historical trajectories or distilled memories.

entry.title: From Generation to Simulation: How Far Are World Models from Being True Simulators?

author.name: Tong Wang, Huan Deng, Mucheng Yang, Yang He, Xiaohui Kuang, Gang Zhao

entry.summary: This survey assesses how far generative world models are from true simulators using eight simulator capabilities as an external yardstick, tracing latent-dynamics, video-generation, and joint-embedding-prediction routes across 200 representative works from 2018 onward.

entry.title: Semantic Reasoning Denoising: Correcting Language Model Reasoning with Semantic Operators

author.name: Yujiao Yang

entry.summary: SRD represents semantic noise in LLM reasoning traces as executable error operators describing error type, location, and corrupted/repaired propositions, then trains a Markov denoising process to correct reasoning trajectories.
