Unlike diffusion LMs that mask tokens, it targets errors in the reasoning process itself.

entry.title: OVIBench: Benchmarking Online Video Question Answering under Interruption

author.name: Naiming Liu, Zhiheng Wu, Shuning Wang, Tie Zhang, Bowen Liu, Tong Wang

entry.summary: OVIBench is the first standardized benchmark for online video question answering under user interruption, categorizing interruptions into Cancellation, False Trigger, and Correction with an offline simulation protocol for reproducibility. It exposes gaps in current VLMs trained for offline single-round paradigms.

entry.title: Enrich-Retrieve-Rank: Scaling Capability Discovery Beyond In-Context Routing

author.name: Nazib Sorathiya, Daniel Zhang, Bardiya Akhbari

entry.summary: Enrich-Retrieve-Rank recasts agent capability discovery as search over registries of thousands of MATS components, using offline metadata enrichment plus online retrieve-then-rank without invoking candidates. In-context routing's top-1 accuracy collapses from 0.85 to 0.12 from N=10 to 7278 capabilities while retrieval scales gracefully.

entry.title: Beyond Verdicts: A Graph-Based Analysis of Human and LLM Reasoning in Scientific Fact-Checking

author.name: Abdul Ghafoor, Muhammad Arslan Manzoor, Yufang Hou

entry.summary: This work introduces typed reasoning graphs for comparing human expert and LLM reasoning paths in scientific fact-checking, going beyond verdict correctness to whether models follow valid reasoning routes. Building on MISSCIPLUS biomedical misinformation data, it reveals divergences between verdict agreement and process alignment.

entry.title: ChebBooster: A Training-Free Approach for Efficient Diffusion Transformer Inference via Chebyshev-Inspired Extrapolation

author.name: Chengjie Lu, Tianchi Deng, Zhengqi He, Chengwen Luo, Xueliang Li

entry.summary: ChebBooster accelerates Diffusion Transformer inference training-free via Chebyshev polynomial extrapolation of cached activations, using the barycentric formulation for numerical stability and avoiding Runge oscillations that plague Taylor-series alternatives. It extends cache reuse reliably over longer intervals.

entry.title: What's the Catch? Evaluating Temporal Consistency in Vision-Language Models

author.name: Marek Hradil, Danae S\'anchez Villegas

entry.summary: TimeCatch evaluates whether vision-language models capture temporal structure by framing temporal grounding as anomaly detection: swapping consecutive frames creates temporal anomalies while Gaussian-noise frames create frame-level anomalies, evaluated across four datasets plus a human study. Results reveal a substantial gap between frame-level and temporal anomaly sensitivity in VLMs.

entry.title: Change Detection in Probability Flow ODE: Online Testing in Diffusion Latent Spaces

author.name: Artem Kraevskiy, Artem Prokhorov

entry.summary: Formulates online change-point detection in diffusion latent spaces using the probability flow ODE of a conditional diffusion model trained on pre-change data. Enables likelihood-ratio-style testing when neither pre- nor post-change distributions have closed forms.

entry.title: NeuroPrefetcher: Storage-Aware Sparse LLM Inference via Delta Prefetching

author.name: Nobel Dhar, Md Romyull Islam, Xuechen Zhang, Gongjin Sun, Sahidul Islam, Bobin Deng, Kun Suo

entry.summary: Targets LLM inference where the model exceeds device memory entirely, exploiting observed temporal locality of MLP neuron activation (82-85% persistence token-to-token) to prefetch sparse weights from storage during autoregressive decoding. Extends beyond quantization and offloading approaches.

entry.title: Most of the LLM routing gap is task type

author.name: Janghoon Lee

entry.summary: Investigates why learned LLM routers stay far below the oracle ceiling and mostly fail to beat always calling the strongest model, analyzing 14 models over 294 questions across seven task types and concluding most of the routing gap is explained by task type rather than recoverable per-query signal.

entry.title: Dual-Grained Agent Memory and Shapley Context Attribution for Multimodal Agentic Learner

author.name: Jieke Wang, Tiancheng Shen, Yibo Yang, Ming-Hsuan Yang

entry.summary: DG-Mem augments frozen MLLMs with dual-grained non-parametric memory (instance exemplars plus category-level IF-THEN schema rules inspired by Complementary Learning Systems), built from training rollouts and consulted read-only at test time, with Shapley context attribution. Enables compounding improvement without weight access.

entry.title: CSymPlan: Certified Symbolic Planning and Control for High-DOF Manipulators

author.name: Aditya Narendra, Ashok Kumar Saini, Mahathi Anand, Mahmoud Khaled, Fares J. Abu-Dakka, Abdalla Swikir

entry.summary: CSymPlan provides certified symbolic planning and control for high-DOF manipulators with offline precomputed reach-avoid feedback policies and online synthesis from changing task and perception information, coupling planning with executable certified controllers.

entry.title: A Reproducible, License-Aware Distillation Recipe for CPUDeployable Safety Classification

author.name: Edson Rodrigues da Cruz Filho, Paulo Ricardo Ferreira Neves, Paulo Henrique Eleuterio Falsetti, Jo\~ao Vitor Pavan, Ian Degaspari, Henrique Vieira Laturrague, Patrick Vieira Laturrague, Guilherme Nielsen Dias, Marccello Wilson Perez Berto, Gustavo Voltani Von Atzingen

entry.summary: The paper distills a strong open guard model into a fleet of tiny students (lexical, shallow encoder, and generative architectures) trained on roughly 97k prompts from 24 datasets across seven safety categories, producing CPU-deployable safety classifiers in milliseconds with license-aware data partitioning.

entry.title: From Association to Causation: Improving Retrieval Precision of Retrieval-Augmented Generation via Causal Relations and an Attention Mechanism

author.name: Jing Liu, Yongxing Qi, Muchen Jiang, Chengnan Hu, Qingqing Peng, Haoming Wang, Yuqing Wang, Yang Yu, Xu Zhang, Ting Wu

entry.summary: MedEventGraph-RAG improves RAG terminal retrieval by modeling query-document relations causally via Reichenbach's common cause principle rather than pure similarity, building patient-specific graphs linking event occurrences to structured rows, note spans, timestamps, and lab trajectories for longitudinal clinical verification.

entry.title: Analyzing and Mitigating Cross-Lingual Degradation in Multilingual Medical VQA

author.name: Jingbo Wang, Sendong Zhao, Haochun Wang, Bing Qin, Ting Liu

entry.summary: The authors build a multilingual medical VQA benchmark across eight languages organized into four capability-isolating scenarios, evaluating five open and closed LVLMs. They find cross-lingual degradation is not uniform and varies by capability, providing fine-grained diagnosis beyond aggregate scores.

entry.title: Beyond the Harness: End-to-End Optimization of Context Artifacts for Enterprise Text-to-SQL

author.name: Kate Gwimm, Carson Eisenach

entry.summary: Arguing enterprise text-to-SQL is bottlenecked by constructed knowledge-base context rather than the model, this paper uses query-DAG decomposition recovered from production SQL to compare oracle query graphs against retrieved context, finding retrieved KB context provides the largest marginal improvement.

entry.title: Toward Effective and Reliable LLM Agents via Dynamic Ontology

author.name: Xiaohui Zhang, Zequn Sun, Chengyuan Yang, Yuanning Cui, Lingbing Guo, Wei Hu

entry.summary: OaK is an ontology-as-a-kernel framework that dynamically constructs task-usable ontologies externalizing domain concepts and relations for LLM agents, improving evidence use and multi-step decisions in domain-specific tasks where implicit semantics cause brittle behavior.

entry.title: Sycophants in the Courtroom: Are LLMs Fragile to Juridical Authority and Evolving Legal Standards?

author.name: Lorenzo Molfetta, Alessio Cocchieri, Luca Ragazzi, Ilaria Bartolini, Marco Patella, Gianluca Moro

entry.summary: RoboShape adds an information-theoretic compression head atop a frozen point cloud encoder, maximizing mutual information between embeddings and object geometry while minimizing MI with sensitive spatial context like room function. Gives robots principled privacy control when sharing 3D scene representations for fleet learning. Uses Donsker-Varadhan MI estimation.

entry.title: Discovering Dual-Origin Slow Wind from Solar Orbiter with Self-Supervised Contrastive Learning

author.name: Henry Han, Jorge Yero Salazar

entry.summary: VarDE proposes allocating sampling effort to minimize uncertainty of the final decision in highly stochastic environments, formalized through smooth decision functions. The framework yields theoretical guarantees for Best Arm Identification, Monte Carlo Tree Search, and Best-Policy Identification.

entry.title: Improving Few-Step Language Flows with Untied Self-Conditioning

author.name: Bocheng Li, Linli Xu

entry.summary: This paper identifies a train-inference mismatch in previous-prediction self-conditioning for flow-matching language models that degrades few-step generation quality, and proposes untied self-conditioning to fix it. The mismatch creates growing redundancy as step width increases.

entry.title: The Multilingual FrameNet Corpus

author.name: Beatrice Fiuman\`o, Nicolas Lazzari, Simone Paolo Ponzetto, Valentina Presutti

entry.summary: The Multilingual FrameNet Corpus harmonizes English Berkeley FrameNet with corpora from nine additional languages into a single open resource, and trained frame semantic parsers consistently beat prior state of the art in multilingual and cross-lingual settings. The corpus and models are openly released.

entry.title: E2S-Pruner: Progressive Two-Stage Evidence Fusion for Visual Token Pruning in Vision-Language Models

author.name: Taoyu Qian, Qi Wang, Daqian Shi, Yuanhao Jiang, Shang Gao, Hualong Yu

entry.summary: E2S-Pruner prunes visual tokens in vision-language models via progressive two-stage evidence fusion that treats each attention head as an evidence source weighted by reliability and inter-head consistency, using three-state token representations. It requires no auxiliary models, trainable parameters, or fine-tuning.

entry.title: Reward-Free Continual Adaptation for Resilient Space Robots

author.name: Andrej Orsula, Miguel Olivares-Mendez, Carol Martinez

entry.summary: This framework enables reward-free continual reinforcement learning for space robots by pre-training latent world models across diverse simulations so reward structure becomes predictable without external tracking during deployment. It addresses realistic constraints where precise reward computation in space is infeasible.

entry.title: ChemDIRT: A Diversified Instruction, Representation, and Task Benchmark for Robust Chemistry-LLM Evaluation

author.name: Eric Inae, Tim Gunn, Chris Bond, Meng Jiang

entry.summary: ChemDIRT benchmarks chemistry LLMs on robustness across diversified instructions, chemical representations, and task formulations, arguing that narrow benchmark performance overestimates consistent reasoning ability. Systematic perturbation of problem phrasing and representation exposes fragility in current models.

entry.title: A Comparative Study of Label-free Representation Quality Metrics in Deep Learning

author.name: Daniel Richards Arputharaj, Daniel J\"onsson, Gabriel Eilertsen

entry.summary: A comparative study of label-free representation quality metrics across 260 vision models and six datasets, grouping metrics into three families with analytical connections and controlled sensitivity experiments. Stratifies reliability by architecture class and task type.

entry.title: Model-Consistent Byzantine-Resilient Decentralized Federated Learning for Collaborative Missions

author.name: Yue Li, Sudip Bhujel, Cameron Lira, Ning Wang, Yang Xiao

entry.summary: Presents DFL-C, a Byzantine-resilient decentralized federated learning architecture guaranteeing global model consistency across nodes, addressing equivocation and poisoning attacks enabled by weak synchrony in decentralized topologies. Targets mission-critical collaborative training without a central server.

entry.title: HAWKEYE: Seeing One Layer Deeper -- A Cohesion-Aware Structural Channel for Temporal Link Prediction

author.name: Jiacheng Ding, Xiaofei Zhang

entry.summary: Shows empirically that 1-hop common-neighbour signals are near-random on sparse temporal graphs while 2-hop cohesive bridges carry discriminative power (discAUC 0.73-0.98), and builds HAWKEYE, a cohesion-aware structural channel improving temporal link prediction over crude co-occurrence encodings like DyGFormer's.

entry.title: SGHA: A Single-Loop Fully First-Order Algorithm for Nonconvex-Strongly-Convex Bilevel Optimization

author.name: Zhihao Gu, Qilong Wu, Junchi Yang

entry.summary: Proposes SGHA, a single-loop fully first-order algorithm for nonconvex-strongly-convex bilevel optimization matching best-known oracle complexity without double-loop or penalty procedures, using a constrained reformulation with regularized Lagrangian and smoothed gradient descent-ascent with finite-difference Hessian-vector products.

entry.title: DIAG: Diagnostic Iterative Alignment and Generation for Data-Efficient Mathematical Preference Distillation

author.name: Guhan Chen, Songtao Tian, Bohan Li, Hejin Wang, YeXin Xie, Zixiong Yu

entry.summary: DIAG adaptively reshapes the problem distribution during iterative preference optimization for math reasoning, diagnosing valid preference-pair yield and focusing training near the student model's competence boundary to counter signal scarcity from overly easy or hard rollouts.

entry.title: FIRM-Video: Check Before You Score for Reliable Text-to-Video Reward Modeling

author.name: Peiyuan Zhang, Xiangyu Zhao, Hongbo Liu, Xiaoxing Hu, Mingxin Liu, Shuran Ma, Yunhang Shen, Jian Hu, Haihan Gao, Haoyu Cao, Xue Yang

entry.summary: FIRM-Video introduces a checklist-driven data construction framework for text-to-video reward modeling based on check-before-score principles: construct dimension-specific checklists, verify each criterion against temporal visual evidence, and aggregate only verified decisions. It decomposes prompts into weighted atomic requirements for instruction following to improve supervision faithfulness.

entry.title: VIG: Visual Information Gain as a Reward Signal for Multimodal Chain-of-Thought Compression

author.name: Wen Luo, Xiaohan Yi, Xiaotao Huang, Liqun Huang

entry.summary: VIG proposes Visual Information Gain, an information-theoretic GRPO reward scoring each reasoning token by how much the image reduces its predictive uncertainty, computed online from two forward passes with and without the image. It compresses multimodal chain-of-thought by penalizing visually-disengaged filler tokens without needing reference chains or annotations.

entry.title: Grounding Isn't Knowing: Do VLMs Need Object Localization for Spatial Reasoning?

author.name: Xiwei Liu, Yulong Li, Xinlin Zhuang, Xuhui Li, Zhixiang Lu, Haolin Yang, Imran Razzak, Yutong Xie

entry.summary: Uses mechanistic interpretability tools (token ablation, layer-wise probing, attention knockout, causal mediation) on LLaVA-1.5 and Qwen2.5-VL to show spatial relation prediction follows a staged grounding-to-reasoning process where coarse anchors suffice but precise boundaries are not required. Clarifies how VLMs do spatial reasoning internally.

entry.title: Selective Cross-View Consistency for World Action Models: Held-Out Viewpoint Robustness Without Test-Time Camera Information

author.name: Bingqi Huang, Bingchuan Wei, Yingkai Cai, Zhaokui Wang

entry.summary: Shows that applying cross-view consistency losses to view-covariant outputs of world action models is provably harmful (shrinking legitimate view-specific content by 1/(1+4 lambda)), and derives selective consistency restricted to view-invariant blocks like action chunks and proprioception. Gives theoretical guidance for WAM training with viewpoint perturbations.

entry.title: Towards insect-like distributed proprioception in actuators and appendages for flapping-wing insect-scale aerial robots

author.name: Alexander Hedrick, Arvind Gupta, Kaushik Jayaram

entry.summary: Introduces embedded piezoelectric polymer sensors integrated into actuators and pitching hinges of insect-scale flapping-wing robots, tracking stroke and pitch angle without off-board motion capture. Fabricated via laminate stacks with accurate chirp-tracking results.

entry.title: Reviewing Model Collapse and Countermeasures

author.name: Xihao Xie, Beichen Hu

entry.summary: A review paper surveying model collapse in generative AI: the degradation that occurs when models are recursively trained on self-generated data. It organizes the growing literature on causes of model collapse and countermeasures, framing trustworthiness implications of synthetic-data training loops.

entry.title: ECHO: A Cognitively Inspired, Auditable Memory Plane for Long-Horizon Agents

author.name: Yu Qian, Hong Miao, Boyang Guo, Tingyi Jiang, Shan Zhao, Tianxing Le, Lintian Li, Meng Liu

entry.summary: ECHO is an auditable memory architecture for long-horizon agents inspired by cognitive mechanisms (episodic encoding, consolidation, reconsolidation, executive control), achieving strong Hit@10 and Recall numbers on LoCoMo and LongMemEval benchmarks with checkable provenance throughout.

entry.title: Role-Specialized Mixture-of-Agents with Open-Weight LLMs for Clinical Prediction

author.name: Jun Hou, Yi Fang, Xuan Wang

entry.summary: This paper studies role-specialized Mixture-of-Agents architectures using open-weight LLMs for clinical prediction from EHR data, combining medical knowledge retrieval with contrastive similar-patient reasoning. Careful ablations localize the main performance effect to the final integrator agent rather than retrieval or other roles.

entry.title: When Does AI for PDEs Yield Scientific Evidence?

author.name: Wenshuo Wang

entry.summary: The paper extends PDE-simulation and inverse-problem benchmarks to evaluate whether AI outputs constitute sufficient scientific evidence for specified claims, distinguishing this from mere predictive accuracy. It is the first such evidence-standard evaluation in AI for PDEs.

entry.title: Compositional Chain-of-Relations for Faithful Knowledge Graph Question Answering with Large Language Models

author.name: Chenhui Liu, Jianpeng Zhou, Jiahai Wang

entry.summary: This paper grounds complex KGQA in the knowledge graph across both candidate retrieval and constraint handling via compositional chains of relations, fixing unreliable entity pruning and ungrounded constraint filtering in existing agent-based methods.

entry.title: Budget-Constrained Embodied Perception: Four Resource Walls and a Pre-Registered Evaluation of Access-Structured Perception on Open Models at less than 31B

author.name: Defu Lin, Wenhui Chen, Ziyao Lin, Jianlin Chen, Peiji Long, Chi Man Vong

entry.summary: This paper formalizes four resource walls constraining budget-constrained embodied perception and introduces ASP, a training-free wrapper combining capped structured state, verbatim episodic index, and query-conditioned budget allocation, evaluated pre-registered on seven open models up to 31B on a license-free benchmark.

entry.title: AgentWeave: Routing Before Reasoning for Efficient Function Calling in Tool-Rich Language Models

author.name: Saurav Singla, Aarav Singla, Advik Gupta, Parnika Gupta

entry.summary: AgentWeave is a deterministic pre-inference routing layer that bounds the model-visible action space using eligibility, requirement, capability, and routing signals before function-calling inference, leaving the downstream model unchanged and reducing schema-processing burden in tool-rich settings.

entry.title: Cognitive Profiling of LRMs' Reasoning Traces Using Bloom's Taxonomy

author.name: Maria-Eleni Zoumpoulidi, Georgios Paraskevopoulos, Alexandros Potamianos

entry.summary: This work annotates large reasoning model traces at the step level using Bloom taxonomy cognitive levels, enabling large-scale analysis of which kinds of thinking occur during reasoning and supporting applications like targeted improvement.

entry.title: Correcting a learned physical invariant improves world-model rollouts

author.name: Richard Bao

entry.summary: Using frozen DreamerV3 trained on pendulum video, this study shows label-free search recovers an energy-like conserved quantity whose drift during autonomous rollouts predicts error, and projecting latents back onto its level set reduces rollout error. It distinguishes dynamically meaningful invariants from merely decodable correlates. A neat probe of what world models actually learn about dynamics.

entry.title: Bi-EZP: LLM-Guided Bilevel Program Evolution for Ensemble Zero-Cost Proxy Discovery

author.name: Yutao Lai, Kezhao Lai, Hai-Lin Liu

entry.summary: Bi-EZP uses an LLM at the upper level of a bilevel optimization framework to generate executable aggregation programs over base zero-cost proxies for neural architecture search. This decouples discrete aggregation structure from continuous coefficient calibration in ensemble proxy discovery.

entry.title: Cross-Subject Generalization in Decoding Perceived Speech from Non-Invasive Brain Recordings

author.name: Aoke Zhang, Bo Wang, Xihong Wu, Heping Cheng, Jing Chen

entry.summary: The CPSD framework decodes perceived speech from non-invasive brain recordings via two-stage training: contrastive pre-training captures subject-shared representations, followed by personal specialization. It improves cross-subject generalization and reduces per-subject training costs.

entry.title: Physical Agentic AI: An Architecture for Orchestrating a Robot Crew with LLMs

author.name: Xinyuan Liu, Eren Sadikoglu, Riana Chatterjee, Ransalu Senanayake

entry.summary: Physical Agentic AI introduces an architectural interface between LLM semantic planning and robot execution, where typed skill libraries let every planned action be verified against robot capabilities, system state, and workflow constraints before actuation. It orchestrates multi-robot crews safely.

entry.title: Triplet2Track: A Hierarchical System with Object-Centric Representations for Reliable Long-Horizon Manipulation

author.name: Jianxiang Liu, Gaojing Zhang, Chuan Wen, Qipeng Liu, Yuxuan Zhao, Ning Guo, Wenzhao Lian

entry.summary: Triplet2Track is a closed-loop long-horizon imitation learning system representing subgoals as instance-grounded triplets translated into continuous track priors, using human videos to reduce reliance on robot-collected data. It improves grounding and online feedback over open-loop hierarchical pipelines.

entry.title: Coarse Indexing, Fine Evidence: Decoupling Temporal Granularity in Long-Video RAG

author.name: Zhe Jin, Zhimin Lin, Bin Zheng, Junhua Fang, Huihua Yang

entry.summary: DAGC decouples coarse query-independent indexing from fine-grained evidence in graph-based RAG for long-video understanding, arguing that fixed temporal granularity unnecessarily couples the two. The training-free density-aware graph construction merges video segments into a compact index while preserving the original evidence granularity for downstream reasoning.

entry.title: BenthicDINO: Physics-Informed Self-Distillation for View-Invariant Side-Scan Sonar Representations

author.name: Taqi Hamoda, Hayat Rajani, Nuno Gracias

entry.summary: BenthicDINO applies physics-informed self-distillation on a DINOv3 backbone for side-scan sonar imagery, enforcing view-invariance through acoustically motivated augmentations simulating speckle noise and range-dependent degradation. This yields view-invariant seabed representations where natural-image SSL augmentations fail.

entry.title: Multi-Winner Voting with Argumentative Ballots

author.name: Ryuta Arisaka, Hirotaka Ono

entry.summary: MVArg generalizes multi-winner approval voting to argumentative ballots expressing defeasible preferences, with corresponding generalizations of justified representation axioms JR, PJR, and EJR. The paper proves MVArg is strictly more expressive than approval voting and characterizes satisfiability of the generalized axioms.

entry.title: MetaCaster: Meta-Harness-Optimized Agent for End-to-End Few-Shot Learning of Lightweight Time Series Forecasters

author.name: ChengAo Shen, Wenchao Yu, Fangyu Wu, Dongjin Song, Hanghang Tong, Dongsheng Luo, Wei Cheng, Haifeng Chen, Jingchao Ni

entry.summary: MetaCaster is a multi-agent framework that automatically generates training data to produce lightweight few-shot time-series forecasters, targeting resource-constrained scenarios where foundation models are uneconomical. Agentic data generation lets specialized compact models train from only a few examples plus textual context.

entry.title: Federated Continual Learning as a Distributed Drift-Plus-Penalty Control Problem

author.name: Nazreen Shah, Naveen Kumar Reddy Somireddy, Zubair Shaban, Ranjitha Prasad, B. N. Bharath

entry.summary: This paper recasts federated continual learning as a distributed drift-plus-penalty stochastic control problem, explicitly regulating forgetting arising from interactions between temporal task evolution and cross-client heterogeneity rather than applying heuristic replay or projection locally. The control formulation yields principled coupling across clients and tasks.

entry.title: Beyond Fixed Directions: Adaptive Representation Analysis of Reasoning and Memorization in LLMs

author.name: Shaheen Nabi

entry.summary: Testing claims that reasoning and memorization in LLMs are separable by a fixed single direction, this study finds a one-dimensional probe matches full-dimensional probes (AUROC 1.00) on Qwen3-0.6B task groups—but after GRPO the direction reorganizes substantially (cosine ~0.45). Fixed-direction assumptions used during RL are therefore unstable. It cautions representation-steering methods relying on static directions.

entry.title: ReCoG: Reciprocal Co-Evolution for Multimodal Graph Learning

author.name: Rui Xue, Tianfu Wu

entry.summary: Proposes ReCoG, which jointly evolves graph structure and multimodal node representations instead of treating topology learning and modality alignment separately. Addresses noisy or semantically misaligned edges in multimodal graphs.

entry.title: Conformal Risk Minimization for Semi-Supervised Domain Adaptation via Optimal Transport

author.name: Manos Giannopoulos, Yi Shen, Michael M. Zavlanos

entry.summary: Combines optimal transport-based semi-supervised domain adaptation with conformal risk minimization to provide distribution-free coverage guarantees for healthcare models deployed across shifted patient populations. Integrates CP during training rather than post-hoc.

entry.title: Recovering Weighted Tangent Geometry from a Single-Scale Score Field

author.name: Ziqi Zhao, Qingjian Ni

entry.summary: Proves that a single-scale score field determines weighted tangent geometry at manifold branch points via an Ornstein-Uhlenbeck eigenfunction equation, turning score values into a linear system for branch center and homogeneity degree. Provides theoretical grounding for score-based generative models near non-smooth data manifolds.

entry.title: Two-level domain-decomposition AdaGrad method for scalable training of graph neural networks

author.name: Laurynas Varnas, Julien Herrmann, Alexander Heinlein, Serge Gratton, Alena Kopani\v{c}\'akov\'a

entry.summary: Introduces DD-AG2m, a two-level domain-decomposition variant of an AdaGrad method with second-order curvature information and momentum for scalable GNN training, alternating between global-graph and partitioned-graph optimization to reduce message-passing coupling costs and communication overhead.

entry.title: When a neural surrogate cannot accelerate a solver: runtime share, closed-loop drift, and the economics of uncertainty gating in a stiff coupled simulation

author.name: L. Th\"ummler, T. Kuroda

entry.summary: Reports a controlled end-to-end negative result showing why a neural surrogate cannot accelerate a stiff coupled radiation-hydrodynamics Newton solve: the target block is only 16.9% of wall clock (capping speedup near 1.2x by Amdahl), plus closed-loop drift and uncertainty-gating economics, none attributable to network quality.

entry.title: Spicing up Genetic Netlist Generation with LLMs

author.name: Stefan Uhlich, Ya\u{g}{\i}z Gen\c{c}er, Andrea Bonetti, Arun Venkitaraman, Chia-Yu Hsieh, Eisaku Ohbuchi, Lorenzo Servadei

entry.summary: Introduces LLM-SPICEMixer, augmenting genetic netlist generation for analog circuit synthesis with an LLM proposal operator (IGEL) prompted with elite circuits to generate new SPICE netlists, reducing expensive simulations and premature convergence of pure evolutionary search.

entry.title: Photorealistic Novel View Synthesis of Human Faces using Next-Scale Transformers

author.name: Federico Stella, Fei Jiang, Zhongshi Jiang, Zohar Barzelay, Emanuel Garbin, Amin Jourabloo, Liuhao Ge

entry.summary: Adapts next-scale autoregressive transformers to photorealistic human face novel view synthesis, achieving higher resolutions, multi-view outputs, and cross-view consistency in one forward pass, trained on synthetic faces without 2D pretraining requirements unlike diffusion approaches.

entry.title: Mitigating Database Leakage in RAG Systems with Keyword-Grounded Fact Substitution

author.name: Ziliang Zhang, Yubo Zhu, Wei Tong, Jingyu Hua, Zijian Wang, Yuan Zhang, Sheng Zhong

entry.summary: Proposes KFS-RAG, defending RAG systems against prompt-injection-driven database leakage by identifying influential keywords via attention rollout plus causal perturbation, generating keyword-grounded facts with an auxiliary LLM, and substituting reformulated context to reduce exposure of sensitive contents.

entry.title: A Source-Grounded Framework for Constructing and Evaluating Progressive Multimodal Diagnostic Dialogues from Clinical Case Reports

author.name: Yufan Wang, Rui Yang, Yi Liu, Yi Lin, Yifan Peng

entry.summary: Provides a source-grounded framework converting clinical case reports into progressive multimodal diagnostic dialogues, plus an evaluation strategy separating final diagnosis, diagnostic reasoning, and image-finding interpretation for medical LLMs. Validated on 24 internal medicine cases with high conversion fidelity.

entry.title: Signal or Noise? A Benchmark Study of Agent Skills in Web Development

author.name: Ziyue Yang, Fan Ding

entry.summary: Introduces WebDev-Skills-Bench evaluating whether injecting Agent Skills into coding agents helps or hurts, controlling for prompt-length artifacts with matched irrelevant controls and leave-one-out ablations across 31 public web-dev skills, 50 projects, and 1,000 ordered tasks.

entry.title: Tomatoes, Potatoes, and Onions: Questioning the Need for Faces in Face Presentation Attack Detection

author.name: Guray Ozgur, Fadi Boutros, Naser Damer

entry.summary: This paper questions whether face presentation attack detection truly needs faces, introducing TPO, a controlled face-free PAD dataset built from print, replay, and recapture recordings of tomatoes, potatoes, and onions under protocols mirroring conventional face PAD datasets. A detector trained on TPO achieves surprisingly strong transferable performance, suggesting PAD artifacts are largely content-independent.

entry.title: Pixel-Space Diffusion via Observation Operators

author.name: Shaojie Guo, Lichen Ma, Haoyang Tong, Yu He, Zipeng Guo, Xiaoan Liu, Feng Yan, Yu Guo, Fei Wang, Junshi Huang, Yan Wang

entry.summary: This paper identifies a scale-time mismatch in pixel-space diffusion: image structures become predictable coarse-to-fine as noise decreases, yet models are forced to predict the full image even under high noise, producing low-SNR gradients. Observation Operator Diffusion aligns supervision trajectories and feature refinement with the intrinsic recovery order of image structures.

entry.title: VISTA: Test-Time Compositional Alignment for Visual Autoregressive Generation

author.name: Hossein Shahabadi, Niki Sepasian, Mahdieh Soleymani Baghshah

entry.summary: VISTA is the first gradient-based test-time alignment framework for next-scale visual autoregressive generation, closing a gap where diffusion test-time alignment methods do not transfer to stateful, discrete, multi-resolution VAR sampling. It targets persistent compositional failures in attribute binding and spatial relations.

entry.title: ByteAction: Byte-space Action Recognition Foundation Model

author.name: Fangcheng Li, Zhen Yu, Kejun Wu, Qiong Liu, You Yang

entry.summary: ByteAction is a foundation model for recognizing human actions directly from compressed image bitstreams without pixel decoding, using dual weakly and strongly corrupted views augmented by Bitstream Pattern Augmentation and encoded with a shared ByteFormer backbone. Byte-space operation confers independence from file integrity and privacy advantages.

entry.title: Can We Perform Online RL for Image Editing without Editing Rewards?

author.name: Qichao Ma, Jikang Cheng, Ling Liang, Zhaofei Yu, Tiejun Huang, Renye Yan

entry.summary: Proposes performing online RL for image editing by mapping editing dimensions onto the mature text-to-image reward ecosystem instead of building costly editing-specific rewards. This could substantially broaden preference optimization for editing models. It matters because reward engineering is a key bottleneck for RL-based visual generation.

entry.title: Can Coding Agents Build Robust Baselines? A Skill-Based Approach for Automating the Medical Imaging Model-Development Pipeline

author.name: Eugenia Moris, Jos\'e Ignacio Orlando

entry.summary: Presents an agentic AI Scientist workflow combining literature-guided reasoning, code generation, and hypothesis-driven experimentation to automatically build competitive medical imaging baselines across segmentation, classification, and detection benchmarks. Tests whether coding agents can automate full model-development pipelines.

entry.title: Position: Robot Privacy as Embodied Boundary Work. Connecting Capabilities, Contexts, and Design Responses in Everyday Robotics

author.name: Liwen He, Shuning Zhang, Chengwen Zhang, Xin Yi, Chun Yu, Jihong Jeung, Xin Tong

entry.summary: A position paper proposing embodied boundary privacy as a capability-by-context framework for how physically present robots reshape spatial, bodily, social, and relational privacy boundaries. Argues data-flow-centric privacy framings are inadequate for everyday robotics.

entry.title: GCS-Bridging: Restoring Connectivity of Disconnected Convex Sets for Graph-of-Convex-Sets Motion Planning

author.name: Xiaokai Zhou, Baoshi Cao, Yang Liu, Kui Sun, Boyu Ma, Zhengpu Wang, Zongwu Xie

entry.summary: GCS-Bridging restores feasibility in graph-of-convex-sets motion planning when start and goal lie in different connected components, reconnecting regions via collision-free point paths followed by convex inflation.

entry.title: RoboRacer Arena: Scaling High-Fidelity Autonomous Racing in Isaac Sim

author.name: Mihaela-Larisa Clement, Agnes Poks, Ezio Bartocci

entry.summary: Constructs a full 3D Gaussian splat reconstruction of the ISS Kibo module interior from grayscale images in the NASA Astrobee free-flyer dataset, outperforming Nerfacto and TensoRF in quality and rendering speed with as few as 500 images.

entry.title: ROS2SmolVLA: Enabling Small Vision-Language-Action Models for Integration into Industrial-Grade Lightweight Robots

author.name: Nils Mandischer, Noah B\"ockmann, Ludwig Holl, Lars Mikelsons

entry.summary: Adapts Hugging Face SmolVLA to Universal Robots within ROS 2 for on-premise industrial deployment, targeting small-batch adaptive production where large cloud VLAs raise compliance and security concerns.

entry.title: LLMs could control their host machines by exploiting inference engines

author.name: beyarkay (Boyd Kane)

entry.summary: Explores whether a malicious LLM could compromise the GPU host machine running its own inference by emitting token sequences exploiting vulnerabilities in engines like vLLM or SGLang, noting hosts hold weights, compute, and privileged datacenter access.

entry.title: Retrieval-grounded robot program generation and simulation-based correction via Model Context Protocol

author.name: Zhichao Zhou, Siyuan Chen, Omkar Salunkhe, Ebru Turanoglu Bekar, Johan Stahre, Anders Skoogh

entry.summary: This work presents a workflow that generates ABB RAPID industrial robot programs from natural language using a dual-stream RAG pipeline grounded in verified documentation and production templates, plus a custom MCP server connecting the LLM client to RobotStudio for automated upload, simulation, and diagnostic-driven correction.

entry.title: When Persona Simulations Are Informative: Graph-Structured Signals for Pluralistic Opinion Sensing

author.name: Taehyeon An, Jaehyeong Park, Donghyuk Shin

entry.summary: The paper introduces Persona-Conditioned Informativeness, an unsupervised diagnostic that measures whether semantically similar personas shift responses concordantly, separating systematic persona conditioning from model priors or sampling noise. It models personas as a similarity graph and applies Local Moran spatial statistics.

entry.title: Improving O-RADS Risk Stratification from Ultrasound Reports: A Comparative Evaluation of Hybrid versus End-to-End LLM Reasoning Strategies

author.name: Xiaotong Tan, Chunli Qiu, Xin Liu, Qing Huang, Guangli Zhou, Bo Gao, Xiaoyan Song, Shuyan Wang, Xiuqin Wang, Wufeng Xue, Ruobing Huang, Dong Ni, Guowei Tao, Jun Cheng

entry.summary: A retrospective clinical study comparing eight LLMs under three reasoning strategies, including a feature-based hybrid decoupling feature extraction from rule-based classification, for O-RADS ovarian risk stratification from free-text ultrasound reports against a radiologist reference standard.

entry.title: CRS-Bench: A Reference-Relative Reliability Benchmark for Medical Image Encoders

author.name: Xingtao Lin, Hangqi Ren, Caiwan Sun, You Chen

entry.summary: CRS-Bench is a controlled benchmark evaluating 15 pretrained encoder families across dermatology, ophthalmology, and radiology beyond clean-test AUROC, considering calibration, label efficiency, and stability under perturbation. It addresses encoder selection as a multi-objective decision when expert annotation is costly.

entry.title: LLM Evaluation on Unseen Questions: Contextual Multidimensional IRT Model

author.name: Ergan Shang, Weijing Tang, Yinqiu He

entry.summary: This paper combines multidimensional item response theory with question context to predict LLM performance on unseen questions, representing models via latent capability profiles informed by question content. It avoids confounding model ability with item characteristics in retrospective averages.

entry.title: Functional compatibility as a determinant of persistent neural learning

author.name: Hossein Javidnia

entry.summary: This paper provides the first controlled causal demonstration that functional compatibility - whether new learning can coexist with preserved behavior - causally determines persistent learning without catastrophic forgetting. Compatibility was deliberately manipulated from matched neural states under common retention requirements.

entry.title: PolyChirp: Multi-Species Birdsong Classification Using TinyML on Low-Power Acoustic Sensors

author.name: Nathan Duboisset, Zhaolan Huang, Felix Bie{\ss}mann, Roudy Dagher, Antoine Lavandier, Emmanuel Baccelli

entry.summary: PolyChirp enables multiclass bird species detection on battery-powered microcontroller sensors, moving TinyML acoustic monitoring beyond single-species binary classification. It combines biological expertise, automated dataset curation, architecture optimization, and novel hardware for full breeding-season deployment on one charge.

entry.title: The Emergence of Relevance Through Axiomatic Attention Patterns During LoRA Fine-Tuning

author.name: Matthew Perlman, Atharva Nijasure, James Allan

entry.summary: Through ablation and attention analysis of LoRA-tuned RankLLaMA, this paper localizes where relevance behavior emerges during reranking adaptation. Restricting LoRA attention updates to a compact mid-network region recovers over half of full-performance gains, coinciding with interpretable lexical matching and query-document interaction patterns.

entry.title: Congruence Decomposition with Neural Block Solvers for Large-Scale PCI Assignment

author.name: Yeqing Qiu, Chengpiao Huang, Ye Xue, Akang Wang, Fan Xu, Zhipeng Jiang, Dong Zhang, Ruoyu Sun, Qingjiang Shi, Zhi-Quan Luo

entry.summary: For large-scale PCI assignment in dense 5G networks, this work exploits arithmetic structure of PCI values to decompose a multi-objective modular-interference problem into blockwise Min-k-Partition subproblems solved by neural block solvers. The congruence decomposition enables tractable joint mitigation of collisions and confusions at practical scales.

entry.title: Stochastic Separability of Embedding Manifolds

author.name: Liqing Zhang

entry.summary: Proves a stochastic separability theorem for embedding manifolds of different object categories, establishing projection measure concentration under general conditions via a new two-layer concentration technique. Provides theoretical validation for empirically observed linear separability of object manifolds in neural spaces.

entry.title: What Does Activation Steering Control? Attribution Across Answer Encodings and Output-Sensitive Subspaces

author.name: Zhiwei Gao, Shaowen Peng, Shoko Wakamiya, Eiji Aramaki

entry.summary: Introduces Cross-Encoding Steering Evaluation, freezing activation-steering interventions while re-encoding answers, revealing that contrastive activation addition often follows extraction indices (answer identifiers) rather than semantic content on NormBank, questioning what steering directions actually control.

entry.title: Semantic Slots for Video Object-Centric Learning

author.name: Khalil Sabri, Guillaume-Alexandre Bilodeau, Nicolas Saunier, Wassim Bouachir

entry.summary: SemanticSlots argues that the bottleneck in video object-centric learning lies in the decoder rather than the encoder, since traditional decoders force slots to be spatially anchored. Its Transformer decoder uses image context so slots act as position-invariant semantic queries that retrieve matching features, allowing slots computed from a single frame to decompose subsequent video frames.

entry.title: Toward a Foundation Plug-and-Play Prior for Computed Tomography Reconstruction via a Multimodal Diffusion Model

author.name: Haley Duba-Sullivan, Patxi Fernandez-Zelaia, Obaidullah Rahman, Amirkoushyar Ziabari

entry.summary: Investigates whether a single multimodal diffusion model trained across several imaging domains can serve as a frozen plug-and-play prior for many sparse-view/low-dose CT reconstruction problems simultaneously, spanning additive manufacturing flaw analysis and other modalities/geometries. Challenges the retrain-per-setting paradigm.

entry.title: The Abstention Protocol: RCA for Clos Fabrics

author.name: Madhava Gaikwad, Deepak Pandey

entry.summary: CoreSec is a production root-cause-analysis system for Clos datacenter fabrics that replaces weighted telemetry fusion with a PAM-style abstention algebra, yielding deterministic decisions and explicit abstention when evidence is ambiguous. Deployed at hyperscale, it provides stable, explainable RCA that converges monotonically as evidence accumulates.

entry.title: Ask or Answer: A Decision Framework for Multi-Turn Health Misinformation Intervention

author.name: Xiaoying Song, Anirban Saha Anik, Jinyu Liu, Qitao Tan, Geng Yuan, Lingzi Hong

entry.summary: RO-PnR learns when to ask clarifying questions versus commit to corrections in multi-turn health misinformation dialogue, optimizing a turn-level reward balancing expected probing gain against interaction cost, while modeling user heterogeneity in knowledge and belief.

entry.title: LLMs for Survey Text Analysis - A Performance Comparison Between Humans and GPT-5 on Inductive Content Analysis

author.name: Leonardo Bergmann, Renata Gheorghiu, Ana Gvritishvili, Alex Mican, Chris Stewart, Topias Tolonen-Weckstr\"om

entry.summary: This study compares five human coders against GPT-5.4 on inductive content analysis of 903 open-ended survey responses, measuring agreement via Adjusted Rand Index. Alignment was moderate (ARI 0.61 for coding, 0.54 for theme generation), informing when LLMs can support qualitative research workflows.

entry.title: DeepSAGE: Stage-Aware Reinforcement Learning for Structured CBT Counseling Dialogue

author.name: Qi Zhang, Heajun An, Prakriti Dumaru, Sang Won Lee, Lifu Huang, Pamela J. Wisniewski, Jin-Hee Cho

entry.summary: DeepSAGE combines an external controller tracking eleven CBT session stages with deep RL selecting therapeutic intentions that guide LLM response generation for counseling dialogue. It outperforms six retrieval-, prompting-, stage-, and policy-based alternatives on stage-aware progression.

entry.title: LLM-based Agents for Forecasting and Prediction: Methods, Training, Evaluation, and Applications

author.name: Xiaogang Xu, Jiaqi Tang, Jianmin Chen, Yingying Yan, Zhenchao Tang, Xiangxin Zhou, Xiaobin Hu, Wei Wei, Jinfeng Wu, Qifeng Chen, Lu Zhou, Jiafei Wu, Zhe Liu, Jianwei Yin, Weimin Zheng

entry.summary: A survey organizing LLM-based forecasting and prediction agents into standalone workflows, tool- and retrieval-augmented agents, and hybrids with statistical or foundation models, covering training methods, evaluation protocols, and sensitivity to input perturbations.

entry.title: SkillAlchemy: Open-World Agent Skill Creation

author.name: Hengjun Wang, Shuyue Wei, Boyi Liu, Jun Yang, Yongxin Tong

entry.summary: SkillAlchemy studies open-world creation of reusable agent skills from underspecified briefs and raw source materials, discovering requirements omitted by the brief via an admission-centered framework. This reduces dependence on human authorship or execution traces for building agent capabilities. It extends the growing agent-skills research direction.

entry.title: Prime Agent: A Self-Improving RLM Harness

author.name: Seth Karten, Alex L. Zhang, Kevin Thomas, Sebastian M\"uller, Elie Bakouch, Daniel Auras, Mika Senghaas, Fares Obeid, Konstantin Dunas, Johannes Hagemann, Sami Jaghouar

entry.summary: Prime Agent is an open-source harness implementing Recursive Language Model abstractions for long-horizon coding-agent workflows: persistent REPL state, continual histories and memories, recursive subagents with agent-to-agent communication, and human-inspectable session views. It standardizes execution, recovery, verification, and resource accounting. Infrastructure contribution for the RLM paradigm.

entry.title: Learning Implicit Constitutive Laws for Dynamic 3D Gaussian Splatting from Monocular Videos

author.name: Xiaoyang Liu, Kai Han

entry.summary: GCA learns implicit constitutive laws of deformable objects from monocular dynamic video using 3D Gaussians, combining LoRA adaptation with rank-based depth alignment modules. It balances physical interpretability against generalization beyond predefined constitutive equations.

entry.title: Learning from the Test: Self-Referential Differential Testing for Deep RL Agents

author.name: Junda He, Jieke Shi, Zhou Yang, Mingfei Cheng, David Lo

entry.summary: Delta is a differential testing framework for deep RL agents that identifies both safety-critical failures and optimality bugs, addressing the testing oracle problem via self-referential comparison. It extends DRL testing beyond the usual focus on safety violations alone.

entry.title: KONTOGRAPH: Verified Point-in-Time Feature Consistency and Amortised Explanation for Real-Time Anti-Money Laundering under a 200 ms Decision Budget

author.name: Ahmed Abolfadl

entry.summary: KONTOGRAPH presents an end-to-end anti-money-laundering pipeline for SEPA Instant payments under a 200ms p99 budget mandated by EU regulation, evaluated on 1.56M simulated payments. Key findings cover temporal graph networks with per-node memory and amortised explanation under verified point-in-time feature consistency.

entry.title: Object-Uni: A Unified Model for Object-Centric Spatial Understanding and Controllable Generation

author.name: Mining Tan, Yinuo Wang, Ziqi Zhou, Weize Quan, Sifei Li, Jingdong Chen, DanDan Zheng, Libin Wang, Weiming Dong

entry.summary: Object-Uni unifies object-centric spatial understanding and controllable generation, treating object pose as explicit geometric grounding for pose perception, spatial reasoning, pose-conditioned generation, and novel view synthesis. It addresses continuous pose representation that existing unified VLMs lack.

entry.title: SDoH-Aware Narrative Anchoring Bias in Medical LLMs for Trustworthy Clinical Decision Support

author.name: Ahnaf Atef Choudhury, Ramkrishna Saha

entry.summary: Using NarrativeShield SDoH MedQA counterfactual cases held in persona-based narratives with fixed answer keys, this paper measures narrative anchoring bias in Qwen2.5-family medical LLMs. Models change clinically relevant responses when identical cases are written in different patient voices tied to social determinants of health.

entry.title: Cultural Moment Benchmark: Evaluating Video Cultural Reasoning and Grounding in Southeast Asia

author.name: Burak Satar, Zhixin Ma, Cheng Yu-Tong, Huy Hoang Tran, Phuong Anh Nguyen, Chong-Wah Ngo

entry.summary: The Cultural Moment Benchmark decomposes video cultural understanding into three stages: symbolization, visual recognition, and temporal localization of sub-events, using 306 expert-curated Southeast Asian concepts across seven countries. Staged evaluation exposes which ability is the bottleneck, unlike collapsed single-score benchmarks.

entry.title: Language Chain in Alignment: Cross-Lingual Ranking Preference Optimization

author.name: Seungyoon Lee, Minhyuk Kim, Jungseob Lee, Heuiseok Lim

entry.summary: CRPO transfers robust English preference knowledge to target-language alignment through hierarchical intra- and inter-lingual preference optimization on parallel pairs, extending beyond binary DPO comparisons via a LambdaLoss-style ranking signal. It addresses the chronic shortage of high-quality non-English preference data.

entry.title: Towards Comprehensive Basketball Understanding

author.name: Yirong Hu, Jiayuan Rao, Yu Zhang, Shangzhe Di, Weidi Xie

entry.summary: BasketballBench offers 7,980 questions across ten tasks spanning text, image, and video from the 2025-2026 NBA season, testing event recognition, action localization, player identification, and structured game-knowledge reasoning jointly. The BasketballSkills agent composes eight perception and retrieval tools under four reusable skills.

entry.title: The geometry of AI validation: Exact certification limits for iid best-of-N search

author.name: Ricardo Fitas

entry.summary: This theory paper derives exact certification limits for iid best-of-N search, representing validation and deployment rules as kernels over a reliability surface and separating sampling-noise reduction (replication) from structural-blindness reduction (new interventions). Closed-form ambiguity widths quantify what best-of-n reliability statistics can and cannot certify about best-of-N deployment.

entry.title: GeoQ: Geometry-Aware Conditional Quantile Error Estimation for Scientific Surrogate Models

author.name: Khoa Nguyen, Daniel Serino, Aviral Prakash, Marc Klasky

entry.summary: GeoQ provides a non-intrusive calibration framework for estimating input-dependent error of neural surrogate models at individual query points. It models error as anchor-averaged calibration plus a learned upper conditional quantile correction using geometry-aware features. This supports safer deployment of surrogates in extrapolative scientific simulations.

entry.title: More Experts, Worse Dynamics: Inverse Scaling and Spectral Bias in Mixture-of-Experts State-Space Models

author.name: Chandresh Pandey

entry.summary: This controlled synthetic study shows that adding experts to mixture-of-experts spectral state-space models can degrade dynamical prediction—inverse scaling—on regime-switching tasks combining chaotic, oscillatory, and noisy regimes. It critically tests the assumption that mixing stable operators adapts to heterogeneous dynamics. Findings caution against naive MoE scaling for time-series control.

entry.title: Activation-Weighted Seeded Residual Coding for Low-Bit LLM Weight Repair

author.name: Zehao Liu, Chuangchuang Fang, Yang Ren

entry.summary: AWSRC is a compact residual codec that repairs low-bit quantized LLM weights using seed-generated bases and activation-weighted error prioritization, storing only seeds, low-bit coefficients, and scales. On Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct it closes most perplexity and accuracy gaps to BF16 with about 0.16 bits per weight overhead.

entry.title: Spectrum-Aware Bounds on Invertibility for Privacy-Enhancing Instance Encoding

author.name: Seokjin Hwang (Ray), Yuting (Ray), Li, Kiwan Maeng

entry.summary: Derives spectrum-aware bounds on invertibility for privacy-enhancing instance encoding, improving on a recent MSE bound that was loose, restricted to randomized encoders, and limited in scope. Provides stronger theoretical guarantees that encodings resist reconstruction.

entry.title: Dataset Complexity Shapes Finite-Distance Loss Geometry in Neural Networks

author.name: Jaeyong Bae, Hawoong Jeong

entry.summary: Links dataset complexity to loss-landscape geometry using a Franz-Parisi local entropy construction estimated with adaptive sequential Monte Carlo in finite networks. Finds greater dataset complexity produces larger decreases in local entropy near trained solutions, connecting data structure to optimization landscape flatness.

entry.title: Generative Neural Networks for Sinkhorn Distributionally Robust Hypothesis Testing

author.name: Fenglin Zhang, Teyan Liu, Jie Wang

entry.summary: Develops a generative framework for Sinkhorn distributionally robust hypothesis testing that learns least-favorable distributions instead of solving large conic programs, deriving an equivalent conditional-KL representation and strong duality results enabling efficient end-to-end sampling.

entry.title: Primal--Dual Alternating Neural Learning for Timely Classification with Performance Guarantees

author.name: Jiaming Qiu, Yingye Zheng, Ying-Qi Zhao

entry.summary: Casts sequential clinical risk classification as multi-objective optimization balancing early intervention benefit against monitoring cost, characterizing optimal decision rules via value recursion and providing performance guarantees on sensitivity, specificity, and cost control.

entry.title: Robustness of Anomaly Detection Models for Industrial Control Systems under Training-Time Data Contamination

author.name: Mustafa Umut Ozbek, Taiwo Ojo, Pooria Madani, Khalil El-Khatib, Li Yang

entry.summary: Systematically evaluates 11 heterogeneous anomaly detectors for industrial control systems on the SWaT benchmark under three training-time contamination strategies, showing how compromised logs, label errors, and injected attacks degrade detectors commonly assumed to train on trustworthy data.

entry.title: Better Retrieval, Worse Robustness:How Multi-hop RAG Amplifies Upstream ASR Errors

author.name: Zhenghua Bao

entry.summary: Empirically shows that structurally richer multi-hop RAG extensions like entity-graph linking and iterative reformulation amplify upstream ASR errors rather than absorbing them, with F1 gaps of 36-60 points between clean text and high-WER accented input across three QA benchmarks.

entry.title: Knowing Isn't Always Saying: When Do Spatial Encodings Reach Answers in Vision-Language Models?

author.name: Zeyu Wang, Xinming Xu

entry.summary: Uses direction patching, a class-conditioned causal intervention, to determine when spatial information encoded in VLM hidden states actually reaches answer logits, finding causal influence only emerges at mid-to-deep depths and that chain-of-thought suppresses direct object-word transport while visually grounded prompts keep it available.

entry.title: Meta-Moderator: Empowering Multi-Agent Debate with Meta-Cognition

author.name: Wentao Hu, Zhuoyue Wan, Jinhao Shen, Chen Jason Zhang, Xiaoyong Wei, Qing Li

entry.summary: Meta-Moderator casts moderation of multi-agent debate as a learnable meta-cognitive process monitoring debate utility, controlling deliberation length, and adjudicating answers, trained independently of debaters via outcome-driven policy optimization to replace fixed budgets and agreement-based stopping.

entry.title: EXPL-FR: Explaining Face Recognition Models via Vision-Language Alignment

author.name: Guray Ozgur, Mustafa Efe Tamyapar, Naser Damer, Fadi Boutros

entry.summary: EXPL-FR explains face recognition models by aligning a vision-language model encoder with the frozen FR embedding space via a lightweight adapter trained on faces alone without text supervision. The shared adapter transfers to the text encoder, turning hundreds of attribute prompts into FR-space anchors, with a verification protocol measuring which concepts genuinely survive the transfer.

entry.title: GaussVid: Sparse-View Gaussian Splatting with 3D-Aware Video Diffusion Priors

author.name: Xinhui Liu, Can Wang, Wei Jiang, Wei Wang, Dong Xu

entry.summary: GaussVid enhances sparse-view 3D Gaussian splatting reconstructions using a 3D-aware video restoration framework built on video diffusion priors, introducing camera-aware conditioning to bridge 2D video generation and multi-view geometric constraints. A large-scale 3DGS video dataset enables specialized fine-tuning that avoids multi-view inconsistencies of naive fine-tuning.

entry.title: Retrieval-Augmented Visual Prompting: Guiding Foundation Models in Two-Photon Imaging

author.name: Salvatore Calcagno, Marco Finocchiaro, Giovanni Bellitto, Daniela Giordano, Concetto Spampinato, Federica Proietto Salanitri

entry.summary: RAVP guides foundation models at inference time in two-photon calcium imaging by injecting retrieved annotated exemplars directly into the input as visual prompts, implemented with SAM 3. Retrieval becomes a form of prompting, enabling adaptation through input design alone without weight updates in a domain with scarce annotations and high appearance variability.

entry.title: Hyper^2: Unleashing Hyperbolic Geometry's Full Potential via Dual-Space Consistency

author.name: Guantian Zheng, Haiyang Xu, Tianyu Gao

entry.summary: Hyper squared argues the modest gains of hyperbolic losses for point cloud completion stem from a cross-geometry mismatch: hyperbolic supervision back-propagates through Euclidean encoders, averaging away position-dependent gradients. Two model-agnostic indicators, feature-loss correlation and effective gradient utilization, make the mismatch testable and motivate dual-space consistency.

entry.title: LiST: Local-Simplex Test-Time LoRA Fusion

author.name: Yihua Shao, Jia Li, Siyu Chen, Xinyu Luo, Yang Liu, Kecheng Chen, Xinwei Long, Lingyu Zhu, Fanhu Zeng, Maolin Wang, Ziyang Yan, Jingcai Guo, Hao Tang, Nicu Sebe, Zhenyi Wang

entry.summary: LiST performs label-free test-time LoRA fusion by converting an adapter bank into a target-conditioned local simplex and searching sample-specific fusion weights at inference, building joint task representations from parameter anchors and prompt behavior vectors, retrieving neighboring adapters, and selecting weights via prompt-level energy without updating backbones.

entry.title: LagrangeGS: Non-Conservative Lagrangian System on Dynamic 3D Gaussian Splatting

author.name: Shogo Sato, Takuhiro Kaneko, Shoichiro Takeda, Tomoyasu Shimada, Riku Inoue, Kazuhiko Murasaki, Ryuichi Tanida

entry.summary: LagrangeGS formulates dynamic 3D Gaussian splatting as a non-conservative Lagrangian system, fixing physically inconsistent trajectories, lack of time-reversibility, and geometric collapse during long-term extrapolation that plague physics-aware extensions fitting velocity fields to visual deformations, with efficient handling of the velocity-Hessian inversion.

entry.title: FOVEA: Focused On-Demand Visual Evidence Adaptation for Cache-Friendly Multimodal Speculative Decoding

author.name: Hengjie Zhu, Dayan Wu, Zihao Zhang, Xinze Liu, Jingxuan Yu, Peng Fu, Zheng Lin, Weiping Wang, Ding Wang

entry.summary: FOVEA improves multimodal speculative decoding by dynamically adapting the amount of visual evidence given to the draft model per decoding stage, showing visual demand varies across tasks and stages. Cache-friendly design reduces overhead while preserving grounding. Contributes to efficient VLM inference.

entry.title: Lifelong Robot Recomposition via Persistent Categorical Modeling for Unified Task-Driven Co-Design, Verification, and Planning

author.name: Steven Swanbeck, Mitch Pryor

entry.summary: Formalizes robotic systems as abstract circuits in symmetric monoidal categories, synthesizing hardware, software, and behavior composition jointly via SMT solving with functors projecting lifecycle-specific views. Aims at lifelong recomposition instead of static design-then-deploy.

entry.title: Safety-Critical Bilateral Teleoperation for Omnidirectional Aerial Manipulation Using Force-Sensorless Haptic Feedback

author.name: Yubin Kim, Jinwoo Lee, Yongjun You, H. Jin Kim, Jeonghyun Byun

entry.summary: Presents an integrated companion robot for elderly care combining active gimbal-based human following, LLM-driven speech interaction, and VLM-based safety monitoring including fall detection. Targets continuous companionship rather than isolated service functions.

entry.title: Enhancing Sim2Real Transfer for Torque-Controlled Robots through Real2Sim Dynamics Estimation and Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Davide Bargellini, Alex Pasquali, Andrea Govoni, Riccardo Zanella, Gianluca Palli

entry.summary: Real2Sim2Real pipeline for torque-controlled arms combining trajectory matching, genetic-algorithm parameter identification of friction/inertia/gravity terms, and domain randomization, demonstrated on a 7-DoF Franka Panda with TQC-based RL.

entry.title: Design of a Biomimetic Joint-Covering Skin with Tissue-Like Structure to Enhance Proprioception in a Musculoskeletal Humanoid

author.name: Akihiro Miki, Shun Hasegawa, Yoshimoto Ribayashi, Kento Kawaharazuka, Kei Okada

entry.summary: Designs biomimetic joint-covering skin with layered tissue-like pressure and stretch sensing for the musculoskeletal humanoid Musashi-W, demonstrating complementary proprioceptive information beyond muscle sensing.

entry.title: Strong Averaging Principle and Long-Time Dynamics for Fast-Slow SDEs with Increasing Time-Scale Separation and Degenerate Noise

author.name: Sebastian Kassing, Asuto Miwa

entry.summary: Establishes a strong averaging principle for fast-slow SDEs with time-varying scale separation tending to zero, relying on dissipativity rather than elliptic regularity to permit degenerate noise, with maximal Lp estimates and asymptotic pseudo-trajectory results.

entry.title: ATHENA: Knowledge-guided agentic neural architecture search for AutoFormer-based electronic health record modeling

author.name: Deyi Li, Qi Xu, Lingyao Li, Tiansheng Wang, Muxuan Liang, Mei Liu

entry.summary: ATHENA is a knowledge-guided agentic neural architecture search framework for AutoFormer-based EHR models that transfers architecture knowledge across hospitals, reducing repeated NAS costs. An LLM-guided agent reuses prior search experience to warm-start new hospital-specific searches.

entry.title: SEAM: Shot Entity-Attribute Memory for Consistent Short-Drama Generation at Scale

author.name: Jiaqi Liu, Maolin Ran, Xiaoyang Lu, Jian Wang, Weiwen Liu, Jianghao Lin, Yong Yu, Weinan Zhang

entry.summary: SEAM is a training-free, model-agnostic memory graph that maintains per-shot entity-attribute state for episode-level short-drama generation, retrieving causally prior context and injecting constraints at the prompt layer to fix character, prop, and blocking continuity drift.

entry.title: SSE-Bio: A Structured Self-Evolving Agent with Agentic Retrieval Policy for Multi-Hop Biomedical Reasoning

author.name: Zhaohan Meng, Zaiqiao Meng, Siwei Liu, Hao Xu, Ke Yuan, Iadh Ounis

entry.summary: SSE-Bio is a structured self-evolving agent for multi-hop biomedical QA that maintains structured state, selectively retrieves knowledge triplets via a trainable proxy policy, and improves reasoning memory through fine-grained template editing instead of global instruction rewriting.

entry.title: Cross-lingual Biography Enrichment via Claim Extraction and Alignment

author.name: Yifei Song, Ziyang Chen, Emil Sayilov, Claire Gardent

entry.summary: CLAW-4L is a benchmark of 300 Wikipedia biography pairs linking English biographies with French, Chinese, or Azerbaijani counterparts, annotated with claims and claim-pair relations for cross-lingual biography enrichment. The accompanying claim extraction and alignment framework enriches English articles with locally grounded facts, focusing on women from non-English contexts.

entry.title: EG-ARSA: An Expert-Grounded Open Model for Visual Road Safety Auditing in Low-Resource Settings

author.name: Md Thamed Bin Zaman Chowdhury, Moazzem Hossain

entry.summary: EG-ARSA transfers institutional road-safety auditing expertise into a compact open vision-language model via Expert-Grounded Distillation, calibrating the teacher against authoritative field audits before permitting large-scale annotation. It targets proactive road safety auditing in low-resource countries where inspections are costly.

entry.title: Reservoir of Importance: Learning Semi-Structured Sparsity with Differentiable Subset Sampling

author.name: Ha Dinh, Xuan Duy Ta, Khoat Than, Khac-Hoai Nam Bui

entry.summary: RoI learns semi-structured N:M sparsity masks via differentiable subset sampling with a compact-logit parameterization, avoiding the parameter and memory overhead of full categorical mask distributions. Targets scalable pruning of large language models at aggressive sparsity.

entry.title: SchemaRouter: Field-Aware Tool Routing for Efficient Heterogeneous Agentic RAG

author.name: Yong-eun Cho

entry.summary: SchemaRouter is a lightweight routing layer for heterogeneous agentic RAG that models tools, endpoints, parameters, response fields, and policies as a schema graph, emitting executable tool plans that specify both which tools to call and which fields to retrieve. It targets over-fetching (latency/token waste) and under-fetching (missing fields) failures.

entry.title: HIRA: A Human-in-the-Loop Retrieval-Augmented Cascade for Document Classification in Regulated Industries

author.name: Shangxuan Tian, Yanhui Chen, Carlos Queiroz

entry.summary: HIRA is a training-free, on-premises retrieval-augmented cascade for document classification in regulated industries, fusing BM25, dense text, and image representations with calibration-weighted reciprocal rank fusion, escalating uncertain cases to a locally hosted LLM verifier and then humans.

entry.title: Clarify User Expertise: Towards Proactive Conversational Agents Tailoring Responses to User Proficiency

author.name: Zhihong Cao, Chen Huang

entry.summary: PASSING enables conversational agents to proactively clarify a user expertise level through targeted inquiries so responses can be tailored to comprehension, complementing prior work on clarifying query ambiguity. The paper shows existing agents cannot reliably infer expertise from queries alone.

entry.title: Weakly supervised concept Bottleneck Learning for Robust Two stage Object centric visual reasoning

author.name: Sparsh Tiwari, Gesina Schwalbe, Bettina Finzel

entry.summary: D-OCB is an object-centric slot-VAE framework extracting human-aligned symbolic predicates under extremely weak supervision for two-stage neuro-symbolic visual reasoning, with dynamic hyperparameter allocation replacing manual loss-balancing tuning.

entry.title: Performance of a domain-specific large language model in answering patient questions in psychiatry

author.name: Alexander J. Hish, Arjun Nagendran, Scott N. Compton

entry.summary: MIND is a psychiatry-focused LLM fine-tuned exclusively on patient education resources, compared against ChatGPT and OpenEvidence on escitalopram questions via rubric analysis and ratings from ten board-licensed psychiatrists. Results inform whether narrow clinical fine-tuning beats general chatbots for patient communication.

entry.title: Beyond Observed Auxiliary Relations: Environment-Conditioned Modeling for Multi-Behavior Recommendation

author.name: Seunghan Lee, Hyunsik Yoo, Jian Kang, Susik Yoon, SeongKu Kang

entry.summary: BOAR is an environment-conditioned framework for multi-behavior recommendation handling missing and unreliable auxiliary signals like clicks and add-to-cart in a unified manner, improving target-behavior prediction over GNN-based propagation baselines.

entry.title: What is mathematics now, and what should it be?

author.name: Jeremy Avigad

entry.summary: Jeremy Avigad argues that neural theorem prover successes obscure a broader vision of what AI can do for mathematics and how mathematicians can engage with AI, advancing an expansive and optimistic perspective.

entry.title: MediSkill-Evo: Process-Constrained Self-Evolution for Evidence-Grounded Clinical Interaction

author.name: Ruoyu Wu, Shenfu Xie, Yinqian Sun, Haibo Tong, Feifei Zhao

entry.summary: MediSkill-Evo is a clinical agent that evolves process knowledge at test time without backbone fine-tuning, using typed memory banks for skills, rules, schemas, and procedures governed by provenance and safety checks. A preference harness binds evidence to sources and prioritizes safety when ranking actions. It targets evidence-grounded clinical interaction under partial observability.

entry.title: Multi-Agent Discovery and Resource-Aware Autonomous Exploration of Scientific Datasets

author.name: Aashish Panta, Hugo Lee, Giorgio Scorzelli, Kyongsik Yun, Valerio Pascucci

entry.summary: The authors propose CIHSI-Net, a deep learning framework using Barycentric Fused Gromov-Wasserstein Balancing for causal inference under multiple simultaneous treatments. It avoids quadratic scaling of pairwise distribution balancing while preserving local proximity structures for counterfactual estimation.

entry.title: TRACE: Artifact-Robust Statistical Shape Modeling from Imperfect Surface Scans - A Case Study in Craniosynostosis 3D Photography

author.name: Sanjay Bhandari, Nawazish Khan, Alzbeta Novotna, Tiffany Jeong, Loretta Bowman, Michael Hernandez, Tobi Somorin, Viraj Govani, Jesse Goldstein, Shireen Elhabian

entry.summary: TRACE constructs statistical shape models directly from artifact-contaminated clinical 3D head photographs for craniosynostosis analysis, predicting anatomically corresponding control points from raw point clouds unsupervised. It enables radiation-free severity analysis without curated scans.

entry.title: Training-Free VLM Personalization via Calibrated Residual Decoding

author.name: Jiaao Yu, Yujian Ma, Xianming Hu, Pengran Wang, Ang Li

entry.summary: A training-free personalization method for vision-language models that separates profile-supported personalized signals from generic model priors via calibrated residual decoding. It compares positive-profile responses against counterfactual conditions to determine whether confidence reflects user-specific evidence.

entry.title: Length-Adaptive Decoding for Masked Diffusion Machine Translation

author.name: Yan Zhan, Mengkai Hou, Wanting Zhang, Zhijun Gao

entry.summary: Entropy-Valley is a training-free length selector for masked diffusion machine translation that scores candidate target canvases by mean predictive entropy from all-mask forward passes. On En-X pairs it recovers substantial fractions of the COMET gain achievable with reference target lengths.

entry.title: ProBel: Propaganda Detection with Techniques, Spans, and Explanations

author.name: Mohamed Bayan Kmainasi, Ali Ezzat Shahroor, Elisa Sartori, Giovanni Da San Martino, Firoj Alam

entry.summary: ProBel aligns binary labels, multi-label annotations over 23 propaganda techniques, technique-labeled spans, and reference explanations for Arabic and English news sentences. It enables matched evaluation across supervision levels and studies how they interact under zero-shot, fine-tuned, and joint training.

entry.title: EMPIRE: Explicit Manipulation Planning as a Learnable Intermediate Representation for Egocentric Hand-Motion Forecasting

author.name: Wen Wang, Ruibing Hou, Hong Chang, Shiguang Shan, Xilin Chen

entry.summary: EMPIRE introduces explicit manipulation planning as a learnable intermediate representation for egocentric hand-motion forecasting in a two-stage framework, preventing motion-generation gradients from interfering with manipulation-aware representations. Stage I learns plans from multimodal demonstrations before motion synthesis.

entry.title: TEE-X: TEE-aware Acceleration Framework for Large Vision Models at the Edge

author.name: Kurt M Wilson, Mohaiminul Al Nahian, Abeer Matar A. Almalky, Sadat Shahriyar, Souvik Kundu, Zhishan Guo, Abdullah Al Arafat, Adnan Siraj Rakin

entry.summary: TEE-X accelerates large vision models inside Trusted Execution Environments at the edge, addressing the overhead TEE adoption imposes when shifting execution from white-box to black-box threat models. It makes confidential ViT inference practical on resource-constrained devices.

entry.title: Do Spoken Language Models Hear Speech as They Read Text? Bridging Structural Gaps Between Speech and Text

author.name: Hyeonyu Kim, Hwayeon Kim, Youngwon Choi, Myeongkyun Cho, Huu-Kim Nguyen

entry.summary: This analysis finds speech and text representations in spoken language models remain weakly aligned despite strong downstream performance, indicating unresolved structural differences between continuous speech and discrete text. It proposes a framework decoupling length mismatch from semantic alignment to improve correspondence.

entry.title: SplitLite: Low-Rank Residual Compression for Split Learning

author.name: Tao Li, Yulin Tang, Qi Guo, Xianhao Chen

entry.summary: SplitLite targets communication costs in split federated LoRA fine-tuning of on-device LLMs by exploiting low effective rank structure in consecutive-epoch activation and gradient residuals. Compressing these residuals substantially reduces client-server exchange overhead during federated fine-tuning.

entry.title: FIDES: A Concordance Protocol for LLM-Generated Trading Strategies

author.name: Arther Tian, Alex Ding, Simon Wu, Aaron Chan

entry.summary: FIDES treats LLM-generated trading strategies as three artifacts needing reconciliation: natural-language rationale, executable code, and backtest track record, scoring say-to-do, do-to-real, and say-to-result concordance gaps in sandboxed lag-one out-of-sample backtests. Across four models and 40 strategies it measures how often claimed edges survive contact with execution and data.

entry.title: Physics-Constrained Deep Learning Model for Contactless Blood Pressure Monitoring from Triaxial Bodyseismography

author.name: Yuanyuan Zhang, Yida Zhang, Jiahui Li, Yuyan Wu, Fei Dou, Xiao Yin, Zhenlin An, Hae Young Noh, Wenzhan Song

entry.summary: Phy-BP estimates blood pressure contactlessly from triaxial bodyseismography using physics-constrained deep learning with adaptive quality control selecting cardiogenic signal segments, addressing fiducial misalignment and hemodynamic variability that plague ballistocardiography. It targets unobtrusive long-term BP monitoring.

entry.title: Reaching the Tail: Calibration Diversity Drives Conformal Coverage under Data Scarcity

author.name: Donald Aadithiyan

entry.summary: This study finds that under data-scarce conformal forecasting of rare macroeconomic events, apparent rare-event thresholds actually reflect calibration-set size: support width of nonconformity scores explains up to 85 percent of coverage variance versus 2 percent for rare-event counts, replicated across five countries. A diversity-maximizing calibration selector is the only tested strategy improving coverage.

entry.title: MSM-Mem: A Universal Medical Structured Multimodal Memory Framework for Medical AI Agents

author.name: Md Asaduzzaman Jabin, Khoa Le, Lin Zhao, Tianming Liu

entry.summary: MSM-Mem equips multimodal medical AI agents with structured memory that accumulates patient history, observations, and diagnostic experience across interactions, unlike stateless MLLM inference. The framework targets longitudinal clinical workflows and progressive improvement of reasoning reliability. It tackles a key limitation of current medical agents.

entry.title: CD-LoRA: Consistency-Driven Low-Rank Adaptation for Multi-Task Fine-Tuning

author.name: Qian Zha, Jinda Liu, Yuan Wu, Yi Chang

entry.summary: CD-LoRA removes routers from LoRA-based multi-task fine-tuning of LLMs, showing via second-order Taylor analysis that stochastic routing causes train-test instability under distribution shift. A consistency-driven alignment mechanism enforces representation congruence instead. It offers a simpler, more stable alternative to routing-based multi-task adaptation.

entry.title: Neural Operator based Multi-Field Reconstruction of Inner Solar Boundary State

author.name: Vignesh Kumar Pandian Sathia, Reza Mansouri, Dustin J. Kempton, Pete Riley, Rafal A. Angryk

entry.summary: Uses neural operator learning to reconstruct a complete multi-field solar magnetohydrodynamic boundary state at 30 solar radii from partial observations like radial velocity and magnetic field. This improves inner-boundary conditions for heliospheric modeling and solar-wind prediction.

entry.title: Mapping the Concept Landscape: Structural Perception of Global Distributions for Transparent Data Pruning

author.name: Dongyue Wu, Tao Ma

entry.summary: MCL performs transparent data pruning by representing each image-caption pair as an explicit entity-event-attribute graph rather than opaque embeddings, aggregating into a dataset-level graph to quantify semantic concept rarity. Improves coverage of rare concepts in pruned subsets.

entry.title: Test-Time Adaptation for ECG Classification via SQI-Gated Self-Training and Beat-Rhythm Consistency

author.name: Wenhan Jiang, Zhipeng Deng, Jiale Zhou, Haolin Wang, Yafei Ou, Yefeng Zheng

entry.summary: BeatRhythm-TTA adapts ECG classifiers at test time using signal-quality-gated self-training and beat-rhythm consistency constraints, respecting cardiac cycle structure and avoiding drift from artifacts under device and population shift.

entry.title: RAD: Rule-Augmented Relational Anomaly Detection

author.name: Noah Dahle, Anne Tumlin, Ngoc Tran, Xenofon Koutsoukos, Tyler Derr

entry.summary: RAD performs anomaly detection directly on multi-table relational databases without flattening, augmenting learned relational representations with symbolic behavioral rules to capture multi-hop dependencies and schema structure.

entry.title: The spatial anatomy of urban wildfire vulnerability: a spatially validated GeoAI framework reveals the roles of building density and vegetation moisture in structure loss during the 2025 Palisades Fire
