author.name: Parastoo Farajpoor, Mohammadreza Narimani

entry.summary: Builds a spatially validated GeoAI workflow analyzing structure loss in the January 2025 Palisades Fire using CAL FIRE inspections of nearly 10,000 residential structures plus satellite and terrain features. Key finding: random cross-validation ROC-AUC of 0.92 drops to 0.75 under 1 km spatial block validation, exposing optimistic bias in city-scale fire risk models.

entry.title: GET: Generative Embedding Translation for Medical Image Segmentation

author.name: Md Maklachur Rahman, Md Hasan Al Banna, Saraf Anjum, Mahmudul Hasan, Tracy Hammond

entry.summary: Proposes GET, a framework that progressively translates image embeddings into mask embeddings within a frozen Stable Diffusion VAE latent space using a tiny 1.07M-parameter U-Net-style translation network, evaluated across five medical segmentation datasets.

entry.title: A Commutator Framework for Selective Spectral Alignment in Deep Neural Networks

author.name: Kaj Nystr\"om

entry.summary: Develops a finite-width geometric framework quantifying incompatibility among weight-generated covariance, gates, and backward sensitivities in deep networks through three families of commutators, with an exact layerwise identity decomposing sources of misalignment and connecting AGOP-NFM commutators to feature learning.

entry.title: KellyBoost: Growth-Optimal Portfolio Construction with Gradient-Boosted Trees

author.name: Jiayu Li

entry.summary: KellyBoost trains a single multi-output XGBoost model whose softmax output is directly the Kelly growth-optimal portfolio, using the exact negative log growth rate as loss with derived analytic gradients and Hessians verified by finite differences.

entry.title: From Diagnosis to Redesign: Using Quantitative Ethnography to Improve Multi-Agent LLM Reasoning

author.name: Vedant Khatri, Anthony Cusimano, Zachari Swiecki, Zhen Xu, Xiner Liu, Renzhe Yu

entry.summary: Applies quantitative ethnography, specifically Epistemic Network Analysis, to the discourse of a five-agent LLM debate system to diagnose why automated essay scoring decisions succeed or fail, then redesigns the system based on findings. Offers a qualitative-quantitative lens on multi-agent coordination.

entry.title: Closed-Loop Bayesian Molecular Inverse Design with Semantic LLM Surrogates

author.name: Yaoyao Xu, Xinjian Zhao, Xiaozhuang Song, Lei Bai, Tianshu Yu

entry.summary: Frames molecular inverse design as closed-loop candidate-pool enrichment under limited oracle budget and proposes using a frozen LLM as the surrogate within Bayesian optimization, preserving substructural and reference-similarity signals that Gaussian-process embeddings discard.

entry.title: Fidelity-Diversity-Consistency (FDC): Data Pruning for Remote Sensing Change Detection

author.name: Dongyao Zhu, Ranga Raju Vatsavai

entry.summary: This work provides the first systematic benchmark of six data-pruning methods for remote sensing change detection across building and forest datasets, CNN and transformer models, and three pruning budgets. It finds existing baselines offer no reliable advantage over random selection, with even the strongest baseline matched or exceeded by about a third of random subsets, then characterizes the underlying mechanism through regression over 540 subsets.

entry.title: FlashReg: GPU-Accelerated 3-Clique Point Cloud Registration for Real-Time Correspondence-to-Pose Estimation

author.name: Ziyang Yu, Xiang Li, Qiong Chang, Jun Miyazaki

entry.summary: FlashReg is a GPU-oriented point cloud registration estimator that avoids materializing dense second-order compatibility graphs, building capacity-bounded sparse second-order graphs directly from binary first-order graphs. A dataflow-optimized three-node clique search selects pivots from compact per-row pools, enabling real-time correspondence-to-pose estimation across indoor and outdoor settings.

entry.title: Through the Schr\"odinger Bridge: Benchmarking Antemortem Image Restoration from Postmortem Autolysis to Enhance Forensic Diagnostics

author.name: Shuang Hao, Jiacheng Yue, Yaxuan Zhao, Fan Wang, Jianhua Ma, Erwen Huang, Chunfeng Lian

entry.summary: This work formalizes forensic histopathology image restoration from postmortem autolysis as a Schrodinger bridge problem, restoring autolyzed tissue images to diagnostically plausible pre-autolysis states despite large non-deterministic morphological changes and absence of paired data. The goal is improved objectivity in determining cause of death and disease diagnosis.

entry.title: Towards Alias-Free 4D Gaussian Representations with Motion-Aware Filtering

author.name: Ankit Dhiman, Kunal A Kathare, Pranav Vignesh, Lokesh R Boregowda, Venkatesh Babu Radhakrishnan

entry.summary: This paper proposes a motion-aware 3D smoothing filter for 4D Gaussian splatting and NeRF-style dynamic representations to eliminate aliasing artifacts under divergent viewpoints such as zoom operations. Unlike static filters adapted from Mip-Splatting, the approach accounts for local motion in dynamic scenes.

entry.title: Sparse Multi-Stage Expert-Agent Routing for Complex Clinical Reasoning

author.name: Sike Xiang, Shuang Chen, Qian sun, Jia Cheng, Yusi Wei, Amir Atapour-Abarghouei

entry.summary: This framework models complex clinical reasoning as stage-wise sparse routing over medical expert agents, maintaining an evolving case state as multimodal evidence arrives and adaptively activating only necessary specialists under consultation resource constraints. It moves beyond static multi-agent workflows and single-pass prediction.

entry.title: UR$^{2}$-MLLM: Uncertainty-aware Revisit Reasoning in Multimodal Large Language Models for Radiology Report Generation

author.name: Yucheng Chen, Yang Yu, Jiazhou Zhou, Yufei Shi, Yongying Lan, Yichi Zhang, Liyi Li, Si Yong Yeo

entry.summary: UR2-MLLM brings uncertainty-aware revisit reasoning to radiology report generation, dynamically revisiting uncertain regions during thinking-with-images reasoning to mimic how radiologists re-examine suspicious findings. It adds uncertainty estimation to guide selective re-inspection of visual evidence.

entry.title: Fast and Compact 3D Gaussian Splatting with Polarized Opacity Prior

author.name: Zi-Ming Wang, Kai-Wen Duan, Kowei Huang, Akihiro Sugimoto, Shang-Hong Lai

entry.summary: This paper attacks 3DGS model bloat by replacing densify-then-prune with an intrinsically compact training framework using an L2 reconstruction loss for error-proportional gradients and a Polarized Opacity Prior that actively manages opacity, reducing redundant low-opacity Gaussians and associated memory and training costs.

entry.title: RS$^3$-Prune: Read-Sparse, Store-Sparse Token Pruning for Video Object Segmentation

author.name: Avilasha Mandal, Sarvesh Shashikumar

entry.summary: RS3-Prune is a training-free token-pruning recipe for memory-bank video object segmentation, instantiating as inference hooks that compress the read-sparse, store-sparse token budget governing per-frame latency and peak GPU memory, enabling long-form video and real-time deployment on memory-bounded accelerators.

entry.title: SymmAdapt: Symmetrical Flow Matching for Source-Free Domain Adaptation in Medical Image Segmentation

author.name: Tal Grossman, Noa Cahan, Hayit Greenspan

entry.summary: SymmAdapt applies Symmetrical Flow Matching to source-free unsupervised domain adaptation for medical image segmentation, jointly segmenting inputs and synthesizing source-like images within one learned flow initialized from a domain-agnostic Gaussian origin, grounding predictions in anatomy rather than shifted texture statistics without accessing sensitive source data.

entry.title: MorphoCLIP: Text-Supervised Contrastive Learning for Perturbation Matching in Cell Painting Images

author.name: Sukhrobbek Ilyosbekov (Northeastern University), Shubham Gajjar (Northeastern University), Rongfei Jin (Northeastern University)

entry.summary: MorphoCLIP links Cell Painting microscopy profiles with text descriptions of compounds, CRISPR knockouts, and ORF overexpressions via contrastive learning with frozen backbones and only a compact cross-channel module trainable on a consumer GPU, enabling bidirectional search between cell images and perturbation descriptions on held-out CPJUMP1 data.

entry.title: CHIMERA Challenge: Biochemical Recurrence Prediction in Prostate Cancer Patients using multimodal datasets

author.name: Robert N. Spaans, Catherine Chia, Tongjie Wang, Adam Kowalewski, Parandzem Khachatryan, Domingos Oliveira, Khrystyna Faryna, Jean-Paul A. van Basten, Geert Litjens, Nadieh Khalili

entry.summary: CHIMERA Challenge establishes a multimodal prostate cancer biochemical-recurrence benchmark integrating mpMRI, histopathology WSIs, and clinical variables from 267 patients across two institutions (801 MRI sequences, 942 WSIs). First standardized multimodal prognostic benchmark in urological oncology.

entry.title: Why Personalization Matters: Cross-Subject Challenges in EMG-IMU-based HRI Activity Recognition

author.name: Ruan Rithelle Chagas de Faria Carminati, Giovanni Braglia, Luigi Biagiotti, Ronnier Frates Rohrich, Andre Schneider de Oliveira, Mikael Nedel Hartmann, Andr\'e Eugenio Lazzaretti

entry.summary: Introduces MAGIC-HRI, a multimodal EMG-IMU dataset with 53 movement classes including sign-language numbers, handover actions, and assembly motions collected from 11 participants, and analyzes cross-subject personalization challenges for activity recognition in HRI.

entry.title: An Interpretable Deep Learning Framework for Material Perception and Classification from Multisensory Tactile Data

author.name: Li Zou, Dave Hogendoorn, Yasemin Vardar

entry.summary: Three interconnected deep learning models map multisensory tactile data to material perception without hand-crafted features, progressing from raw interaction signals to perceptual attribute distributions to material classification. Improves interpretability of robotic touch perception.

entry.title: A Unified Neural-Aided Alignment and Calibration Method for AUVs

author.name: Guy Damari, Zeev Yampolsky, Itzik Klein

entry.summary: Fully neural-aided DVL initialization pipeline for AUVs replacing conventional model-based alignment and calibration stages, removing complex maneuvers, surface satellite references, and simplified error models.

entry.title: Spinning Quadrotor: Hover Thrust Augmentation with Passive Lifting Surfaces

author.name: Aniketh Parkala, Harikumar Kandath

entry.summary: Proposes intentionally spinning quadrotors that convert power otherwise spent suppressing yaw into aerodynamic lift from passive surfaces, showing a 22 percent hover-thrust reduction in preliminary hardware tests with low-Reynolds airfoil selection.

entry.title: ExploreAI: Agentic Exploration Knowledge Bases for Reproducible Observable-Regression Testing of Black-Box VR and 3D Applications

author.name: Jiajie Wang, Kebin Peng, Wei Wang, Xiaoyin Wang, Sen He, Xue Qin

entry.summary: ExploreAI is an LLM-driven agentic framework for reproducible observable-regression testing of black-box VR and 3D applications, mimicking human exploratory testing decisions such as choosing objects to inspect and deciding when missing evidence warrants another attempt.

entry.title: Software Frameworks for Explainable AI in Time Series Classification: A Systematic Review

author.name: Louis Peter, Nils Gumpfer, Jana Fischer, Christin Seifert, Jennifer Hannig

entry.summary: A systematic review of software frameworks for explainable AI in time series classification, examining available explanation-generation tools, their evaluation practices, time-series-specific limitations, and cross-framework consistency. It maps a fragmented landscape into a structured comparison.

entry.title: A-CPES: A Reference Framework for Agentic AI in Cyber-Physical Energy Systems

author.name: Xiaoyu Zhang, Qiuye Sun, Jiachen Xu, Zhongming Yao, Yushuai Li

entry.summary: A-CPES proposes a three-ring nested authorization framework positioning agentic AI as the outer loop of cyber-physical energy system control, calling optimization models rather than being called by them. It maps dispatcher work loops that automation has never covered onto agentic capabilities.

entry.title: SA-RSQ: A Versatile Sparse Representation Framework for Multi-modal Recommender Systems

author.name: Xiang Wang, Shigang Quan, Tingzhen Chang, Kang Yang, Sitong Chen, Yabo Fan, Xingxing Wang, Zhaodian He

entry.summary: SA-RSQ uses Top-K sparse routing and softmax weights to store compact index-probability tuples for multimodal features in industrial recommenders, decoupling storage from codebook dimensionality and avoiding straight-through estimators, validated on a food-delivery advertising dataset.

entry.title: Multi-Task Learning for Non-Canonical Phoneme Recognition via Articulatory Feature Decomposition

author.name: Sophia Riaz, Haoze Zheng, Amos Roche, Miyu Zhang, Anamika Ragu, Salvatore Penachio, Kaustav Mukherjee, Aneesh Jonelagadda

entry.summary: This work decomposes non-canonical phoneme recognition into articulatory feature dimensions (manner, place, voicing) via hierarchical multi-task learning, better capturing structured articulatory errors in pathological speech. It addresses the scarcity of labeled clinical speech by exploiting linguistic structure.

entry.title: Pre-Decoding Acoustic Triage for Budgeted Vision-Language Captioning of Untrimmed Egocentric Video

author.name: Masoud Jalayer, Changyi Li, Yu Xiao

entry.summary: This work proposes audio-first triage for budgeted VLM captioning of untrimmed egocentric video, selecting windows worth VLM invocation using audio scored before any video decoding occurs. It avoids the paradox of visual triage requiring the expensive video processing budgets aim to save.

entry.title: GeoRisk-RAG: A Hierarchy-Aware Risk Framework for Improving RAG Reliability through Selective Answering

author.name: Meenu Ravi, Shailik Sarkar, Lulwah AlKulaib, Yordanos Tessema, Chang-Tien Lu

entry.summary: GeoRisk-RAG adds hierarchy-aware geographic risk assessment to RAG so models can abstain when answers are semantically similar but geographically invalid, critical in natural hazard management. It prioritizes selective answering since confidently wrong answers carry high downstream risk.

entry.title: Hyperbolic Hierarchical Clustering for Visual Representation Learning

author.name: Jianan Wei, Guikun Chen, Zhiyuan Weng, Chunchao Guo, Yujia Wang, Wenguan Wang

entry.summary: ClusterMixer replaces opaque token mixers in vision backbones with a transparent, interpretable token mixer grounded in hyperbolic hierarchical clustering. It revisits classic clustering as a backbone component while remaining competitive on accuracy-cost trade-offs.

entry.title: AraDetox: A Multi-Dialect Arabic Detoxification Dataset

author.name: Mo El-Haj

entry.summary: AraDetox provides 10,500 harmful Arabic social-media posts and 84,000 detoxified rewrites across Modern Standard, Gulf, Levantine, and Egyptian Arabic, generated with GPT-5 and Gemini 2.5 Flash and validated via human evaluation. Findings show detoxification is largely meaning-preserving rewriting with high semantic similarity despite lexical reformulation.

entry.title: Cross-Domain, Multi-Task Data-to-Text Generation without In-Domain Training Data

author.name: Yifei Song, Kun Efimov-Zhang, Claire Gardent

entry.summary: This paper studies cross-domain data-to-text generation where neither in-domain training text nor test references exist, comparing data-driven knowledge distillation against zero-shot inference and out-of-domain fine-tuning across tables, knowledge graphs, charts, and time series. Structure-preserving augmentation via structural templates supports distillation quality.

entry.title: When Names Cross Scripts: A Source-Grounded Benchmark for Historical Entity Reconciliation in the Mongol World

author.name: Xiang Chen, Zeyu Zhang

entry.summary: MHER is a provenance-controlled benchmark for historical entity reconciliation across languages and scripts in the Mongol world, containing 396 balanced name-pair instances plus a stricter source-grounded subset with entity-disjoint splits. Experiments across five generative systems show source-grounded evidence lifts paired accuracy dramatically.

entry.title: Do Time-Series Foundation Models Pay Off for Industrial Monitoring? A Cost-Aware Empirical Study

author.name: Guan-Hua Wen, Kuan-Yu Chen

entry.summary: A cost-aware empirical study assessing whether time-series foundation models (MOMENT-small, Chronos, others) pay off for industrial monitoring across degradation-risk, anomalous-sound detection, and forecasting-residual diagnostics. Finds lightweight classical baselines remain competitive under task-specific constraints.

entry.title: Traceable Spectral Inference via Influence Functions: Efficient Data Attribution and Error Proxies for the Ariel Mission

author.name: Nikki Grens, Lu\'is F. Sim\~oes, Kai Hou Yip, Theresa Lueftinger

entry.summary: Applies influence functions for training data attribution to ESA Ariel mission spectroscopy pipelines, reformulating influence in terms of prediction for label-free use and exploiting closed-form ridge solutions of extreme learning machines for efficient computation. Also derives a conservative error proxy.

entry.title: Which Histories Matter for Time Series Forecasting? Learning Predictive Relevance with Future Supervision

author.name: Yong-Hoon Choi, Youngjin Cho

entry.summary: Defines predictive relevance for historical retrieval in time-series forecasting as expected future utility conditioned on inference-time information, trained with realized futures as privileged supervision, reranking similarity-based candidates with a lightweight listwise MLP while keeping inference strictly past-only.

entry.title: LLM Pedagogical Behavior in AI Tutoring Interactions

author.name: Suhyeon Lee, Juneha Baek, Jaehyeong Park, Donghyuk Shin

entry.summary: Develops a validated five-level scaffolding scale measuring how directly LLM tutors assist students, and applies it to 14,637 responses from 203 students in a university course, finding over 95% of responses fall in the highest-assistance Explaining or Solving categories.

entry.title: AnaDiffusion: Anatomically CompositionalLatent Diffusion for Controllable 3D Brain MRI Generation

author.name: Huiwen Han, Lulin Liu, Bangya Liu, Yuanhao Cai, Nuo Chen, Xiaoqing Wang, Ziqian Xie, Chenyu You, Shuiwang Ji, Degui Zhi, Zhiwen Fan

entry.summary: AnaDiffusion factorizes 3D brain MRI generation into anatomically meaningful part diffusion models followed by part-to-whole assembly and global refinement, enabling local anatomical controllability absent from monolithic generators. Useful for medical simulation and counterfactual anatomy studies.

entry.title: Generate in the Chart, Not on the Boundary: Function-Symbol Grounding for Hard Constraints in LTN-GANs

author.name: Nijesh Upreti, Vaishak Belle

entry.summary: Within Logic Tensor Network GANs, the authors compare grounding logical axioms as predicates (scoring samples fuzzily) versus as function symbols embedded in generation, showing function-symbol grounding enforces hard structural constraints like orderings and positivity more reliably than predicate-level grounding or constraint clamping layers.

entry.title: Robustness Analysis of Agentic AI to Inconsistent and Incomplete Tool Responses

author.name: Jiachen Xu, Torben Bach Pedersen, Zhongming Yao, Xiaoyu Zhang, Yushuai Li

entry.summary: This qualitative pilot study injects controlled faults into a retail customer-service agent domain and reads log-probability channels to distinguish incomplete tool failures from well-formed falsehoods at the moment the return arrives. It scores single decision points rather than full agent runs.

entry.title: Joint Causal Structure and Cluster Discovery Using Variational Inference

author.name: Avni Rajpal, Anubhav Kumar, Rishabh Karnad, Mohammad Emtiyaz Khan, P. K. Srijith

entry.summary: This paper jointly infers latent variable clusters and causal structure among them via variational inference, using categorical and Bernoulli variational distributions over clusters and graphs. It removes the assumption that group structure is known a priori in applications like brain imaging and climate modeling.

entry.title: Clinical Graph-JEPA: Predictive Patient-State Knowledge Graphs for Cognitive Decision Support

author.name: Kushagra Yadav, Nalin Prabhath, Amit Lamba, Goeun Han, Yining Mao

entry.summary: Clinical Graph-JEPA combines multi-agent relation proposal, ontology-aware normalization, deterministic evidence scoring, and JEPA-based latent refinement to build predictive patient-state knowledge graphs from MIMIC-IV records. Graphs are treated as predictive representations rather than static extraction artifacts for cognitive decision support.

entry.title: Don't Repeat Yourself: Stopping Verbatim Loops at Sampling Time

author.name: Philipp Emanuel Weidmann, Allen Roush, Judah Goldfeder, Sanjay Basu, Ravid Shwartz-Ziv

entry.summary: DRY penalizes candidate tokens only when generating them would extend the current suffix into an exact continuation of an earlier span, stopping verbatim loops at sampling time with sequence breakers protecting formatting. It suppresses looping across models from 1.5B to 120B parameters without degrading fluency.

entry.title: Hierarchy-Aware Supervised Uncertainty Estimation for Black-box LLM Taxonomic Reasoning

author.name: Shuting Xie, Nathaniel Lesperance, Graham W. Taylor

entry.summary: This work trains hierarchy-aware supervised uncertainty estimators using proxy features from an open-source tool LLM to predict rank-wise correctness of black-box LLM taxonomic reasoning in biodiversity monitoring. Supervised estimators lift micro AUROC from 0.57 to 0.75-0.80 over likelihood baselines.

entry.title: LITERARYBIGFIVE: Author-Personalized Text Generation in a Unified Interpretable Space

author.name: Jinghui Zhang, Lang Gao, Ao Li, Mingzhe Li, Ruihong Zeng, Zirui Song, Kentaro Inui, Xiuying Chen

entry.summary: LiteraryBigFive reframes authorial style as coordinates in an interpretable space inspired by Big Five personality dimensions, enabling author-personalized text generation without per-author fine-tuning. The dimensional representation improves generalization and interpretability over independent stylistic labels.

entry.title: Reading the Room: Implicit Confusion Encoding in Recurrent World Model States

author.name: Donald Aadithiyan

entry.summary: This single-author empirical study shows DreamerV3-style RSSM recurrent states encode their own confusion nearly orthogonally to directions of maximal variance, detectable by linear probes (AUROC 0.72) even when prediction error is held fixed, and functionally distinct from ensemble disagreement or reconstruction error. A discounted count of recent high-error steps explains most probe variance.

entry.title: Macro-Action Topological Navigation under Noisy Localization using Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Simon Hakenes, Tobias Glasmachers

entry.summary: Builds an RL navigation agent for photorealistic 3D apartments from raw pixels that estimates its own pose onboard using ORB feature banks fused through an EKF, removing reliance on simulator ground-truth pose. Handles sequential multi-object retrieval with changing target positions.

entry.title: Hierarchical Exponential-Gaussian Mixtures for Watch-Time Distribution Prediction

author.name: Sofia Gulevskaia, Mikhail Trapeznikov, Aleksandr Poslavsky, Alexander D'yakonov

entry.summary: Large-scale reproduction of the Exponential-Gaussian Mixture Network for watch-time prediction reveals variance collapse, component redundancy, and inactive components; proposes Hierarchical Exponential-Gaussian Mixtures with skip-watch decomposition and KL-based regularization to fix these failure modes.

entry.title: SketchFlow: Zero-Shot Vector Sketch Generation via GMM Prior Flow in CLIP Latent Space

author.name: Jin Zhou, Hongliang Yang, Pengfei Xu, Hui Huang

entry.summary: SketchFlow generates vector sketches zero-shot by formulating cross-modal alignment as continuous optimal transport between text and sketch distributions in CLIP latent space, using flow matching with a GMM prior. It bypasses scarce fine-grained text-to-sketch paired data and unstable optimization-based alternatives while generalizing to unseen categories.

entry.title: SpatialDiff: 3D-Aware Object Movement via Implicit Spatial Modeling

author.name: Zheng Liu, Zijian He, Huiguo He, Weizhi Zhong, Yejun Tang, Huan Yang, Kun Gai, Guanbin Li

entry.summary: SpatialDiff enables precise 3D-aware object movement in complex scenes during image editing by implicitly modeling spatial structures, handling cases where objects span depth layers or are partially occluded. Its innovations move beyond planar 2D features and explicit positional information that fail to capture true 3D relationships.

entry.title: Vehicle speed dataset for the major European road network derived from Sentinel-2 imagery, 2022-2026

author.name: Maciej Adamiak, Sascha Fendrich, Julian Psotta, Alexander Zipf

entry.summary: This dataset derives individual vehicle speed observations across the European E-road network for 2022-2026 from Copernicus Sentinel-2 optical imagery, exploiting inter-band acquisition delays so moving vehicles appear displaced across blue, green, and red bands. Displaced intensity peaks are linked into trajectories and converted to speeds.

entry.title: HeatTok: Enhancing Remote Sensing Image Understanding via Thermodiffusion-based Tokenization

author.name: Yingying Yan, Jiaqi Tang, Wei Wei, Qianzhou Wang, Jinjian Wu, Botong Geng, Jianmin Chen, Yuyang Xia, Lei Zhang

entry.summary: HeatTok improves remote sensing image understanding in MLLMs via thermodiffusion-based tokenization that merges adjacent homogeneous regions into semantically independent, object-aligned irregular tokens, replacing patch partitioning that causes semantic mixture and fragmentation for irregular geo-object contours, with dedicated geometric positional encodings.

entry.title: Seeing the Unseen: Semantic-in-Gaussian for Sparse-View 3D Generalization

author.name: Zeyang Bai, Yunpeng Wang, Yunbiao Wang, Jun Xiao

entry.summary: SeeU advances generalizable sparse-view 3D Gaussian splatting with Semantic-in-Gaussian design: a Cross-view Entropy-Aware module aggregates multi-view semantic and geometric cues into embeddings guiding a Conditional Gaussian Transformer, addressing incomplete surfaces and structural collapse in partially observed regions.

entry.title: NemoSplat: Feed-Forward 4D Gaussian Splatting for Media-Aware Underwater Reconstruction

author.name: Xiaopeng Guo, Wai Chung Tse, Yipeng Zhu, Hanwen Zhang, Huajian Huang, Sai-Kit Yeung

entry.summary: NemoSplat is the first feed-forward 4D Gaussian Splatting framework for media-aware underwater dynamic reconstruction from uncalibrated marine videos, handling light attenuation and moving objects that break standard feed-forward trackers. Extends generalized reconstruction to a harsh domain.

entry.title: On the Optimized Use of Non-Orthonormality Constraints for the Quasi-Static INS Alignment of Autonomous Underwater and Surface Vehicles

author.name: Carlos Renato C. Durao, Felipe O. Silva, Itzik Klein, Vin{\i}cius M. G. B. Cavalcanti, Adriano Frutuoso, Ettore A. de Barros, Jay A. Farrell

entry.summary: Improves quasi-static inertial navigation alignment for autonomous marine vehicles with an optimized TRIAD coarse-bias-estimation method and enhanced zero-velocity-update EKF fine alignment. Targets faster convergence and better bias observability than conventional two-stage approaches.

entry.title: Quantifying geographic domain shift to decouple the geospatial transferability of human mobility flow generation models

author.name: Zhiyong Zhou, Song Gao, Qianheng Zhang, Feng Zhang, Zhenhong Du

entry.summary: The study quantifies geographic domain shift to explain why human mobility flow generation models transfer poorly across regions, introducing a geographic domain shift metric grounded in domain adaptation theory and evaluating four representative models on commuting flows across 2,265 US counties.

entry.title: Addressing the Selection Problem in Explainable AI

author.name: Claire Vlases, Katelyn Morrison

entry.summary: The paper formalizes the selection problem in explainable AI: users struggle to map their natural-language uncertainty onto the appropriate XAI technique given siloed technique-oriented interfaces. It offers a philosophical formalization using premise-conclusion logic and argues interfaces should start from user uncertainty.

entry.title: Let the Bullets Fly: Multimodal Fake News Detection with Temporal-Aligned Generative Danmaku

author.name: Xiansheng Luo, Chaowei Zhang, Zewei Zhang, Yi Zhu, Jipeng Qiang

entry.summary: Genda simulates temporal Danmaku (bullet comment) dynamics with a trigger predicting timing and intent, generating aligned comments to provide discriminative social signals for fake news detection despite real-world accumulation latency.

entry.title: Artificial Empathy: Towards a Framework for Unsupervised Agency Detection and Policy Reconstruction

author.name: Peter Kuhn, Chris Pang, Sonakshi Chauhan

entry.summary: This framework uses an RL agent trained on an independent task as a prior about agentic dynamics to perform unsupervised agency detection and policy reconstruction of other agents from observation alone, a less constrained problem than inverse RL.

entry.title: Walking on the DARKSIDE

author.name: Aldo Gangemi, Emanuele Bottazzi

entry.summary: This paper shows that Logic-Augmented Generation methods like POLANYI++ can reify fabricated authorities or flawed analogies from input text into structured knowledge graphs, making errors hard to detect downstream. It proposes DARKSIDE, an approach to detect such sophisticated nonsensical inputs before they contaminate Extended Knowledge Graphs. Relevant to trustworthiness of LLM-driven structured knowledge extraction.

entry.title: StrategyBench: Evaluating Explicit Strategy Induction in Large Language Models

author.name: Jinghan Tan, Yuanzheng Wang, Lu Chen, Zijun Chen, Yuqian Wang, Maosong Sun

entry.summary: StrategyBench evaluates whether LLMs can explicitly induce task strategies from few-shot examples rather than relying on direct in-context imitation, using strategy-inducible BIG-Bench tasks with metrics for strategy quality and downstream utility. It probes a human-like abstraction ability relevant to data-scarce adaptation. Findings inform how ICL sensitivity can be reduced.

entry.title: PepLLM: ESM-Guided Llama for Structured Protein-Peptide Binding Interface Analysis

author.name: Hao Qian, Shikui Tu, Lei Xu

entry.summary: PepLLM instruction-tunes Llama with ESM protein embeddings to generate machine-readable JSON annotations of protein-peptide binding interfaces, covering burial state, hydrogen bonds, salt bridges, hotspots, hydrophobicity, and electrostatics. Moves beyond classification toward structured mechanistic interface understanding for drug discovery. Applied bio-ML with a useful output format.

entry.title: Variance Driven Exploration: A Provable and Efficient Methodology for Pure Exploration in Highly Stochastic Environments

author.name: Khang Luong, Nam Nguyen, Hoang Ta, Hung The Tran, Tuan Dam

entry.summary: WebVisus is a constrained, resource-aware multi-agent system that discovers and autonomously explores remote multiresolution scientific datasets given a natural-language research question. Agents adapt data resolution and retrieval quality to available client memory while examining slices, volumes, and timesteps.

entry.title: On Predicting Vulnerability Severity Using In-Context Learning: An Industrial Case Study

author.name: Daniel Rodriguez-Cardenas, David Nader Palacio, Anna Schmedding, Yiyang Lu, Aadil Mallick, Bill Hudson, Chris Gourley, Michael Roytman, Chris Shenefiel, Evgenia Smirni, Denys Poshyvanyk

entry.summary: An industrial case study predicting CVSS v3.1 vulnerability severity from C/C++ snippets using locally deployable open-source LLMs with in-context learning, motivated by confidentiality concerns around cloud services. It validates Big-Vul as a proxy for proprietary data and varies prompting configurations.

entry.title: FreKoo++: Learning Continuous Spectral Dynamics for Temporal Domain Generalization

author.name: En Yu, Xiaoyu Yang, Wei Duan, Guangquan Zhang, Jie Lu

entry.summary: FreKoo++ unifies continuous Koopman modal dynamics with adaptive spectral disentanglement for temporal domain generalization under concept drift, handling multi-scale drift patterns and irregular observations. Source-domain parameters are mapped to a compact latent space with spectral dynamics.

entry.title: TransHands: Repurposing Human Pose Encoders as Hand Pose Encoders

author.name: Milo Piccioli, Gianluca Amprimo, Claudia Ferraris, Gabriella Olmo

entry.summary: TransHands transfers motion representations learned from large body pose corpora to 3D hand pose estimation via a backbone-agnostic two-stage fine-tuning strategy with a lightweight hand-specific input adapter. This sidesteps the scarcity of large 3D hand pose datasets.

entry.title: Do Not Copy/Paste: Soft Barriers for Copying in AI-Assisted Programming

author.name: Iyiola E. Olatunji, Alberick Euraste Djire, Jacques Klein, Tegawend\'e F. Bissyand\'e

entry.summary: This paper frames copy-paste of AI-generated code as an unmanaged AI code handoff boundary and proposes soft barriers - friction mechanisms mediating transfer into editors or commits. It argues assistants should be evaluated on how they mediate code transfer, not only what they generate.

entry.title: RACO: Reliability-Aware Coarse-Goal Optimization for Inspection-Oriented UAV Vision-Language Navigation

author.name: Sen Wang, Yiming Sun, Jiaxuan He, Pengfei Zhu

entry.summary: RACO targets inspection-oriented UAV vision-language navigation where agents must stop in valid regions and avoid confirming distractors, introducing LG-UVI derived from CityNav/CityRefer. It addresses unreliable coarse goals that drift toward plausible but incorrect object regions.

entry.title: XTC: Head-Aware Sampling by Excluding Top Choices

author.name: Philipp Emanuel Weidmann, Allen Roush, Judah Goldfeder, Sanjay Basu, Ravid Shwartz-Ziv

entry.summary: XTC is a lightweight decoding operator that excludes dominant plausible choices when at least two exceed an absolute threshold, promoting diversity in open-ended generation where probability mass concentrates on generic continuations. Across 60 experiments it improves output quality without harming coherence.

entry.title: Fairness-Aware Mixture-of-Experts via Subgroup Reweighting and Gate Regularization

author.name: Sunhee Hwang

entry.summary: This paper identifies routing-induced bias as a failure mode in mixture-of-experts models where subgroup imbalance skews gate assignments, proposing subgroup reweighting and gate regularization for fairness-aware MoE training. It bridges single-stage shared-representation and two-stage decoupled fairness approaches.

entry.title: Deep Learning-Based Multi-User Communication Design for Dense IoT Networks: Interference-Aware Finite-Blocklength Communication and Preliminary MIMO Extensions

author.name: Arkadeep Sinha, Shubham Paul, R. Manivasakan

entry.summary: This paper extends a deep-learning SiameseNet transceiver design from 2 to up to 8 users for dense IoT networks operating at finite blocklengths under multi-user interference. The learned redundancy approach achieves strong block error rate performance versus non-orthogonal access baselines without joint detection.

entry.title: Adaptive Item-based Collaborative Structures via Noise Rescheduling in Diffusion for Generative Recommendation

author.name: Jiaqi Wang, Tianying Liu, Heng Chang, Jihong Guan, Wengen Li, Shuigeng Zhou

entry.summary: ANR-DiffRec integrates item-based collaborative filtering priors into discrete diffusion recommendation models, adding adaptive noise schedules that respect item-level structural dependencies instead of uniform denoising. It addresses both semantic-only item representations and indiscriminate noise treatment.

entry.title: Loss-Parameterized Fisher Width Along Learning Trajectories

author.name: Vu Khac Ky

entry.summary: This theory paper tracks loss-parameterized Fisher width along learning trajectories, deriving exact trace-shape factorizations and showing in Gaussian-teacher logistic models that teacher-aligned states maximize Fisher width and trace below log-2 loss, with gradient flow selecting this branch asymptotically. It connects loss levels to geometric properties of learned representations.

entry.title: Rethinking Communication Metrics: How Should We Measure Meaning?

author.name: Niloofar Tavakolian, Hakimeh Purmehdi, Jungyeon Baek

entry.summary: This survey unifies evaluation metrics for semantic communication systems across telecommunications, NLP, and vision, focusing on meaning preservation rather than symbol reconstruction. It catalogs KPIs for text- and image-based systems under a single evaluation-centered taxonomy. It fills a genuine fragmentation gap in a growing field.

entry.title: Bounded Precision-Geometry Scaling for Robust Multi-Task Learning under Loss Scale Mismatch

author.name: Krishna Subedi

entry.summary: BPGS stabilizes multi-task learning when task losses span orders of magnitude by mapping each task log-variance through a bounded sigmoid parameterization anchored to detached batch statistics. Task weights are provably invariant to uniform loss rescaling. It improves robustness of homoscedastic uncertainty weighting on standard benchmarks.

entry.title: How Architecture and Training Affect TPC Representations Across Experiments

author.name: Tyler Wheeler, Michelle P. Kuchera, Raghuram Ramanujan, William Sieland, Ryan Krupp, Daniel Bazin, Connor L. Cross, Hoi Yan Ian Heung, Andrew J. Jones, Ruchi Mahajan, Saiprasad Ravishankar, Pranjal Singh, Benjamin Votaw, Chris Wrede

entry.summary: Using frozen-encoder probes on time projection chamber (TPC) physics data, this work evaluates how learned representations transfer across experiments and detector systems toward foundation-model approaches in experimental physics. Probes reveal task-relevant structure before fine-tuning and disentangle architecture versus training contributions. It informs reuse strategies for physics foundation models.

entry.title: Resilient Concurrent Causal Discovery for Topological Event Sequences

author.name: Jiyu Tian, Junhao Dong, Mingchu Li, Lingling Fang, Liming Chen, Andreas Holzinger, Zheng Yan, Yew Soon Ong

entry.summary: RCCD performs causal discovery on topological event sequences, capturing concurrent many-to-one causal interactions via influence-aware hyperedge attention and hyperedge causal convolution while remaining robust to incomplete sequences. It targets reliability analysis of networks. The method handles concurrency that prior causal discovery approaches miss.

entry.title: Stochastic gradient descent with initial regularization

author.name: Nabil Kahal\'e

entry.summary: Analyzes SGD with initial regularization (SGDIR), deriving dimension-free excess-risk upper bounds for squared loss that reach m^-3+epsilon rates in favorable regimes, with matching lower bounds up to polylog factors. Covers noiseless and noisy cases under moment, source, and capacity assumptions.

entry.title: From Multimodal Observation to Interpretable Suggestions: Counterfactual Time-Expanded Relational Modeling of Surgical Teams

author.name: Vincenzo Marco De Luca, Antonio Longa, Giovanna Varni, Andrea Passerini

entry.summary: A tempo-relational framework using time-expanded graphs to model surgical team dynamics from multimodal observations, enabling counterfactual generation of interpretable teamwork suggestions. Designed for low-data regimes typical of operating rooms.

entry.title: Sharp Barron Regularity Results for Coulombic Many-Electron Wave Functions

author.name: Pingbing Ming, Hao Yu

entry.summary: Establishes sharp Barron regularity bounds for Coulombic many-electron wave functions after extracting universal Jastrow cutoff factors, proving the s<2 range is optimal among universal factorizations. Relevant to the mathematical foundations of neural-network ansatzes for quantum many-body problems.

entry.title: Scale-invariant Optimal Sampling for Rare-events Data with Sparse Models

author.name: Jing Wang, HaiYing Wang, Qiang Zhang, Hao Helen Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes a scale-invariant optimal subsampling function for massive rare-events data with sparse models, fixing the problem that existing subsampling probabilities depend on feature scaling and can be arbitrarily distorted by inactive features under inappropriate transformations.

entry.title: EGAMA-RC: Risk-Calibrated Evidence-Gated Adaptive Malware Analysis for Robust and Interpretable Memory-Forensic Triage

author.name: Isaac Kofi Nti

entry.summary: Presents EGAMA-RC, a risk-calibrated evidence-gated framework for memory-forensic malware triage combining SHAP-guided refinement, adversarial and open-family testing, novelty scoring, and runtime-aware routing so low-risk samples auto-accept while uncertain cases escalate to review.

entry.title: Quantum Reservoir Computing with Physics-Informed Correction for Reduced-Order PDE Forecasting

author.name: Krishna Bhatia, Harsh, Shalini Devendrababu

entry.summary: Proposes a hybrid quantum reservoir computer plus PINN-based physics-informed corrector for reduced-order PDE forecasting, improving chaotic Kuramoto-Sivashinsky predictions over QRC alone while noting Burgers remains dominated by simple baselines.

entry.title: Beyond chlorophyll: machine learning estimates of diagnostic phytoplankton pigments from multispectral ocean colour data

author.name: David Moffat, Angus Laurenson, Victor Martinez-Vicente, Gemma Kulk, Xuerong Sun, Robert J. W. Brewin, Shubha Sathyendranath

entry.summary: Applies machine learning to multispectral ocean-colour satellite data to retrieve diagnostic phytoplankton accessory pigments beyond chlorophyll-a, enabling large-scale inference of plankton community composition relevant to marine ecosystems and the carbon cycle.

entry.title: Evidence-State Reliability Under Controlled Degradation: Parser-Validity Divergence in a Multi-Stage LLM Pipeline

author.name: Naimur Rahman

entry.summary: Operationalizes Evidence-State Reliability, an evaluation layer checking whether intermediate evidence in multi-stage LLM pipelines stays complete, grounded, and usable separately from structural parser validity, tested on GLM-5.2 (an existing model released mid-2026) across 60 base cases under four degradation conditions.

entry.title: Don' t Box Me In: Dynamic Cultural Adaptation and Cognitive Tracking for Social Understanding

author.name: Chongyuan Dai, Yaling Shen, Shengeng Tang, Hui Ma, Jinpeng Hu

entry.summary: Proposes DyCAC, a training-free framework that treats culture as a dynamic, context-dependent influence rather than a static demographic attribute in LLM social understanding, combining dynamic cultural adaptation with continuous cognitive tracking of interlocutors. Addresses the gap where hybrid cultural identities break fixed-profile approaches.

entry.title: DelistBench: Evaluating Search-Enabled LLMs for Auditable Corporate-Event Database Completion

author.name: Xuan Yao, Li Shuping, Dai Yang, Zhou Yi, Ke-Wei Huang

entry.summary: Defines Search-to-Record, a database-assurance task where search-enabled LLMs reconstruct corporate-event records such as delisting announcements from public sources, and releases DelistBench with 1,200 records. Web access improves announcement-date accuracy by 34-48 points, with the best system reaching 81.5% joint accuracy within seven days.

entry.title: Definitional Sensitivity in Media Bias Detection: A Multi-Definition Dataset and Benchmark

author.name: Martin Wessel, Timo Spinde, J\"urgen Pfeffer, Gianluca Demartini

entry.summary: Shows through a between-subjects experiment with 354 participants and parallel LLM evaluation that differing definitions of media bias lead humans and four LLMs to annotate systematically different constructs, exposing definitional sensitivity that undermines comparability of bias-detection datasets.

entry.title: BIMScript: Material-Aware Structured Scene Programs for BIM Ingestion

author.name: Prakash Kondibhau Naikade, Thomas B. Moeslund, Andreas M{\o}gelmose

entry.summary: BIMScript extends structured scene-program languages like SceneScript with per-element material and condition attributes to support automated ingestion of buildings into BIM tools. It builds a vision-language-model-supervised material-passport corpus over 100k synthetic scenes with 1.9M pseudo-labeled elements and answers what a scene is made of, how fast it can be produced, and where each element is within one grammar.

entry.title: Beyond Visual Similarity: Entity-Aligned Retrieval for Knowledge-Based Visual Question Answering

author.name: Hangrui Xu, Zhengxian Wu, Yunyao Yu, Zhuohong Chen, Rui Cong, Xiangwen Deng, Zhifang Liu, Peng Jiao, Haoqian Wang

entry.summary: KBMR proposes the first MLLM-based embedding retriever for knowledge-based visual question answering, mapping images into a semantic space that preserves entity identity better than CLIP-style dual encoders. It addresses noisy Wikipedia supervision to improve retrieval on long-tail entities where visual similarity misleads.

entry.title: HP-UniIF: Hierarchical Prompt Learning for Unified Image Fusion

author.name: Xingxin Xu, Siqi Zhao, Xin Li, Xinjie Yao, Yiming Sun, Pengfei Zhu

entry.summary: HP-UniIF proposes a unified image fusion framework leveraging diffusion priors to bridge heterogeneous fusion, degradation restoration, and downstream perception within one pipeline. A depth-wise hierarchical conditioning scheme addresses limited adaptability of diffusion models to domain-, degradation-, and task-level objectives simultaneously.

entry.title: Towards Bitstream-corrupted Harsh Visual Understanding: Through Bitstream Language Modeling as Robust Semantic Priors

author.name: Chaoran Huang, Fangcheng Li, Tianyi Liu, Wenyang Liu, Kejun Wu

entry.summary: BLMSP tackles understanding of videos decoded from severely corrupted bitstreams by learning bitstream-native semantic cues through bitstream language modeling and injecting them as priors into off-the-shelf vision models. This addresses irreversible pixel distortion and semantic loss that break standard models in real-world multimedia communication.

entry.title: BC-IHV: Conditioning the Color Space for Stable Rectified-Flow Low-Light Enhancement

author.name: Yi Ai, Zheng Chen, Yuanhao Cai, Yulun Zhang, Xiaokang Yang

entry.summary: BC-IHV proposes Structure-Anchored Rectified Flow for low-light enhancement, maintaining structural correspondence through separate chromaticity and intensity stems, a scale-matched condition pyramid, and location-specific attention assignment. It treats fixed invertible color coordinates as actively reshaping RGB-domain gradients rather than mere representations.

entry.title: ViSMoE: Visual-Aware Sparse Mixture-of-Experts for Embodied Referring Expression Grounding

author.name: Shuo Feng, Piji Li

entry.summary: ViSMoE equips sparse Mixture-of-Experts with a visual-aware routing policy for embodied referring expression grounding, processing views and objects differently instead of using a vanilla vision encoder that produces ambiguous representations. The agent must select navigation views and identify target objects among candidates.

entry.title: Robust Global Structure-from-Motion via View Graph Pruning

author.name: Jiamin Xu, Lixing Yao, Weichen Dai, Renshu Gu, Zunjie Zhu, Weiwei Xu, Gang Xu

entry.summary: This work proposes subgraph-guided view graph pruning for robust global Structure-from-Motion, exploiting internal consistency of reliable subgraphs to identify and remove erroneous edges caused by visually ambiguous matches before joint pose estimation.

entry.title: Competitive Memory Readout for Robust Video Object Segmentation: 2nd Place Technical Report for the MOSEv2 Track of the 8th LSVOS Challenge

author.name: Mingqi Gao, Sijie Li, Jungong Han

entry.summary: This second-place technical report for the MOSEv2 track of the 8th LSVOS Challenge at ECCV 2026 builds on SAM 3 and introduces Competitive Memory Readout, explicitly incorporating same-class competitor evidence when retrieving target memory to avoid confusing annotated targets with visually similar distractors.

entry.title: SAM3Dual: A 3rd Place Solution to the MOSEv2 Track, 8th LSVOS Challenge

author.name: JeongRae Kim, Chaehyun Kim, Changwon Lim

entry.summary: SAM3Dual achieves third place in the MOSEv2 track of the LSVOS Challenge with a training-free inference extension of SAM 3 separating temporal memory into short-term and long-term branches combined via a deterministic sequence-relative fusion schedule modulated by previous-frame confidence. All parameters stay frozen with no task-specific training.

entry.title: DECO: Depth-Guided Co-Visibility Reasoning for Low-Altitude UAV Visual Localization

author.name: Yibin Ye, Xichao Teng, Shuo Chen, Xiaokai Song, Dongdong Guan, Qifeng Yu, Zhang Li

entry.summary: DECO improves low-altitude UAV visual localization in GNSS-denied environments via depth-guided co-visibility reasoning, addressing the mismatch that orthographic reference maps record top-down surfaces while vertical structures like facades are compressed or missing, causing redundant matches and inaccurate PnP poses.

entry.title: When Do VLMs Help Arabic Manuscript OCR? A Cross-Dataset Study

author.name: Moshiur Farazi, Firoj Alam, Abderrahmane Maaradji, Zakaria Maamar, Hamdy Mubarak, Wajdi Zaghouani

entry.summary: This cross-dataset study evaluates traditional OCR, general-purpose VLMs, Arabic-specialized VLMs, and OCR-conditioned VLM correction across eight Arabic text datasets spanning historical manuscripts, aged prints, clean print, and handwriting. No single approach dominates: VLMs approach Tesseract on line-level manuscripts, beat it page-level, and OCR-conditioned correction often wins overall.

entry.title: Hybrid Generative-Discriminative Object Placement

author.name: Siyuan Zhou, Li Niu

entry.summary: This paper applies spiking neural networks to object detection in forward-looking sonar imagery for power-constrained autonomous underwater vehicles, contrasting sparse accumulate-only SNN compute against CNN energy costs exemplified by YOLOv8m at 322 mJ per inference. Sonar is the primary sensing modality in dark or turbid waters.

entry.title: Large-Small Model Collaboration for Zero-Shot Surgical Phase Recognition

author.name: Yiyi Zhang, Ying Zheng, Wenxin Fan, Yu Zhu, Yuchen Yuan, Litao Zhao, Zheng Li, Pheng-Ann Heng

entry.summary: LaST combines surgical foundation models with lightweight task-specific models for zero-shot surgical phase recognition: the FM provides frame-level priors while the small model handles temporal dynamics. Targets generalization to unseen clinical domains. Addresses a real deployment gap in surgical AI.

entry.title: Misanthrope: A Privacy-Preserving Keypoint Detector

author.name: Francesco Vultaggio, Predrag Djindjic, Markus Gerke, Sebastian Tschiatschek, Phillipp Fanta-Jende

entry.summary: Misanthrope trains a privacy-preserving keypoint detector via self-distillation to avoid detecting keypoints on people, mitigating inversion attacks that reconstruct sensitive scene content from local features shared with remote servers. A concrete privacy defense for SLAM and visual localization pipelines.

entry.title: Progressively Learning Heterogeneous Skills in a Unified Latent Space

author.name: Yue-Yi Zhang, Ming Gong, Linpu He, Wei-Shi Zheng, Zhilin Zhao

entry.summary: HetSkills progressively learns heterogeneous skills (tracking, text-to-motion) in a unified latent space for physics-based character control, treating the latent space as a shared executable interface with motion intuition distillation preventing shortcut learning. Advances reusable skill composition in character animation.

entry.title: MomADv2: Reliable Temporal Memory for End-to-End Autonomous Driving

author.name: Ziying Song, Shengkai Zhang, Lin Liu, Peiliang Wu, Lei Yang, Dongyang Xu, Bin Sun, Li Wang, Shaoqing Xu, Caiyan Jia, Yadan Luo

entry.summary: MomADv2 introduces selective state-space planning memory for end-to-end autonomous driving, filtering historical planning queries by temporal continuity and command consistency so stale memory cannot mislead decisions when driving commands change. Improves long-horizon planning reliability.

entry.title: Gimbal-Based Human Tracking for Companion Robots Using Continual Learning

author.name: Cong-Thanh Vu, Ching-Chieh Liu, Yen-Chen Liu

entry.summary: Describes gimbal-mounted camera tracking of humans for companion robots with an active control strategy maintaining the target in view under occlusion and rapid motion, plus a continual learning component for person re-identification. Removes reliance on wearable tags or fixed cameras.

entry.title: Vision-Guided Morphing Quadcopter for Multi-Geometry Payload Transport through Narrow Passages

author.name: Aashish Sahu, Shriram Hari, R. Prasanth Kumar

entry.summary: Vision-guided morphing quadcopter with four hybrid arm-leg structures driven by a tendon mechanism that synchronously retract or expand, enabling grasping of varied payload geometries and traversal of narrow passages.

entry.title: VikPath: A Vision Kansformer Framework for Effective Obstacle Avoidance in Self-Supervised Pathfinding

author.name: Junyao Wang, Yulin Xu, Mohammad Abdullah Al Faruque

entry.summary: VikPath uses a Kansformer (KAN-transformer hybrid) for self-supervised obstacle-avoiding pathfinding, removing dependence on labels generated by conventional planners like A*.

entry.title: Distillation of the AI2040 Alignment Roadmap

author.name: Towards_Keeperhood

entry.summary: A community distillation of the AI2040 alignment roadmap separating macro-plan choices for a frontier company navigating an intelligence explosion from its safety strategy, with diagrams and structural reorganization.

entry.title: Import AI 470: No rights for machines; automating environment generation with SPADE; and building better GPU kernels with Hawkeye

author.name: Jack Clark

entry.summary: Import AI 470 covers a METR study finding AI strongly accelerates cyber vulnerability discovery, moderately aids mathematics, with unclear effects on AI research itself, plus SPADE environment generation and Hawkeye GPU kernel work.

entry.title: LLM-Based Selection of Incongruent Verbal and Nonverbal Behavior for Virtual Humans

author.name: Parisa Ghanad Torshizi, Stacy Marsella

entry.summary: This work uses LLMs to select incongruent verbal and nonverbal behavior for virtual humans, modeling how nonverbal channels can reinforce, qualify, or contradict speech based on roles, relationships, and internal states including emotional leakage.

entry.title: Hybrid Panels: Toward Human-AI Collaboration in Survey Research

author.name: Julia Romberg, Tobias Gummer, Gabriella Lapesa, Tanja Kunz, Claudia Wagner

entry.summary: This position/pilot paper proposes hybrid panels - longitudinal AI-enabled surveys that iteratively align LLMs with a target population to address declining response rates and nonresponse bias in social research. A first pilot demonstrates the iterative alignment workflow.

entry.title: Counterfactual Transition Graphs: Evaluating Cross-Class Transition Quality

author.name: Syed Muhammad Hamza Zaidi, Szymon Bobek, Grzegorz J. Nalepa, Myra Spiliopoulou

entry.summary: This paper proposes counterfactual transition graphs where nodes are classes and edge weights are counterfactual reliability between class prototypes, revealing structural relationships a confusion matrix cannot show. On hand-movement classification, counterfactual reachability does not align with classifier accuracy structure.

entry.title: Towards Actionable Surgical Team Dynamics: from Teamwork to Counterfactual Annotations

author.name: Vincenzo Marco De Luca, Antonio Longa, Andrea Passerini

entry.summary: Introduces an extended multimodal dataset for surgical team interaction analysis built from real operating room recordings, adding speaker diarization, transcripts, and multi-level annotations of team performance. Companion to a time-expanded relational modeling framework.

entry.title: Exploring Long-period Architectures: Four New Planet Candidates from Kepler with Periods >342 days

author.name: Matthew T. Hansen, Jason A. Dittmann

entry.summary: Builds a CNN-based transit detection pipeline leveraging Kepler spacecraft diagnostics to find long-period planets (>342 days), identifying four new candidates and partially correcting the short-period detection bias of the standard Kepler pipeline.

entry.title: SAVER: Selective Auditing of Verbal Evidence for Error Recovery in VLM Change Reasoning

author.name: Youdi Li

entry.summary: SAVER observes that correct VLM outputs on visual change reasoning contain explicit verbal evidence while incorrect ones often lack it, and proposes a lightweight rule-based auditor that triggers structured reprompting only when evidence is missing or inconsistent, improving accuracy across three benchmarks and four VLMs.

entry.title: When the Edit Changes the Patient: Measuring Identity Preservation in Counterfactual Retinal Images

author.name: Andrea Posada, Wenke Karbole, Bach Ngoc Doan, Alexander Weers, Solmaz Abdolrahimzadeh, Maria Patsiamanidi, Kahkashan Haider, Vaishali Khare, Daniel Rueckert, Andrew Lotery, Sobha Sivaprasad, Martin J. Menten

entry.summary: Explicitly measures identity preservation in counterfactual retinal OCT editing across source-anchored, structured-prompt, and paired-training editing methods, challenging the assumption that anchoring to the source image preserves biometric identity. Important caution for counterfactual medical imaging research.

entry.title: Reproducible Vision-Guided 6-DoF Robotic Manipulator with a Mixed Stepper-Driver Architecture and Browser-Native Control

author.name: Lasan Perera, Deneth Priyadarshana, Dulana Pitiwaduge, Isitha Dinujaya, Mokshan Colambage

entry.summary: Presents the NeuralNexus Arm, an open-source low-cost 6-DoF robotic manipulator built by undergraduates, with a mixed stepper-driver architecture on a single STM32 microcontroller and a browser-native control interface. Emphasizes reproducibility through detailed design and debugging documentation.

entry.title: VisAdj: Learning Adjacency Matrices from Node-Link Images

author.name: Jiahao Xie, Guangmo Tong

entry.summary: VisAdj learns adjacency matrices directly from node-link diagram images using an attention-sparse neighbor sampler and a line-graph transformer that models dependencies among candidate edges as tokens, outperforming KNN-heuristic baselines on synthetic graphs, road networks, and vessel images.

entry.title: Jiuge-Tuiqiao: An Interpretable Human-AI System for Classical Chinese Poetry Refinement

author.name: Yufeng Han, Lifan Deng, Cunliang Kong, Wenhao Li, Xin Cong, Yuzhuo Bai, Kangyang Luo, Maosong Sun

entry.summary: Jiuge-Tuiqiao is an interactive human-AI system for classical Chinese poetry refinement built around user-driven control, ancient-text-grounded evidence, and AI-assisted generation, with prosody feedback and interpretable suggestions from collocations and ranked classical lines.

entry.title: Vision-Language Models for Occupational Physical Exposure Assessment: Estimating External Hand Forces in Manual Material Handling Tasks from RGB Video

author.name: Mohammad Sadra Rajabi, Aanuoluwapo Ojelade, Sunwook Kim, Maury A. Nussbaum

entry.summary: A VLM-based pipeline estimates dynamic triaxial bilateral external hand forces during manual material handling from RGB video, combining text-guided ROI localization, pretrained vision transformers, and known box mass across 35 participants. It replaces instrumented objects or specialized sensing for ergonomic exposure assessment.

entry.title: Adapter-Based Few-Shot Continual Learning for Malicious Packet Recognition

author.name: Kyle Stein, Guillermo Francia, III Eman El-Sheikh, Andrew Arash Mahyari

entry.summary: This work applies Few-Shot Class-Incremental Learning to malware packet recognition, proposing a hybrid framework combining self-supervised learning with adapter-based modules to balance stability and plasticity when new malware classes arrive with few labels. It avoids catastrophic forgetting and full retraining.

entry.title: Counter with Evidence! A Multi-Agent Memory Efficient Reasoning Framework for Hate Category Informed Counterspeech Generation

author.name: Sujoy Nath, Aswini Kumar, Tanmoy Chakraborty

entry.summary: FIRE decomposes hate speech into five categories (misinformation, stereotype, conspiracy, dehumanizing, non-factual) and maps each to a targeted counterspeech style via a multi-agent, memory-efficient reasoning framework, contributing FactualCS, a 4,784-instance dataset with category annotations and reasoning traces.

entry.title: AquaFlow: A Monocular Gaussian Splatting SLAM for Underwater Streaming Reconstruction

author.name: Yingxiang Xu, Kerui Ren, Wenqi Guo, Changjian Jiang, Tao Lu, Linning Xu, Mulin Yu

entry.summary: AquaFlow performs monocular Gaussian Splatting streaming reconstruction underwater by fine-tuning a 3D vision foundation model on underwater data for pose and pointmap estimation plus medium-guided Gaussian initialization. Complements NemoSplat in tackling aquatic degradation for SLAM-style reconstruction.

entry.title: Hate Speech Classification In Roman Urdu: A Comparative Study On Parameter Efficient Fine-Tuning And Prompt Engineering

author.name: Toneema Zubair

entry.summary: A comparative study of hate-speech classification for Roman Urdu, a low-resource informal language, evaluating prompt tuning, LoRA-based parameter-efficient fine-tuning, and prompt engineering under various data conditions. It identifies which techniques work best when labeled data is scarce.

entry.title: PatchWrite: One Line, Not One Section -- Compile-Gated, Validity-Preserving Editing for AI-Drafted Manuscripts

author.name: Weiwei Yang

entry.summary: PatchWrite constrains AI manuscript editing to compile-gated, validity-preserving line-level edits with evidence locks requiring cited keys and numeric tokens to be attested by registries or logs, rejecting candidates that fail checks. Stress tests show whole-section rewriting mutates unrelated metrics far more often.

entry.title: Wazobia Eval: A Benchmark for Nigerian Pidgin Emotion Understanding, Sarcasm Detection, and Cultural Reasoning

author.name: Stephanie Okoye

entry.summary: Wazobia Eval is a benchmark for Nigerian Pidgin emotion understanding, sarcasm detection, and cultural reasoning, with 550+ manually annotated examples and a 16-category culturally specific emotion taxonomy. Fills a gap left by translation- and sentiment-focused evaluations of African languages. Standardized protocols enable comparable measurement.

entry.title: Real-TurnTurk: A Multimodal Turkish Corpus for Turn-Taking Prediction

author.name: Ahmet Tu\u{g}rul Bayrak, Fatma Nur Korkmaz, Bekir Berker T\"urker, Mustafa Serta\c{c} T\"urkel, Alper Kaplan

entry.summary: Real-TurnTurk introduces a multimodal Turkish corpus of unscripted dyadic conversations with synchronized video, per-speaker audio channels, and time-aligned transcriptions for turn-taking prediction. A genetic algorithm is employed to optimize prediction features in this underexplored language setting.

entry.title: Self-Supervised Graph Representation Learning for In-The-Wild Wearable and Smartphone based Emotion Recognition

author.name: Ioannis N. Ziogas, Leontios J. Hadjileontiadis, Ahsan H. Khandoker, Aamna Al Shehhi

entry.summary: This paper applies self-supervised graph masking augmentations with subgraph sampling and multi-task inductive graph neural networks to wearable/smartphone emotion recognition on K-EmoPhone. It handles scarce, biased in-the-wild labels via combined supervised, semi-supervised, and SSL mechanisms.

entry.title: DiaRelay: Relaying Dialogue Context with a Constant-Size Memory for Emotion Recognition in Conversation

author.name: Zihao Zhou, Bin Yang, Jinghui Qin, Kebing Jin

entry.summary: DiaRelay maintains a constant-size dialogue-level memory relayed across turns for emotion recognition in conversation, avoiding re-encoding costs of enlarged windows while retaining long-range evidence. Its context-conditioned transformations go beyond fixed-rank LoRA adaptations.

entry.title: FedCC: Towards Addressing Label Distribution Skews in Distillation-Based Federated Learning

author.name: Wenxuan Ye, Onur Ayan, Xueli An, Georg Carle

entry.summary: FedCC addresses label distribution skew in distillation-based federated learning, where clients share predictions on an unlabeled public dataset but majority-class bias degrades calibration without ground-truth labels. The proposed correction algorithm mitigates client bias simply and effectively.

entry.title: FrugalSOT - Frugal Search Over the Models

author.name: Pradheep P, Yuvanesh S, Harish KB, Keerthan Saai Reddy S, Joshva Devadas T, Naveenkumar J, Hemalatha K

entry.summary: FrugalSOT is a resource-aware model selection architecture for on-device NLP inference on constrained hardware like the Raspberry Pi 5. It estimates request complexity and cascades requests from simple to complex models against a continuously updated relevance threshold. It addresses a real deployment problem for edge LLM usage.

entry.title: Contrastive Representation-Guided Genetic Minority Oversampling for Imbalanced Time-Series Classification

author.name: Wenbin Pei, Yunrong Hao, Zhen Liu, Guan Wang, Bing Xue, Yiu-Ming Cheung, Qiang Zhang

entry.summary: Introduces a frequency-domain representation-guided multi-tree genetic programming method for oversampling minority classes in imbalanced time-series classification. Aims to improve diversity and generalization over interpolation and deep generative oversampling.

entry.title: Channel-Token Attention for Reliable Dynamic Spectrum Access under Bursty Primary-User Traffic

author.name: Krishna Acharya, Dinanath Padhya, Utsab Dahal, Ashish Kandel, Binod Sapkota

entry.summary: Presents TACAN, a Transformer policy for dynamic spectrum access representing channels as tokens with occupancy history and modulation-classification entropy, warm-started from a greedy policy and refined with PPO, evaluated under bursty primary-user traffic in a 20-channel setting.

entry.title: Partial-Moment PINNs for Caldeira--Leggett Parameter Learning in Quantum Brownian Motion

author.name: Krishna Bhatia

entry.summary: Builds a moment-level PINN recovering Caldeira-Leggett quantum Brownian motion parameters from partial moment traces, enforcing the CL/HPZ ODEs via automatic differentiation with PSD covariance and fluctuation-dissipation constraints, outperforming finite differences and Kalman-EM on synthetic data.

entry.title: L\"etzCross: A Cross-Lingual Page-Level Benchmark for Multimodal Retrieval over Luxembourgish Documents

author.name: Omar El Bachyr, Fred Philippy, Laura Maria Bernardy, Saad Ezzini, Jacques Klein, Tegawende Bissyande

entry.summary: Develops an interpretable feature-engineering framework for early disruption prediction in the short-pulse ADITYA tokamak, using statistical descriptors like skewness, kurtosis, and wavelet energy entropy from initial plasma evolution before ohmic converter activation. Fills a gap since most disruption predictors target long-pulse devices.

entry.title: HelaBERT: Enhancing Sinhala Language Understanding with Dual Pooling Classification Head

author.name: Thisen Ekanayake, Nisansa de Silva

entry.summary: Presents HelaBERT, BERT-based masked language models pre-trained from scratch on roughly one billion tokens of Sinhala with a morphology-tailored SentencePiece tokenizer, in Small (~23M) and Large (~110M) variants, evaluated across four Sinhala classification tasks.

entry.title: CaRGo-T: Causal Reasoning Graph-of-Thought improves Multimodal Humor Comprehension

author.name: Abhilash Nandy, Rahul Seetharaman, Aman Bansal, Rounak Saha, Manav Nitin Kapadnis, Millon Madhur Das, Pawan Goyal, Niloy Ganguly

entry.summary: SPOC-SQL decomposes text-to-SQL into four sequential subtasks mirroring SQL execution logic and applies stage-specific fine-grained preference optimization so models learn key intermediate decisions rather than optimizing whole queries monolithically.

entry.title: Region-Weighted Losses and Model Fusion for Cross-Modal PET Attenuation Correction

author.name: Khoa Tuan Nguyen, Joris Vankerschaver, Wesley De Neve

entry.summary: This challenge solution for BIC-MAC synthesizes pseudo-CT from non-attenuation-corrected PET, DIXON MRI, and topograms, finding that loss design matters more than architecture: L1 error in Carney attenuation-coefficient space weighted by anatomical region enabled unregistered MRI to help as extra inputs. A fixed convex combination of two independently trained models provided further gains.

entry.title: Entity-Constrained CBCT Retrieval for Low-Resource Dental Record Completion

author.name: Nhi Ngoc-Yen Nguyen, Thai Nguyen, Kiet Huynh Cao Tuan, Huy-Hieu Pham

entry.summary: ECCR completes dental records from CBCT scans under extreme annotation scarcity by separating evidence availability from evidence authority: a corpus-derived prior supplies complete records while a frozen 3D encoder retrieves image-conditioned diagnosis evidence constrained to supported entities. The parameter-free framework avoids harmful unsupported entities in FDI positions and ICD codes.

entry.title: AirAlign: Geometry-Aware Relative Pose Alignment for UAV Last-Meter Navigation

author.name: Jinyi Zhou, Shuo Feng, Yufei Wu, Piji Li

entry.summary: AirAlign performs RGB-only relative pose alignment for UAV last-meter navigation using a pretrained visual geometry reconstruction backbone to extract geometry-aware features from source-target pairs. Scene-disjoint cross-validation folds improve data efficiency under severe viewpoint and appearance variation.

entry.title: C$^2$Path: Class-Conditional Pathway Decoupling for Vision-Language Incremental Object Detection

author.name: Lecheng Xu, Feifei Shao, Ouyangzi Ye, Zhen Wang, Lin Li, Kexin Li, Zhao Wang, Changqin Huang

entry.summary: C2Path addresses class knowledge coupling in vision-language incremental object detection through class-conditional pathway decoupling, establishing dedicated updatable pathways using token-level class cues to prevent boundary erosion and representation entanglement when learning new categories.

entry.title: Trustworthy Visual Quality Inspection under Data Scarcity in Manufacturing

author.name: Panagiotis Sapoutzoglou, Jessy Ribaira, Martin Kanounnikoff, Bas Tijsma, Christian Gei{\ss}, Maria Pateraki

entry.summary: This work addresses trustworthy automated visual inspection in manufacturing under defect scarcity, mitigating data limitations while providing calibrated confidence estimates so routine decisions automate and ambiguous cases route to humans. It explicitly handles the asymmetric costs of false rejects versus false accepts.

entry.title: Close Shortcut Wins Long: Seeking Diverse and Stable Generators for Data-Free Knowledge Distillation

author.name: Kailin Lyu, Zherui Zhang, Junhao Dong, Kexue Fu, Weiguang Pang, Rongtao Xu, Qizheng Wang, Di Wu, Chee-Keong Kwoh, Longxiang Gao, Shibiao Xu, Changwei Wang, Ce Hao, Yu Zhang

entry.summary: CSWL identifies generative shortcut learning in the frequency domain as a cause of pattern collapse in data-free knowledge distillation generators, introducing frequency-domain interventions to close shortcuts and win longer-term diversity and stability. It targets over-reliance on teacher preferences in generator-based DFKD.

entry.title: Self-Calibrating Dense Displacement Fields for Reliable Co-Registration of Large Optical Satellite Imagery

author.name: Shoukun Sun, Zhe Wang, Sanaz Salati, Jiyin Zhang, Hui Wang, Xiaogang Ma

entry.summary: This work presents self-calibrating dense displacement fields for co-registration of large optical satellite imagery, addressing documented sub-pixel-to-tens-of-pixels offsets that degrade change detection and fusion. It handles pairs differing along sensor response, scene content, viewing geometry, resolution, and mosaic seams without embedded motion-model assumptions tuned to development data.

entry.title: Adapting Dense Vision-Language Relationships for Multi-label Classification with Partial Label

author.name: Cheng Chen, Yifan Zhao, Jia Li

entry.summary: LDSA adapts dense vision-language relationships from CLIP for multi-label classification with partial labels, replacing unstable statistical priors with densely contrastive constraints that excavate prior-adaptive relationships from multimodal pretrained models to recover missing semantics without catastrophic overfitting.

entry.title: AcroMELD: Recovering Interactive PDF Forms with Structure-Aware Graph Set Transformers

author.name: Samuel Abramov (Accessful GmbH)

entry.summary: AcroMELD detects missing interactive form fields in visually form-like PDFs using a 39.4M-parameter detector combining high-resolution vision transformers with label-free PDF primitives, employing an 896-query set spanning visual proposals, structure-seeded proposals, and learned recovery queries linked through geometry-biased graph-set layers.

entry.title: Learning Sample-wise Rank-aware Interpolation Weights for Composed Visual Data Retrieval

author.name: Boseung Jeong, Taegyu Park, Donghyeon Kwon, Hyunsouk Cho, Suha Kwak

entry.summary: SRAIN revisits simple linear interpolation for composed visual data retrieval, predicting query-specific interpolation weights measured by discriminability from negatives and proximity to targets, offering a scalable alternative to slow MLLM-based query fusion with prohibitive latency.

entry.title: Following Motion for Sequential Modeling in Video Frame Interpolation

author.name: Jaehyun Park, Nam Ik Cho

entry.summary: MGMVFI adapts selective state space models (Mamba) for video frame interpolation by using optical flow to define a motion-adaptive scanning order, aligning causal state updates with motion trajectories. Improves SSM suitability for dynamic video tasks at linear complexity.

entry.title: ENCORE: Entropy-Guided Cropping and Attention Regularization for Robust Vision--Language Understanding

author.name: Yuanhao Sun, Huawei Ji, Jiaxin Ding, Luoyi Fu, Xinbing Wang

entry.summary: ENCORE discovers that early-layer cross-modal attention entropy correlates with answer grounding quality in lightweight VLMs, then uses entropy-guided cropping at inference and attention regularization in training to preserve prompt-relevant region integrity. Improves robustness of fixed-resolution sub-image encoders.

entry.title: An end-to-end-trained vision-language model for native-language prostate pathology report generation

author.name: Christian Grashei, Fabian G\"ulhan, Maximilian Legnar, Fabian St\"ogbauer, Cleo-Aron Weis, Carolin Mogler, Peter Sch\"uffler

entry.summary: End-to-end-trained slide-level vision-language model generating native-language (German) prostate pathology reports, with tokenizer and model trained from scratch for language independence and an automated pipeline producing 17,344 core-specific pairs. Tackles English-centric encoder limitations in clinical reporting.

entry.title: SVD-Based Typicality Maps for Out-of-Distribution Detection in Vision Transformers

author.name: Aldo Sean Sartor, Leandro de Souza Rosa, Andriy Enttsel, Mauro Mangia, Riccardo Rovatti

entry.summary: Derives post-hoc OOD detection scores for ViTs by SVD-factorizing affine layer weights, projecting activations onto leading singular vectors, fitting class-conditional density models per layer, and stacking typicality maps across depth into Prototype Alignment and related scores. Geometry-of-weights approach requiring no retraining.

entry.title: TONAV: Task-Oriented Navigation and Action-Velocity Chunk Learning for Articulated Object Quadrupedal Mobile Manipulation

author.name: Haoran Lin, Mingyu Yang, Pengfei Qi, Kehan Chen, Qiang Diao, Liangji Zeng, Wenrui Chen, Yaonan Wang, Kailun Yang

entry.summary: TONAV unifies task-oriented navigation with action-velocity chunk learning for quadrupedal mobile manipulation of articulated objects, coupling reachability with manipulation-ready configurations and stable contact via position-velocity-coupled teleoperation data collection. Full-stack quadruped manipulation framework.

entry.title: Stakeholder Insights for Designing In-Home Social Robots for Dementia Disorientation Detection and Caregiver-Aware Intervention

author.name: Emmanuel Akinrintoyo, Nicole Salomons

entry.summary: Stakeholder interview study (14 caregivers and practitioners) identifying requirements for in-home social robots that detect dementia-related disorientation and intervene caregiver-awarely. Frames disorientation support as an under-examined socio-technical challenge.

entry.title: What Does CLIP Learn for Regional Geolocalization? Probing Visual Cues and Scene Configuration After Adaptation

author.name: Changyu Lee, Yeonsoo Park, Abdullah Alfarrarjeh, Seon Ho Kim

entry.summary: Using 9,085 Greater LA street-view images across eight regions, the study probes what CLIP learns for regional geolocalization after adaptation, comparing zero-shot, frozen readouts, partial updates, LoRA, and full fine-tuning. Frozen encoders remain near zero performance, revealing adaptation-dependent visual cue use.

entry.title: AI-based worker guidance in assembly and disassembly operations using multimodal ego/exo-centric data capture and structured task knowledge

author.name: Vivek Chavan, J\"org Kr\"uger

entry.summary: This paper extracts structured task knowledge for assembly/disassembly guidance from expert demonstrations using joint encoding of egocentric and exocentric video with narration. Evaluated on a real-world disassembly case study showing procedural structure capture beyond static image methods.

entry.title: Graph Representation Learning of Lightweight IoT Ciphers

author.name: Jonathan Cook, Sabih ur Rehman, M. Arif Khan

entry.summary: Applies graph representation learning to differential cryptanalysis of SIMON and SIMECK lightweight IoT ciphers, extracting four differential attributes from partial difference distribution tables to identify high-probability differential clusters efficiently.

entry.title: Spyre-Accelerated Retrieval-Augmented Generation on IBM LinuxONE: A Cloud-Native Architecture for Secure, High-Throughput Enterprise AI Inference

author.name: Sandeep Bokkasam, Pankaj D

entry.summary: The paper describes a six-subsystem RAG architecture running entirely on IBM LinuxONE mainframes using the Spyre PCIe accelerator for generative inference and Telum II on-chip acceleration for classification, orchestrated via Red Hat OpenShift. It targets secure enterprise inference where data residency and compliance prevent moving records to external GPU clusters.
